(rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on transport and tourism) − madam president, commissioner, cars and vans together account for more than half of the total greenhouse gas emissions in the european transport sector. the amendment of regulation (ec) no 510/2011 on the reduction of co2 emissions from new light commercial vehicles has a significant impact on both light commercial vehicle users, the automotive and related industries and the environment and aims to reduce fuel consumption and related costs for owners of light commercial vehicles. the 2020 target for vans of 147 g co2/km implies annual fuel consumption reductions of 17% compared to the 2017 target of 175 g. this will stimulate research and innovation in the automotive sector, promoting green growth and green jobs and improving the international competitiveness of the european union industry, while also reducing the union's dependence on oil imports. we welcome the commission's decision to adopt a statement to respond to parliament's request for co2 emissions targets for 2025. we also welcome the shift of the post-2020 decision from 2014 to 2015, which will allow for better documentation with a fairly determined impact. the commission should therefore, by 2015, review and report to the european parliament and the council on its findings on an assessment of the reduction rate needed in line with the union's long-term climate objectives and the implications for the development of cost-effective co2 reduction technologies for light commercial vehicles. i conclude, madam president, by saying that the report should include, where appropriate, proposals to amend this regulation. when drawing up such proposals, the commission should ensure that they are as neutral as possible from a competitive point of view and that they are socially fair and sustainable.
question referred under the 'blue card' procedure i would like to ask mr tatarella: did you know that from the moment a new type of eco-friendly engine is designed, it takes about seven years before it is introduced on the market? that is why i believe that a vision beyond 2020 is needed and this is also provided for in the report on eco-efficient transport by stoa where, together, we are members. so i want you to look at the post-2020 outlook from this perspective, which is that any new green engine doesn't come to market until seven years after it's designed.
madam president, in the european union we agreed to have a european policy to combat climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. that is why tomorrow i will be supporting the regulation we are debating today, which has reached an acceptable compromise on the limits for these greenhouse gases emitted by light commercial vehicles. i would like to point out, however, that the additional effort and costs for the european car industry must be matched by the efforts of third countries, whether large or small car producers. i therefore believe that both the council and the european commission and the european parliament must act to achieve this reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from motor vehicles globally. if we fail to achieve this global target, then we will not only see an increase in global greenhouse gas emissions, but we will also negatively affect the competitiveness of the european automotive industry, which supports millions of jobs in europe.
mr president, i welcome your return and wish you well, commissioner, in the transition to a low-carbon economy, carbon capture and storage technology could be one of the main ways of reconciling the growing demand for fossil fuels with the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. i regret that the majority of the eur 1 billion made available to pilot carbon capture and storage projects in 2009 through the european economic recovery programme has remained unspent and, despite considerable effort and substantial support from the european union, union demonstration projects for commercial-scale carbon capture and storage are experiencing delays. i believe that any policy and strategy on carbon capture and storage should only be based on solid evidence of the positive impact of this technology on the environment, on the stability of union industry, on jobs in the union, and on affordable energy prices for both the public and industry. we call on the commission and the member states to take far-reaching action to stimulate international cooperation and promote the use of climate change mitigation technologies to reorient the burgeoning economies towards a low-carbon development alternative. however, we would point out that carbon capture and storage technologies pose significant environmental risks to both people and agriculture.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the theme 'smart specialisation: creating a network of centres of excellence for an effective cohesion policy'. we call on all regions and member states, if they have not already done so, to accelerate the development of their smart specialisation strategies, so as not to risk delayed receipt of eu funding for relevant operational programmes due to the lack of such a strategy. 'smart specialisation strategy' means national or regional innovation strategies that set priorities with the aim of creating a competitive advantage by developing and matching research and innovation strengths with business needs, in order to address emerging opportunities and market developments in a coherent way, avoiding overlap and fragmentation of efforts, and which may take the form of or are embedded in a national or regional strategic research and innovation (r&i) policy framework. we encourage regions to invest in cross-sectoral and cross-technological activities that can generate cross-links across the entire regional economy, so that the widest range of businesses can contribute to and benefit from more jobs and stronger growth.

in writing. − equal access to quality healthcare is an internationally recognised fundamental right, particularly in the eu. however, the exercise of this right is still constrained in some member states by financial, regional and availability of medical staffing problems. in addition, the economic crisis is leading to cuts in national healthcare budgets, which implies the need to find solutions to increase the effectiveness of health systems and ensure their sustainability. that is why, in voting for the ehealth action plan 2012-2020, i voted for improving access to health services, reducing health costs and ensuring greater equality between european citizens. i believe that ehealth has a very high potential and can bring benefits to healthcare professionals, patients, informal carers and even public authorities. the commission must therefore continue to work towards the widespread adoption of ehealth across the eu. as women are involved at all levels of the health sector, the commission and the member states should consider equal access for women to ehealth, not only as patients but also as carers, ict specialists and decision-makers.
in writing. − i believe that ehealth services for family (informal) carers, who are still predominantly women, need to be encouraged and promoted at european level in order to support them in their often difficult care tasks and to enable them to provide the best possible care.
in writing. − in order to ensure safe and effective healthcare and to provide quality services to patients, i consider it important that certain measures in the field of ehealth are adopted today. these measures are aimed at reducing waiting times for patients, improving working conditions for healthcare workers and facilitating access to healthcare services, especially for people living in remote areas. our main objective is the interest of the patient and the improvement of the quality of care for citizens. to this end, i believe that closer cooperation between healthcare providers and a common definition of certification and authentication schemes should be achieved.
in writing. − i support the eu action plan on ehealth. regional disparities between member states are a continuing impediment to improving the quality of life of eu citizens, as shown by a 2013 european commission study that ranks bucharest, the capital of romania, 27th out of 28 in citizens' perceptions of satisfaction with the health system. for example, in strasbourg, 93% of citizens are very satisfied or satisfied with the health system, while in bucharest the percentage does not exceed 29%. even though the organisation of health systems is a matter for the authorities of the member states, the european institutions must take measures and encourage concrete actions that could save the lives of europeans. such actions may include improving ict (information and communication technology) infrastructure and, in particular, stimulating investment in health infrastructure. it is our duty to raise the standards in the health system for all member countries. i therefore ask the european commission to ask the romanian authorities to strictly adapt to the requirements of the action plan, without which the objectives of the union and the interests of the citizens cannot be achieved!
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the ehealth action plan 2012-2020: innovative healthcare for the 21st century. equal access to quality universal healthcare is an internationally recognised fundamental right, particularly in the eu. information and communication technologies (icts) have reached a level of development sufficient to be applied in ehealth systems, and this is demonstrated by positive experiences in different eu member states and around the world, with numerous benefits at national level. i believe it is important to give importance to databases (such as cloud computing), their location and protection and i believe that the security of these databases should be a priority. the legal and data protection issues of ehealth systems should also be a priority and, given the highly sensitive nature of patient health data, a balance between data protection and access to data is necessary and liability issues need to be clear. ehealth applications should be accessible to all. accessibility should be a mandatory condition for the creation of any software product or application in order to prevent inequalities in access.
in writing. − in recent years, there has been increased attention to the problem of fraud in the food sector, following cases of fraudulent labelling of several food products. i believe that the recent cases of fraud in the food sector have damaged consumer confidence in the food chain, also having a negative impact on the agri-food sector, a key sector of the eu economy. i believe that a harmonised definition of food fraud at eu level is needed, that we need to create a european network to combat food fraud and the use of dna testing more widely to eliminate any kind of fraud.
in writing. − recent cases of food fraud have had a negative impact on the agri-food sector and have deeply damaged consumer confidence. the eu regulatory framework for food safety and the food chain has been designed to provide a high level of food safety for consumers in the european union but, however, current legislation is still fragile and not always reliable, and improvements to the situation on the ground are therefore needed. that is why i hope that, with today's vote in the european parliament's plenary, the prevention and fight against fraud in the food sector will become an integral part of eu policy. this will help to deter and control fraud in the food chain more effectively and restore the confidence of european consumers. i believe that member states and european regions should make available to control authorities sufficient human, financial and technical resources to carry out effective controls and inspections, in order to avoid an additional administrative burden for smes. furthermore, in the absence of a european legislative framework on meat from cloned animals, the commission should present as soon as possible a legislative proposal on animal cloning and develop a method for the tracing and identification of meat from cloned animals.
in writing. − as transparency is a key component of the approach adopted by the commission and the member states to food safety controls, i believe that member states and european regions must make available sufficient human, financial and technical resources to the control authorities.
in writing. − in order to protect the health of citizens and guarantee the quality of the products that reach consumers' tables, it was decided to step up european action to combat food fraud. it was called for a common definition of food fraud and for increased inspections of products, as well as for strengthening anti-fraud programmes and introducing more severe sanctions, especially in the case of fraud that puts the health of citizens at risk. the commission has also proposed legislation to make it compulsory to label meat and fish with an indication of the country of origin and to require food business operators to report fraudulent behaviour, in order to ensure greater protection for consumers and producers.
in writing. - i welcome the initiative of this report. cases of fraud in the food sector are perhaps among the most difficult to report and penalise, affecting a very large number of people. there are a number of challenges for which the european institutions must find solutions. for example, long and complex supply chains, which facilitate fraudulent cases and the closure of businesses that are then opened in other member states without the member state being notified, due to the lack of information exchange, are just some of the challenges. the commission's food and veterinary office does not have the necessary powers to deal with all irregularities in the food sector. a new team specialised in combating fraud in the food sector should therefore be set up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and appreciate that the text adopted today sends a strong signal to those who - in one form or another - are involved or tempted to take advantage of legislative loopholes to engage in such fraud. the report also serves as a reminder to the commission to take the points raised and the proposals made into account.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the food crisis, fraud in the food chain and its control. i voted for paragraph 41, which calls on the commission to present its report on mandatory origin labelling for meat used as an ingredient and to follow up legislative proposals making the indication of the origin of meat mandatory for processed food products, while taking into account the impact assessments it carries out and avoiding excessive costs and administrative burdens. we call for better labelling of processed products containing fish, in particular as regards the origin of the fish and the fishing techniques used. we invite the commission to present legislative proposals on quality schemes for agricultural and food products, concerning a labelling system applicable to 'local farming and direct sales', in order to help promote the markets concerned and help farmers to increase the value of their products. we invite the commission and the member states to continue to encourage national and european research and development programmes, to develop and implement technologies and methods used to detect food fraud, such as sensor technology, data analysis and product fingerprinting, and to facilitate the market availability of short-term tests.
in writing. − increasing the efficiency of workplace inspections is one element in maintaining a high level of competitiveness of european economic actors. in the current context, still dominated by the effects of the financial and economic crisis, ensuring a high level of competitiveness for european enterprises by reducing the level of undeclared work, which represents 18,8% of the union's gdp and even 30% of the gdp of some member states, is of paramount importance. at the same time, increasing the effectiveness of these inspections should also ensure a high level of safety at the workplace. reducing the number of victims of accidents at work can be achieved by establishing a more effective system of monitoring compliance with safety rules.
in writing. − the economic crisis should not be an obstacle but an incentive to improve and strengthen workplace inspections to ensure the protection of workers. labour inspectors have a key role to play in enforcing workers' rights, preventing abuses by employers and promoting economic and social development. it is necessary to establish a european agency to deal with all cross-border issues related to inspections at the workplace. these could include controls on cross-border service providers as well as 'post box' enterprises, the introduction of specialised european training programmes and the organisation of cross-border checks. it is also important to have a european social security card, on which all the necessary data, such as the work schedule or social security, are recorded, so that the labour inspector can analyse all the necessary data on the spot. such a card has already been piloted in the construction sector and successfully implemented in sweden and luxembourg. it should be noted that the europe 2020 strategy draws attention to the need to increase the number of women in the labour market and it is important that labour inspectors have knowledge of working conditions for both women and men.
in writing. − as workplace inspections play a fundamental role in ensuring the exercise of rights, ensuring compliance with the law, knowledge of rights and obligations by those involved and the prevention of accidents and abuse, i believe that labour inspectors in the member states should be authorised to carry out field inspections, use intelligent inspection tools, cooperate with all relevant authorities, have an appropriate range of competence and work independently.
in writing. i voted in favour of this important report on labour inspections and for a strategy for improving working conditions in the european union. the text proposes the implementation of several tools which should make it possible to strengthen labour inspections in europe. several recent studies have shown that in 2012, undeclared work accounted for almost 18.8% of wealth produced in europe. this is a serious situation because it leaves the door open to abuse, exploitation of workers and social dumping. we need to strengthen the capacity of labour inspection authorities, which are often under-resourced and under-staffed. their work must ensure that workers' rights are respected and defended, involving both employers' and trade union representatives. it is however deeply regrettable that the european right voted against the introduction of a social responsibility clause in the european competition rules, which would have allowed the most serious cases of fraud to be penalized.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on effective workplace inspections as strategies to improve working conditions in europe. inspections at work play an important role in protecting workers' rights, ensuring health and safety at work and combating unsafe working environments, preventing breaches of labour protection rules, and promoting fair and socially responsible economic growth, as they help to ensure the effective payment of wages and social security contributions, thereby increasing tax revenues and social security funds, and ensuring that workers are insured against occupational disease and accidents and receive pensions. we urge member states to increase the human and financial resources of their labour inspectorates, to reach the target of one inspector per 10 000 workers, in line with the recommendations of the international labour organisation. we draw attention to the specific situation of home and remote workers who, in the context of working at home or away from their employers, may be subject to breaches of labour law if employers fail to fulfil their legal obligations towards them.
in writing. − i believe that employee financial participation schemes are formulas capable of providing direct financial benefits, superior to simple remuneration schemes, both in the form of capital participation and profit participation. the encouragement of such participation schemes should be considered by national and european authorities. however, in the current economic context, marked by the effects of the economic and financial crisis, the risks borne by employees participating in such schemes are considerable. therefore, it is important that they are closely monitored by the competent national and european authorities. member states should consider removing transnational barriers faced by european undertakings operating employee participation schemes. more attention should be paid to the issue of avoiding the possibility of double taxation or tax discrimination.
in writing. − employee financial participation, through greater involvement of workers in the decision-making processes of the enterprises for which they work, helps to strengthen good governance and ensures part of the financial benefits of a successful enterprise. employee financial participation can also strengthen smes by providing innovative financing mechanisms, as workers want to invest in the shares of the employing enterprise, capitalizing on the expansion. developing long-term investment by workers in their enterprises can help to provide stability and certainty, which strengthens smes and thus makes jobs more secure. this employee participation is highly conditioned by national legal frameworks and conditions. tax and taxation policies are essential for the design and implementation of employee financial participation schemes by enterprises in each member state. subsidiarity issues and continuing doubts about possible tax harmonisation make any concrete legislative action on these areas at eu level unlikely and inappropriate. the eu could provide a 'reference framework' with general guidance on basic principles and good practice to help guide decision-making at national and company level on employee financial participation schemes.
in writing. − i believe that member states should be encouraged to use, in cooperation with the social partners, worker participation organisations and the commission, existing information portals one-stop shops accessible to employers and employees, or to develop new ones, to explain the benefits and benefits as well as the risks of employee financial participation, the available national incentives and the different models in place, in order to enable employees and employers to make informed decisions on employee financial participation schemes, to identify the best option for contracts signed at company level and to better assess the options available to them and the challenges of employee participation in an employee financial participation scheme. i suggest that these single information portals should be attached to or included in existing competent bodies or authorities at national level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the financial participation of employees in the income of enterprises. an undertaking may choose one of three main models of employee financial participation: profit participation (in cash, tiered or equity), individual employee participation (shares or share options) and employee participation plans (esops). we stress that the financial participation of employees in the company's income involves a number of potential risks for them. therefore, financial participation should not be used to avoid compliance with labour law or as a means of reducing acquired social and labour rights or to use pressure to increase labour market flexibility. we encourage member states, in cooperation with the social partners, workers' participation organisations and the commission, to use existing information portals one-stop shops accessible to employers and employees, or to develop new ones, to explain the benefits and benefits as well as the risks of employee financial participation, the available national incentives and the different existing models. we suggest that these single information portals be attached to or included in existing competent bodies or authorities at national level.

in writing. − social protection plays a key role in the european economic model, providing a guarantee of a minimum income, healthcare, education and social inclusion for disadvantaged citizens. although a matter for national states, social protection policy enjoys common objectives and indicators, thanks to the open method of coordination. unfortunately, social assistance is not guaranteed for all residents, who lack access to basic services, which places them in a vulnerable position. moreover, some eu citizens are discriminated against in the countries where they are temporarily resident, on the basis of prejudices that they would strictly pursue the attainment of an assisted status. i would point out that we must not start from the mistaken premise that migrant workers are exclusively concerned with social protection. i know an overwhelming number of compatriots who are actively looking for a job in the countries where they have settled, categorically refusing easy welfare status. i also draw attention to the danger that self-employed persons are not fully protected, benefiting from lower social rights. in many countries, this form of activity is abused by employers to avoid social contributions, and is a serious distortion of competition. the fundamental right must be guaranteed to all workers, regardless of their status, in accordance with european legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on social protection for all, including self-employed workers. i believe that member states should ensure the responsible and sustainable long-term financing of social security systems, especially in times of economic crisis, and develop a preventive component of social security systems and put more emphasis on activation measures, bearing in mind that one of the most important factors of social investments is that they allow reconciliation of social and economic objectives and can contribute to the long-term maintenance and development of the economy. i voted to see social investment as an investment, not an expense. i believe that the commission should examine legislation and monitor the implementation and coordination of social security systems, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity. we draw the attention of member states to the fact that eu migrant workers working in another member state should not be subject to discriminatory social protection measures. i believe that all migrant workers in the eu should enjoy the same social security rights and have the possibility to be insured when working in another member state.

in writing. − as shadow rapporteur, i welcome the adoption of this resolution on the european strategy on plastic waste, which can make an important contribution to the review of waste legislation to be completed this year. plastic has certain intrinsic characteristics that can create problems from a waste management point of view. that's why i think it's become imperative that, both at the european level and at the national level, we better manage how plastic is interfering with our environment and our health. i recall that the environment is one of the four policy areas most prone to breaches of legislation and i believe that the application of the rules already adopted in the field of waste will undoubtedly also contribute to much better recycling and recovery of plastic waste. there are disparities between member states in the way they manage plastic waste, which is why i have advocated a cautious approach in setting binding targets or targets if we want the targets we set to be achievable.
in writing. - plastic has become an inevitable material in our modern world. plastics are versatile and durable, but their durability can make disposing of them problematic. once in the environment, especially in the marine environment, plastic waste can persist for hundreds of years. up to 10 million tons of waste, mostly plastic, ends up in the world's seas and oceans every year, turning them into the largest landfill of plastic waste on the planet. in our 'use and throw away' society, plastic is often perceived as a cheap and easy to throw away material and recycling rates are low. half of the plastic waste generated in europe ends up in landfills, which should be avoided, as plastics can contain hazardous elements and dumping can generate unwanted emissions and concentrated and polluting residues.
in writing. − i believe that energy recovery of plastic waste should only be used when all other possibilities have been exhausted and provided that technologies with appropriate purifiers are used to avoid damage to the environment and human health.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the european strategy on plastic waste in the environment. full implementation of eu waste legislation could save €72 billion a year, increase the annual turnover of the eu waste management and recycling sector by €42 billion and create over 400 000 jobs by 2020. we call for more public and private investment in research and technology to achieve more sustainable plastics (e.g. lower consumption of raw materials while maintaining the same quality and the same possibility of reuse and recycling) and better integration of different types in production processes and recycling activities without compromising the quality of materials. we argue that horizon 2020 could provide opportunities to address this important societal need and that the benefits would be significant for both the environment and citizens, from the creation of new economic activities to the reduction of marine litter and health risks. it can provide young people in particular with the opportunity to integrate into the labour market by engaging in new fields of activity.

the rapporteur for the opinion of the regi committee. − mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to warmly congratulate the rapporteurs and all the colleagues who have brought their powers and expertise to improve and simplify public procurement legislation. it should be stressed once again that the current public procurement system is particularly complex and difficult to apply at member state level without generating a high percentage of errors and irregularities. it is therefore of the utmost importance to improve the efficiency of the management and allocation of public money in general, but especially of european funds. in concrete terms, we need clear, simple, precise, predictable and transparent, credible guidelines to support the member states and, in particular, local and regional authorities. as regards small and medium-sized enterprises, given their high potential for absorbing labour, for innovation and for development, they must be encouraged by specific means, by appropriate measures and encouraged to participate in this public procurement process, both at local and regional level.
mr president, there can hardly be a more timely debate on public procurement. reform is not only needed, it is long overdue. as shadow rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy, i especially welcome the debate on the award of concession contracts. in this day and age it is unacceptable that there are still numerous cases of contracts being directly awarded without any transparency. when a third of businesses, associations and public authorities have said they are aware of such cases, it is no wonder that the existing legislation is not providing the right framework. if there is room for corruption outside the existing legal outline, the questions of who gets access – and how they get access – to such contracts should be better defined within specific criteria. that is why we have fully supported specific obligations regarding selection and award standards, which must ensure fair competition.
public procurement policy plays a key role in the efficient use of public funds, contributing to the achievement of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the revision of the public procurement directives is an ambitious and realistic project, which supports local and regional authorities. the updating of the rules aims at simplifying them, making them more efficient and user-friendly, and at establishing rigorous procedures based on award criteria that also take into account innovation and sustainability. given that public procurement constitutes a significant part of the economy, estimated at 19% of eu gdp, the successful review and implementation of public procurement rules can contribute significantly to overcoming the current crisis of the european economy. i welcome the simplification measures, which are designed to facilitate the participation of smes in public procurement, with an impact on job creation, development and innovation. congratulations to the reporters.

the reporter. - mr president, commissioner šemeta, ladies and gentlemen, the hercule iii programme will finance the purchase of equipment and concrete actions to combat smuggling of cigarettes and other goods, counterfeiting and fraud. in 2011 alone, member states lost over eur 11 billion in tax revenues due to cigarette smuggling. this money obviously went into the pockets of those who control organized crime. smuggling methods are evolving rapidly and new modes of operation are emerging. for example, in 2012, the crew of a russian cargo plane smuggled some 4 million cigarettes into finland. they did this by flying weekly to finland. in july 2012, slovak authorities discovered a smuggling tunnel built from uzhgorod, ukraine, to slovak territory. the funds to be allocated by hercule iii, the regulation which we will vote on tomorrow and which i hope will be adopted, are intended for: the purchase of scanning equipment to identify contraband in lorries and tirs; the purchase of automatic systems for the recognition of codes on containers and registration plates; the purchase of electronic surveillance equipment and for encrypted communications. between 2007 and 2013, romania, my country, received about 3.5 million euros through the hercule ii budget. in 2013, nine projects in romania received funding under hercule ii for the purchase of automatic number plate recognition systems needed by the police to detect and track vehicles suspected of being involved in illegal activities, for the training and transport of service dogs, for the purchase of equipment for detecting false or falsified documents and for the purchase of tracking and tracing equipment. hercule iii has a budget of over eur 104 million and is the third generation of the hercule programme. as rapporteur, my aim was to ensure that hercule iii addresses the weaknesses identified in the implementation of the hercule ii programme. therefore, among the changes are: the evaluation of the concrete results of the activities financed by the hercule programme (for example, a concrete evaluation is the amount of contraband cigarettes that have been confiscated using the money from this programme); transparency in the management of the programme, because we want to know what the member states are doing with this money; cooperation and coordination between the member states, olaf and the commission. at least 75% of the budget of the hercule iii programme will be invested in technical assistance, i.e. in the purchase of appropriate and modern equipment. i'm telling you, this equipment is expensive. for example, an x-ray container scanner costs about 1.5 million euros. another important issue the co-financing rate from the european commission is kept at a maximum of 80% of the eligible costs. for member states with a high risk of smuggling, the co-financing rate goes up to 90%. according to the 2013 annual risk analysis of frontex, the level of cigarette smuggling and counterfeiting is higher in the member states which border by land or sea with ukraine, the russian federation and belarus. it is crucial to defend those member states that cannot afford sufficient resources because, in the end, all member states benefit from this measure. it goes without saying that once smuggled into the european union, into one member state of the union, the products are smuggled into all the states of the union. it is therefore in the interest of all union states, even if they are not at the union border, to contribute financially to ensuring the protection of the european union's borders against smuggling. finally, i would like to thank the irish and lithuanian presidencies, under whom we negotiated and held the trilogue, the rapporteurs from the other groups, the european commission and even olaf, with whom we had many disputes but reached a consensus on the finalisation of this regulation.

reflects the agreement reached with the council on 14 may 2013 under the irish presidency. the report strikes a balance between road safety and improving working conditions on the one hand, and respecting drivers' privacy and data on the other. i would like to stress in particular the following points of the compromise reached following the three rounds of trilogue with the irish presidency. parliament supported the introduction of the smart tachograph as it will help improve the implementation of legislation and will be a means of reducing the level of administrative burden related to tachograph obligations for transport companies in the medium and long term. we want the smart tachograph to be efficient, but affordable. the smart tachograph will include two new functions: remote communication, used to carry out checks, and recording of location data. in addition to introducing new safeguards related to data protection and confidentiality, the agreement further elaborates these functions. as regards distance communication, in no case may it lead to automatic fines or penalties for the driver or the undertaking. member states are required to equip their control officers with remote communication equipment before a set deadline. the distance communication mechanism should use a simplified and therefore accessible technology that limits member states' investments as much as possible. as regards the recording of location data, more points than the beginning and end of the daily working period have been introduced for a better application of controls. the recording shall be carried out automatically and after three hours of continuous driving. the satellite signal to be used will be free of charge. the agreed time-frame for the placing on the market of the smart tachograph is 36 months after the entry into force of the detailed technical specifications. all tachographs connected to a computer application shall use a standardised interface after a period of 36 months. the requirements for tachographs now include specific references to competition in the manufacturer's market. new provisions were also included in the text of the regulation on the functions of tachographs, the data to be recorded, warnings and the display of information to the driver. the text introduces new safeguards on data protection and privacy in a specific data protection article in chapter 1. parliament insisted that a provision on modernisation be included in the text so that 15 years after the introduction of the smart tachograph on the market, all new vehicles should be equipped with such a tachograph. the text strengthens the role of control officers. the commission will establish the content of the training courses for control officers in the european union, including a common interpretation of social legislation. as regards temporary cards, the control of non-resident drivers will be improved by granting them permission to use digital tachographs. the provisions on the liability of transport companies have been amended to make the text clearer as regards the obligations and liability of companies. the provision on the merger of driving licences and driver cards has been deleted from the text and i have asked the commission to withdraw its proposal. as regards regulation (ec) no 561/2006 on the harmonisation of certain provisions of social legislation relating to road transport, parliament's main concern has been to ensure that the legislation applies only to professional drivers. the agreed text does not impose the obligation to use tachographs for vehicles of less than 7,5 tonnes used for the transport of materials, equipment or machinery used by the driver in the exercise of his profession and used only within a 100 km radius of the business premises and provided that the driver's main activity is not driving the vehicle. i conclude by saying that, as regards the national derogations referred to in article 13 of regulation (ec) no 561/2006, the agreed text follows the commission's proposal to double the range from the current value of 50 km to 100 km.

in writing. - i voted in favour of adopting the regulation on tachographs in road transport, repealing council regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on recording equipment in road transport and amending regulation (ec) no 561/2006 of the european parliament and of the council on the harmonisation of certain provisions of social legislation relating to road transport. i voted against amendment no. 1 which calls for the rejection of the agreement on digital tachographs. the tachograph is used in road transport to monitor compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods, with a view to ensuring road safety, decent working conditions for drivers and fair competition between transport undertakings. the aim of the regulation, which will replace the current one dating from 1985, is to reduce the scope for fraud, to enforce social rules more effectively and to reduce administrative burden by making full use of new technologies and introducing a range of new regulatory measures. the text of the new regulation brings improvements in terms of remote communication for carrying out checks, recording of location data, intellectual property rights, data protection and confidentiality, the role of control officers and the liability of transport companies.

in writing. − the small and medium-sized enterprises sector is one of the most dynamic sectors of european economies. since its contribution not only to community gdp but also to european competitiveness and innovation is essential, i believe that ensuring greater legal certainty for economic operators in this sector and guaranteeing their access to the concession market is an important objective for the european union. in addition, in order to facilitate a dynamic and competitive approach, i believe that the institutional process in this sector must reflect the european union's interest in developing strategic infrastructure and services.
in writing. − the adoption of the new directive on the award of concession contracts ends a period of legal uncertainty as regards service concessions, which are governed solely by the principles of the treaty, often interpreted differently by the member states. this situation has led to the absence of competition and direct award of contracts, which has encouraged corruption and patronage. the text of the directive is simpler and less prescriptive than the original proposal and is an instrument with which i hope public authorities will be able to work effectively. the establishment of procedural safeguards, combined with the freedom of public authorities to organise proceedings in the way they consider most appropriate, is, in my view, the right approach. the text adopted also takes account of the specific nature of the concessions, leaving the necessary flexibility, for example, for amending existing contracts. contrary to some rumours, i would like to stress that this directive does not lead to the privatisation of public services, as it enshrines the freedom of the authorities to organise these services as they see fit. the directive also contains some aspects that are not necessarily ideal, such as the exclusion of the water sector and the overly broad definition of cooperation between public authorities, but overall this first text is good, any shortcomings can be remedied later on the basis of experience.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the award of concession contracts, which adopts the european parliament's position at first reading. the absence of clear rules at union level governing the award of concession contracts creates legal uncertainty and obstacles to the free movement of services and disrupts the functioning of the internal market. as a result, economic operators, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, are deprived of their rights in the internal market and miss out on important business opportunities, while public authorities may fail to identify the optimal use of public money so that union citizens benefit from quality services at the best prices. according to the position adopted, the directive lays down rules applicable to procurement procedures used by contracting authorities and contracting entities through a concession, the value of which is estimated to be at least equal to the threshold of eur 5 186 000. the value of a concession shall be the total turnover of the concessionaire generated during the contract, exclusive of vat, as estimated by the contracting authority or contracting entity, in exchange for the works and services covered by the concession, and for goods ancillary to those works and services.
mr president, we all know that the directive on the modernisation of public procurement in the european union brings some improvements, but in my view these are insufficient. we still have favouritism, we still have nepotism, we still unfortunately lack the procedures for implementing this legislation, that is, it is implemented differently from one member state to another, and there is still no correlation between european public procurement legislation and the implementation of projects financed by european funds, which could lead to more competitiveness, which is again lacking. unfortunately, these elements are not reflected in this new legislative act. moreover, it seems that some countries are finding ways through various portals to give their friends their own public contracts.
in writing. − the legislative proposal to amend public procurement procedures must take into account the institutional competences of the authorities initiating such procedures. i also consider that any legislative approach at this level must be compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. the formulation of the requirements for participation in public procurement should also take into account the economic impact at the level of economic operators. i believe that this set of conditions should not become an obstacle to the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises in tenders for contracts with public authorities. i think it should be borne in mind that the current process of change should not address other issues such as the liberalisation of public services or the privatisation of the providers of these services. last but not least, the amendment of the provisions on public procurement should also take into account national rules governing social security.
in writing. − at international level, public procurement represents a significant percentage of world trade: the public procurement sector accounts for between 15 and 20% of gdp in developed countries. at multilateral level, the reference normative act is the international agreement on government procurement, which has recently undergone a review process completed in march 2012. this review was completed in order to increase the transparency and openness of international procurement markets and to simplify procedures. i believe that there is a need for a progressive opening up of international public procurement markets on the basis of a commonly accepted system of rules, based on reciprocity, fairness and compliance with international social, environmental and labour standards. the european union currently provides international operators with a significant degree of openness to its public procurement market, which is often not applied in the same way by other major international trading partners.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new european regulations on public procurement, which were adopted by parliament and will make it possible to obtain a better value for money when awarding works, goods or services. public procurement accounts for around 18% of eu gdp, which is an important lever for economic growth and for achieving specific societal objectives. this new legislation revises the current rules on public procurement. the aim is to encourage fair competition and to allow for better value for money, with a focus on environmental and social considerations and innovation, which is a very positive development. this new legislation is of great importance as it also provides for stricter provisions on subcontracting and facilitates the submission of tenders by small and medium-sized enterprises. the introduction of a new criterion of 'most economically advantageous tender' in the award procedure will allow public authorities to place greater emphasis on quality, environmental and social aspects while taking into account the price and life cycle costs of the tender.
in writing. − in 2010, european public authorities spent eur 2 406 billion on public works, goods and services. given the financial windfall it represents, around 20 % of the european union budget, public procurement is particularly vulnerable to fraud and corruption practices and attractive to organised crime networks. i support the modernisation of the euʼs public procurement rules and the adoption of this directive. conflict of interest is an open door to corruption and distorts fair competition. therefore, i welcome that the new directive, through article 21, pays greater attention to fighting conflicts of interest in public procurement. in particular, minimum criteria have been introduced to establish which factors constitute conflict-of-interest situations. i believe, however, that we should have gone further by streamlining the process of sharing information about problematic economic operators by using technological solutions, and by focusing additionally on preventing and discouraging these conflicts of interest before they occur, as i proposed in my amendments to the directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on public procurement, which adopts the european parliament's position at first reading. the award of public contracts by or on behalf of the authorities of the member states must respect the principles of the treaty on the functioning of the european union: free movement of goods, freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services, and the principles deriving therefrom, such as equal treatment, non-discrimination, mutual recognition, proportionality and transparency. according to the position adopted, the directive lays down rules applicable to the procurement procedures used by contracting authorities in connection with public procurement contracts and design contests the value of which is estimated to be at least equal to the following thresholds (excluding value added tax): eur 5 186 000 for public works contracts; eur 134 000 for public supply and service contracts awarded by central government authorities and design contests organised by those authorities; eur 207 000 for public supply and service contracts awarded by regional and local contracting authorities and design contests organised by those authorities; eur 750 000 for public service contracts for social and other specific services listed in annex xiv.
in writing. − the procedures governing these areas must take account of the european union's particular interest in supporting the small and medium-sized enterprises sector, one of the engines of european development and competitiveness. equally, i believe it is important that any change at this level also reflects the rigors involved in the provision of services of public interest. i also support measures to increase the fairness of this decision-making process. the trust of european citizens in the union depends overwhelmingly on the commitment of the european institutions to increase the transparency of decision-making, especially in such a sensitive area as public procurement, to effectively combat corruption and to prevent fraud.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the procurement by entities operating in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors, which adopts the european parliament's position at first reading. in order to guarantee the opening to competition of procurement by entities operating in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors, provisions should be laid down to coordinate procurement procedures for contracts exceeding a certain value. such coordination is necessary for the implementation of the principles of free movement of goods, freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services, and the principles deriving therefrom, such as equal treatment, non-discrimination, mutual recognition, proportionality and transparency. according to the position adopted, the directive lays down rules applicable to the procurement procedures used by contracting entities in relation to contracts and design contests the value of which is estimated to be at least equal to the following thresholds (estimated value excluding value added tax): eur 414 000 for supply and service contracts as well as design contests; eur 5 186 000 for works contracts; eur 1 000 000 for service contracts for social and other specific services listed in annex xvii.
in writing. − the european union has established itself as one of the world's leading promoters of the principle of free trade. through both its values and its concrete actions, the union has worked to integrate all states into the world economy by strongly supporting the progressive abolition of barriers to international trade. especially as the economic and financial crisis continues to affect european companies and citizens, public procurement, which represents a considerable part of community gdp, must be a driver for the development of competitiveness and innovation in the european economic sector. i believe that the proposal to exclude from the public procurement procedure unfair tenders involving goods and/or services from outside the eu is justified.
in writing. − the importance of ensuring access to goods and services in public procurement markets underpins this report. it is particularly desirable to ensure that tender procedures are transparent and that they allow the participation of several competitors operating in the relevant territory. the tendering procedure is a prerequisite for the implementation of development and growth policies, without which there can be no real exit from the crisis. i therefore thank the rapporteur and all the colleagues who have worked on this important dossier.
in writing. − the public procurement market is open to international competition, reflecting the union's commitment to free trade, while third countries do not offer reciprocal access to their markets. economic operators in the eu are thus faced with restrictive practices by some of the union's trading partners. moreover, there has been an increase in protectionist measures to the detriment of european companies. i support this report because i believe that the european union must urgently take action and put an end to these restrictive practices by adopting more aggressive negotiations. if third countries have access to the union's public procurement market, it would be appropriate for union economic operators to have access to the third country's public procurement market. restricting market access for third countries is not the desired solution, but if any form of negotiation fails, it can be used as a last resort. moreover, it is important that any measures taken by the union in this respect are applied uniformly at european level in order to prevent fragmentation of the internal market.

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'common carrier'. i also voted to postpone the vote on the legislative resolution. i voted for amendment 17, which defines honey as a naturally sweet substance produced by bees. honey is essentially made up of various types of sugars, in particular fructose and glucose, and other substances such as organic acids, enzymes and solid particles resulting from the collection of honey. directive 2001/110/ec ensures the preservation of the natural characteristics of honey by limiting human intervention that could alter the composition of honey. in particular, that directive prohibits the addition of any food ingredient to honey, including food additives or any other additives other than honey. similarly, the directive prohibits the removal of any constituent element of honey, including pollen, unless this is unavoidable when removing impurities. these requirements are in accordance with the codex alimentarius standard for honey. i also voted for amendments nos 18, 19 and 20, which stress that pollen should not be considered as an ingredient. pollen, being a natural component specific to honey, is not considered an ingredient within the meaning of article 2 (2) (f) of regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 of the products defined in annex 1 to this directive.

he is seeking the presidency of the council. - the mr president, ladies and gentlemen, allow me to welcome the delegation from korea, a country with which we share the same struggles for freedom and a country with which the european union is seeking to further deepen its relations. i would first of all like to thank the european parliament for putting this very important matter on the agenda of this sitting. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we have had intensive discussions in the council on the subject of free movement and i should like to inform you of the main points that have emerged from our recent discussions. first, the overwhelming majority of member states fully support the free movement of persons and consider that this right should be preserved and promoted. the free movement of persons is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union and is at the heart of the european integration process. it is also one of the aspects which clearly benefits our citizens. secondly, the majority of member states do not want any confusion between the concepts of 'freedom of movement', 'mobility', 'migration' and 'migrants from other countries of the european union'. under european union law, its citizens should not be treated in the same way as migrants from third countries in the context of free movement. there can be no doubt as to the legal distinction between the different status and scale of entitlements. the right of citizens of the european union to move and settle within the european union, whether for economic or other purposes, is fundamentally different from the possibilities available to nationals of third countries who are subject to immigration rules. thirdly, everyone agrees that while freedom of movement is a right, it also entails certain duties and obligations. in this context, the council has examined allegations of abuse of the rights of free movement. the european commission, under mandate from the council, conducted an evidence-based inquiry which included data collection from the member states themselves. the results were interesting and important in the context of today's debate. the information gathered and assessed by the european commission suggests that european union citizens move primarily for the purpose of working, rather than for the purpose of obtaining social benefits in other member states. in fact, they are less likely to be unemployed than citizens of the host country, so they actively contribute to the host country's economic development. of course, no one can say that there are no abuses of the system. there are always isolated cases of abuse, either by the nationals of the member states themselves, by nationals of other member states or by nationals of third countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. there is a legal framework, there are specific safeguards, which enable the member states to take the necessary measures to deal with such cases of abuse. however, the treaty does not allow for additional pan-european measures, restrictions on nationals of certain member states, quotas for european union nationals, arbitrary expulsions or other similar measures of discriminatory treatment. i would like to be absolutely clear on this point. a very large number of member states, together with the commission, agree that the issue is not a matter of european law or a matter of action at european level, but rather how european legislation is applied at local level. this could include measures to deal with specific situations. the recent european commission communication on the free movement of persons presents a number of possible actions that can be implemented at national level. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are closely following the attacks and the negative publicity surrounding the principle of free movement. we believe that especially today, when we are experiencing a rise in populism and xenophobia, public positions should be based on real facts and not on dangerous generalizations or stereotypes. the free movement of persons is one of the most important benefits of the european integration process. this is a priceless asset which we must preserve now and for future generations, and i assure you that the presidency is committed to ensuring that this happens.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, today is a timely debate, because in recent weeks much has been said and written on this subject. that is why it is a debate in which institutions need to make their voices heard very clearly. the commission believes that we must again and again state clearly that all eu citizens are entitled to free movement – without exception. they enjoy the right to free movement as a direct consequence of being european citizens and of their member state being a member of the european union. free movement is one of those basic rights citizens enjoy. if you look at our eurobarometer, it is also the right which they cherish most. i would like to make it very clear: it is a right which is not up for negotiation. free movement gives the citizens the right to live, work and study anywhere in the union: an important right which over 14 million citizens utilise. they reside in another member state on a stable basis. there is also a very strong economic case for free movement, because it not only benefits those who move, it also benefits the economies to which they move and the economies from which they have moved. the gdp of the eu-15 is estimated to have increased by almost 1 % in the long term as a result of the free movement after the 2004 enlargement. the data – which is provided by the member states – shows that the main motivation for eu citizens to move to another member state is for work. of all citizens residing in another eu country in 2012, more than three quarters – 78% – were of working age as compared to 66 % among nationals. the overall employment rate of mobile eu workers – 68 % – is higher than that of the non-mobile citizens – 65 %. also, and this is very important, mobile eu citizens tend to be net contributors to the costs of the public services they use in the host country. as a matter of fact, those who are not in employment represent a very limited share of the total number of mobile citizens. they are therefore unlikely to represent a real burden on the welfare systems of host countries. now, we have heard very clearly the concern which has been raised by some member states, that free movement has been abused on their territories, causing difficult social situations in certain localities. the commission has listened to those member states and it has gathered data – provided by those member states – to better grasp the dimension of the problem. to present its findings, the commission adopted in november a communication on the free movement of citizens and their families which provides facts and figures, clarifies the rights and obligations and explains the conditions and limitations offered by the eu rules on free movement. to make it very clear: the current rules on free movement, including access to social benefits, contain sufficient safeguards to prevent eu citizens becoming an unreasonable burden on the host country. having said that, we would also like to say clearly that we stand ready to help the member states in their efforts to fight fraud and abuse. while those seem to occur only on a small scale, they must nevertheless be taken very seriously, because abuse – or the feeling that there is abuse – destroys free movement. that is why the commission, with a five-point action plan, proposed to give a helping hand to the member states when implementing the right to free movement on their territories. the member states and the eu here share the responsibility to make these rules work and to uphold them for the benefit of the citizens, of growth and of employment. this also includes countering public perceptions which are not based on facts and economic realities. in exercising this responsibility, national authorities can count on the support of the commission. please rest assured that the commission is ready to uphold eu law. this is our duty as guardian of the treaties: we will ensure that any measure adopted in any member state is fully compliant with eu law. i know from experience that i can count on the strong support of the european parliament when it comes to these questions. our citizens also know that they can count on us, and that is what we have to deliver. (applause)
member of the commission. − mr president, the free movement of workers is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union and the cornerstone of the eu single market. the free movement of workers benefits individual workers by giving them access to a greater range of job opportunities and experience, and it also benefits the economies and welfare systems of the host countries. in order to ensure that eu workers are better able to exercise their right to free movement in practice, the eu treaty also includes rules to ensure that they do not face discrimination in terms of access to jobs or working conditions. these rules include the coordination of social security, as it is necessary to treat workers from other member states and national workers equally in terms of other social benefits and tax advantages. the eu also offers help to people who are interested in working in another member state through the european employment services (eures) job search network, for example. we will make a proposal to upgrade this later this week. the free movement of workers has been subject to transitional measures in five out of seven enlargements. on 1 january 2014, the transitional measures concerning the freedom of movement for romanian and bulgarian workers ended. those nine member states which were still applying restrictions in 2013 have now lifted them. the commission is monitoring this process to ensure that rights are not violated and that all questions receive an answer. fairness – and the perception of fairness – is important. concerns have nevertheless been expressed, even by some members of this parliament, about the risk that increased flows of people would put an excessive burden on the social security systems of some member states. but the evidence shows that people actually go where they find jobs and not benefits. this is confirmed by a recent report published by the commission, as well as by previous experience. because eu migrants are more likely to be economically active than nationals of the host member states and less likely to claim social benefits, they are net contributors to the host country welfare system in the vast majority of the member states. in this context, let me express my satisfaction for the agreement reached at trialogue level concerning the proposal for a directive on measures facilitating the exercise of the right of free movement of workers. this directive is aimed at ensuring better national enforcement of the eu rules in the field of free movement of workers. it provides for the existence of at least one body in every member state to provide assistance and information to eu workers and their family members on their eu rights. thanks to amendments proposed by the parliament, it will also be empowered to liaise and cooperate with similar bodies in other countries. i am confident that the adoption of the directive will lead to all-round better support concerning the rights of migrant eu workers. vice-president reding recalled the communication on free movement of eu citizens and their families which the commission adopted last year. amongst the five actions foreseen by the communication, one concerned the publication of a practical guide on the habitual residence test. this guide was published on monday, 13 january 2014 and will help member states to apply eu rules on the coordination of social security and to safeguard against abuse. the guide was jointly drafted by representatives from member states and the european commission. there are clear safeguards in eu law to prevent people from abusing the social welfare systems of other eu countries, and this guide will make it easier for national and local authorities to apply the habitual residence safeguards in practice, with the objective of facilitating the free movement of people throughout the european union. it is also useful to recall that no member state has provided any evidence of widespread or systematic abuse of social welfare by people from other eu countries.
