mr. president, i wish to express my regret and outrage that romanians and bulgarians are the targets of an aggressive smear campaign. the stakes are clear, with the european elections and, as in the case of the uk, the forthcoming national elections. beyond the xenophobic rhetoric, i would like to note that the migration of romanians to the member states confirms that free movement is a pillar of the european union, both as an essential right of citizens and as an economic reality. nine out of ten romanians living in germany are working legally and contributing to the social system. in the uk, only 1.4% of the 120,000 romanian immigrants receive social assistance, as opposed to the national average rate, with 9.5% of the british population receiving state aid. that is why, mr president, i believe it is the duty of all democratic and pro-european forces to combat the incorrect attempt to turn romanians into service-guilty for the inability of some national governments to provide viable anti-crisis solutions.
in writing. today's debate is extremely important for the future of the eu itself. i believe that the statements by the european commission and the council which are the subject of this debate correctly address the issue of the mobility of european citizens, because this means, in practice, for the most part, free movement within the eu. mobility generates added value, is a factor of economic growth and is appreciated as such in most of europe. recently, the times reported that there are about 5,000 vacancies on romanian job sites in 2014 alone, compared to 60,000 vacancies in the uk in 2013. at the same time, however, i believe it is extremely important to make a clear distinction between mobility and migration within the eu, which is why i appreciate the ec's answer to my question on the need for this distinction. this is not a formal one, but concerns entirely different situations, in substance. today in the ep plenary we talked about immigrants in general, about legal and illegal immigration, which should be fought. but european citizens cannot be subject to these rules, which is why it is necessary to clarify the two concepts, including terminology. ambiguity about this legal difference between european citizenship and immigrant status and between different sets of rights and treatment can lead to additional tensions in the european space.
in writing. romanian citizens face a systematic and unfair campaign of stigmatisation. their only fault is that, as of 1 january, they are full european citizens with the removal of restrictions on the labour market. for populist-electoral reasons, many untruths are conveyed, ignoring the evidence. immigrants are not a burden but an economic aid to the host countries. the specialised studies also estimate that romanians will not compete with the population of the uk and other member states for jobs. on the contrary, it is complementarity in the labour market, not substitution. given their average age and experience so far, romanians will not represent an additional pressure on social systems - not even the british one, however much the demagogic thesis of 'social tourism' may be stirred up. romanian emigrants leave their country to work, not for social benefits that can only be accessed under restrictive conditions, especially in the uk. last but not least, i would like to draw attention to an unfairly ignored reality: british and german statistics indicate a shift in the axes of migration, with countries on the southern flank of the eu providing 50% more immigrants in the last year than before.
in writing. the agitation unleashed in some eu member states over the so-called flood of romanians and bulgarians since 1 january 2014 has proved to be unfounded. undoubtedly populist, extremist politicians have tried to manipulate people without having facts, on mere assumptions. unfortunately, such distortions in the political world are quite common. but it is unacceptable that the government of a member state, and the government of the united kingdom, should stop publishing a government report on immigration, simply because reality does not justify the general unrest that was unleashed in that country before 1 january 2014.
in writing. the right to free movement is one of the fundamental principles of the european union. under the treaty of accession of romania and bulgaria, member states could introduce restrictions on the free movement of workers for a maximum of 7 years from the date of accession of those two states. in the period 2007-2013, some member states introduced such restrictions for romanian and bulgarian workers, while others decided as of 1 january 2007 not to apply any restrictions or gradually abandoned them. today, it is unanimously accepted that romanian workers have participated in the economic and social growth of the states in which they have resided and worked. i have been campaigning since 1 january 2007 for the free movement of romanian and bulgarian workers. i believe that removing these barriers ensures equal working conditions and eliminates social dumping, thereby protecting migrant workers and native workers alike. we therefore call on member states to refrain from introducing any discriminatory measures against migrant workers on the grounds of populism. the european union is founded on the principle of equal treatment of all its citizens, a fundamental principle for the trust contract between the union and its citizens.
ladies and gentlemen, i am still thinking about how to explain to my fellow romanians that while we are kept outside the schengen area, although we fulfil the criteria for membership, a citizen from outside the union, if he has money, can buy maltese citizenship, that is, european citizenship and all the benefits that flow from it. i don't know how to explain it to them, because that's unacceptable. some european political leaders, instead of speaking out against the maltese trade in european citizenship, tried to distract attention by referring to the granting of romanian citizenship to citizens of the republic of moldova. it's probably easier for them to forget the tragic historical decisions and blame the restoration of a lost right, even though other countries have done the same. it is not romania and moldova that are the problem, but the trade in european citizenship, because it seriously affects one of the most important values of the union.
i want to express my disapproval of the maltese law, which offers the possibility for non-eu citizens to obtain citizenship in exchange for a sum of money. i am a citizen of a member state who has been waiting for years to be admitted to schengen, and this is not happening, although all the accession criteria have been met, as both the european commission and the parliament have found. so 30 million european citizens, romanians and bulgarians, cannot travel without border controls, but any russian, chinese or papuans, whether gangster or oligarch, will be able to do so unhindered, if they have a proper bank account. this seems to me downright revolting and unfair.
member of the commission. − mr president, i am also speaking on behalf of viviane reding, who had to leave unexpectedly early, when i thank you for your contributions to this debate. your contributions highlight the growing importance of these questions in the european union, in which national decisions are in many instances no longer neutral vis-à-vis other member states and the european union as a whole. european union citizenship implies a stakeholding with the union and depends on a person’s ties with europe and its member states. talking about the member states, you know that my area of responsibility is enlargement and neighbourhood. i have to confess that in the area of enlargement i have already faced the issue whereby a candidate country was about to adopt a similar arrangement. my line at that time was very clear – firstly, the issue of the responsibility of the member states once you become one, and secondly, the need for awareness that such a decision has a clear european union dimension and that this issue needs to be addressed in the spirit of the values of the european union. we have taken on board what was said here today and what has been expressed in european parliament resolutions. we will continue to be attentive to this issue. listening to this debate, on behalf of viviane reding i would like to confirm that the european commission will offer its assistance in addressing this important issue within the treaties in a debate in which we will address the differences between citizenship on one hand and the residence permit on the other, a debate which will in no way question the prerogative of member states or dilute member state sovereignty.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank the members for this interesting debate. i have taken good note of the concerns and strong feelings expressed on this issue and, as i said in my opening remarks, i will certainly ensure that the council is fully informed of your concerns. however, as i also said at the outset, the council has not discussed the specific issue which is the subject of this debate and has certainly not developed a standpoint on it, for the reasons which i have already explained. it is up to the member states individually to lay down their own rules governing nationality. there is no harmonisation of national legislation in this area. however, the member states must ensure that their domestic legislation fully respects eu law. if there is any suggestion that this is not the case, that is a matter for the commission, which is the institution responsible for ensuring respect for eu legislation.
in writing. citizenship is not a commodity that can be bought or sold, it is the relationship that a person has with the state and other citizens. however, the granting of the nationality of a member state also means the granting of european citizenship with all the rights attached to it, rights which are recognised and can be exercised in all the member states of the union. the sale of citizenship is an undemocratic, unfair process that creates inequalities and inequities. citizenship should only be granted where there is a genuine link between the citizen concerned and the state whose citizen he wishes to become. to obtain citizenship of a state, there must be a root and an identity, otherwise the sovereignty of that state is diluted. i wish to express my concern about the maltese citizenship sale law, the maltese government's draft legislation being unacceptable and undemocratic! i am also deeply disappointed by the recent example of one of europe's political leaders. the romanian delegation of the european people's party strongly rejects these claims. romania does not sell romanian citizenship to anyone. the overwhelming majority of cases in which romania has granted citizenship to moldovans are cases of regaining citizenship by people who lost it for reasons beyond their control!

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, it is a pleasure for me to contribute to your debate on the 2012 progress report on iceland and the post-election perspectives. let me first of all congratulate the rapporteur, mr preda, for his high quality report, which is to the point and well balanced. it also delivers an important message to iceland, which cannot be repeated often enough: the european union remains fully committed to continuing and completing the accession negotiation process if iceland wishes to do so. the commission acknowledges the icelandic government’s decision to put the accession negotiations on hold. that message was communicated by me, as well as by presidents barroso and van rompuy, in meetings with the icelandic foreign minister and prime minister last summer. in october, as part of its 2013 enlargement package, the commission produced a short factual report on iceland. this was not a standard ‘progress report’ like those of previous years. it summarised levels of alignment with the acquis in iceland, chapter-by-chapter, without providing any forward-looking recommendations. in the report, as well as in the overall strategy paper, the commission concluded that iceland had reached an advanced stage of the accession negotiations – with, as has been said, 27 chapters opened and 11 provisionally closed – when they were put on hold. we noted that iceland remained and still remains an important partner for the european union, in particular in the light of its membership of the european economic area and its participation in the schengen area. we have taken note of the fact that the icelandic government has commissioned a study on the state of play of the accession negotiations and developments in the european union, which will be presented to the icelandic parliament for discussion early this year. allow me to conclude with two remarks regarding the accession-related funds which iceland has been receiving through the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa). firstly, following careful assessment and in line with sound financial management, we concluded that all ongoing ipa projects should be discontinued. it is not possible to justify using european union taxpayers’ funds, the purpose of which is to support pre-accession, when the icelandic government itself has called a halt to the process. additionally, the commission will not sign any new commitments under our current ipa i instrument. secondly, with regard to the new instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa ii), which covers the years 2014-2020, the commission, in agreement with the icelandic government, has suspended preparatory work for iceland under this framework.

mr president, although industrialization has been neglected in recent times, i nevertheless supported this report, which makes a number of improvements, good but insufficient, in terms of the relaunch of industrialization in the european union. we all know that industrialisation directly contributes to the creation of new jobs. or, at the moment we are facing across the european union a lack of skills to find solutions for creating new jobs. moreover, industrialisation is highly dependent on european funding. here again, the maximum consideration is not given to how much could be used to industrialise, in particular, the newly joined countries of the european union and to create jobs. that is why i think the commission should come up with a much bolder approach, make concrete and binding proposals to each government at national level and at the same time have a strategy for monitoring and sanctioning governments that fail to implement such strategies.
in writing. − the economic crisis and rising production costs have hit european industry and led to job losses for many european citizens. reindustrialisation, in response to the problems identified, must be a priority at eu level. europe has the capacity to innovate and the know-how to develop high-performing industry, but it faces problems with production costs, especially those related to resources and energy. the european union needs a competitive industry characterised by innovation, energy efficiency and sustainability, and an appropriate legislative framework to support the continued growth of the industry. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the crisis has dealt a severe blow to european economies. it has affected the industrial sector, causing the loss of 3.8 million jobs. the crisis and lack of prospects are affecting social well-being and worsening poverty. to meet these challenges, i believe that the eu needs a comprehensive growth strategy. european industry is indispensable to solving the multitude of problems facing the eu. it provides jobs, goods and services, as well as tax revenues, and is a key player in europe's transition to a low-carbon economy. europe needs to make appropriate use of public funds, mobilise private sector funds for research and innovation activities and encourage transnational and transregional cooperation through innovative business groups, academia and research organisations. this cooperation should be accompanied by smart specialisation strategies that take into account the potential of each region and territory.
in writing. − i believe that at european level the commission must honour its commitment to develop indicators to monitor and evaluate the reindustrialisation process, and these indicators must be not only quantitative but also qualitative, to ensure that this process is sustainable and compatible with environmental protection.
in writing. − this report makes very clear what the economic crisis has shown us in a rather painful way, namely that an industrial base is absolutely indispensable if the eu is to ensure the prosperity of its citizens. the diagnosis is very clear: the european economy has in recent years focused far too much on services and has entered a process of deindustrialisation, due also to lack of competitiveness, but this process has dramatic effects on employment and the overall economic situation. the paradigm shift and the european commission's take-up of the industrial policy initiative so that we are seeing a 'rebirth of european industry' is real progress. the potential is there, all that is needed is a coherent strategy to support competitiveness while ensuring the sustainability of the european economy. it is therefore absolutely essential to support innovative sectors and new technologies that have significant growth potential. support for smes will be another key point, because they are the backbone of the european economy and they also bring the most innovation. such a strategy also requires investment, but a smart use of european funds through multiannual programmes such as horizon 2020 can already be one of the sources of funding.
in writing. − i welcome the commission’s focus on industrial policy, as it is essential for economic development, and, taking into account the fact that industry creates one in four jobs, solving the problem of unemployment. the main objectives of this report should be to advocate a renaissance in industry, and innovation in the field, for a sustainable eu.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in order to deal with the financial and economic crisis and to give a new impetus to the economy, a strategy focused on reindustrialisation is needed. taking into account the different economic and social realities of the different member states and the global competitors of european industry, which have been developing sound industrial strategies for years, it is necessary to start a modernisation process which will strengthen the centres of innovation and eliminate the developmental lags. industrial policy must therefore find the right mix of strategies that combine competitiveness and sustainability in order to improve the framework, recreate productive capacity and generate jobs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on reindustrialising europe to promote competitiveness and sustainability, as it is an important point of the european industrial strategy. the consolidation of european industry needs to be based on technological and financial innovation, while the social and ecological market economy can be supported by commercial innovation, with small and medium-sized enterprises contributing to the digitalisation of the internal market. i also believe that broadband services are key to industrial development and can contribute to economic growth and job creation, and that investments in the construction of a high-capacity broadband network should be a union priority. the commission can support the standardisation and interoperability of new technological products and services by encouraging cooperation at european level between companies, service providers and research centres, the participation of regions and the transfer of knowledge between the research communities in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on reindustrialising europe to promote competitiveness and sustainability. industry is the largest value creator in the economy, creating approximately two additional jobs in the goods and services sectors for every one industrial job. i consider it particularly important that the 'industrial revival for a sustainable europe' (rise) strategy can revitalise industry and repatriate production to the eu, paying attention to supply chain management and taking into account specific local and regional production cultures and demand, while promoting important emerging sectors necessary for a sustainable economy and society. they claim that the rise strategy requires a short-term agenda to protect the production tool and know-how in order to respond to the urgent challenges (such as overcapacity, restructuring, unfair competition) of certain sectors, as well as a roadmap and a timetable in a long-term framework. they should promote the modernisation, sustainability and competitiveness of europe's industrial base through a value chain-aware policy that covers enterprises of all sizes, pays due attention to core industries and promotes the maintenance of the production chain in europe.
in writing. − building on the coal and steel community, the eu is now in the paradoxical position of having to face the negative effects of a general deindustrialisation. the global crisis has only revealed that the massive deindustrialisation of member states towards a predominantly service-based economy is a vulnerability. over the past two decades, the eu's industrial decline has intensified, with it on the verge of losing out to global players concerned with strengthening, diversifying and researching and innovating their industries for the 21st century. the report on reindustrialising europe to promote competitiveness and sustainability adopted today in the european parliament supplements the commission's view of the acute need to rebuild europe's industry, which until recently was characterised by performance and competitiveness. i voted for this report because i am convinced that the eu needs a strategy to combat the crisis by launching a new economic dynamic that creates jobs, reindustrialisation being an essential component, without which such a plan will not have the desired result.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament decision on the council recommendation on the appointment of a member of the executive board of the european central bank, giving a favourable opinion on the appointment of sabina lautenschläger as a member of the executive board of the european central bank. by letter of 8 january 2014, the european council consulted the european parliament on the appointment of sabina lautenschläger as a member of the executive board of the european central bank for a term of office of eight years. the vote was in favour, given that the committee on economic and monetary affairs of the european parliament assessed ms lautenschläger's qualifications, in particular with regard to the conditions laid down in article 283 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and, as follows from article 130 tfeu, the imperative of the ecb's full independence in the field of monetary policy. the commission also held a hearing with ms lautenschläger on 13 january 2014, during which she made an introductory statement and then answered the questions put by the members of the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the reduction in the excise duty on traditional rum produced in the french overseas departments will reduce the competitive disadvantage of these areas. we're talking about remote island areas with a small land area, difficult terrain and climate. these areas are often economically dependent on a limited number of products, such as cane sugar rum. therefore, the reduction of up to 50% below the normal national level of the excise duty on alcohol for these specific products will be a compensation but also a support to the competitive value chain of traditional rum from these areas. it is also an important step in support of the eu's objective of stimulating the economies of the outermost regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision authorising france to apply a reduced rate of certain indirect taxes to 'traditional' rum produced in guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion. the decision authorises france to apply, in the territory of metropolitan france, to 'traditional' rum produced in the french overseas departments a reduced rate of excise duty which may be lower than the minimum rate of excise duty laid down in directive 92/84/eec but which may not be more than 50% lower than the normal national level of excise duty on alcohol. the reduction in the excise duty shall be limited to an annual quota of 120 000 hectolitres of pure alcohol. this derogation shall expire on 31 december 2013. the purpose of this measure is to compensate producers in the french overseas departments for the competitive disadvantages caused by remoteness, insularity, small area, difficult terrain and climate, economic dependence on a small number of products, in particular the value chain of rum from cane sugar, factors whose persistence and combination seriously impair their development. france shall submit a report to the commission by 31 july 2017 in order to assess whether the reasons justifying the granting of a reduced rate continue to exist.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i too believe that the rules of procedure should be amended to solve a number of problems relating to the application of the rules on the immunity of members. alignment of these rules with the case law of the european court of justice was also needed, which can give greater consistency to parliament's decisions in this area. it should be borne in mind, however, that only if a member is acting in that official capacity can he be granted immunity. the commission is also proposing to amend the rules of the european parliament in this area to ensure that any abuse is avoided.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the decision amending the rules of procedure of parliament as regards the waiver and defence of parliamentary immunity. parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of members but a guarantee of the independence of parliament as a whole and of its members. in exercising its powers in respect of privileges and immunities, parliament shall act in order to preserve its integrity as a democratic legislative assembly and to ensure the independence of members in the performance of their duties. any request addressed to the president by a competent authority of a member state for the waiver of the immunity of a member or by a member or a former member for the defence of privileges and immunities shall be announced in parliament and forwarded to the committee responsible. the commission shall examine without delay, but taking into account their relative complexity, requests for waiver of immunity or for the defence of privileges and immunities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution and therefore against the placing on the market of a genetically modified maize, as i consider that the studies published so far on the safety of this species are inconclusive. this is all the more important as the european food safety authority has acknowledged that in its risk assessment of this maize it did not take into account the tolerance to the herbicide glufosinate ammonium, although this feature could lead to a wider use of glufosinate, especially as the use of this product is expected to end in 2017. the agency also drew attention to the fact that some butterfly species may be endangered when exposed to pollen from maize 1507. in these circumstances, where there are still questions about the safety of this genetically modified maize, a more detailed analysis is required, taking into account all the issues, and only after the completion of this analysis can the discussion on the authorisation of the cultivation of the genetically modified maize resume.
in writing. − i voted to reject the proposal for a decision on the placing on the market for cultivation, in accordance with directive 2001/18/ec of the european parliament and of the council, of a maize product (zea mays l. line 1507) genetically modified for resistance to certain harmful lepidoptera. no gmos have been approved for cultivation in the eu since 2010, when the amflora potato was authorised. this authorisation was annulled by the general court of the eu on 13 december 2013 and the only crop authorised for cultivation is monsanto mon 810 maize, the renewal of which has been pending for several years. the vast majority of consumers are concerned about genetically modified food, as indicated, inter alia, in the special eurobarometer 354 of 2010. we oppose the adoption of the proposal for a decision concerning the placing on the market of a maize product (zea mays l. line 1507) genetically modified for resistance to certain harmful lepidopterans. we also call on the council to reject the commission's proposal. we ask the commission not to propose the authorisation of any new strain of genetically modified organism and not to renew authorisations already granted until the risk assessment methods have been significantly improved.
as for the fundamental right of free movement, it seems that we are constantly talking to each other. no one disputes that one of the most fundamental rights of eu citizens is the right to choose freely where to live and work in the eu member states, but recently there has been a rise in voices that would still welcome certain groups of citizens with reservations. it is only certain groups, because nobody wants to exclude them from the european labour market, such as computer scientists, doctors, managers, only manual workers with often uncertain job opportunities, who sometimes still depend on the social systems of the states. abuses must be screened out, but we must not forget that the role of social systems is to help workers in difficult situations. it is not a fault of the system that this assistance is also used by workers from other states.
mr president, i welcome the adoption of this resolution. freedom of movement is a fundamental right of all union citizens, which is not negotiable. the european union would not have the same meaning for european citizens if they could not travel, work or study in any of the member states. we should not be surprised if we find ourselves in a situation where citizens lose their faith in the european project, and this is because of some electoral-motivated speeches, which feed the extremist rhetoric that is unfortunately gaining ground in europe. that is why we need to tell european citizens the truth and talk about the benefits to the host economies, about the contribution of these workers to filling the labour gap in the local market and their contribution to the social security systems of the host countries. there is also too little talk about recruiting highly qualified labour from countries such as romania, poland or bulgaria doctors, nurses, it specialists. the number of doctors who have left romania in recent years exceeds 15,000, which creates a real problem for the health system. many of them work in the uk. so we cannot agree to the union's rules and values only when they benefit us.

in writing. − i believe that member states must make full and transparent use of the resources available under european funds, such as the european social fund and the european regional development fund, to promote integration, social inclusion and the fight against poverty and to support the efforts of local communities to cope with an increase in the number of disadvantaged citizens, whether or not they are nationals of their country.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which concludes a major debate on the fundamental right of european citizens to freedom of movement. it is essential to recall the fundamental principles of eu law on freedom of movement. in the current pre-electoral context, there is a proliferation of populist arguments and aggressive ads that call into question one of the fundamental freedoms on which the union is built. i welcome the fact that this resolution highlights the benefits of freedom of movement for the economy of both host and mobile labour supplying countries. the mobility of european citizens is one way of tackling labour shortages in a large number of sectors. on the other hand, it is important to reiterate that mobile citizens working in another member state contribute more to the social security systems of the host countries than they benefit from them. only 2.8% of european citizens live in another member state, but they are a crucial element in the success of the internal market, contributing to the dynamism of the economy. indeed, more people are economically active in their host countries than in their host countries.
in writing. - it is absolutely regrettable that after more than 50 years of trying to facilitate free movement, we have a debate about the possibility of taking a step backwards by restricting this freedom. i can therefore only support a resolution which recalls the fundamental nature of this freedom in the eu and which restores certain truths about the impact of intra-european migration on national social systems on the basis of statistics published by the member states themselves. i am outraged by the attitude of some european leaders who forget the benefits that free movement has brought to their own country, only presenting the isolated abuses, which they extrapolate as a generalized phenomenon. if there are abuses, they must obviously be fought. but i do not think that a european citizen who exercises his right to free movement automatically commits an abuse. but that is how things are presented to the citizens of certain european countries. such an attitude is deeply dishonest and the result is that freedom of movement is sacrificed on the altar of the electoral ambitions of parties which have no real solutions to the underlying problems and which prefer to disinform their own citizens and denigrate the citizens of certain member states, ignoring the risks of re-awakening nationalist and xenophobic sentiments.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on respect for the fundamental right of free movement in the eu. the right to free movement is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu, enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union as a cornerstone of european integration, and is directly linked to eu citizenship. we strongly disagree with the position taken by some european leaders who have called for changes to be made and for the free movement of citizens to be restricted. we call on member states to avoid any measures that could affect the right to free movement based on eu primary law. we reject outright any proposal to cap the number of migrants in the eu, as it contradicts the principle of the eu treaty on the free movement of persons. we stress that labour mobility contributes to the competitiveness of the european economy. we call on the commission and the member states to ensure the strict application of union law so as to guarantee that all eu workers are treated equally and are not discriminated against in terms of access to employment, employment and working conditions, remuneration, dismissal, social benefits and tax benefits, thus ensuring fair competition between businesses. we urge the national authorities to combat all unjustified restrictions or obstacles to the right of free movement of workers, together with any exploitation of workers.

in writing. − i believe that european union citizenship involves an interest in the union and depends on a person's links with europe or its member states or personal links with eu citizens, and i believe that it should never become a commodity that can be traded.
in writing. i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on observed cases of sale of eu citizenship. in particular, the maltese government has recently taken steps to introduce a system of outright sale of maltese citizenship, which automatically implies the outright sale of european citizenship without residence requirements. these measures are intolerable because they undermine the mutual trust of the member states on which the union is based. it is unacceptable that some eu member states are putting their passports up for sale and thus allowing wealthy foreigners to gain access to european citizenship and benefit from the absence of border controls as nationals of schengen countries, while two eu member states, romania and bulgaria, are still excluded! i call on the european commission to indicate as soon as possible whether these schemes comply with the european treaties, the schengen border code and the provisions on non-discrimination. european citizenship should never become a commodity like any other!
in writing. − i supported this resolution because i consider the sale of european citizenship to be at least abnormal. citizenship is a symbol of belonging to a community with which the citizen has certain rather strong ties and shares a set of values. it cannot be considered a commercial good. such an approach strips european citizenship of any symbolism and is unfair to those who already have that nationality and to those who are making efforts to integrate, hoping to obtain it one day. it is very true that member states have exclusive competence to define the criteria on the basis of which citizenship is granted. it should not be forgotten, however, that along with the citizenship of a member state, a third-country national also receives european citizenship, with all the rights and freedoms it entails. given the existence of the schengen area and freedom of movement, the granting of citizenship against payment ceases to be a purely national matter. i therefore believe that member states must show responsibility and take account of the secondary effects that such initiatives may have on other member states and, by implication, on mutual trust between them.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the sale of eu citizenship. some eu member states have introduced schemes which directly or indirectly involve the sale of eu citizenship to third-country nationals. eu citizens have the right to move and reside freely within the eu, the right to vote and stand as candidates in municipal and european parliamentary elections, regardless of the state in which they live in the eu, under the same conditions as nationals of that state, and the right to receive assistance from the embassy or consulate of another eu member state outside the eu under the same conditions as nationals of that country if their country is not represented. any national system that may involve the sale of eu citizenship undermines the very concept of european citizenship. we call on the member states to recognise and assume their responsibilities for protecting the union's values and objectives. we invite the commission to assess the different citizenship systems in the light of european values and the spirit and letter of eu law and practice and to develop recommendations to prevent these systems from undermining the values on which the eu is founded, as well as guidelines on access to eu citizenship through national systems.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in south sudan. the republic of south sudan is one of the poorest and least developed countries in the world, with 50% of its population living below the poverty line, the highest maternal mortality rate, one of the highest infant mortality rates, an illiteracy rate of approximately 75% and only one third of the population having access to clean water. we strongly condemn the recent outbreak of fighting in south sudan and call on all parties to lay down their arms and immediately end the violence that has resulted in civilian deaths, injuries and damage and displaced hundreds of thousands of people since the beginning of the crisis in december 2013. we urge all parties concerned to respect international humanitarian and human rights law, as well as to grant access and protection to humanitarian agencies that come to the aid of the suffering civilian population, and to open humanitarian corridors for the delivery of supplies and equipment. we call on the international community to honour its commitments on funding to south sudan and the region and to mobilise its resources to respond as swiftly as possible to the worsening humanitarian situation in south sudan.

in writing. − homelessness remains a problem across europe, and the nature of the homeless population is changing. homelessness has a negative effect on both the homeless person and society. despite progress in many member states in tackling the phenomenon, there is a clear need for support and policy coordination at european level. not only does the definition of homelessness vary widely between member states, but data collection and reporting are also highly heterogeneous. i believe that the eu needs to develop a common framework to support and monitor member states in developing policies to tackle homelessness.

on behalf of the epp group. thank you, mr president. i would like to thank mrs mccarthy, the commission and the council for having brought about this european regulation. as a colleague of mrs mccarthy, i want to thank her very much for her work in the econ committee, i want to tell her that whenever she has expressed a point of view we have appreciated that point of view and, of course, i regret that she will not be running for the european parliament again. i want to make it very clear here that one of the most destructive effects on the capital market is the loss of confidence by investors in those who are experts in different market organizations, in companies, and who sometimes try and succeed in manipulating the market by leaking information from within a small group of individuals. in my country, romania, i witnessed one of the most serious cases of market manipulation, of stock market manipulation, when a major oil processing company was listed on the market. individuals who had inside information in the first few seconds participated in the purchase of shares, then in the next few seconds, making extremely large gains. the case was brought before the romanian courts, but unfortunately the romanian courts were not accustomed to dealing with such cases, there were no clear provisions in the criminal code on the punishment of such market manipulation and, consequently, the guilty are today free and clear. i shall vote in favour of this report and i hope that we can really put a stop to this destructive practice. thank you. thank you.
on behalf of the s&d group. thank you, mr president. ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to welcome this proposal for a directive, which aims to strengthen the legislative framework on market abuse by harmonising the penalties for this type of behaviour at european union level. the proposal includes both minimum and maximum prison sentences and the possibility of sanctioning legal persons. a person found guilty of manipulating financial markets could, for example, receive a minimum sentence of four years in prison. we cannot forget the libor/euribor scandal, whereby a number of major banking institutions manipulated financial information in order to give a better picture of their credit situation and to win large sums of money. this false information has caused harm to consumers and investors and distorted the real economy. at the same time, given the serious consequences of the financial crisis and the current fragility of the european economic system, we cannot risk further destabilisation of markets. in this context, i believe that a single european regime of criminal sanctions in this area is necessary to discourage abuse in those member states which currently have less stringent rules and to ensure the proper functioning of the european internal market. we cannot let those bankers go unpunished who, through their irresponsible behaviour, are endangering the integrity of the financial system, risking to cause significant damage to the lives of millions of people. thank you. thank you.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation because i consider it important to include greenland in the kimberley process certification scheme. greenland is included in the list of overseas countries and territories and, under the treaties, the purpose of our association with these regions is, among other things, to develop economic relations. however, this strengthening of eu-greenland economic cooperation is dependent on the region's ability to develop and diversify economically. in this context, it is important to support the participation of this area in the kimberley process with a view to facilitating the exploitation of the mining potential in the region.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 2368/2002 as regards the inclusion of greenland in the implementation of the kimberley process certification scheme. the proposal aims to enable greenland to participate in the kimberley process certification scheme (kpcs) for rough diamonds through its cooperation with the eu. the mechanism provided for in the proposal would allow the import and export of rough diamonds between greenland and the union, as well as to other participants in the certification scheme, provided that all imports and exports of rough diamonds are verified and, in the case of exports, certified by the union authorities in accordance with the rules laid down in regulation (ec) no 2368/2002 implementing the kimberley process certification scheme for international trade in rough diamonds. the kimberley process is a joint initiative of governments, industry and civil society aimed at ending the trade in war diamonds rough diamonds used by rebel movements to finance wars waged against legitimate governments. this proposal for a regulation is based on article 207 tfeu and concerns certain amendments to regulation (ec) no 2368/2002 necessary to allow greenland to be part of the eu certification scheme.
in writing. - i voted in favour of both moreira reports because i believe that the greenlandic economy will benefit from the decision to participate in the kimberley certification system - of course, provided that all imports and exports of rough diamonds are verified and, in the case of exports, certified by the union authorities. in addition, the involvement of civil society and industry is a good start to having a process based on integration, cooperation and effectiveness with greenland. last but not least, i believe that any country or territory that accepts and effectively implements the kimberley process rules should be welcomed into this system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision establishing rules and procedures to enable greenland to participate in the kimberley process certification scheme. the eu participates in the system as a whole, including all 28 eu member states. the eu implements the kimberley process through the six union authorities. any shipment of rough diamonds imported into/exported from any eu member state will be sent to one of the union authorities for verification and only after that will it be sent back to its destination and released for free circulation within the eu. approximately 99.8% of the world's rough diamonds are produced by kimberley process participants, which means that an essential initial step for any country with diamond potential is to become part of the process, otherwise it cannot legally export rough diamonds. greenland is not a country, so it cannot become a participant in the kimberley process. this proposal for a council decision pursuant to article 203 tfeu establishes a specific regime for the movement of rough diamonds between greenland and the eu. it also stipulates that any trade in rough diamonds between a third country and greenland must be approved in advance by an eu authority.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and i consider that the amendment of the regulation in question is an important component in the process of achieving the single euro payments area. in addition, this is supported by the latest statistical data from the european central bank, which shows that the overall migration rate to the euro area increased from 59,87% in october 2013 to 64,1% in november 2013 for credit transfer transactions within the single euro payments area. however, i think it is important to note that the commission's outreach efforts to the competent authorities in the member states and efforts to promote sepa migration have not been effective, as smes, small governments and local authorities continue to be the least prepared for an effective migration.
in writing. - data on migration to sepa transfers in the euro area show an increase from 40% in june 2013 to around 64% in november 2013, while the overall migration rate to sepa direct debits reached only 26%. the delays in the statistics also indicate that several member states are behind schedule on the targets set for 1 february 2014. the coordination of migration activities still to be carried out is crucial to avoid flooding of payment systems. i therefore welcome the proposal that, among other things, a single transitional period should apply to both sepa transfers and sepa direct debits.
in writing. - i support the introduction of an additional period of 6 months for the transition of payment systems of banks and payment service providers in member states participating in the creation of a single euro payment area (sepa). by 1 february 2014, 17 countries were to replace their national credit transfer and direct debit systems with single systems in sepa. the current utilisation rate is around 64% for credit transfer in sepa and 26% for direct debit in sepa. ten member states recorded a double increase of between 10% and 15% in sepa transactions in the last quarter of 2013. i suggest that in the next 6 months the european central bank accelerate and complete the sepa migration process.
in writing. - regulation no 260/2012 is an important component of the process of completing a single euro payments area (sepa), in which no distinction is made between cross-border and national payments in euro. the main objective of regulation (eu) no 260/2012 is to migrate from national credit transfer and direct debit systems to harmonised sepa credit transfer (sct) and sepa direct debit (sdd) systems, inter alia by making available to union citizens a single international bank account number (iban) that can be used for all sepa credit transfer and direct debit transactions in euro. in the absence of full migration to sct and sdd, delays in those payments cannot be excluded, which would affect all payment service users and in particular smes and consumers. it is essential to avoid any disruption of payments caused by the fact that the migration to sepa is not fully completed by 1 february 2014. i argued that payment service providers could continue until 1 august 2014 to process euro payment transactions in formats other than those provided for credit transfers within sepa and direct debits within sepa.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption in plenary of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 260/2012 as regards the migration to union-wide credit transfer and direct debit operations; i voted for this report because it wants to introduce a transition period to allow the continuation of parallel processing of payments in different formats, i.e. to continue processing payment transactions through their traditional systems, in parallel with the use of sct and sdd systems. i also agree that such a temporary maintenance of traditional non-sepa compliant systems for another six months should be considered an exceptional measure, and that the shortest possible duration is necessary, given that a rapid and comprehensive migration is needed to realise all the benefits of an integrated payments market.

in writing. - the report by mr mccarthy deals with criminal sanctions in cases of insider dealing and market manipulation. i believe that this is an important and necessary regulatory intervention, especially when we consider that the sanctions currently in place to combat such abuses are not sufficiently effective in some member states and are not very effective in deterring them. the report calls for the introduction of effective criminal sanctions (imprisonment of at least four years) for insider trading, market manipulation and aiding and abetting such offences.
in writing. - i welcome the proposal for a directive on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation. recent cases, such as the manipulation of the libor index in the uk, make it very clear that millions of citizens across the european union are vulnerable to market manipulation. very often, false information is thrown into the press with the aim of manipulating exchange rates, stock market benchmarks, interbank interest rates, or credit market interest rates. we can no longer turn a blind eye to such speculation! let us not forget that the root cause of the economic crisis was financial problems. or, the way out of the crisis is also linked to the confidence that investors and the general public have in financial markets. i think that a directive imposing criminal sanctions on those who manipulate the market is welcome. as you know, the sanctions currently in force in the member states are weak and heterogeneous. we need uniform and severe sanction systems against financial crime. only then can we restore and defend the integrity of the eu's financial markets. to that end, competent authorities should have the necessary resources to detect and investigate market abuse.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation, which adopts the ep's position at first reading. in view of the consequences of the financial crisis, it has become clear that market manipulation has the potential to cause widespread harm to the lives of millions of people. the recent libor scandal, which highlighted a serious case of benchmark manipulation, has demonstrated that relevant problems and gaps in this area have a major impact on market confidence and can lead to considerable losses for investors and distortions in the real economy. the absence of a common regime of criminal sanctions at union level gives rise to market abuse in member states with less stringent regimes. in addition, the imposition of criminal sanctions for market abuse offences will have a stronger deterrent effect on potential offenders. this directive establishes minimum rules on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and illegal disclosure of inside information and market manipulation in order to guarantee the integrity of financial markets in the union and to enhance investor protection and confidence in those markets.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation; i voted in favour of this report, convinced that to get out of the financial crisis and to respond to the challenges facing capital and financial markets, where a new bubble can form at any time, a single european sanctions regime is needed for individuals and for firms that manipulate capital markets or provide confidential information, contrary to the law. eu rules in this sector, which provide for minimum sentences of up to four years in prison for those found guilty, will lead to a return of confidence in financial markets. the clear rules will also help courts in all 28 member states when they are dealing with cases of market manipulation.
in writing. - in the light of the eu's europe 2020 targets, increasing energy efficiency is essential. i therefore consider that the proposal to inform the european commission of investment projects in energy infrastructure in the european union is a timely one, and that it contributes to the achievement of the objectives set. these changes have the potential to respond to new energy challenges and to give the european commission the opportunity to come up with proposals to increase competitiveness in the energy sector. the new procedures envisaged are also necessary precisely to allow the investment framework in this sector to be made more efficient.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and i think it is appropriate to maintain the provisions of the previous regulation. the obligation for member states to notify the commission every two years of data and information on investment projects in the production, storage and transport of oil, natural gas or electricity is useful in many ways. for example, the connecting europe facility needs all this information in order to correctly identify investment needs or to coordinate and develop the field of energy infrastructure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the notification to the commission of investment projects in energy infrastructure in the european union and replacing regulation (eu, euratom) no 617/2010 adopting the european parliament's position at first reading. the new energy context requires significant investment in all types of infrastructure, across all energy sectors, and in the development of new types of infrastructure and new technologies to be adopted by the market. the liberalisation of the energy sector and the further integration of the internal market give economic operators a more prominent role in investment. at the same time, new public policy requirements, such as fuel mix targets, will change member states' public policies towards new and/or upgraded energy infrastructure. this regulation establishes a common framework for the notification to the commission of data and information relating to investment projects in energy infrastructure in the oil, natural gas, electricity, including electricity from renewable sources and energy from coal and lignite, and cogeneration of electricity and useful heat sectors, as well as investment projects in the production of biofuels and the capture, transport and storage of carbon dioxide generated by those sectors.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption in plenary of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the notification to the commission of investment projects in energy infrastructure in the eu; we voted for this new regulation as a further step towards strengthening the common energy market. its main objective is to ensure that the commission is regularly and accurately informed about investment projects in eu energy infrastructure so that it can fulfil its energy tasks. in this way, the identification of future potential supply and demand imbalances and investment obstacles will be easier to achieve. last but not least, the new regulation complements the connecting europe facility in identifying investment needs in energy infrastructure with a view to achieving the internal energy market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the nomination of klaus-heiner lehne as a member of the court of auditors. mr lehne's 20 years of experience as a member of the european parliament, as well as his holding of responsible posts such as chairman of the committee on legal affairs and chairman of the conference of committee chairmen, coupled with his deep legal background, make him, in my view, the best candidate for this post.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision to give a favourable opinion on the council's proposal to appoint klaus-heiner lehne as a member of the court of auditors. in accordance with article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the members of the court of auditors shall be chosen from among persons who are or have been members of the external financial control institutions in their state or who possess specific qualifications for that office. they shall provide all guarantees of independence. the members of the court of auditors shall be appointed for a term of six years. the council, after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt the list of members drawn up in accordance with the proposals made by each member state. the term of office of the members of the court of auditors may be renewed. the european parliament's committee on budgetary control assessed the qualifications of the proposed candidate, taking into account in particular the conditions laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. also, during its meeting of 23 january 2014, the committee on budgetary control heard the candidate nominated by the council to be a member of the court of auditors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the future role of the european court is particularly important, given its role in helping to improve the financial management of the union by acting as the independent guardian of the financial interests of citizens. the european court of auditors shall provide assurances as to the veracity of the accounts and the legality of the transactions and their entry in the accounts in any given financial year, in which independence, integrity, impartiality and professionalism are crucial. last but not least, i too find it inconvenient that certain appointment procedures have led to conflicts between parliament and the council over the candidates.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the future role of the european court of auditors appointment of the members of the court of auditors: consultation of the european parliament. the european court of auditors was set up by the 1975 budget treaty to audit the eu's finances. as the eu's external auditor, it contributes to improving the financial management of the union by acting as the independent guardian of the financial interests of eu citizens. the european court of auditors, as a professional audit institution, is required to apply, inter alia, international auditing standards applicable to the public sector. we consider that, as the external auditor for the union institutions, the european court of auditors can provide the legislative bodies with not only a statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts, but also as to the legality of the operations and their entry in the accounts in any given budgetary year. it is also in an eminent position to provide the legislative body and the budgetary authority, in particular parliament's committee on budgetary control, with valuable advice on the results achieved by union policies, to improve the performance and effectiveness of union-funded activities, to identify economies of scale and scope as well as spill-over effects between member states' national policies and to provide parliament with external assessments of the commission's assessments of public finances in the member states.
thank you, mr president. i voted in favour of the report because the parliaments of the member states have an important say in the drafting of european legislation, and this is clear evidence of the transparency of decision-making procedures in the european union. on the other hand, some national parliaments have not understood the spirit of these provisions of the union treaties. i give you the example of the chamber of deputies in romania, which last year gave a negative opinion on the proposal to establish the european public prosecutor's office. i suppose the majority of socialists are afraid that such an institution might reveal possible irregularities in procurement procedures carried out with european funds. i say this because the reasoning for this opinion is not coherent and does not clearly explain why this proposal was considered to infringe the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it underlines once again that the european institutions must respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union and in protocol no 2 to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which are of a general nature and impose obligations on the institutions in the exercise of the union's competences, except that the principle of subsidiarity does not apply in those areas which fall within the union's exclusive competence. at the same time, the report strengthens the role of the european institutions, such as the scrutiny exercised by the ep but also by national parliaments, the power of the court of justice to check the legality of legislative acts, the role of the european commission as the guardian of compliance with the treaties and all community legislation, etc.
in writing. - there is no doubt that smart regulation is an essential tool to better regulate the different general and local needs, to reduce administrative burdens and to simplify the application and legal certainty throughout the european union. the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making is now inadequate in relation to the current legislative context, as generated by the treaty of lisbon, and further steps are therefore needed to improve the legislative process and the adequacy of eu regulation, in full respect of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. - union rules must be simple, clear and effective, accessible in all official languages and with a clear added value. according to a eurobarometer survey published in spring 2013, 24% of citizens in the member states identify the union with the concept of bureaucracy. in addition, 74% of them believe that eu legislation creates even more red tape in their own countries. these percentages are worrying and need to be reduced. we need to change the way we legislate through coordinated action by the union, national institutions and local and regional authorities. relations between the european institutions and national and local authorities must respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. we need to provide citizens with clear legislation that is easy to understand and does not involve any unnecessary administrative burden. i support the renegotiation of the 2003 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making and its binding legal force.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on eu regulatory adequacy, subsidiarity and proportionality 19th report on better lawmaking for 2011. we consider that the impact assessment of new regulations on smes or large companies can neither have the effect of discriminating against workers on the basis of the size of the companies where they work, nor affect the fundamental rights of workers, which include the right to information and consultation, working conditions, well-being at work and their social security rights, nor prevent the improvement of the protection they enjoy at work with regard to existing occupational risks or some new risks. i argue that legislation proposed and adopted at european level should be simple, effective and efficient, provide clear added value, be easy to understand and accessible in all the official languages of the member states, and provide maximum benefits at minimum costs. i argue that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality must be respected by the european institutions in the legislative process. we call on the commission to come forward with concrete proposals to reduce the overall regulatory burden in the eu without undermining health and safety at work.

in writing. - the electricity grid: we all use it, we recognise its usefulness and we are aware that our life would be almost impossible without electricity. few people know that the electrical grid works today similar to the way it was thought to work almost 100 years ago. without deviating from the norm, electrical grids around the world have so far served only the primary purpose for which they were designed. progress, however, is not possible without abstracting, for a moment, from limits. smart grids aim to transform electricity grids from simple electricity transmission lines into networks that facilitate continuous communication between all those connected to them. this type of grid is now a global priority, because it saves money by immediately detecting potential power leaks or failures, protects the grid against attacks and power outages, introduces alternative forms of electricity generation and thus significantly reduces co2 emissions.
