in writing. - natural and man-made disasters are occurring with increasing frequency in the european union, which should be a cause for concern given the damage and high costs they cause. storm floods, river overflow, and forest fires are the most common. there is a need to better inform union citizens, as they are not aware of the different risks that may arise or tend to underestimate them. i believe that good information would increase disaster prevention and mitigation and protect the population from potential losses. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, in particular through the european neighbourhood instrument (enpi).
in writing. - the impact of natural and man-made disasters in europe has increased rapidly in recent years, while the capacity of member states to respond is often limited. in this context, i believe that disaster prevention must be a priority of european risk management policy. the reduction of the consequences of disasters is more effective than simply providing insurance cover or repairing the damage later. i would like to draw attention to the need to involve communities in disaster risk education activities in order to develop a rapid response behaviour. i therefore welcome the decision to establish the international day for natural disaster risk reduction as a means of promoting a global culture of mitigation, in particular prevention, mitigation and preparedness. last but not least, measures to increase europe's preparedness for natural and man-made disasters must target rapid and well-targeted efforts to rehabilitate and rebuild after a disaster.
in writing. - i supported the report on insurance against natural and man-made disasters and i would like to draw attention to the special situation of agriculture among the areas most seriously and frequently affected by disasters such as floods and heavy snowfalls, as well as other extreme weather events. the new regulations on the common agricultural policy provide for a financial contribution from european funds, crop, animal and plant insurance. this support may amount to up to 65% of the insurance premium due. in view of the enormous damage caused to agriculture by natural disasters with an impact on crops and food prices , member states have a duty to prepare in advance an incentive and effective framework to allow the maximum use of this opportunity offered by the common agricultural policy. as natural disasters are by definition unforeseen phenomena, the preparation of the legal framework for insurance premium subsidisation cannot tolerate any delay.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on insurance against natural and man-made disasters. storm floods, forest fires and floods caused by river surges and high winds are among the main natural disaster risks facing europe and, even if their number is increasing at a rapid pace, it is still impossible to estimate their increasingly powerful effects in terms of damage and costs. we believe that further research could lead to a detailed framework of the different situations concerning the understanding and prevention of environmental risks and to a reduction of uncertainty in this area. we welcome partnerships between insurance companies and research institutes on pooling resources, skills and risk expertise to better understand the issues involved, thereby preparing citizens and the communities in which they live to deal more effectively with natural disaster risks. we believe that closer cooperation between the public and private sectors could help member states and local authorities to identify high-risk areas, decide on prevention measures and prepare for coordinated action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on insurance against natural and man-made disasters because it focuses on prevention, underlining that the eu has a very important role to play in developing a more responsible society, paying sufficient attention to precautionary measures, and in creating a culture of prevention that raises citizens' awareness of natural and man-made risks. i also welcome the fact that the report invites member states to exchange best practices and experience in order to protect citizens against unforeseen events and develop a network for the exchange of information and to reach an agreement on cross-border coordination and management. the resolution also refers to the commission's efforts to raise public awareness of disasters, stressing that natural and man-made disasters require different types of insurance and are covered by two different insurance markets and therefore cannot be analysed together.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the nomination of ms sabine lautenschläger to the post of vice-chair of the supervisory board of the european central bank. i consider that ms lautenschläger's career is impressive and her previous positions are further evidence of her extensive experience in the field of banking and financial supervision.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on the proposal of the european central bank for the appointment of the vice-chair of the supervisory board of the european central bank, approving the ecb's proposal for the appointment of sabine lautenschläger as vice-chair of the supervisory board of the ecb. on 21 january 2014, the european council appointed sabine lautenschläger as a member of the executive board of the ecb in accordance with article 283 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. by its letter of 22 january 2014, the ecb submitted to parliament a proposal to appoint sabine lautenschläger as vice-chair of the supervisory board of the ecb for a five-year term. the committee on economic and monetary affairs of parliament assessed the qualifications of the proposed candidate, in particular in view of the requirements laid down in article 26 (2) and (3) of regulation (eu) no 1024/2013. the commission also held a hearing with the proposed candidate on 3 february 2014, during which she made an introductory statement and then answered questions from the members of the commission.
madam president, i voted in favour of this recommendation and i believe that, following the example of the agreement concluded with switzerland, the union should also consider strengthening cooperation in the field of competition with other economic partners. the novelty of this report, the exchange of evidence, will facilitate investigations into anti-competitive actions. in addition, the degree of integration between the economies of the various states is very high, and many of these practices affect cross-border trade and, by implication, european citizens. however, i cannot fail to note that this agreement lacks legal obligations. so if one of the parties can invoke certain important interests to disapply the provisions of the agreement, i wonder if in practice its usefulness will be as great as what we now find in theory.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council decision on the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on cooperation in the enforcement of their competition laws. following the conclusion of cooperation agreements on competition with the usa, canada, japan and south korea, the commission is now about to conclude a 'first second generation agreement' with the swiss confederation. unlike previous agreements, this agreement also includes provisions on the exchange of evidence obtained by competition authorities when they investigate the same case, which will contribute to more effective enforcement of competition law. the swiss confederation is the eu's third most important economic partner. there is a high degree of integration between the economies of the various states and many anti-competitive practices affect cross-border trade. the implementation of the agreement will be facilitated by the similarities between the rules and practices applicable within the eu and the swiss confederation. the eu should build on the experience gained from this agreement and take the necessary steps to conclude other 'second generation' agreements with other partners, no matter how many obstacles may arise due to differences in rules and practices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, which deals with an important aspect of the new agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on cooperation in the enforcement of their competition laws. i refer here to the legally binding provisions on such enhanced cooperation and the definition of 'important interests' in that agreement. therefore, in order to fill these possible legislative gaps, as well as to ensure the effective implementation of this agreement, it is essential that the member states and switzerland, through their national competition authorities, cooperate fully with the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on european union cooperation agreements in the field of competition policy implementation. we welcome the proposed agreement between the eu and switzerland on cooperation in the enforcement of their competition laws. the member states and their national competition authorities should cooperate fully with the commission to ensure the effective implementation of this agreement. we consider it essential to closely monitor the implementation of this agreement in order to learn from experience and identify any issues of concern and we invite the commission to carry out such monitoring. we invite the commission to actively promote cooperation in the enforcement of competition policy at international level, in particular in multilateral fora such as the world trade organisation (wto), the international competition network (icn) and the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd). we ask the commission, in view of the future negotiations on competition agreements, to provide more comprehensive and frequent information to parliament.
madam president, i voted in favour of the recommendation because the member states must ratify the arms trade treaty as soon as possible. i would also like to call on third countries to speed up their internal ratification procedures. although the legal act is not as ambitious as we would have liked, i believe that it still creates the premises for an even stricter regulation, at international level, of the arms trade in the future. romania, for example, already applies more restrictive rules on the arms trade, so the impact in this respect will not be major for my country. romania's arms exports are much lower today than in 1990, but even under these conditions the national defence industry has a particularly important strategic component.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation on the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the international arms trade treaty. unlike weapons of mass destruction and landmines, the trade in conventional weapons is not subject to any legally binding international instrument. the arms trade treaty is designed to fill this gap. it establishes a common international standard to regulate international trade in conventional arms and, to some extent, ammunition and their parts and components. it also aims to prevent and eliminate the illicit trade in such weapons. the current situation of the arms trade, which is totally unregulated, has catastrophic effects on peace, security and development in some of the world's most vulnerable countries. the aim of the international arms trade treaty is to control arms exports to third countries, and more particularly to try to stop arms exports to areas where there is a danger of human rights violations or even genocide. it is our responsibility to bring greater transparency to this sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution of 5 february 2014 on the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the arms trade treaty. the arms trade treaty was adopted on 2 april 2013 by a resolution of the united nations general assembly. three states voted against the treaty (north korea, iran and syria) and 22 states abstained (including china, india and russia), which could lead to slow ratification and possibly incomplete implementation in these countries. the att sets a common international standard for regulating international trade in conventional arms and, to some extent, ammunition, parts and components. it also aims at preventing and eradicating the illicit trade in such weapons.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe it is the duty of member states to implement control systems for arms transfers. transparency in this area is essential, especially in a context where many weapons end up in the hands of groups whose sole purpose is to destabilise certain regions or countries. however, it is also important that non-eu states ratify this treaty in order to allow for the creation of a strengthened international arms export control system. last but not least, i believe that this treaty lays the foundation for greater cooperation between the signatory states in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the arms trade treaty (att) approving the proposal for a council decision. the treaty aims to establish the highest possible common international standards for the regulation of the international trade in conventional arms, the prevention and eradication of the illicit trade in conventional arms, in order to support international and regional peace, security and stability and the reduction of human suffering. we believe that the effective implementation of the treaty can make a significant contribution to strengthening respect for international human rights and humanitarian law worldwide. we invite states parties, with regard to export control and the application of articles 6 (prohibitions) and 7 (1a-iv) (export and assessment of export requests) of the att, to pay particular attention to goods that can be used for both civilian and military purposes, such as surveillance technology, but also spare parts and corresponding products used in cyberwarfare or for non-lethal human rights abuses, and propose to consider the possibility of extending the scope of the att to include services associated with the export of dual-use goods and weapons and technology.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which represents an important victory for social and economic rights in the framework of european regulation against imports which are subject to dumping and subsidies from third countries. the revision of this regulation will allow the eu to impose higher customs duties on countries exporting subsidised or dumped products to the eu when these countries do not comply with the basic conventions or basic environmental standards set by the international labour organisation (ilo). the european parliament's vote calls on the commission to be more cautious in its international commitments at a time when european industry is under increasing pressure from international competitors. the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the european instruments for defending the union's trade policy must be further modernised to protect european industries and the millions of jobs they create against illegal and unfair trade practices by certain third countries!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments adopted by the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community and regulation no 597/2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community. it is necessary to amend certain provisions of the regulations in order to improve transparency and predictability, to provide for effective measures to combat retaliation by third countries, to improve effectiveness and enforcement and to optimise review practices. the lack of homogeneity and fragmentation of sectors, which are largely composed of smes, make it difficult to access trade defence procedures, due to the complexity of those procedures and the high costs involved. access for smes should be improved by strengthening the role of the sme helpdesk, which should support smes in lodging complaints and reaching the thresholds necessary to initiate investigations. administrative procedures associated with trade defence procedures should also be better adapted to the constraints of smes.
madam president, i voted in favour of this report because the treaty of lisbon requires us to bring european legislation into line with the law. i also think that this process should be expedited, given that it has been four years since it came into force. the report makes a number of important improvements to the commission's powers. i am referring in particular to ensuring the safety of seafarers and reducing bureaucratic burdens. furthermore, the commission will have to choose the most cost-effective option and respect the sustainable development pillars in the process of adopting delegated acts. last but not least, the commission's report on the state of play of the adopted acts will assess their effectiveness and, by implication, that of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - i believe that there should be an agreement between the commission and the competent national plant protection authorities and in no case giving the commission all the powers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system for ensuring compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. the regulation aims at aligning regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 with the lisbon treaty and it is important that in the future revision of that regulation the commission examine: the european parliament's requests concerning the distinction between passive and fixed fishing gear; the relevance of the 10% tolerance levels for logbook data; the conditions for notification of entry into ports; possible derogations from the weighing conditions; the administrative burden of weighing requirements; the conditions for allocating and transferring points for offences and the publication of data related to offences. i would stress that it is particularly important that the commission organise appropriate consultations during the preparatory work, including at expert level, for example with the regional advisory councils. when preparing and drawing up delegated acts, the commission should ensure a simultaneous, timely and appropriate transmission of relevant documents to the european parliament and to the council.
in writing. - the harmonization of national provisions in the field of equipment and protective systems intended for use in potentially explosive atmospheres must have as its primary objective the maintenance of a high level of public safety and the protection of the safety of workers at the workplace. at the same time, i believe that these initiatives, which aim to harmonise the legislative conditions at european level, represent a step forward towards improving the conditions for the functioning of the single market and have the potential to encourage the increase in the competitiveness of european economic operators in this sector of activity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it removes the shortcomings of the current regulations and represents an important step towards completing the single market, which must be based on fair competition. this new framework is simplified compared to the previous one, so it will allow for a consistent implementation of technical rules and will by implication lead to a reduction in the number of non-compliant, unsafe products on the market. the most important issues this time are those relating to consumer protection and the safety of the products they use. i believe that special attention should be paid to distance selling, in the sense that it is necessary to intensify the supervision of this sector which is constantly developing. last but not least, i am convinced that all these measures will improve the conditions for the free movement of goods within the union.
in writing. - the alignment of the product directive proposal to ncl is an important step towards the completion of the eu single market, which will ensure the same treatment for non-compliant products and economic operators and will increase confidence of both producers and consumers by clarifying the obligations of economic operators. on the other hand, the new directive will provide member states' authorities with more efficient tools for carrying out market surveillance checks, all of which will lead to a reduction in the number of non-compliant and unsafe products on the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to equipment and protective systems intended for use in potentially explosive atmospheres (reform). the directive covers products which, when placed on the market, are new to the union market: they are either new products manufactured by a producer within the union or new or second-hand products imported from a third country. it should also apply to all forms of supply, including distance selling. it is necessary to ensure that products from third countries entering the union market comply with this directive, in particular that manufacturers have applied the appropriate conformity assessment procedures for the products concerned. provisions should therefore be laid down requiring importers to ensure that the products they place on the market comply with the requirements of this directive and not to place on the market products which do not comply with those requirements or present risks. provisions should also be adopted requiring importers to ensure that conformity assessment procedures have been applied and that product marking and documentation drawn up by manufacturers are available for inspection by the competent national authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the placing on the market and supervision of explosives for civil use (reform). it is necessary to clarify in this directive that certain articles have been identified on the basis of the united nations recommendations on the transport of dangerous goods as pyrotechnic articles or ammunition and therefore do not fall within the scope of this directive. commission directive 2004/57/ec of 23 april 2004 on the identification of pyrotechnic articles and certain ammunition within the meaning of council directive 93/15/eec on the harmonisation of the provisions relating to the placing on the market and supervision of explosives for civil uses, which currently contains a list of such articles, should therefore be repealed. pyrotechnic articles require appropriate measures to ensure the protection of end-users and the safety of the public. pyrotechnic articles are subject to directive 2013/29/eu on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of pyrotechnic articles. this directive should therefore not apply to pyrotechnic articles. in order to ensure a consistent level of quality in relation to conformity assessment, it is also necessary to lay down requirements for notifying authorities and other bodies involved in the assessment, notification and monitoring of notified bodies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the amendments to the directive will ensure greater consistency and remove any discrepancies in the text which might otherwise create legal uncertainty. however, i consider that a number of transitional provisions are necessary to give economic operators the time needed to adapt to the new regulatory framework. last but not least, i am confident that with the implementation of the harmonised framework, the number of non-compliant products on the market will decrease considerably, while the confidence and safety of consumers and producers will increase.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of non-automated weighing instruments (reform). the directive covers non-automatic weighing machines which are new to the union market when they are placed on the market. they are either new non-automatic weighing machines manufactured by a manufacturer established in the union or new or second-hand non-automatic weighing machines imported from a third country. member states should protect the public against incorrect results of weighing operations carried out by non-automatic weighing machines when used in certain fields of application. economic operators should be responsible for the conformity of non-automated weighing instruments with the requirements of the directive in relation to their respective roles in the supply chain, in order to ensure a high level of protection of the public interests covered by the directive and to guarantee fair competition on the union market. it is necessary to ensure that non-automatic weighing machines from third countries entering the union market comply with this directive and in particular that manufacturers have applied the appropriate conformity assessment procedures for the non-automatic weighing machines concerned.
in writing. - ensuring a high standard of electromagnetic compatibility at european level is both an advantage for consumers and an incentive for european manufacturers in this field. i also believe that the reduction of bureaucratic restrictions, a consequence of these proposals, is a welcome move which will help to strengthen the market in this important sector for european economies. the provision of contact details for virtual communication between consumers and economic operators in this sector is also an important step towards increasing the level of protection of the rights of european consumers. last but not least, i welcome the provisions to strengthen producer responsibility.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. while we will now have a clearer and more harmonised legal framework, the responsibilities of member states remain essential to ensure the conformity, operation, installation and maintenance of products entering the single market. in addition, the appropriate packaging and labelling, in particular by mentioning the instructions for use, safety measures and all contact details, benefits both producers and, above all, consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to electromagnetic compatibility (reform). this text envisaged a number of amendments to directive 2004/108/ec on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to electromagnetic compatibility and repealing directive 89/336/eec. member states should be responsible for ensuring the protection of radio communications, including reception of broadcasts and amateur radio services operating in accordance with the radio regulations of the international telecommunications organisation (itu), as well as electricity supply and telecommunications networks and equipment connected to them, against electromagnetic disturbance. the relevant provisions of national law providing for protection against electromagnetic disturbances need to be harmonised in order to guarantee the free movement of electrical and electronic equipment without reducing the justified levels of protection in the member states. this directive concerns products which are new to the union market at the time of their placing on the market. these products are completely new, manufactured by a manufacturer established in the union or are imported from a third country, whether they are completely new or second-hand.
in writing. - the marketing of these electrical equipment throughout the european union must first of all comply with public health and safety requirements, especially as regards their impact on civil infrastructure. a related objective of the harmonisation process is to increase the level of protection of vulnerable consumers in the case of non-professional use of such equipment. last but not least, it is important that these measures do not affect the competitiveness of european economic actors and the ability of the market in this sector to meet consumer demands. i support the adoption of this proposal, which has the potential to reduce bureaucratic restrictions and thus contribute to the development of the electrical equipment market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and of the whole harmonisation framework. electrical equipment is a consumer good and economic operators should be responsible for its conformity in order to ensure the highest level of protection of the health and safety of consumers. in the event that electrical equipment is not intended for professional use, the safety of children, the elderly and persons with disabilities must be emphasised. in this respect, labelling plays an important role: the instructions for use must be written in accessible and clear language and potential hazards must be explicitly mentioned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of electrical equipment designed for use within certain voltage limits (reform). the directive covers electrical equipment intended for use within certain voltage limits which is new to the union market when it is placed on the market. this means that it is either new electrical equipment manufactured by a manufacturer established in the union or new or second-hand electrical equipment imported from a third country. all economic operators involved in the supply and distribution chain should take appropriate measures to ensure that they make available on the market only electrical equipment which complies with this directive. it is necessary to provide for a clear and proportionate distribution of obligations corresponding to the role played by each economic operator in the supply and distribution chain. the manufacturer, being the person with the most detailed knowledge of the design and production process, is best placed to carry out the conformity assessment procedure. conformity assessment should therefore remain the sole responsibility of the manufacturer. there is no conformity assessment procedure in this directive which requires the intervention of a notified body.
in writing. - any process of harmonising legislation on the marketing of lifts and related products must take into account the imperatives of public safety with special attention to vulnerable consumers such as the elderly, children, etc. it is also important that the effect of the regulations does not distort fair competition in the single market and the level of competitiveness of european economic actors. last but not least, in view of the imperative assumed by the european union and the member states to build an inclusive society, i believe it is extremely important that the member states and the european authorities respect international regulations on the rights of persons with disabilities in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it brings a number of clarifications to the legislative framework, and deals with issues of public safety. as regards lifts, i believe that the most important measures that can be taken to guarantee the safety of their use are those relating to regular checks and technical inspections. last but not least, special attention should be paid to children, the elderly and, in particular, people with disabilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of lifts and safety components for lifts. elevators covered by this directive are considered to be finished products only after they are permanently installed in buildings or structures. the commission has not established that the union industry is able to benefit from the measures in force. this directive covers safety components for lifts which are new to the union market at the time of their placing on the market. more specifically, they are either new safety components manufactured by a manufacturer in the union or new or second-hand safety components imported from a third country. economic operators should be responsible for the compliance of lifts and safety components for lifts with this directive, depending on their role in the supply chain, in order to ensure a high level of protection of the health and safety of persons and, where appropriate, the safety of goods and to guarantee fair competition on the union market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it clarifies the shortcomings of the previous regulation by setting out a number of essential safety requirements that simple pressure vessels must meet in order to be made available on the eu market. the entire 'goods package' also aims to create a global framework for streamlining product legislation to make it more uniform and easier to understand for both economic operators and market surveillance authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of simple pressure vessels (reform). this directive concerns simple pressure vessels which are new on the union market when they are placed on the market; this means that they are either new simple pressure vessels manufactured by a manufacturer established in the union or simple pressure vessels, new or second-hand, imported from a third country. member states should ensure, within their territory, the protection of the health and safety of persons and the protection of domestic animals and property against the risks arising from leakage from simple pressure vessels or from their explosion. all economic operators involved in the supply and distribution chain should take appropriate measures to ensure that they make available on the market only simple pressure vessels which comply with this directive. the manufacturer, being the person with the most detailed knowledge of the design and production process, is best placed to carry out the conformity assessment procedure for simple pressure vessels. conformity assessment should therefore remain the sole responsibility of the manufacturer.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because a new regulatory framework was needed to address the shortcomings in the current eu legislation. in this respect, the whole harmonisation package will help to complete the single market, while ensuring both fair competition and, above all, the safety of the products available on the market. i believe that conformity assessment procedures for products are very important and that market surveillance should focus on ensuring the highest level of safety for consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of measuring instruments (reform). measuring instruments that provide accurate and traceable measurements can be used for various measurement operations. measurement operations that meet considerations of public interest, public health, public order and safety, environmental and consumer protection, the collection of taxes and duties and the fairness of commercial transactions, which directly and indirectly affect the daily lives of citizens in many ways, may require the use of legally verified measurement instruments. the statutory metrological control requires compliance with the specified performance requirements. i consider that the performance requirements to be met by measuring instruments should guarantee a high level of protection. conformity assessment shall provide a high level of confidence. member states should, as a general rule, impose legal metrological control. if metrological control is required by law, only measuring instruments which comply with the common performance requirements shall be used. the legal metrological control should not raise barriers to the free movement of measuring instruments. the provisions applicable should be the same in all member states and the proof of conformity should be accepted throughout the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and i would like to welcome this initiative to strengthen and improve passenger rights. we are talking about an industry that generates huge profits at european level and at the same time is at the forefront of complaints by european consumers. for example, most of the complaints registered by the european consumer centre in romania in 2012 concerned the lack of assistance or the refusal to grant compensation for delayed or cancelled flights and for lost or damaged baggage. i was also put in the position of waiting for hours in line for boarding, without receiving a bottle of water or information regarding the possibility of receiving compensation for these incidents. consumer protection must be put above the financial interests of this industry! that is why i support the amendments to the regulation.
in writing. - since the entry into force of this regulation, problems have been identified with regard to a number of different interpretations due to the gaps in the regulation, the uneven application in the member states and the difficulties of passengers in exercising their rights when air carriers breach the legislation. it is important to encourage airlines to think about ways to improve the services they offer and their overall approach. the report comes with a number of measures to support air passengers: the role of national enforcement bodies is better defined and extended to baggage claims. a complaints procedure has been introduced, with clear deadlines and a precisely defined role for a new body to be set up with the task of resolving complaints. new provisions have been introduced regarding denied boarding, missed connecting flights and prolonged delays. a non-exhaustive list of exceptional circumstances has been established to clarify the cases in which air carriers are exempted from compensation. the obligation for air carriers to inform passengers adequately and in a timely manner has been strengthened. new provisions have been introduced on the transport of mobility equipment and musical instruments.
in writing. - the free movement of people at european level has led to a steady increase in air travel and, by implication, in the number of companies offering such services, as well as the emergence of new routes and connections between different cities and regions in europe and other countries outside the eu. in this context, i support the rapporteur's proposal on the need to provide specific protection for passengers in the event of a flight being cancelled due to the insolvency of an air carrier or the suspension of an air carrier's activity following the withdrawal of its operating licence, with reimbursement of expenses or repatriation, as the case may be. on the other hand, better cooperation between airports, air operators, ground handling companies and air traffic control services is needed to minimise the impact of multiple flight disruptions on passengers, by providing assistance services and by re-routing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i support the harmonisation of certain aspects of insolvency law. in order to ensure greater legal certainty for both companies and authorities, there needs to be predictability in the field. in the context of the economic crisis, insolvency proceedings have increased and often have a cross-border component. i also considered it necessary to align the current legislation with the case law of the european court of justice.
in writing. - the european parliament in this report supports some essential points on insolvency proceedings in the context of eu company law. in particular, the european parliament had already pointed out the existence of certain areas of insolvency law where harmonisation was useful and feasible. the report proposes a specific solution to deal with insolvency situations involving groups of companies. it is proposed to appoint a coordinator with the task of presenting a group coordination plan identifying a set of measures for the resolution of the situation of the group companies. it is important to emphasize that this plan must be followed after approval by a judge.
in writing. - in times of financial crisis and budgetary constraints, it is important to support insolvent debtors and prevent them from going bankrupt. at union level, corporate insolvency increased from around 130 910 cases in 2007 to 174 917 cases in 2011. a significant increase (6.1%) was recorded in central and eastern europe. it is regrettable that insolvency laws still vary considerably between member states, causing serious problems for businesses operating across borders. the provisions of the current european regulation on insolvency proceedings are interpreted and applied differently across the union. legislative harmonisation and appropriate solutions are needed to be applied in all member states. i support the amendments proposed by the commission and their implementation as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted for the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation no 1346/2000 on insolvency proceedings, adopting the position of the european parliament at first reading. they argue that the scope of this regulation should be extended to procedures that promote the rescue of a debtor in serious financial difficulties in order to help sound businesses survive and to give entrepreneurs a new chance. the scope should, in particular, also include procedures which provide for the restructuring of a debtor in a pre-insolvency stage or which maintain the existing management team, as well as those discharge procedures concerning consumers and self-employed persons. since such procedures do not necessarily involve the appointment of a representative in insolvency proceedings, they should be covered by this regulation where they take place under the control or supervision of a court. the insolvency regulation establishes a european framework for cross-border insolvency proceedings. the regulation applies where the debtor, whether a natural or legal person, has assets or creditors in more than one member state. the regulation determines the court with jurisdiction to open insolvency proceedings.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption in plenary of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 on insolvency proceedings; i also welcome the fact that, in a relatively short time, the commission has responded, in practice, by this initiative to the request of the european parliament made in 2011 in its own-initiative report containing recommendations to the commission on insolvency proceedings in the context of eu company law. cross-border insolvency proceedings are no longer an exception but a current phenomenon, affecting not only large undertakings/groups of undertakings but also smes. the arguments in favour of the reform process are many, including the need to modernise eu insolvency law to shift the focus from simply winding up a company to giving companies in difficulty a second chance. i voted for this report because it supports the harmonisation of 'insolvency law' in the eu, which is fully achievable at the moment.

in writing. - the aviation industry has undergone significant changes in recent years, associated with an increase in passenger numbers and flights on the liberalised european market. this generally positive development was accompanied to some extent by a number of unfair practices and a reduction in the quality of services, with negative consequences for travellers. in addition, since the entry into force of the regulation in 2004, problems have been identified with regard to a number of different interpretations, due to the grey areas and gaps in the current regulation, the uneven application in the member states and the difficulties of passengers in exercising their rights when air carriers breach the legislation. the incomplete and inconsistent implementation of the existing regulation by air carriers and national authorities is creating confusion for both passengers and the industry. in addition, passengers are not yet fully informed about their rights and are dissatisfied with the conditions and costs associated with their realisation.
in writing. - with the evolution of the aviation sector, which has allowed us to move faster within the european territory and beyond, there has also been a tendency towards unfair practices and a reduction in the quality of the services offered. this has had a negative impact on passengers over the years. for these reasons, we felt it was appropriate to work towards improving the existing framework of rights for passengers and we have approved this report, which increases the rights available to passengers in the event of non-performance or unfair practices.
in writing. - in recent years there has been an increase in the number of passengers and the number of flights in europe. this is beneficial for the union economy, facilitating free movement and reducing fragmentation of the single market. at the same time, this development of the aviation industry raises new problems at european level, in particular with regard to consumer protection. with the increase in the number of passengers, the quality of services decreases, if there is no good regulation in this regard. i support this report because there is a need for comprehensive legislation in this area to reduce confusion among passengers about their rights and among airlines about their obligations. many passengers refuse to go to court because of the high costs they have to bear in dealing with large international companies. this is exploited by airlines and results in the violation of fundamental rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 261/2004 laying down common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights and regulation (ec) no 2027/97 on air carrier liability for the carriage of passengers and their baggage by air. air transport services are paid for in advance by passengers and therefore air tickets should be considered as 'contracts with result', with airlines guaranteeing the fulfilment of contractual obligations with due diligence. i welcome the improvements brought about by the new regulation, in particular in terms of passenger information, baggage, cancellation or delay of a flight, and in the event of insolvency or bankruptcy of an air carrier. thus, in the event of a passenger cancelling the flight, air carriers should be obliged to reimburse, free of charge, the fees already paid by the passenger. financial protection of passengers in the event of the bankruptcy of the airline is an essential component of an effective system of passenger rights. in order to strengthen the protection of airline passengers in the event of flight cancellations due to the insolvency of an air carrier, air carriers should be required to provide sufficient evidence to guarantee the reimbursement or repatriation of money to passengers.
in writing. - i voted against the report because the transition to a low-carbon economy must be gradual and without shocks to the economies of the member states, especially in the context of the crisis. it is clear that in the long term the union will have to move to a low carbon economy, but not at any cost and at the expense of economic recovery in europe. whether we are talking about nuclear energy, unconventional hydrocarbons or wind and solar energy, we must find a balanced energy mix that allows the development of states with the least possible impact on the environment. for example, romania has made efforts in recent years to diversify its energy supply sources, moving towards both conventional and unconventional and renewable sources.
in writing. - the 2030 framework for climate and energy policies must pay particular attention to the objectives of progress towards a competitive economy that uses fewer resources and can create new opportunities for quality jobs. measures are needed to anticipate and meet the skills needs for newly created jobs, to make changes in education and training systems and to meet new challenges in existing jobs that are becoming greener. active labour market policies should have clear objectives, respond to the needs of workers and the labour market, and avoid a shortage of skilled labour in new sustainable technologies and ensure access to quality jobs in the green economy for young people, women and disadvantaged groups. research on more sustainable resource extraction and innovative technologies should be encouraged to better protect the environment and improve working conditions for workers in the sector. the commission and the member states should promote more sustainable solutions for resource extraction.
in writing. - because energy efficiency is not yet a genuine global policy priority, studies suggest that we risk two thirds of the world's energy potential being untapped by 2035, with population and economic growth driving demand for energy to rise by more than 40% by 2030. already 95% of global warming is due to human activities, and climate change is increasing from year to year. european investments in energy efficiency, renewable energy and smart infrastructure would stimulate the fight against the negative effects of global warming and help reverse the upward trend in energy prices. that is why i support this report, which sets out an ambitious framework for action from significantly reducing energy consumption to completing the internal energy market. this is a key condition for the eu's overall energy security, based on sustainable and renewable energy sources within the eu, as europe is a continent limited in resources and dependent on imports, which account for 60% of natural gas, 80% of oil and 50% of coal used for energy production at eu level.
in writing. - i abstained on the vote on amendment 27. i believe that the european union and, by implication, romania need a greater degree of energy independence and responsible exploitation of available resources. at the same time, the views of local communities must be taken into account at all times when the exploitation of these resources is being considered, especially when the safety assurance is not fully convincing. we want cheap energy, but safety has to come first. another reason for abstaining was that the european parliament cannot impose its views on local authorities, as this would violate both the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of local administrative autonomy. i also abstained in the final vote because the report contains many important provisions but also some that are at least questionable.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on a 2030 framework for climate and energy policies. increasing energy efficiency should be considered as one of the main components of the eu's climate and energy policy. energy efficiency contributes to conserving resources, reducing energy bills, dependence on imported fuels, trade deficits, improving the long-term competitiveness of the eu economy, and facilitating the reduction of eu greenhouse gas emissions. we call on member states to swiftly implement the energy efficiency directive and the energy performance of buildings directive. the potential of each economic sector and each economic situation must be taken into account when designing new energy efficiency policies. we call on the commission and the member states to set a binding eu target for 2030 of reducing domestic greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% compared to 1990 levels. measures to improve energy efficiency should focus on the energy supply and demand side as a whole, including transformation, transmission, distribution and supply, as well as on industrial consumption, consumption in buildings, including consumption by households, and transport.
in writing. - i believe that better integration of the internal market for banking services is essential to stimulate economic recovery in the union. the current financial and economic crisis has demonstrated that the functioning of the internal market in this area is in jeopardy. the main reason for the eu-wide responsibility and procedures is that, within the banking union, banking supervision through a single system, which will be the responsibility of the ecb, and bank resolution must be exercised by authorities at the same level. the establishment of a single resolution mechanism is therefore welcome as it will generate a single set of rules applicable to all failing banks in the participating member states and ensure effective procedures for the sound management of bank failures, minimising the cost to taxpayers and the economy.
in writing. - i voted for the amendments adopted by the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation laying down uniform rules and a uniform procedure for the resolution of credit institutions and certain investment firms in the framework of a single resolution mechanism and a single bank resolution fund and amending regulation (eu) no 1093/2010. the proposal for a regulation establishes uniform rules and a uniform procedure for the resolution of the following entities which are established by the participating member states: (a) credit institutions established in the participating member states; (b) parent undertakings established in one of the participating member states, including financial holding companies and mixed financial holding companies, where they are subject to consolidated supervision by the ecb in accordance with article 4 (1) (i) of regulation (eu) no 1024/2013; (c) investment firms and financial institutions established in the participating member states where they are subject to consolidated supervision by the ecb of the parent undertaking in accordance with article 4 (1) (i) of regulation (eu) no 1024/2013. a participating member state is a member state whose currency is the euro or a member state whose currency is not the euro but which has established close cooperation in accordance with article 7 of regulation (eu) no 1024/2013.

in writing. - i voted for the european parliament resolution on the situation in ukraine. demonstrations sparked more than two weeks ago by president yanukovych's decision not to sign the association agreement with the eu are still ongoing in the capital, and the discontent is spreading to other cities, including regions in eastern ukraine. we call for a political solution to the crisis and insist on a democratic debate on the ways and means to overcome the spirit of confrontation and division that ukraine is facing. we call on president yanukovych to put an end to the reprehensible mobilisation of berkut specialised riot police and other security forces, which provoked, kidnapped, harassed, tortured, beaten and humiliated the partisans of the euromaidan movement, as well as to arbitrary arrests and excessive prolonged pre-trial detentions. we call on the eu, the us, the imf, the world bank, the ebrd and the eib to continue preparations for a long-term financial support package to assist ukraine in its efforts to cope with the worsening financial and social situation and to provide economic support to support the government's initiation of the comprehensive reforms needed by the ukrainian economy.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the situation in syria. since the beginning of the violent crackdown on peaceful protesters in syria, more than 130 000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed. according to the un office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs, over 9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in syria, of which over 6.5 million are internally displaced, with over 2.3 million syrian refugees, mainly in turkey, jordan, lebanon, egypt and iraq. more than half of those affected are children, who suffer from hunger, malnutrition and disease. the lack of access to food, water, basic healthcare, sanitation, shelter and education is a critical dimension of this humanitarian catastrophe, and the delivery of humanitarian aid is hampered by lack of security, denial of access by the syrian authorities and obstacles posed by infrastructure. we condemn the assad regime's frequent violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, including acts of violence, systematic torture and executions of prisoners. we believe that the political solution should guarantee the unity, territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence of syria. we support the geneva ii conference on syria, which should be the first step towards a process leading to a political and democratic settlement of the conflict, and we stress the importance of continuing the geneva ii process.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 6 february 2014 on the commission communication entitled 'elimination of female genital mutilation (fgm) '. sadly, according to who, an estimated 140 million children, girls and women, have been subjected to this crude form of gender-based violence globally. this cruel practice has been reported in 28 african countries, yemen, northern iraq and indonesia. we reiterate the call on the commission to present an eu legislative proposal establishing prevention measures against all forms of violence against women and, as indicated in the stockholm programme, a comprehensive eu strategy on this issue, including further structured joint action plans to end genital mutilation in the eu. we reiterate the call on member states to use existing mechanisms, in particular directive 2012/29/eu, including training of those working in the field of the protection of women and girls, and to prosecute and punish any resident who has committed the crime of fgm, even if the crime was committed outside the borders of the member state concerned. we demand that the principle of extraterritoriality be included in the criminal law of all member states so that the offence can be punished equally in all member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because inland waterway transport is not yet exploited to its full potential in the union. this is because, unfortunately, waterways are not always of the highest standard. whether it is transportation blockages or other infrastructure problems, there are still shortcomings. therefore, member states, with the financial support of the commission, must make every effort to revive inland waterway transport. i give you the example of the danube-main-rhine canal which, although it could become the main freight transportation axis between east and west europe, is not used to its full capacity. only in recent years, after the adoption of the danube strategy, have some countries such as romania or serbia made joint efforts to streamline navigation on the danube.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the naiades ii programme an action programme on inland waterway transport. the inland waterway transport sector makes a significant contribution to the eu transport system by transporting goods between ports and the hinterland. we welcome the commission's initiative to update and renew the naiades programme by 2020 and support the specific actions defined in the naiades ii action programme for 2014-2020. i stress the importance of ensuring adequate funding for new technologies, innovation and sustainable transport services within existing eu programmes such as the connecting europe facility, horizon 2020 and the cohesion fund to stimulate the use of innovation outputs and improve the environmental performance of inland waterway transport, and i ask the commission to develop concrete funding programmes to achieve this. we call on the commission to submit proposals on the mobilisation of the reserve funds, using them together with the financial instruments available under the existing union funds. we also invite member states to continue to develop national strategies to stimulate inland waterway transport, taking into account the european action programme, and to encourage regional and local port authorities to do the same.
the author. - mr president, commissioner füle, as the author and initiator of these resolutions, i thank my colleagues from all the political groups for understanding the gravity of the situation in the transnistrian region and for supporting me and cristi preda in putting this subject on the plenary agenda. the regime's provocations in tiraspol culminated yesterday with the detention and humiliation of the headmaster of the lyceum lucian blaga, two employees and six peacekeepers. these tensions are also fuelled by the presence of russian troops in the region, which is why i have called for an amendment to replace them with a civilian peacekeeping mission. at the same time, i believe that the much-lauded 5+2 has shown its limits and inefficiency and needs to be reconsidered. the union must become a full member on an equal footing with russia and be much more vocal in resolving the transnistrian conflict. finally, i call on pro-european prime minister leancă to support the right to education in romanian more firmly.
the question is "blue cardboard". mrs vergiat, i would like to know what you consider an emergency: if arresting a school principal simply because he wants classes to be taught in romanian is not an emergency, what is an emergency for you?
the european union has already taken action to ensure that the rights of the child are respected and that the rights of the child are protected. outward discrimination takes on increasingly threatening forms. the accounts of romanian schools have been blocked and the headmaster of the lucian blaga high school in tiraspol was arrested yesterday. the reason? he brought from the ministry of education in chisinau the salaries of his colleagues in the official currency of the republic of moldova, which was considered a crime, and the salaries were confiscated as undeclared foreign currency. it is unacceptable that the right to education is used as a tool of negotiation and pressure in the geopolitical games of the self-proclaimed authorities of the transnistrian region. the residents of this region, who are citizens of the republic of moldova, want their rights to be respected, including the right to education in the only official language of the moldovan state, the romanian language. the political situation in the area, as complicated as it is, should not affect children, parents, teachers and schools. education must be depoliticized and harassment of any kind against romanian-language educational institutions must stop. i think it's our duty to make sure that the messages we send out don't go unanswered. i think it is necessary for a delegation of the european parliament to go to transnistria to ensure that the exercise of the fundamental right to education returns to normal. i am convinced that the visa liberalisation with the republic of moldova will also have a positive impact in the field of education. that is why i hope for a favourable vote in the coming weeks in the libe committee and in the plenary and i hope that this visa liberalisation will materialize by the end of this mandate of the european parliament.

the agreement amending regulation 443 of 2009 sets the target of 95 grams of carbon dioxide per km as from 2020 as the average of the emissions for the fleet of new passenger cars registered in the european union. increasing the efficiency and sustainability of new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles will reduce the union's dependence on oil imports. the beneficiaries of the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions from cars will be both consumers and the environment. it is important not only to reduce fuel consumption but at the same time to maintain the competitive advantage of the european automotive industry on the global market. however, the lack of an alternative fuels infrastructure and of common technical specifications for the vehicle-infrastructure interface could be an obstacle to the marketing of very low carbon vehicles. therefore, it is also important to provide the necessary infrastructure that would facilitate access to energy efficient vehicles. in conclusion, it is important to give the car industry the time it needs to adapt its production lines - we know that it takes seven years from the time of design to the time of market entry for such a vehicle.
in writing. – legislation has driven fuel efficiency and genuine co2 reductions since 2009. the negotiations on this file have been difficult and i congratulate my colleagues on the final outcome which, although not as ambitious as we might have hoped, will ensure that passenger cars continue to become more and more fuel efficient in the coming years. this will mean lower fuel costs for drivers, less localised atmospheric pollution, and lower greenhouse gas emissions. i particularly welcome the provision to revise and update the test methods to ensure a more accurate measurement of co2 emissions from cars and to prevent manipulation of emission readings.

rapporteur. - madam president, i would like to start by saying ‘mission fulfilled’. raportoare. - obiectiv îndeplinit. acum dezbatem și mâine votăm directiva privind punerea sub sechestru și confiscarea banilor și a bunurilor provenite din infracțiuni. confiscarea banilor infractorilor se va face mai ușor și mai repede și toți vom avea de câștigat. în primul rând, vor câștiga cetățenii pentru că, în bugetele publice, vor fi mai mulți bani pentru școli, spitale sau pensii. vor câștiga bugetele naționale și bugetul uniunii, pentru că acestea vor crește. numai în 2009, traficul de droguri, contrafacerea, traficul de ființe umane și de arme mici au produs 2,1 trilioane de dolari și numai 1% din aceste venituri uriașe sunt puse sub sechestru sau confiscate. aceasta înseamnă nimic. banii rămân la infractori și noi pierdem. confiscarea nu este folosită în toate statele membre, iar legile la nivel național sunt inegale, consecința este dezastruoasă: lăsăm miliarde de euro pe an să fie spălați și băgați în economia ilicită sau subterană, sau în rețele criminale. negocierile au fost dure, dar avem astăzi o directivă nouă, prin care introducem norme minime la nivelul uniunii și introducem noi modalități de confiscare. de exmplu, se vor putea confisca bani și bunuri chiar dacă inculpatul este bolnav sau a plecat din țară și procesul penal nu se finalizează printr-o condamnare. un pilon important al directivei este confiscarea extinsă a veniturilor care nu se pot justifica legal. de exemplu, dacă ești condamnat pentru o sumă mică de trafic de droguri - 1000 de euro - judecătorul îți evaluează toată averea și, dacă nu o poți justifica, ți-o confiscă, prezumând că provine tot din trafic de droguri. în calitate de raportor am urmărit cu prioritate să aplicăm confiscarea extinsă în cât mai multe cazuri. astfel, ea, potrivit directivei, se va aplica în cazurile de: 1) corupție activă și pasivă în sectorul public și privat, plus corupție în cazul oficialilor europeni; 2) participarea la rețele de crimă organizată; 3) pornografie infantilă; 4) criminalitate informatică și 5) orice infracțiune pedepsită de lege cu cel puțin patru ani închisoare. un alt pilon important al acestei directive este confiscarea de la terți. grupurile de criminalitate organizată transferă bunuri și bani către terțe persoane în scopul de a evita confiscarea. de exemplu: o persoană acumulează venituri prin infracțiuni, apoi vinde sau face cadou sau pune pe numele altora aceste venituri. în aceste situații confiscarea se va putea face dacă bunul se vinde sub prețul pieței sau se donează sau există indicii că nu a fost o tranzacție reală. în plus, am reușit să introducem în directivă noțiunea de reutilizare socială a bunurilor confiscate. aceasta înseamnă că proprietățile confiscate vor putea fi folosite în interesul comunităților afectate sau în scopuri sociale sau, ca în italia sau marea britanie, pentru cumpărarea de mașini sau alte echipamente necesare în lupta împotriva marii criminalități. această directivă trebuie însă urmată de un pas și mai curajos: într-o declarație comună, inclusă în directivă, parlamentul și consiliul cer comisiei să studieze posibilitatea introducerii procedurii de confiscare, în lipsa unei condamnări penale, chiar prin proceduri civile. confiscarea civilă a dat rezultate foarte bune în statele uniunii în care se aplică. de exemplu, în marea britanie, hotărârile civile de confiscare au vizat numai într-un an de zile, 2011 -2012, 11 milioane de lire sterline. sau: în aprilie 2013, bunuri în valoare de 1,2 miliarde de euro au fost confiscate de la un om de afaceri italian cu legături mafiote - între aceste bunuri: 43 de companii, 98 de proprietăți, 66 de conturi bancare și altele. deci, numai dacă luăm averile infractorilor vom putea îndrăzni a crede că reducem marea criminalitate. trimiterea unor oameni la închisoare, dar lăsarea banilor murdari în circulație, nu mai poate fi tolerată. de aceea, trebuie să facem și pasul confiscării prin proceduri civile. aș vrea să mulțumesc, înainte de a termina, comisiei, celor două președinții sub care am negociat, cea irlandeză și cea lituaniană, celorlalți raportori din grupurile politice, în special ritei și soniei.
