in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on certain provisions relating to financial management for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability. ensuring the sound implementation of the european fisheries fund programmes is of particular importance for investments in the fisheries sector. the implementation of programmes is often difficult because of the liquidity problems generated by budgetary consolidation. this is the case for member states that have received financial assistance under an adjustment programme. to date, seven countries have received financial assistance and agreed a macroeconomic adjustment programme with the commission - cyprus, hungary, romania, latvia, portugal, greece and ireland. to ensure that these member states (and any other member state that may benefit from such assistance programmes in the future) continue to implement fisheries policy programmes on the ground and continue to allocate funds to projects, this proposal contains provisions that will allow the commission to make higher payments to these countries during the period in which they benefit from the support mechanisms, without changing the total funds allocated to them under the fisheries policy for the period 2007-2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the commission's proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1198/2006 to support member states currently receiving financial aid and those that could benefit from adjustment programmes so that they can continue to have financial resources to implement their sectoral fisheries policy projects. i welcome this aid, especially in the case of cyprus, greece, ireland and portugal, which are still subject to severe budgetary constraints that create liquidity problems due to the need for budgetary consolidation and complicate the implementation of operational programmes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the regulatory procedure with scrutiny needed to be adapted to article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and to other relevant legislation. while not amending essential aspects of the legislation, delegated or implementing acts play a particularly important role in ensuring the effective application of legislative instruments by providing legal consistency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation adapting articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to a series of legal acts providing for the use of the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. the treaty of lisbon introduced a distinction between the powers delegated to the commission to adopt non-legislative acts of general application, supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of a legislative act (delegated acts), and the powers conferred on the commission to adopt uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding union acts (implementing acts). where implementing powers are conferred on the commission, those powers should be exercised in accordance with regulation (eu) no 182/2011. i support amendment 1 which confers the power to adopt delegated acts on the commission for a period of five years from the date of entry into force of this regulation. the commission shall submit a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. the delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the european parliament or the council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the commission's proposal is designed to simplify the application of certain legislative acts by means of the delegated or implementing acts procedure. as a large part of the community acquis consists of legislative acts adopted before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the legal consistency of the regulatory procedures with scrutiny with the provisions of the treaty was absolutely necessary to ensure the consistent implementation of those acts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation adapting to article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union a series of legal acts in the field of justice providing for the use of the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. this proposal concerns aligning five legislative acts in the field of justice which still contain references to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. those instruments need to be aligned by a separate proposal, as they were adopted on the basis of a legal basis falling within title v of part three of the tfeu and are therefore not binding on all member states and are thus incompatible with the legal bases of the other basic acts. the five legislative acts are: regulation no 1206/2001 on cooperation between the courts of the member states in the taking of evidence in civil or commercial matters; regulation no 805/2004 on the creation of a european enforcement order for uncontested claims; regulation 1896/2006 establishing a european order for payment procedure; regulation no 861/2007 establishing a european procedure with regard to small claims; regulation no 1393/2007 on the service in the member states of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters (service of documents) and repealing regulation no 1348/2000.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and i support greater transparency with regard to delegated or implementing acts adopted by the commission. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council. last but not least, in order to ensure democratic control of the way the commission exercises its powers, i have argued that the period during which it has the power to adopt delegated acts should be limited and renewed on the basis of a report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation adapting to article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union a series of legal acts providing for the use of the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, significantly modifies the framework of the powers conferred on the commission by the legislator. the treaty makes a clear distinction between, on the one hand, the powers delegated to the commission to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope which supplement or amend certain non-essential elements of a legislative act (delegated acts) and, on the other hand, the powers conferred on the commission to adopt implementing acts. i support amendment 1 which empowers the commission to adopt delegated acts for a period of five years from the date of entry into force of this regulation. the commission shall submit a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. the delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the european parliament or the council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the nomination of mr oskar herics as a member of the court of auditors because his professional experience to date recommends him as an excellent candidate for this post. legal studies, followed by extensive practice in public finance and audit, are evidence of high professional qualifications in the field. in addition, the candidate shall demonstrate a guarantee of independence - a fundamental requirement in the exercise of his future duties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on the proposal to appoint oskar herics as a member of the court of auditors, which gives a favourable opinion on the council's proposal to appoint oskar herics as a member of the court of auditors. the european parliament's committee on budgetary control assessed the qualifications of the proposed candidate, taking into account in particular the conditions laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the candidate nominated by the council to be a member of the court of auditors was also heard by the committee on budgetary control at its meeting on 17 february 2014. following these hearings, the committee on budgetary control delivered a favourable opinion.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that this procedural change to the parliament's rules of procedure is likely to increase the transparency of our work. there are certain perfectly justified situations which do not allow a member to be present in plenary sessions. in this context, it seemed to me normal that if a member was on maternity or paternity leave, his absence from plenary sessions would be 'motivated'.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament decision amending rule 136 of the rules of procedure on participation in meetings. i voted for amendment no 1 which amends rule 136 (2) of the rules of procedure. the names of members whose attendance is attested by the attendance sheet are entered in the minutes of each sitting, together with the mention present. the names of members whose absence is approved by the president shall be entered in the minutes of each sitting, together with the words 'absence with reasons'. at present, the concept of maternity or paternity leave does not exist in the legal provisions governing parliamentary mandate. but this is a valid reason for absence from official meetings. article 136 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament governs the list of attendance. in its current version, the distinction is made only between members present at a meeting. the article does not provide for justified absences. the amendment suggests that the minutes of each sitting should include the names of members whose absence has been approved by the president. the sole purpose of this amendment is to reduce the negative impact on the attendance list of members and on the 'parliamentary activity indicators'. this measure has no financial implications.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the new regulations which aim to reduce co2 emissions from new cars to 95g/km. i welcome the gradual introduction of the mandatory 95g/km target to 95% of new cars and to a single year: 2020. i believe that these new provisions will encourage the certification and introduction of technologies or technology packages (green innovations) that further reduce the associated co2 emissions, the 95g target representing a saving of 15 million tonnes of co2 emissions per year, and that also contribute to reducing fuel consumption, for the benefit of the consumer. i am convinced that improving the efficiency of cars means a more efficient use of resources in europe, and therefore a step towards sustainable growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because road transport is a sector in which greenhouse gas emissions are increasing rapidly. therefore, coordinated, long-term action is needed to achieve the 2050 targets. the union has a duty to strengthen and maintain its international leadership in the fight against climate change. however, too frequent changes in the targets create uncertainty for the automotive industry and affect global competitiveness. i believe that long-term strategies are needed to stimulate investment in this area and that this regulation should also set targets for 2025 as the industry can benefit from this political signal. only through legal certainty can we promote green growth and jobs, improving the competitiveness of the union's automotive industry.
in writing. - improving the efficiency of cars is part of the europe 2020 resource efficiency agenda, which will ensure the shift to a resource-efficient and low-carbon economy for sustainable growth. in addition, by improving the efficiency and sustainability of new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles, the union's dependence on oil will be reduced. the production of more fuel-efficient vehicles in the eu will create new jobs, particularly in the chemical and electronics industries, as well as in high-technology in europe. i believe that member states, the commission and regional and local authorities should make efforts to identify and disseminate best practices for stimulating demand for ultra-low emission vehicles, so that the strong sales growth in some european countries is taken up in all member states.
in writing. - i voted for the proposal for a regulation on the reduction of co2 emissions from new cars. the further development of the global market for advanced technologies aimed at improving the efficiency of passenger cars is in line with the commission communication of 21 january 2011 entitled 'a resource efficient europe - the flagship initiative of the europe 2020 strategy'. it supports the shift towards a resource-efficient and low-carbon economy with a view to achieving sustainable growth. from 2020, this regulation sets a target of 95g co2/km as the average of the emissions for the new passenger car fleet registered in the union. it is important that this regulation is as neutral as possible from a competitive point of view, socially fair and sustainable. by 31 december 2015, the commission shall review the specific emissions targets and modalities set, as well as other aspects of this regulation, including whether the utility parameter is still necessary and whether the most reliable utility parameter is mass or footprint, with a view to setting the co2 emissions targets for new passenger cars for the period after 2020.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i too support amending the current regulation to give greater coherence to the concept of the european trade mark. the enhanced role of the office for harmonisation in the internal market will provide greater legal certainty for holders of intellectual property rights. the existence of the european trade mark guarantees the protection of inventions throughout the union, which is why it is important that ohim has enhanced powers of verification and authorisation. this can encourage innovation and research, which are essential conditions for economic recovery in europe. i emphasise the importance of innovation and research because in recent years the union has lost ground compared to, for example, the united states. if we do not invest massively in these areas and ensure that inventions are properly protected, the exodus of researchers to other regions will continue.
in writing. - in the european union, a trademark can be registered either at national level, at the industrial property office of a member state, or at eu level, as a community trademark. the regulation also created the office for harmonisation in the internal market (ohim) to ensure the registration and administration of community trade marks. this acquis on trade marks has not been substantially amended, while the business environment has evolved significantly. the main objective of the proposal is to harmonise the trademark registration systems in all eu member states and to ensure consistency and complementarity between the european trademark system and national systems, to make them more efficient for businesses by reducing costs and complexity. i believe that this could result in a substantial increase in innovation and economic growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 207/2009 on the community trade mark. the purpose of the mark is to distinguish the goods and services of an undertaking. all signs, in particular words, including names of persons, designs, letters, figures, colours as such, the shape of the product or its packaging or sounds, may constitute european union trade marks provided that such signs use generally available technology and are capable of: distinguishing the goods or services of one undertaking from those of others; and are represented in the register of european union trade marks in a manner which enables the competent authorities and the public to determine with clarity and precision the subject-matter of the protection conferred on the proprietor. the proposal for a revision of the community trade mark regulation has the following main objectives: to adapt the terminology to the treaty of lisbon and the provisions to the common approach on agencies; to simplify the procedures for applying for and registering a european trade mark; to increase legal certainty by clarifying the provisions and removing ambiguities; to establish an appropriate framework for cooperation between the office for harmonisation in the internal market (ohim) and the national offices, with a view to promoting convergence of practices and developing common instruments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because we have too often been confronted, both in romania and in other states, with situations where a person was definitively convicted, but remained with the goods or money obtained illegally. this not only encouraged potential offenders but also diminished citizens' trust in the judiciary. romania already has an extensive asset forfeiture law, as early as 2012, as a result of the efforts of former right-wing governments to fight corruption more effectively. however, the legislation is not properly implemented and confiscation cases are too few. i therefore hope that the current government will transpose the directive in time and promote the strictest possible rules in this area; this, although the last two years of left-wing government do not give me cause to be optimistic in this respect.
in writing. - the proposal for a directive on the freezing and confiscation of proceeds of crime in the eu was adopted by the european commission on 12 march 2012. the draft directive lays down minimum rules for member states on the freezing and confiscation of criminal assets by means of direct seizure, equivalent value seizure, extended seizure, seizure not based on a conviction and confiscation from third parties. the adoption of those minimum rules will strengthen the harmonisation of freezing and confiscation regimes in the member states and thus facilitate mutual trust and effective cross-border cooperation. it will also be a step forward towards strengthening the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders, an important aspect of the fight against serious and organised cross-border crime in the eu. the report envisages strengthening the provisions on confiscation not based on a conviction and extended confiscation to make them more effective, thus helping to prevent the proceeds of crime from being used to commit other crimes or reinvested in lawful activities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which aims to implement rules on the confiscation of the proceeds of crime in the european union. this directive lays down minimum rules for member states concerning the freezing and confiscation of assets of criminal origin by means of direct confiscation, confiscation in value, extended confiscation, confiscation in the absence of a conviction and confiscation of assets of third parties. i supported this text in the plenary vote because the adoption of these minimum rules will make it possible to harmonise the freezing and confiscation regimes in force in the member states, which will strengthen mutual trust and the effectiveness of crossborder cooperation. it is a step towards strengthening the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders, an important aspect of the fight against large scale cross-border organised crime within the union. the provisions on confiscation without conviction and extended confiscation need to be further strengthened to make them more effective and genuinely capable of preventing the proceeds of crime from being used to commit other crimes or reinvested in lawful activities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the freezing and confiscation of the proceeds from crime in the european union. since financial gain is the main motive behind cross-border organised crime, it is necessary that competent authorities have the means to detect, freeze, manage and confiscate the proceeds of crime. the activity of organised criminal groups is not limited by borders, with these groups increasingly acquiring assets in member states other than those in which they are established, as well as in third countries. the adoption of minimum rules will harmonise the freezing and confiscation regimes in the member states and thus facilitate mutual trust and effective cross-border cooperation. in accordance with the position adopted, member states shall take the necessary measures to allow for the confiscation, in whole or in part, of instruments and products or of property the value of which corresponds to such instruments or products, provided that there is a final conviction for an offence, which may also result from proceedings in absentia. member states shall also take the necessary measures to allow for the confiscation of products or other property the value of which corresponds to products which have been transferred, directly or indirectly, by a suspect or accused person to third parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that we must have a uniform application at european level of the system of intellectual property protection. unfortunately, most studies show that in my country, trademark registration is seen as an optional element. moreover, by doing so, entrepreneurs in romania are exposing themselves to risks. among them are counterfeiting and fraud, which lead to financial losses. of course, the authorities are partly to blame. whether it is because they do not explain clearly enough how important it is to register a trademark, or because the costs are simply too high and the procedures too complicated, the result is the same: legal uncertainty and financial loss.
in writing. - this revision of the directive, which harmonises certain aspects of the trade mark legislation of the eu member states, provides an opportunity to learn from the good practices identified and to further strengthen the harmonisation measures adopted by national trade mark offices in respect of substantive law and procedural aspects of trade mark legislation. the eu business community comprises over 20 million businesses with very different needs. the trade mark system should be sufficiently simple and flexible to provide its users with access to protection that meets their needs. some users want to obtain protection in only one member state, while others want to obtain uniform protection in all 28 member states of the union. there are many users who rely on the national system to ensure their protection in different member states. in order to assist those users who rely on the services of several national offices to obtain protection, it is appropriate to harmonise the procedures so that users do not have to use completely different procedural approaches in the different member states where they seek to obtain protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks (reform) adopting the position of the european parliament at first reading. it is essential to ensure that registered trade marks enjoy the same protection in the legal systems of all member states and that trade marks at national level enjoy the same protection as european union trade marks. in line with the extended protection granted to european union trade marks which enjoy a reputation in the union, extended protection at national level should also be granted to all registered trade marks which enjoy a reputation in a given member state. this directive and the parallel proposal to amend the community trade mark regulation are to be considered as one package. they have as their main common objective to stimulate innovation and economic growth by making trade mark registration systems throughout the eu more accessible and efficient for businesses, by reducing costs and complexity and increasing speed, predictability and legal certainty. those adjustments shall be complemented by efforts to ensure the coexistence and complementarity between the union trade mark system and national trade mark systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because europol could play a very important role in coordinating the fight against cross-border crime. i therefore believe that the institution could be strengthened and its powers extended. i welcome the introduction of the possibility for europol to open ex officio investigations when cyberattacks from a third country take place against several countries in the union. coordination in such situations is essential, especially after more and more institutions in some member states, including romania, have been the target of cyber-attacks in recent years. even if these attacks were largely repelled, identifying the perpetrators could be done more quickly and efficiently with the participation of europol.
in writing. - the eu has faced an increase in serious and organised crime and a diversification of its forms. the 2013 europol assessment of the threat posed by serious and organised crime in the eu concludes that 'serious and organised crime is an increasingly dynamic and complex phenomenon and remains a significant threat to the security and prosperity of the eu'. the proposal clearly defines europol's field of action, its functions and how cooperation with the member states should be carried out. the proposal also sets the following objectives: to align europol with the requirements of the lisbon treaty by laying down the legal framework for europol in the regulation and by introducing a mechanism for scrutiny of europol's activities by the european parliament together with national parliaments; to improve europol's governance by increasing its efficiency; to provide europol with a stronger personal data protection architecture by empowering the european data protection supervisor to supervise, in a fully independent manner, europol's processing of personal data and by stepping up the exchange of information.
in writing. - as the eu is facing an increase in organised crime, with a diversification of the forms in which it manifests itself, especially at cross-border level, this requires much closer cooperation between member states in preventing and combating crime. in these circumstances, i support the proposal to redefine the legal framework for the work of the european police office (europol) through a more effective legal instrument, enabling it to have a better capacity to react to crime, which is increasingly globalised and with an increasingly diversified and sophisticated mode of operation, as shown by the increasing share of cybercrime, for example. it is already causing significant damage to the eu economy. i voted in favour of aligning europol with the requirements of the lisbon treaty by laying down europol's legislative framework in the regulation and by introducing a mechanism for monitoring europol's activities by the european parliament together with national parliaments.
in writing. - the increase and diversification of crime at different levels represents a significant threat to the security and prosperity of the union. it is therefore necessary to intensify cooperation between the european police office and the member states, by means of increased information exchange and by using the national units as a contact point for europol. citizens' safety is one of our priorities and the system of information exchange established by the regulation will finally allow us to achieve high levels of data security and protection.
in writing. - it is important that the union has an agency for law enforcement cooperation and training (europol) with a clear scope, well-defined competences and ensuring effective cooperation with the member states. according to a study carried out in 2012 for europol's management board, the number of articles in the international press mentioning europol's work increased from 8 653 in 2008 to 25 854 in 2011. this significant increase demonstrates the importance and growing involvement of this agency in preventing and combating serious crime and terrorism. i support the european commission's proposal to adopt a regulation through the ordinary legislative procedure establishing an effective european police office with its own organisational structure. the fight against crime within the union is a priority and we need to ensure that europol has the funding and tools to fulfil its mission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training (europol) and repealing decisions 2009/371/jha and 2005/681/jha. europol shall support and strengthen the work of the competent authorities of the member states and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime. the list of offences is specified in annex 1 and affects two or more member states, implying a common approach by the member states given the scale, importance and consequences of the offences. article 88 of the treaty provides that europol is to be the subject of a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. it also provides for the establishment of the procedure for scrutiny of europol's activities by the european parliament, to which national parliaments are associated, in accordance with article 12 (c) of the treaty on european union and article 9 of protocol no 1 on the role of national parliaments in the european union. it is therefore necessary to replace decision 2009/371/jha by a regulation laying down rules on parliamentary scrutiny. europol is established to improve mutual cooperation between law enforcement authorities in the european union and to strengthen and support their action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because access to the union for students and researchers from third countries must be facilitated, especially when it comes to the countries of the eastern neighbourhood. there are many reasons. firstly, we offer a chance for young people outside the union to develop academically. secondly, we can take advantage of the best foreign students and place them on the european labour market, and our economies can benefit. in parallel with these measures, we must provide facilities for third-country nationals who wish to study in the union. i give you the example of romania, which awards a number of 5[nbsp ]500 scholarships to students from the republic of moldova, and many of them, generally very well prepared, later decide to stay in my country and thus contribute to the development of the economy.
in writing. - given the current labour market conditions in many member states and the problems of social dumping in the internal market, the objective is twofold: to strengthen labour markets to better match skills and labour market shortages and, respectively, to guarantee equal treatment and non-discrimination for all categories of workers within the eu and in third countries. to ensure this, a minimum level of protection must be guaranteed and, at the same time, the conditions for the entry of skilled labour must be ensured. efforts towards a well-managed and proactive migration policy to attract highly qualified third-country nationals to the eu are fully supported. proposals to make the provisions for paid trainees and au pairs mandatory should be based on a broader regulatory framework, guaranteeing social protection and equal treatment. additional provisions on access to the labour market for family members of eligible persons or other provisions for extending the residence status of researchers after the completion of their activities should take into account the principle of subsidiarity and should be respected, without prejudice to the competence of member states to regulate these matters.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to establish common conditions of entry and residence for third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, paid and unpaid training, voluntary work and au pairs. the aim of this text is to improve the provisions applicable to these groups of third-country nationals and to make the european union more attractive. the union needs to be competitive on the world market and at the same time provide guarantees and ensure equal treatment. the inclusion of new categories of trainees and paid trainees and au pairs is a positive development, such as enhanced access to the labour market for students, the time limits for the authorisation procedure and the possibility to stay and look for a job or to set up a business after finishing research or studies. many studies show that the eu as a whole will need more than 11 million additional immigrants over the period 2010-2020 to cope with its ageing population. this directive should help to combat this worrying phenomenon and improve the eu's dynamism.
in writing. - it is important to promote the union's values and culture among foreign students and intellectuals. according to a european commission press release of march 2013, in 2011, the number of third-country nationals coming to the union to study was: 64 794 in france, 35 037 in spain, 30 260 in italy or 27 568 in germany. these figures demonstrate the attractiveness of obtaining a degree in a member state, but also the need for a rigorous and clear legal framework to regulate the status of this category of students. i support the commission's proposal to allow third-country nationals to remain in the union for a sufficient period after completion of research or studies, to look for a job or to start a business. we need qualified graduates and investment to increase our competitiveness on the world market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, paid and unpaid vocational training, voluntary service and au pair work. i voted for amendment no 46, which states that, outside of their study time and subject to compliance with the rules and conditions applicable to the relevant activity in the host member state, students have the right to be employed and may have the right to engage in an independent economic activity. the host member state may take into account the labour market situation, but not in a systematic way that could lead to the exclusion of students from the labour market. i voted for amendment no 47, which states that, after completion of the research project or studies in the member state, third-country nationals are entitled to stay in the territory of the member state for a period of 18 months to seek employment or to open a business, if the conditions laid down in article 6 (a) and (c) (f) are still met.
in writing. - the european union's continued position as a major player in international relations cannot be achieved without promoting the values and principles on which the union is built. as the european union remains the main provider of humanitarian aid globally, it is appropriate that this dimension of the european union's external policy be doubled by an increase in the importance of volunteering-related activities. i therefore support the report's proposals. the institutional conditions allow for the creation of a european voluntary corps, capable of dealing with both the rigours of humanitarian situations that require the attention of the european union and the need to promote, by example, the principles and values of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because this proposal is one of the missing links in the union's development aid policy. it is known that the union is by far the largest donor of assistance globally. the emergence of a european volunteer corps can increase the effectiveness of the union's humanitarian aid. in addition, we will have the guarantee that our support actually reaches those who need it most. it will also be a win for the union's image, as we will no longer be seen as a distant entity that just sends aid to disadvantaged areas. of course, all these objectives will be achieved if this volunteer corps is well trained and adequately funded.
in writing. - the number of humanitarian crises, both natural and man-made, and their scale and complexity worldwide have increased significantly. therefore, humanitarian actors are increasingly called upon to come up with an effective response. thousands of europeans volunteer abroad to help victims of disasters and crises. there are others who, if they could, would like to get involved. the emergence of this body would fill the gaps in current humanitarian volunteering and would also contribute to raising public awareness and spreading the idea of european citizenship. solidarity is a fundamental value of the union, and volunteering is a concrete and visible expression of that solidarity. the union must ensure adequate humanitarian aid to respond to the increased number and scale of humanitarian crises.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps eu aid volunteers. the adopted regulation establishes a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps as a framework for the joint contributions of european volunteers to support and complement humanitarian aid operations in third countries. it lays down the rules and procedures for the operation of the 'eu aid volunteers' initiative and the rules for the granting of financial assistance. the regulation establishing the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps shall apply to: 1. the selection, training and mobilisation of eu humanitarian volunteers to support and complement humanitarian aid in third countries; 2. actions supporting, promoting and training the mobilisation of eu aid volunteers to support and complement humanitarian aid in third countries; 3. actions inside and outside the union aimed at strengthening the capacity of third country hosting organisations in humanitarian aid. the financial envelope for the implementation of this regulation for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020 shall be eur 147[nbsp ] 936 000 in current prices.
i would like to thank all the colleagues who voted in favour of this report on behalf of the 60 000 beneficiaries of the food aid programme in cluj county, romania, the county i represent in this parliament. this support is essential for millions of families across the european union, to whom we owe protection and solidarity. i would also like to make an appeal to the member states to simplify the granting of such aid so that beneficiaries are not humiliated by complicated procedures and long queues. i also call for accountability in public procurement related to the implementation of the programme. for example, in romania last year, the food aid program was a failure because some auctions were poorly organized, resulting in many families not receiving the food they needed. once again on behalf of those less fortunate than us, thank you!
in writing. - the european union takes responsibility for those who are currently suffering from food and material deprivation, whose numbers have steadily and alarmingly increased amid the worsening effects of the economic crisis. unfortunately, millions of people live in extreme material poverty and are unable to meet their most basic subsistence needs, lacking access to sufficient and quality food. in these circumstances, the ultimate aim of poverty policies and the new fund for european aid to the most deprived is to enable the european union to continue to help and contribute to alleviating the worst forms of poverty and social exclusion. meeting the europe 2020 target of reducing by 2020 by at least 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by these problems is an imperative for the european union and for the member states alike.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and welcome the fact that the fund for european aid to the most deprived will be implemented in 2014-2020. it was clear that this fund was absolutely necessary to achieve the europe 2020 targets, in particular the reduction of the number of people living in poverty. the crisis has affected living standards in the european union, increasing the number of people at risk of poverty. the actions to be supported by the fund should give priority to the provision of food and basic material assistance.
in writing. - a particularly serious form of material deprivation is homelessness. in 2009-2010, there were 4,1 million homeless people in the union. the crisis is leading to an increase in the number of homeless people, and families with children, young people (up to 20% in denmark and 15% in the netherlands) and people from migrant families are increasingly affected. the proposed fund for the period 2014-2020, worth eur 2,5 billion, would establish a new instrument, supporting national food poverty response mechanisms and devoting part of its resources to the provision of material assistance in the form of non-food items to homeless people and/or children, as well as to ancillary measures aimed at the social reintegration of assisted persons. the fund shall target directly the most deprived persons or households in the member states whose assistance needs are identified by the national authorities or partner organisations, or indirectly by providing food and goods to the homeless or children. member states are required to plan and provide assistance in accordance with national systems, and the criteria for allocating assistance will fall under the responsibility of member states or partner organisations.
in writing. - voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the fund for european aid to the most deprived. even if the measures and the budget provided for have a low impact compared to other instruments for combating poverty at european level, in particular the structural and investment funds, i believe that it is useful to continue funding a european fund for the most deprived. all the more so as lifting at least 20 million european citizens out of poverty is one of the clear objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. as regards the extension of the scope and objectives of the fund for european aid to the most deprived, they consider that synergies with the european social fund should also be explored, in particular in terms of combating social exclusion and poverty. in addition, the inclusion of provisions on combating food waste, by implication by encouraging donations, is more than welcome.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the monitoring of the delegation of legislative powers and the control by the member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. the treaty of lisbon introduced the possibility for parliament and the council to delegate some of their powers to the commission in a legislative act. according to the historical case law, the adoption of essential rules in the field in question is reserved to the legislative body, which means that the adoption of rules whose adoption requires political decisions falling within the responsibility of the legislative body cannot be delegated. the power to supplement and amend non-essential elements of a legislative act may be delegated only. we call for the allocation of sufficient staff and technical resources for delegated and implementing acts, inter alia, to ensure an efficient internal flow of information. we recommend that permanent rapporteurs for delegated and implementing acts be appointed in each committee, thus ensuring coherence within the committee concerned and with other committees. we further ask in particular the members of the negotiating teams to pay particular attention to delegated and implementing acts when reporting to the committee responsible after each trilogue.

in writing. the common european sales legislation is in my view a bold step forward towards a more integrated single market. many businesses are currently reluctant to sell products and services in other member states because of the divergent consumer protection laws they have to comply with, incurring significant adaptation costs. consumers are also reluctant, fearing that they will not be as well protected as if they were buying in their country of residence. these problems clearly represent an obstacle to businesses and consumers enjoying the benefits of the single market. it's a bold step because, given the different levels of protection, harmonization is an extremely difficult exercise. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the protection of consumers are respected. still, as an optional instrument, i think it's worth a try. we will then see to what extent consumers and businesses opt for this regime, we will see how it works, and on the basis of experience we will then be able to progressively improve this legislation.

in writing. - the single market is a key driving force behind economic growth. however, to ensure growth and jobs, improving the implementation of existing rules is crucial. that is why we need a course of action to ensure that the rules on the single market work well in practice. the establishment of a coherent and integrated industrial policy is an essential element for the recovery of european economies and the development of a stable way out of the crisis. better protection of citizens' rights, both as workers and consumers, is fundamental to enhancing confidence in the single market and encouraging responsible behaviour. the coordination of single market policies should aim at rediscovering a new model of competitiveness based on knowledge and innovation.
in writing. - as emphasised in several forums and also at a recent european council, the single market continues to be a key driving force for growth and employment. it therefore needs to be governed with a strong sense of purpose and to be able to meet the challenges of a globalised world. the single market must therefore be coordinated in a way that takes account of the priorities proposed by the european parliament, protects consumers and businesses and, more generally, represents a real opportunity for the competitiveness of operators on the market.
in writing. - i support the inclusion of the single market in the 2014 european semester to accelerate the integration of the single market into the european union. this project needs to be prioritised if the union is to benefit from a strongly integrated single market by the end of 2020. by may 2013, an average of 30 commission findings of infringements of union-wide single market laws were awaiting resolution by the court of justice. the average duration of these is approximately 26 months. however, at least 7 of the 28 member states do not yet use other specialised tools for single market legislation such as solvit, the platform established in 2002. i ask the commission to communicate better and more clearly to the member states which are the means of informing and resolving infringements of single market laws, in order to give consumers confidence in the proper functioning of the union's legislative system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the governance of the single market in the context of the european semester 2014. the commission has identified services, financial services, transport, energy and the digital market as key areas for improving the functioning and deepening of the single market. an accessible and efficient european transport structure, an ambitious european industry and the creation of a single energy market that supports the competitiveness of european businesses and guarantees universal access to affordable energy for households and consumers are also vital for the eu's single market. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties. industrial policy should include ensuring the application of single market rules, a comprehensive strategy on the external dimension of the single market, with a particular focus on coherent consumer protection policies and improved access to capital and infrastructure to increase the competitiveness of enterprises and facilitate their access to new markets. we stress that by removing barriers to the free movement of people, goods, services and capital, the single market gives businesses the opportunity to operate on a wider scale, thus strengthening their capacity to innovate, invest, increase productivity and create jobs.
in writing. - the convergence process in the eu has been hit by considerable difficulties due to the economic and financial crisis, which has particularly affected the less-favoured regions of europe. the decline in the process of establishing interregional cohesion is reflected in the widening disparities in indicators such as gdp per capita or the unemployment rate. european citizens and societies need a coherent cohesion policy that addresses, in addition to the absorption of european grants, the efficiency of investments in terms of their capacity to create jobs, to provide assistance to smes and, not least, to support the development of the research and innovation sector. i support this motion for a resolution to increase transparency and to orient cohesion policy towards better defined standards, looking in detail at the results achieved. i support the priority approach to funding lines and public expenditure in the field of education, research and innovation, as well as to combating the effects of unemployment in order to overcome the negative effects of the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which contains a number of important conclusions on cohesion policy in the period 2007-2013 and is also useful given that cohesion policy continues to be the main source of eu public funding in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework. these conclusions are particularly important in a context where the economic, financial and social crisis has severely slowed down the convergence process, thus exacerbating disparities between regions. the evaluations of the report have an important role in future debates in the field and should provide a starting point, based on lessons and past experience, in improving the implementation of the set objectives.
in writing. - cohesion policy is the main source of eu public funding in the context of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, and the new cohesion policy framework places a strong emphasis on the need to concentrate investment at regional and local level on a limited number of areas considered to be the most important, such as job creation, smes, employment (especially among young people), labour mobility, training and education, research and innovation, etc. the commission and the member states need to increase investment in entrepreneurship, start-ups and self-employment as a means of creating more jobs, especially as smes and micro-enterprises account for over two thirds of all private sector jobs in the eu. the commission and the member states should also adopt growth-friendly policies that prioritise spending on education, lifelong learning, research and innovation, as austerity measures are not sufficient to tackle the current economic crisis.

in writing. - cohesion policy is one of the most important instruments contributing significantly to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. cohesion policy funding targets investment at regional level and is implemented through partnerships between authorities, the business community and civil society. cohesion policy is the main source of public investment in many member states, as funding accounts for more than half of total public investment in regions and urban areas. investment needs are different. most of the less developed regions, including those in romania, face problems such as poor or non-existent infrastructure, especially in the field of transport or energy efficiency. i am convinced that involving local and regional authorities in the definition of national development strategies can help to correctly identify specific challenges, reducing administrative burdens. i would point out that the partnership agreements stipulate the involvement of those authorities and consultation with the business community, academia and civil society. increasing investment in the entrepreneurial environment, support for the creation of new businesses and self-employment are vital levers for the development of smes. the importance of this report is particularly high because the improvement in employment and specialised development are measurable results of these investments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 7th and 8th commission interim reports on eu cohesion policy and the 2013 strategic report on the implementation of the 2007-2013 programme. evaluation plays an essential role in policy debate and learning, but while the provision of monitoring data and implementation information improves the quality of the targets set, the uneven quality of progress reports makes it difficult in many cases to provide a complete and accurate picture of progress towards the objectives at regional and local level. the economic, financial and social crisis has halted the convergence process, thus exacerbating disparities between regions and ending a long period in which regional disparities in terms of gdp per capita and unemployment in the eu have declined considerably, affecting primarily the weaker regions of the union. in this context, it is very important that both the commission and the member states increase investment in entrepreneurship, supporting the creation of new businesses and self-employment to create as many jobs as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the 7th and 8th commission interim reports on eu cohesion policy and the 2013 strategic report on the implementation of the 2007-2013 programme. cohesion policy continues to be the main source of public funding for the eu in the context of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework. the new cohesion policy framework underlines the need to concentrate investment at regional and local level on a limited number of areas considered to be the most important, such as job creation, smes, employment (especially among young people), labour mobility, training and education, research and innovation, ict, sustainable transport and congestion reduction, sustainable energy, the environment, promoting the institutional capacity of public authorities and efficient public administration, urban development and cities. we believe that fiscal consolidation policies are insufficient to stimulate growth and promote investments that create quality and sustainable jobs. measures to support the economy and encourage progress are therefore necessary. we call on the commission and the member states to increase investment in entrepreneurship, business start-ups and self-employment as a means of creating more jobs.

in writing. - i voted to change the structure of the report which assesses the european union's finances on the basis of the results of projects undertaken by the european commission at the end of each year of activity. in accordance with article 318 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the european commission is required to present, in addition to the financial report, an evaluation report on the finances, based on the results achieved in projects that are to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the evaluation report has been produced so far for the years 2010 and 2011. however, none of the evaluations shows whether or not funds are invested effectively in projects initiated by the european commission. it considers that a new structure for the preparation of the evaluation report is urgently needed to enhance transparency in the use of eu funds. i ask the european commission to make the necessary changes by the time the next evaluation report is published.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the evaluation of the union's finances on the basis of the results achieved: a new instrument for an improved discharge procedure of the european commission. we consider that, by focusing on the union's finances on the basis of the results achieved, the evaluation report provided for in article 318 tfeu complements the compliance-based approach presented by the court of auditors in chapters 1 to 9 of its annual report and enables parliament to exercise its power of political control over the actions of european public authorities more effectively. we welcome the commission's intention to structure its evaluation report in line with the new performance framework for the next multiannual financial framework and to base its report on this framework. i believe that such a performance framework should include the following three main elements: the achievement of the programme objectives (results), the good management of the programme by the commission and the member states, and how the programme results and good management contribute to the achievement of the main objectives of the union. we ask the commission to submit to the european parliament and the council the evaluation report on the union's finances on the basis of the results obtained, as provided for in the second paragraph of article 318 tfeu, before 30 june of the year following the financial year under evaluation.

in writing. - the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that member states and the union shall take measures to develop a coordinated strategy for employment and, in particular, to promote a trained, skilled and adaptable workforce and labour markets able to respond to economic change. the europe 2020 strategy proposed by the commission enables the union to steer its economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, accompanied by high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion. the strategy has the main role in implementing the employment and labour market objectives of the new strategy. member states should continue to make all efforts to address the following priorities: increasing labour market participation and reducing structural unemployment, developing a skilled workforce that meets labour market needs and promoting quality jobs and lifelong learning, improving the performance of education and training systems at all levels and increasing participation in tertiary education, promoting social inclusion and combating poverty. the employment guidelines adopted in 2010 should be maintained for 2014.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. according to that decision, the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states as defined in the annex to the council decision of 21 october 2010 on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states are maintained for 2014 and are taken into account by the member states in their employment policies. these comprise 4 sections: increasing labour market participation among women and men, reducing structural unemployment and promoting quality jobs; developing a skilled workforce to meet labour market needs and promoting lifelong learning; improving the quality and performance of education and training systems at all levels and increasing participation in tertiary or equivalent education; promoting social inclusion and combating poverty
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the action programme to reduce administrative burdens in the eu must continue. for budgetary reasons, but also to avoid situations where member states apply different treatment to the same intra-community transaction, the harmonisation of current vat legislation and practices must be constantly pursued. in this regard, the european commission's objectives of enhancing the efficiency of vat collection, reducing red tape, and reducing costs for member states' authorities and taxpayers are welcome. last but not least, standard returns can also be a vat control tool available to member states to eliminate vat fraud, especially in cross-border activities.
in writing. - as is well known, the european union's value added tax is a general consumption tax on a broad basis, calculated on the basis of the value added of all commercial activities involving the production, distribution of goods and the provision of services. unfortunately, we are now seeing a deficit in the effectiveness of the vat collection system in the eu, which must therefore be improved by removing bureaucratic obstacles and reducing the costs that they impose both on the administration of the member states and on taxable persons. the proposal adopted today strikes a reasonable balance and proportionality between the need to reduce the burden on business and the need to remove the obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. - i support the introduction of a standard vat return by amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of vat. this change will ease the bureaucracy in the tax collection process and reduce the high level of fraud recorded up to 2011. a study published by the european commission in september 2013 shows that the total amount of vat not collected in the european union amounted to eur 193 million in 2011. for example, italy lost €32 billion, germany €27 billion, and the united kingdom €19.4 billion. romania also had a loss of 8% of gross domestic product due to the uncollected value added tax. i stress the urgent need to reduce these losses caused primarily by fraud by introducing the standard vat return.
in writing. - i voted for the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax as regards a standard vat return. businesses increasingly complain that when doing business in the eu it is difficult to comply with vat rules, especially in the case of e-commerce and the supply of goods in the internal market, where the customer is a natural person and the supplier has to register, declare and pay vat in the customer's member state. these obligations can create obstacles to cross-border trade and a standard vat return can reduce these obstacles. a standard vat return will enable all undertakings to provide each member state with standardised information, presented in a common format, preferably electronically. thus, an undertaking filing a vat return in one member state can easily complete and file a vat return in another member state because the information and the way of filing are standardised. i support the introduction at eu level of a single standard vat return that would be available to all businesses.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the common system of value added tax. i hope that the introduction of the standard vat return will make it possible to reduce the administrative burden of vat collection by up to eur 15 billion per calendar year, as estimated by the european commission. i believe that this reduction could represent a welcome saving for public expenditure in eu member states, and not just in times of crisis. i agree with the rapporteur and welcome the objective set out in the commission's proposal to make vat collection more efficient, while reducing red tape and related costs for both the tax authorities of the member states and taxable persons.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which provides for a derogation to introduce specific measures in favour of areas which affect the economic and social situation of the outermost regions. this measure will allow portugal to apply a reduced rate of excise duty to certain products which are produced and consumed locally in the autonomous region of madeira and the autonomous region of the azores. in particular, it concerns the reduced excise duty on rum and liqueurs produced and consumed in madeira and on liqueurs and spirits produced and consumed in the azores. such a provision is necessary, in particular because the transport to the islands of certain raw materials, which are not produced locally, entails additional costs compared to the transport of the finished product.
in writing. - i support the extension of decision 2009/831/ec for the outermost regions by 6 months, as i believe that its expiry should coincide with the entry into force of the new regional aid guidelines for 2014-2020. producers in the regions of madeira and the azores face higher production costs due to their geographical position as outermost regions and this decision may help them to compensate for the additional cost levels.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2009/831/ec as regards its period of application. decision 2009/831/ec authorises portugal to apply until 31 december 2013 a reduced rate of excise duty to rum and liqueurs produced and consumed locally in the autonomous region of madeira and to liqueurs and spirits produced and consumed locally in the autonomous region of the azores. article 2 of that decision limits that derogation to certain products. portugal may apply to those products an excise duty rate lower than the alcohol excise duty rate laid down in article 3 of directive 92/84/ec and lower than the minimum alcohol excise duty rate laid down in that directive, without falling more than 75% below the national level of the alcohol excise duty. on 28 june 2013, the commission adopted new regional aid guidelines for the period 2014-2020. given that those guidelines enter into force on 1 july 2014, it is justified to extend the period of application of decision 2009/831/ec by six months in order to coincide with the expiry date of the current guidelines.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2004/162/ec as regards its application to mayotte as from 1 january 2014. decision 2004/162/ec authorises france to apply, until 1 july 2014, exemptions or reductions from the dock dues for certain products manufactured in the french overseas departments of guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion. the annex to that decision sets out the list of products to which the exemptions or reductions may be applied. the french authorities informed the commission of their intention to introduce a dock dues in mayotte under similar conditions to those in guyana and asked the commission for authorisation to apply a tax regime differentiated according to whether or not the products are locally manufactured. the proposal for a council decision aims to adapt council decision 2004/162/ec so that it becomes applicable to mayotte. the proposal also lays down, for mayotte, the lists of products for which france will be authorised to apply, within certain limits, exemptions or reductions from the so-called dock dues for certain locally manufactured products.
