in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of a comprehensive framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of indonesia, of the other part, with the exception of readmission issues. relations between the european union and the republic of indonesia are to be governed by the comprehensive framework agreement on partnership and cooperation (cfa). we call for better infrastructure and connectivity, as well as an improved regulatory framework, to be pursued through cooperation under the provisions of the acp on trade and investment, taxation and customs, economic policy dialogue, environment, industrial policy and smes, and transport. we urge the eu and indonesia to use apcs in order to achieve long-term geostrategic benefits in addressing global security challenges in bilateral, regional and global multilateral fora, such as addressing climate change and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, combating terrorism, corruption, organised crime, drug trafficking, money laundering and terrorist financing, cooperation in data protection, as well as continuing cooperation in other areas not explicitly covered by apcs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because, in addition to being a very large country, indonesia also has a particularly important geostrategic position, which makes the union interested in deepening relations with this state. the potential for developing eu-indonesia trade relations is very high, given that trade between the two sides was only 23 billion in 2011. as the largest country in asean, indonesia could become a more important regional player and the union should take advantage of this prospect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of a framework agreement on global partnership and cooperation between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of indonesia, of the other part, with the exception of readmission issues, approving the conclusion of the agreement. indonesia is the world's fourth most populous country, the third largest democracy, the largest predominantly muslim country with millions of adherents of other faiths, and a diverse society of over 240 million citizens of various ethnicities, languages and cultures, 40% of whom are under the age of 25, strategically located in an archipelago of over 17,000 islands stretching 5,400 km east to west across the indian and pacific oceans. i support the conclusion of the agreement in the light of the draft framework agreement on comprehensive partnership and cooperation between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of indonesia, of the other part, and having regard to the recommendation of the european parliament's committee on foreign affairs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because indonesia, being a highly populated country with a low average age but also with a high degree of poverty, is prone to emigration trends. the commission also found that the indonesian exporting producers were not able to obtain sufficient quantities of the product concerned from the sampled exporting producers to meet the requirements of the undertaking. the readmission clause is therefore a particularly important component in the relations between the union and indonesia. i would point out, however, that this clause should be suspended when human rights violations occur, so as not to encourage any abuse by the authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the comprehensive framework agreement for partnership and cooperation between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of indonesia, of the other part, on readmission matters, approving the conclusion of the agreement. i support the conclusion of the agreement in the light of the draft framework agreement on comprehensive partnership and cooperation between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of indonesia, of the other part, and having regard to the recommendation of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because most of the illegal immigrants who arrive on the territory of the european union arrive here via turkey. the readmission agreement could thus make a major contribution to reducing illegal immigration, but also to stopping criminal phenomena such as drug or human trafficking. however, i cannot accept that ratification by the turkish side is conditional on progress in the dialogue on visa liberalisation in the eu. turkey is a particularly important partner of the european union and sincere cooperation in full solidarity is essential to advance and deepen the dialogue.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision to conclude the eu-turkey agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation. at the moment, the most common route used by migrants and refugees from all over the world on their way to the eu is the overland route through turkey to greece. turkey is thus the main transit country for illegal immigration into the eu. in order to make the return of migrants who have entered the union illegally possible, the eu and turkey have agreed to open negotiations on a readmission agreement. this agreement obliges the parties to readmit their own nationals, as well as, where appropriate, third-country nationals without residence permits and stateless persons, and sets out procedural and technical criteria for readmission. the negotiations were concluded in 2011. turkey only initialled the agreement, with the turkish side suddenly making the signing of the agreement conditional on the development of a roadmap on visa liberalisation by the union. the subsequent commission action plan on the gradual liberalisation of visas makes such liberalisation conditional on turkey implementing legislative and administrative reforms on the security of identity documents, cooperation with the border authorities of the european union and respect for fundamental rights. the action plan was adopted by the council on 30 november 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of my colleague renate sommer's recommendation on the readmission agreement with turkey, considering that it could make a significant contribution to limiting illegal immigration from turkey to the eu. i believe that the implementation of the provisions of this agreement will be beneficial in combating cross-border crime, in particular trafficking in human beings, and would ease the pressure on greece and therefore on the european union. however, i am disappointed that turkey is delaying the ratification of the readmission agreement, making it conditional on the european union introducing concrete measures to facilitate the issuance of visas for turkish citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation, but i hope that such measures will only be taken in exceptional circumstances, as multilingualism is one of the cornerstones of this parliament. each language must be given equal treatment for reasons of transparency, accessibility and cultural diversity. moreover, the european parliament is distinguished from the other institutions of the union by its obligation to ensure the highest degree of multilingualism. i therefore support this recommendation, but the necessary efforts to ensure comprehensive interpretation services must be stepped up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision to extend the application of rule 147 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament until the end of the eighth parliamentary term. in accordance with rule 147, derogations from rule 146 are authorised until the end of the seventh parliamentary term if and to the extent that the number of linguists for an official language is insufficient, although all necessary measures have been taken to that effect. for each official language for which a derogation is deemed necessary, the bureau shall, on a proposal from the secretary-general, determine whether the necessary conditions are met and shall review its decision every six months. thus, although the capacity for translation into croatian is steadily increasing following croatia's accession to the eu, it may not be possible to ensure full coverage of the needs in this language once the eighth legislature has started. it is also estimated that the irish and maltese languages will not have the capacity to provide full interpretation services in these languages at the beginning of the eighth parliamentary term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and welcome the fact that electronic voting will be extended to the reports of the european parliament. i also welcome the fact that the final vote in parliament's committees will also be able to be carried out electronically at the request of at least a quarter of the committee members. i believe that this will increase the degree of transparency in decision-making and that european citizens will be able to better monitor how their representatives in parliament pursue and defend their interests.
in writing. - i voted to amend rule 166 on the final vote and rule 195 (3) on the vote in committee of the rules of procedure of the european parliament. when taking a decision on the basis of a report, parliament shall vote by a single vote and/or finally by roll-call in accordance with rule 167 (2). the vote on amendments shall be by roll-call only following a request made in accordance with rule 167. the single and/or final vote in committee on a report shall be by roll call in accordance with rule 167 (2). voting on amendments and other votes shall be by show of hands, unless the chair decides to use electronic voting or a quarter of the committee members request a roll call vote. i would stress the importance of these amendments to the rules of procedure, as they will ensure full transparency of the decisions taken in the committees and in the european parliament's plenary.
in writing. - the economic development of the european union is a major objective of public policy, especially as rail transport is one of the factors that can make a decisive contribution to the resumption of the economic growth process. increasing the economic efficiency of rail transport and creating a single european railway area are the appropriate instruments to achieve this. in these circumstances, i believe that the start of a process of liberalisation can lead to both an increase in the efficiency of the railway system and an increase in the importance of rail transport in european economic activities. however, the objectives of ensuring high quality services and maintaining a high level of european competitiveness must be pursued further.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the rail network in use has decreased by 2% in the last 10 years, while the motorway network has expanded by 27%. the potential of rail infrastructure in the internal market is huge and at the same time a determining factor of sustainable growth. in many member states, the markets for domestic transport services are closed to competition, which limits their development. i believe that the new railway package has the potential to realise a genuine internal market in the sector. to this end, it is essential that the relevant legislation is effectively and fully applied in all member states within the time limits set. the opening of the market for domestic passenger services will increase competitive pressure on national rail systems. mobility will increase and costs will fall, to the benefit of european travellers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend the directive establishing the single european railway area, as regards the opening of the market for domestic rail passenger services and the governance of railway infrastructure. the completion of the opening of the union rail market should be considered essential for rail transport to become a credible alternative to other modes of transport in terms of price and quality. the opening of the market for domestic passenger transport will lead to greater flexibility and more opportunities for companies and passengers. the opening will also benefit railway staff as it will improve their chances of providing services to new entrants to the market. experienced workers can add value to new actors, leading to improved working conditions. the issue of improving railway safety should be given serious consideration during the process of opening up the market for domestic rail passenger services in order to avoid creating new administrative obstacles that would undermine the maintenance and improvement of safety. it is also important for railway undertakings to be involved in the development of integrated ticketing systems, in particular for local and regional transport, in order to increase the attractiveness of rail passenger transport.
in writing. - the development of rail transport is important for the european union as a whole, not just from the economic perspective that this strategic direction implies. at a time when member states' economies and societies are still making major efforts to create the conditions for the resumption of economic growth, investments in the development of railway infrastructure or in the upgrading of rolling stock represent an opportunity that should not be missed. at the same time, the development of rail transport can create jobs and help to support the research and innovation process, which is essential to maintain a high level of competitiveness of european companies. on the other hand, the development of rail transport has an important social role. in the same way, the increase in the number of rail passengers can make a positive contribution to european policies to reduce the impact on the environment and combat climate change.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it has become clear that the efficiency, and in particular the quality, of public services for rail passenger transport needs to be improved. this is vital in my view in the efforts to complete the opening of the union rail market. the commission notes that the 2012 eurobarometer survey showed that the number of railway undertakings in the union is increasing, with a number of undertakings having a higher capacity than the number of undertakings in the union. the new targets set are therefore an essential step towards rail being a credible alternative to other modes of transport in terms of price and quality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 as regards the opening of the market for domestic rail passenger services. rail transport plays an important role in terms of both social, environmental and mobility planning and can significantly increase its overall share of european passenger transport. in this respect, investments in research, infrastructure and rolling stock can contribute significantly to new growth, thus directly leading to higher employment in the rail transport sector and indirectly through increased mobility of workers from other sectors. rail transport can become a major modern industry of the union, provided that member states agree on enhanced cooperation. the completion of the opening of the union rail market should be considered essential for rail transport to become a credible alternative to other modes of transport in terms of price and quality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the conditions for the technical specifications for interoperability are essential for the safety of rail transport. compliance with the rules on technical standards in terms of design, maintenance, upgrading or the professional qualification of personnel often makes the difference between a safe means of transport and a unsafe one. in this context, the fourth railway package will enhance the quality and efficiency of rail transport services by removing the last remaining administrative and technical barriers and in particular by establishing a common approach to safety and interoperability rules. all these measures are necessary to increase economies of scale for railway undertakings operating across the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the interoperability of the rail system in the european union, as part of the fourth european railway package. with over 8 billion passengers a year, 10% of freight transport and 800[nbsp ]000 jobs, rail transport plays an important role in the european union. one only has to look at the figures to understand the need for harmonised legislation: there are currently over 11000 national technical and safety rules, which are clearly barriers to the opening up of the railway sector. the elimination of these can improve rail transport services and will make it possible to achieve european environmental policy also through the rail transport lever. we must avoid a repeat of the experience of the third european railway package, which has not yet been fully transposed by all eu member states. it is imperative that the remaining legislative provisions be implemented as a matter of urgency so that the fourth package, including the railway interoperability directive, can be correctly and fully transposed across the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the interoperability of the rail system in the european union. in order to enable union citizens, economic operators and regional and local authorities to fully benefit from the advantages of an area without internal borders and to achieve the objective of territorial cohesion, it is advisable, in particular, to improve the interconnection and interoperability of national rail networks and access to those networks, including for passengers with disabilities, by implementing any measures that may prove necessary in the field of harmonisation of technical standards. this directive lays down the conditions to be met for achieving interoperability in the union rail system in a way that ensures compatibility with the provisions of the directive on the safety of the union rail system. those conditions shall relate to the design, construction, commissioning, upgrading, renewal, operation and maintenance of the elements of that system, as well as the professional qualifications and health and safety conditions of the personnel contributing to its operation and maintenance. the pursuit of this objective necessarily requires the establishment of an optimal level of technical harmonisation, which makes it possible to participate in the gradual creation of the internal market for equipment and services for the construction, renewal, upgrading and operation of the rail system in the union.
i voted in favour of this report and the whole rail package. trains are less polluting and safer than other means of transport, but they account for only 6% of passenger transport in the union. i believe that a well-developed rail system brings economic, social and operational benefits. competitiveness will lead to lower prices, smoother road traffic and a lower environmental impact. but reform of this system must start with passenger safety. even though it ranks second in the ranking of the safest means of transport, the number of accidents is high: over 2 000 incidents in 2011, resulting in almost 1 200 deaths. tragedies like last summer's in spain can and must be avoided.
in writing. - rail transport remains essential for the european union as the safest form of public transport. despite the success of measures to increase railway safety, there are still steps to be taken in this direction. in this context, it is necessary to improve safety measures for people using level crossings and for people living in the vicinity of railway lines. clarifying the distinct responsibilities of the actors involved in the rail transport process, managing the increasing complexity of this system, driven by the increasing intensity of its cross-border dimension, are just some of the factors that make it necessary to concentrate the union's efforts in this direction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of modernising the european parliament and council directive on railway safety. although rail transport is the safest mode of transport in the european union, rare accidents can have disastrous consequences, resulting in huge human and financial losses. we all remember the tragedy of july 2013 in santiago de compostela, spain, where 79 people lost their lives and 140 were injured. as part of the new european railway package, i also believe that it is important to improve railway safety in practice through the amendments to this directive. the new directive corrects the legislative shortcomings of the old directive 49/2004, the provisions of which were, as is well known, used for protectionist purposes. i support the idea of introducing a single safety certificate for the whole union, issued by the railway agency. the introduction of the single certificate will improve railway safety as well as the certification process, with benefits that translate into savings of time and resources at european level.
in writing. - i voted for the proposal for a directive on railway safety. rail transport is already the safest mode of transport in the eu and has improved its safety performance in recent decades. although rail transport performance has increased from around 200 billion travel kilometres in 1970 to over 300 billion today, the average annual death rate of rail passengers has decreased from around 400 in the early 1970s to less than 100 today. safety should be ensured not only for passengers and staff, including contractors' staff, but also for persons using level crossings and persons living near railway lines. in line with technical and scientific progress, railway safety should be further improved, taking into account the expected improvement in the competitiveness of the railway mode of transport. this directive contains minimum provisions, member states being allowed to introduce more stringent legislative provisions only in accordance with article 8, designed to ensure the further development and improvement of safety on the union's railways and improved market access for rail transport services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the european union agency for railways contributes to the integration of european rail systems by strengthening train safety and ensuring the possibility of crossing the borders of the member states. the proposed amendments are necessary because a number of developments have taken place in european railways and rail transport since 2004 when the original draft regulation establishing the agency was drafted. the legal status needed to be clarified, new rules introduced and, in particular, existing processes simplified. all these measures will lead to an improvement in the functioning of the agency, and by implication to the guarantee of high safety and quality standards on eu railways.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the european union agency for railways and for the repeal of regulation (ec) no 881/2004. the fourth railway package proposes important changes to the agency's tasks. this regulation provides in particular for the performance of tasks related to the issuing of vehicle authorisations and safety certificates, in particular in cross-border traffic at union level. this implies a more important role for the agency. the agency should contribute to the creation and effective functioning of a single european railway area without borders, which ensures a high level of safety and at the same time improves the competitive position of the railway sector. this objective should be achieved by contributing, in technical terms, to the implementation of european union legislation by increasing the level of interoperability of railway systems and to the development of a common approach to safety in the european railway system. the agency should also fulfil the role of european authority responsible for issuing, at union level, authorisations to place on the market railway vehicles and vehicle types, safety certificates for railway undertakings and authorisations to put into service european rail traffic management system (ertms) subsystems which are located or operated throughout the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because regulation no 1192/69, which allowed member states to grant compensation to a limited number of railway undertakings for the payment of obligations such as special family allowances and pensions, is no longer relevant or necessary.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to repeal council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. at european level, a number of legislative measures have been adopted which have opened up the markets for rail freight and international rail passenger transport to competition. directive 2012/34/eu of the european parliament and of the council of 21 november 2012 on the establishment of a single european railway area (recast) established certain fundamental principles, which provide that railway undertakings must be managed on the basis of the principles applicable to companies, that the entities responsible for allocating capacity and charging railway infrastructure must be separate from the entities operating rail services, that there must be a separation of accounts. it has also been established that any railway undertaking authorised in accordance with eu criteria must have access to railway infrastructure on fair and non-discriminatory terms and that infrastructure managers may benefit from state funding. the deadline for transposition of directive 2012/34/eu into national law is 16 june 2015. this regulation shall enter into force two years after its publication in the official journal of the european union.
i supported this report because although at union level the annual rate of passenger air transport incidents has been relatively low, in my country the situation is different. in 2012, the number of reported civil aviation events increased by 51% compared to the previous year, which is more than worrying. unfortunately, there are also unfortunate incidents that lead to the tragic loss of human lives, as was the case with the recent accident in the apuseni mountains. i hope that this regulation will help to reduce the number of accidents involving aircraft and the number of deaths caused by them. this can be achieved by improving existing systems at national and european level and by using the experience of civil aviation events to correct safety problems and prevent real catastrophes.
in writing. - as air traffic is forecast to grow strongly by 2030, parliament discussed the need to strengthen air safety prevention systems. the proposal for a regulation aims to strengthen and deepen the proactive accident prevention system through analysis and rapid exchange of information, contributing to the achievement of the objectives set out in the 2011 white paper on transport. this information will be collected in an anonymous and secure database, the central european register (cer), to which easa and member states will have free access in order to enhance aviation safety throughout the territory.
in writing. - in order to avoid an increase in the number of aviation accidents due to the intensification of air traffic, a number of proactive measures are needed. while the accident investigation systems in the union are functioning, more efficient systems for data collection and analysis are needed. those systems should be applied uniformly throughout the union in order to be interpreted in the same way in all member states. it is also necessary to improve the protection of aviation employees when they report an incident. employees should enjoy the same level of protection throughout the union, thereby increasing aviation safety. such reporting can prevent possible aviation accidents and reduce loss of life.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the adoption of the regulation on the reporting, analysis and follow-up of civil aviation occurrences. this regulation aims to improve aviation safety by ensuring the reporting, collection, storage, protection, exchange, dissemination and analysis of relevant safety information relating to civil aviation. this regulation thus ensures: the prompt adoption of safety measures, where appropriate, based on the analysis of the information collected; the permanent availability of safety information through the introduction of rules on confidentiality and the appropriate use of information, as well as the harmonised and enhanced protection of the reporter and persons referred to in occurrence reports; and the examination and treatment of aviation safety risks at both union and national level. there should be an exchange of information on events within the union in order to improve the detection of actual or potential hazards. this exchange of information should also allow member states to have access to all information relating to events occurring on their territory or in their airspace but which are reported to another member state. it is important to emphasise that the sole objective of occurrence reporting is the prevention of accidents and incidents, and not the establishment of fault or liability.
i voted in favour of the report because, even though europe has some of the safest roads in the world, the number of road casualties is still alarming. the ecall system has the potential to save thousands of lives and increase safety on european roads. i welcome the fact that the draft has been translated into a regulation, in a context where the 112 directive has shown its shortcomings. the commission will have the role of actively monitoring transposition in the member states, as only correct implementation can bring concrete results. in romania, the percentage of accidents with deaths or serious injuries is higher than the european average. this is also one of the reasons why it was the first european country to prepare the necessary infrastructure for the ecall system.
in writing. - i believe that it is of the utmost importance that major efforts are made, at the level of national authorities as well as at the european level, to ensure a high degree of efficiency and interoperability in the implementation of the e-call system. in this context, i support the proposal for all member states to sign the memorandum envisaging the implementation of this system. i also believe that the european parliament's call to the member states of the european union to ensure a high level of institutional efficiency of this system is entirely legitimate. the implementation of this system is necessary as its existence can lead to a significant reduction in the response times in the event of major accidents, both in urban and rural areas.
in writing. - very often, new technologies can contribute to our safety and even to saving human lives. the ecall system is one such application in the field of road safety and i believe that, despite the data protection objections, it should be supported. it's very true that this system is based on data collection. however, i think we have to take into account that the system is a latent one, which is activated only in the event of an accident, just as an airbag opens only in the event of a vehicle impact. what's constantly being transmitted would just be the last 3 digits that correspond to the gps location. however, i believe that the proposal contains sufficient data protection safeguards. i supported, however, an amendment which would allow drivers to turn off the system if they considered it too intrusive, so that individual users could explicitly agree to the collection of vehicle position data, as with other technological applications that collect personal data. even though this amendment was not adopted, i nevertheless supported the final report because the argument of saving lives seems to me to be stronger than any minor breaches of data protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on type-approval requirements for the installation of an ecall in-vehicle system and amending directive 2007/46/ec. i believe that it is necessary to make it compulsory to have an automatic warning system on board cars in case of an accident, because such a system will reduce the number of deaths from car accidents. loss of life is an economic and social burden on the union which should not be neglected. the ecall system has the capability to reduce the response time of the competent authorities by automatically notifying the nearest intervention centre in less time than a human intervention. even if the passengers are unable to speak because of the injuries they sustain, a minimal set of data is sent. in this way, the emergency services are informed of the existence of an accident and its location within a very short time. the lack of progress in voluntary implementation of the system based on the report " ecall: a new 112 service for citizens " is regrettable . i support the european commission's assessment that mandatory introduction is the only option to achieve positive results in this respect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on type-approval requirements for the installation of an ecall in-vehicle system. the installation of an ecall service on board all motor vehicles and in all member states has been one of the union's top priorities in the field of road safety since 2003. i would stress that there is still a need to improve the functioning of the 112 service across the union so that it can provide assistance in emergency situations in a timely and effective manner. i would stress the importance of the installation of a 112 ecall system on board vehicles as the union ecall system is expected to reduce the number of deaths as well as the severity of injuries caused by road accidents in the union by rapid alerting of the emergency services. the necessary and coordinated upgrade of the infrastructure of the electronic communications network for making ecalls and of the psaps for receiving ecalls would make the service available to all citizens and therefore contribute to reducing the number of deaths and severity of injuries, healthcare costs, traffic congestion caused by accidents and other costs.
i voted in favour of the report. one of the most important lessons of the crisis was the need to ensure consumer protection in all financial areas. the insurance sector is no exception, and the directive, as amended, should therefore promote fair competition and transparency. i also welcome the extension of its scope. consumer protection requires regulation of all sales of insurance products offered, whether by intermediaries or by businesses. moreover, these services and products must follow three main principles: focus on the customer's needs, provide long-term prospects and, most importantly, guarantee solvency. all this because mobility requires the strengthening of a genuine european internal market for insurance packages.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposals to amend the insurance intermediation directive and to open negotiations with the council of the european union to speed up their adoption. i voted against amendments nos 6 and 7, which reintroduced the practice of tied sales. i voted for amendment 9 which states that information on all costs and expenses, including costs and expenses associated with the intermediation service and the insurance product that are not caused by the materialization of the underlying market risk are aggregated to allow the client to understand what the overall cost is and the cumulative effect on the profitability of the investment and, upon the client's request, a detailed breakdown. where possible, this information shall be provided to the client on a regular basis, at least annually, for the duration of the investment. i also voted for the new definition of 'insurance-based investment products' so that they do not include general insurance products as set out in annex i to directive 2009/138/ec, life insurance contracts payable only on death or disability, pension products, occupational pension schemes or individual pension products where the employer or employee has no choice of pension product or provider.
i hold this report and i voted in favour of it. while we are talking about an exclusive competence of the member states, improving public health must be a priority at national and european level. i welcome the fact that the objectives of the programme also include the prevention of diseases at union level and support for solutions to cross-border health threats. in this context, i would like to draw your attention to a situation which, in my view, represents an imminent danger: more and more parents are refusing to vaccinate their children because of lack of information, possible adverse effects or religious reasons. we need serious education campaigns to do this, so that parents understand that vaccines are safe and, very often, vital.
in writing. - i welcome the establishment, through today's vote in the european parliament's plenary, of the 'health and economic growth for citizens' programme, the third multiannual eu action programme in the field of health for the period 2014-2020, as i believe that the health and well-being of european citizens is a sound investment in the future of the eu. a high level of health protection must be ensured in the definition and implementation of all union policies and activities. in this regard, the union should complement and support national health policies, encourage cooperation between member states and promote coordination between their programmes, while fully respecting the responsibilities of national authorities for the definition of their health policies and the organisation and delivery of health and medical care services. promoting good mental and physical health at eu level is an integral part of europe 2020: a european strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. keeping a population healthy and active for longer and involving them to play an active role in managing their health, including by improving the health literacy of the population, will have overall positive health effects, including reducing health inequalities, and a positive impact on citizens' quality of life, productivity and competitiveness.
in writing. - the health for growth programme, with an overall financial allocation of eur 446 million for the period 2014-2020, is part of the europe 2020 strategy and aims to encourage innovation and sustainability in healthcare. potential candidates for funding will be national authorities, public and private bodies, international organisations and non-governmental organisations through co-financing. it is therefore essential that the procedures and access to these budgets are as simple as possible so that member states and professionals in the sector can make the best use of them to improve the well-being of european citizens.
in writing. - i welcome the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the third health programme of the european union. i fully support the idea of complementarity between the european health programme - health for growth - and the opportunities for funding the health sector from the structural funds, as well as horizon 2020. i believe that the european commission should encourage the eastern european countries to apply for this funding, for example by organising an information campaign. i look forward to the results of the european health programme in developing strategies to combat chronic diseases. i'll give you the example of hepatitis, where solutions are urgently needed. unfortunately, hepatitis has a high prevalence in romania. romanian hepatitis patients receive neither screening nor adequate treatment, so the disease becomes chronic.
in writing. - i fully support the adoption of the new health programme and the improvements made to it by parliament. as some ngos pointed out, there was not enough reference to diet and physical activity in the original proposal, and we have added these important points and increased the focus on preventative health actions. emphasis on a small number of preventative actions will bring a broad range of health benefits at relatively little cost. i also welcome the specific mention of action on neurodegenerative diseases such as alzheimer’s, which will become more prevalent as the population ages.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a 'health for growth' programme, the third multiannual eu programme of action in the field of health for the period 2014-2020. in accordance with article 168 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), a high level of human health protection is to be ensured in the definition and implementation of all union policies and actions. the union is to complement and support national health policies, encourage cooperation between member states and promote coordination between their programmes, while fully respecting the responsibilities of the member states for the definition of their health policies and the organisation and delivery of health and medical care services. in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, the programme should focus on a set of well-defined objectives and actions with clear and proven union added value and focus support on a smaller number of activities in the priority areas. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, emphasis should be placed on areas where there are clear cross-border or internal market problems or where significant benefits and efficiency gains can be derived from union cooperation.

on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, i strongly believe that we as the european union must set an example of how much human rights mean to us and how determined we are to protect them in our own home, europe. of course it is the duty of each national legal system to observe the rights and liberties provided for by the eu treaties and the charter. but we should be able to both monitor and sanction each and every member state if they fail to carry out their duty. this is why i firmly believe that we need an objective and effective mechanism aimed at monitoring compliance with the copenhagen criteria by every member state. so far, only the accession countries have been subjected to such scrutiny and, in addition, a cooperation and verification mechanism was set up only for romania and bulgaria. when a majority of member states has the power of verification on just two countries, such a mechanism becomes a political weapon. this was crystal clear on at least two occasions: firstly, when the eu decided not to use the tools provided for by the treaty for a wide scrutiny on hungary; secondly, when some member states invoked such scrutiny to deny romania’s and bulgaria’s rightful claim to enter the schengen area. it is high time we ended the double standards when it comes to judging how well one member state upholds the rights enshrined in the treaty, or how well their justice system works. we are a union, and we should share the same rights and have the same penalties applied if we break the rule of law.

member of the commission. - mr president, the commission welcomes this opportunity to discuss visa policy with parliament. the commission will adopt the ‘visa code package’ on 19[nbsp ]march. i know that the resolution by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs suggests that the commission should have presented the evaluation report and only later submitted a proposal amending the visa code. this would, however, have meant a delay in tackling issues on which urgent action is required to facilitate travel for legitimate travellers. in light of the positive economic impact of visa policy on the wider european union economy, and in particular on tourism, we felt that it was important to move on to firm proposals immediately. we have drawn upon the results of a public consultation organised in spring last year, a study on the economic impact of short-stay visa facilitations, and, not least, on an impact assessment. all of these inputs will be made public next month. we included this package in our 2013 work programme and regret that its adoption has been slightly delayed. we needed extra time as the package now contains two legislative proposals, and more time was needed to ensure that the proposals are balanced and comprehensive. it is important to remember that the primary objective of the common visa policy is to prevent irregular migration and safeguard public order and security, as a corollary to the schengen area without internal borders. so the commission has sought to strike a balance in its forthcoming proposal between those objectives and the need to facilitate travel for legitimate travellers. the proposal is based around the objective of easing the administrative burden for both applicants and consulates. we plan to do this by fully exploiting the benefits of the visa information system and differentiating between the treatment of known or regular travellers and unknown, first-time applicants on the basis of clear, objective criteria. additionally, we propose that provisions on the harmonisation of practices and procedures carried out in local schengen cooperation be strengthened. the second legislative proposal in the visa package concerns a new type of visa – a ‘touring visa’. it would be used for an intended stay in the territory of two or more member states of up to one year, with the possibility of extension for an additional year. this type of visa is sought by many third-country nationals, be they tourists, performers, researchers or others with a legitimate interest in, and need for, travelling in the schengen area for more than 90[nbsp ]days in a given 180-day period without being considered as ‘immigrants’. and now let me briefly mention the ‘visa lists’. the amendment, related to the regular review of the visa that you are adopting this week, will allow visa-free travel for nationals of 19 third countries, most of them small island nations in the caribbean and pacific regions, as well as the united arab emirates, peru and colombia. this relatively long list of new visa-free countries shows the willingness of the eu to strengthen links with countries in different parts of the world, and contradicts those who say the eu is making it increasingly difficult for people to travel to the schengen area. the commission is satisfied that the final compromise, in addition to transferring 19 countries to the visa-free list, also gives more prominence to the criteria used in assessing the visa status of third countries, by transferring these criteria into the body of the legal text. at the same time, we have reviewed the list of criteria and we have added new ones, namely economic impact and human rights considerations. this will help to make the common visa policy more coherent with other areas of the eu’s action. just last month another amendment entered into force, establishing a new suspension mechanism that aims to ensure that visa-free travel with third countries is not abused. the mechanism allows, under strict conditions and after thorough assessment by the commission, for the temporary reintroduction of visa requirements for citizens of a visa-free third country when there is an emergency situation caused by abuse of the visa-free regime by nationals of these countries. the commission hopes, as does parliament, that member states will seek to use the mechanism responsibly and only when all relevant criteria are fulfilled. and it must be clear that there is no automatism: a request to trigger the mechanism will not automatically lead to the suspension of the visa-free regime. that same amendment revised the reciprocity mechanism. the commission could not agree with the legal form given to that mechanism. we hope nevertheless that it will put more pressure on some of our partners to abolish visa requirements for eu citizens. we have seen a positive development recently with canada abolishing the visa requirement for czech citizens. finally, the other amendment offering the holders of moldovan biometric passports visa-free travel to the eu is a fulfilment of the eu’s commitment made in the visa dialogue with the republic of moldova. now that the latter has fulfilled its commitments, it meets all the benchmarks set out in the action plan for visa liberalisation.
on behalf of the epp group. first of all, i would like to thank my colleagues, the members of the european parliament, for the support they have given so far to resolve this issue - visa liberalisation for the republic of moldova. i also thank the council and the commission, in particular commissioner stefan füle, for their efforts and the speed with which they have dealt with this matter. citizens of the republic of moldova deserve to travel visa-free to the european union. the reports drawn up by the evaluation committee showed that the republic of moldova has fulfilled its commitments, in some cases even exceeding them. the moldovan authorities, the citizens have made great efforts. the pro-european coalition in chisinau deserves all the credit, i think, for having withstood very strong pressures, both from within and from without. today's vote will show that the union is delivering on its commitments to the extent of the partners' efforts. moldova becomes the first country in the eastern neighbourhood to benefit from this visa liberalisation facility. the epp group supports the european path of the republic of moldova. but it is important to ensure that moldova remains committed to the european path. the european union must be involved in clarifying the situation in transnistria. the current format, 5+2, has not brought the expected results. i think that formula needs to be reconsidered and i think that the union should be given a very important role. i think the outside pressures have to stop. i think that the russian federation should withdraw its last troops from transnistria, thus leaving moldova and the citizens of moldova to decide for themselves which path they want to take. i once again congratulate moldova on meeting its obligations and on its attachment to the european family.
the abolition of the visa requirement for citizens of the republic of moldova is of major significance in the context of developments in ukraine. the european union is now sending a strong signal to its eastern neighbour. the european commission's proposal to move the republic of moldova from the negative to the positive visa list recognises the progress made by the chisinau authorities over the last three and a half years. the republic of moldova is the first eastern partnership country to fulfil all the conditions for visa liberalisation. after the initialling of the association agreement, moldovan citizens will soon enjoy the benefits of a fundamental right of the european project: free movement. in the new geopolitical context that is being defined, a common, coherent and fair visa policy is becoming imperative, and this means, first of all, the integration of romania and bulgaria into the schengen area, in order to put an end to an unfair and frustrating division within the union. i believe that the concern for the harmonization of visa policy must also be directed towards the application of the principle of reciprocity in relations with third countries which maintain the visa requirement for some member states of the union, and i am referring in particular to the usa and canada, cases in which we are faced with the risk of making the current deadlock permanent. i welcome the commission's commitment to promoting the dialogue on a mutually beneficial visa regime and i continue to encourage it to take a bolder and more firm approach.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation because it is a major development towards a genuine single market for european consumers. the emergence of a common contract law system will encourage european citizens to buy more from other countries. they will thus be able to choose the best offers with the guarantee that their rights are uniformly protected throughout the union. and for merchants, the passage of this act is good news. they are currently discouraged from entering into cross-border transactions due to differences in the laws of the member states. their losses are in the tens of billions of euros a year, with only 10% of european businesses doing cross-border business.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common european sales law is intended to be an essential pillar of the future european contract law. the initiative i support is designed to solve the difficulties created in the internal market by the differences between national rules on contract law. the proposed text is the result of parliament's cooperation with the institute of european law and marks a significant step in the process of drawing up the community legal framework. distance selling is particularly targeted, especially the online sales sector, which is developing very rapidly in relation to the legal rules in force at eu level. i voted in favour of the report, particularly because it provides for a system of remedies available to consumers and a restructuring of the rules on the return of purchased goods.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the common european sales legislation. contract law barriers prevent consumers and traders from exploiting the full potential of the internal market and are of particular importance in the field of distance selling, which should be one of the tangible results of the internal market. in particular, the digital dimension of the internal market is becoming essential for both consumers and traders, as consumers increasingly shop online and the number of traders selling online is also increasing. given that the means of communication and information technology are constantly developing and becoming more accessible, the growth potential of internet sales is very high. in view of this situation and in order to overcome such obstacles created by contract law, the parties should be able to agree on a single set of contractual rules governing distance contracts, and in particular online contracts, which they conclude, which have a uniform meaning and interpretation in all member states, namely a common european law on sales.
in writing. - the consumption of tobacco products is one of the biggest public health challenges in romania and the european union. with 75% of smokers starting before the age of 18, the attraction of young people to tobacco products is growing. given these alarming statistics, the main objective of the compromise reached is to discourage smoking among children and adolescents, precisely to reduce tobacco consumption in the medium and long term. i believe that the new measures will help to reduce the number of smokers. regulations requiring that 65% of the surface of a cigarette pack be covered by visual health warnings, or establishing a positive list of additives and banning flavourings such as vanilla or chocolate, are measures that will discourage young people from starting to smoke. i voted for this compromise.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, as a young mother, i really understand the risks we are exposing our children to when it comes to smoking. in addition to the negative example of adults, there is the problem of the effects of passive smoking, which is often as harmful as active smoking. they also draw attention to smoking during pregnancy, which can lead to very serious complications, thus endangering the life of the fetus or even the mother. whether we're talking about preterm births or even birth defects, my conclusion is that warning messages alone are not enough. i think that media campaigns would be more useful which could be financed by the excise taxes that cigarette manufacturers pay to the states.
in writing. - smoking remains the leading preventable cause of death in the eu, killing around 700 000 people a year. the incidence of smoking among young people (15-25 years) is currently 29%, higher than the overall population. 70% of smokers start before the age of 18, and many do so at an even younger age. i welcome and absolutely need new measures to discourage young people from smoking, such as stronger health warnings and the banning of packaging and flavours that may be particularly attractive to young people. tobacco products are not ordinary products and, given the particularly harmful effects of tobacco, health protection should be of high importance, in particular to reduce the prevalence of smoking among young people. to this end, member states should carry out more tobacco prevention campaigns, in particular in schools and through the media. i also welcome the measures to strengthen counterfeiting security to combat illicit trade in tobacco and tobacco products, in particular along the union's external borders.
in writing. - the revision of this legislation was necessary to discourage smoking, and particularly its attractiveness among young people, thus supporting the overall objectives of our public health policies. i believe that some pragmatic solutions have been found with regard to health warnings, flavourings and marketing of slim cigarettes. although we should not mislead consumers, since cigarettes are just as harmful if they have different flavours or sizes, i do not think we should go too far. so keeping products that mimic cigarettes, for example, on the market is a good thing. the reason i abstained in the final vote is related to the provisions relating to electronic cigarettes. the compromise text is better than the implementation of the pharmaceutical legislation proposed by the commission, but it is still not ideal. it's been shown that e-cigarettes have lowered sales of regular cigarettes, the former being less harmful. i therefore consider it illogical to discourage these products, inter alia, by setting a level for the nicotine content. i preferred to abstain because the text as a whole brings significant improvements and i do not think the ep should have rejected it just because of the devices related to electronic cigarettes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products. directive 2001/37/ec lays down union-wide rules on tobacco products. in order to reflect scientific progress as well as developments in the market and the international context, substantial amendments to that directive would be necessary and it should be repealed and replaced by a new directive. it is necessary to lay down a number of new definitions in order to ensure uniform implementation of this directive by the member states. where different obligations imposed by this directive apply to different product categories and the relevant products fall within more than one of those categories, the most stringent obligations should apply. member states shall require manufacturers and importers of plant products for smoking to submit to their competent authorities a list of all ingredients and the corresponding quantities used in the manufacture of such products, by brand name and by type. manufacturers or importers shall also inform the competent authorities of the member states concerned if the composition of a product is changed in such a way as to affect the information provided under this article.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on sexual exploitation and prostitution and their impact on gender equality. i voted for amendment 2 whereby parliament recognises that prostitution, forced prostitution and sexual exploitation are highly gender-specific issues and violations of human dignity, contrary to the principles of human rights, including gender equality, and therefore contrary to the principles of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, including the purpose and principle of gender equality. i voted for amendment no 3, which stresses the obligation to respect the right to health of all women, including the right to their bodies and sexuality, without coercion, discrimination and violence. i voted for paragraph 18 which stresses that child prostitution can never be voluntary, children having no capacity to 'give consent' to the practice of prostitution. parliament urged member states to combat child prostitution (involving persons under 18) as vigorously as possible, as it is the most serious form of forced prostitution and urgently calls for zero tolerance, based on prevention, protection of victims and punishment of clients. parliament drew the attention of the member states to the important role of education in preventing prostitution and the organised crime associated with it and recommended the organisation of special educational, awareness-raising and prevention campaigns.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i support strengthening solvit. in addition to solving citizens' problems informally, without bureaucratic procedures, this network has the advantage of being free of charge. the major drawback is that neither the commission nor the member states are making sufficient efforts to increase the visibility of solvit. we're talking about only 1,300 cases in the last year. i think there are actually many more european citizens who have problems with the application of european law in other member states. whether it is the recognition of diplomas or access to health services in other member states, solvit has proven its usefulness. i therefore call on the commission and the governments of the union to launch public awareness campaigns on the role and benefits of solvit as soon as possible.
in writing. - the solvit network has proved to be very useful and effective in solving problems faced by eu citizens and businesses due to non-compliance with european law, free of charge and quickly. therefore, this network should be further developed and promoted. many european businesses, and in particular smes, for whom the network would be most useful, are not aware of solvit. both the european institutions and national authorities should be more involved in promotion activities because solvit could substantially reduce the administrative costs faced by smes in the single market. however, i agree with the european commission's approach of promoting the 'europe of the people' portal as a single point where citizens and businesses can find information on the various practical aspects of the eu, and that it should also link solvit to those who need its services. the report raises the issue of funding again. in order to ensure that solvit is not a victim of its own success, it will need resources commensurate with its competences. better funding could also perhaps solve, at least in part, the problem of training staff to deal with the more complex cases faced by businesses.
in writing. - union citizens must be informed of their rights within the single market and of the options available to them if they are faced with unfair decisions or discriminatory administrative formalities in a member state other than their own. if a public authority in another member state fails to comply with european legislation, solvit is there to help citizens and businesses who face obstacles. according to a study presented by the european commission, since it became operational in 2002, more than 2000 cases have been solved by the solvit online network to date. approximately 70 cases are reported each month at union level. of these, 4 out of 5 are resolved within approximately 60 days. these statistics demonstrate the importance of the solvit platform in ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market mechanism. i support the commission's proposal to implement new concrete measures to increase the efficiency of the solvit network.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on solvit. we welcome the commission's efforts to improve the work of the solvit network in the resolution of cross-border disputes relating to the internal market. solvit plays an important role as a key problem-solving tool and therefore as a means of ensuring a higher level of compliance with union law in relation to the single market. we believe that the potential of the single market can only be realised if businesses and citizens are aware of the rights and opportunities that are available to them and are able to put them into practice effectively. they argue that these objectives can only be achieved if member states ensure the effective implementation of single market legislation and if good quality information and effective problem-solving mechanisms are made available. we call for the visibility of the solvit network to be increased and the level of public information about it to be increased, and for the service to be brought closer to citizens who are unaware of the existence of the network. we invite the member states and the commission to ensure equal access to solvit centres and online portals, for example for people with disabilities or the elderly, and to develop all possible options to establish contacts between users and solvit centres in this context.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the directive is a very important step towards creating a genuine european area of freedom, security and justice. cooperation in criminal matters, from the very beginning of the investigation phase, will be able to speed up proceedings and ensure that verdicts are delivered on the basis of all available evidence. this will help both the investigated and the investigating authorities. in addition, cooperation on interception of calls could strengthen the fight against cross-border organised crime or even terrorism. the possibility of video or telephone interviews will also facilitate the procedures. however, i would like to see the european investigation order not abused, especially as the executing state will bear the costs of the investigations.
in writing. - one of the objectives of the european integration process is precisely to promote the free movement of persons, while guaranteeing their security, by creating an area of freedom, security and justice. the importance of the european criminal space is a priority in the european integration process, given the gradual emancipation of traditional cooperation mechanisms. after promoting judicial and police cooperation as a compensatory measure for the disappearance of internal borders, the european union is now going further, beyond interstate cooperation, with a view to gradually building a homogeneous criminal area. progress in this area should be based on the following principles: mutual recognition, coordination of investigations and protection of fundamental rights in criminal cases, thus respecting the measures defined in article 82 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the complementary link between mutual recognition and harmonisation is thus reaffirmed, with the emphasis that mutual recognition cannot be achieved without harmonisation. member states should provide, in the application of this directive, for transparent policies regarding the processing of personal data and the exercise of the right of the data subject to have recourse to legal remedies for the protection of his or her personal data.
in writing. - i support the creation of a european criminal area and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the european investigation order is one of the most effective tools to facilitate the exchange of information, the collection and transmission of evidence in criminal matters between member states. according to eurostat, the number of union citizens serving a custodial sentence increased from 29 832 in 2006 to over 638 000 in 2010. this increased crime rate demonstrates the need to create appropriate procedures and tools for the functioning of the single european area of freedom, security and justice. the european investigation order will help to administer relevant and conclusive evidence in criminal cases, which will lead to a better administration of justice. this cooperation between member states on the taking of evidence will also lead to a quicker trial of cases within a reasonable time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft directive on the european investigation order in criminal matters. the european investigation order is a judicial decision issued or validated by a judicial authority of a member state to implement one or more specific investigative measures in another member state for the purpose of obtaining evidence in accordance with this directive. the european investigation order may also be issued for the purpose of obtaining evidence already in the possession of the competent authorities of the executing state. the issuing of a european investigation order may be requested by a suspect or accused person, or by a lawyer on his or her behalf, within the framework of the rights of defence applicable in accordance with domestic criminal procedure. this directive does not have the effect of modifying the obligation to respect fundamental rights and legal principles as enshrined in article 6 of the treaty on european union, including the right of defence of persons subject to criminal proceedings, and is without prejudice to the obligations of judicial authorities in this regard.
citizens of the republic of moldova were deprived of freedom of expression, association and movement during the soviet period. the former soviet empire installed a barbed wire fence along the entire western border, and my colleagues in the baltic countries certainly remember this. in 2009, after a long communist rule, the pro-european coalition in chisinau, then led by mr vlad filat, removed hundreds of kilometres of barbed wire, demonstrating its unreserved commitment to european integration. today, we are voting in response to the symbolic gesture of removing the barbed wire, allowing the citizens of the republic of moldova to move freely within the european union. by this step we bring the romanians back from across the prut into the great european family.
in writing. - the purpose of this proposal is to amend the annexes to regulation (ec) no 539/2001 listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement. the commission proposal to exempt the citizens of the republic of moldova from the visa requirement is based on the considerable progress made by that country in the last three and a half years of the visa liberalisation dialogue. at the eastern partnership summit in vilnius in november 2013, the republic of moldova initialled the association agreement with the eu and became the first eastern partnership country to fulfil all the requirements of the visa liberalisation action plan allowing for the implementation of visa liberalisation. the significance of visa liberalisation for ordinary people is considerable as it brings concrete benefits to the citizens of the republic of moldova, many of whom already hold a romanian passport. despite moldova's geopolitical location, internal difficulties, and recent developments in its neighbourhood, the eu remains a compelling alternative for the republic of moldova. on the other hand, the eu has a major opportunity to send a strong political signal to the republic of moldova and help transform the lives of millions of people.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing the list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from this requirement. in accordance with the joint declaration adopted at the prague eastern partnership summit on 7 may 2009 and with the completion by the republic of moldova of the visa liberalisation action plan, the commission considers that the republic of moldova has met all the benchmarks set out in the visa liberalisation action plan. given that it meets all the benchmarks, the republic of moldova should be exempted from the visa requirement. this exemption should apply to holders of biometric passports issued by the republic of moldova in accordance with the standards of the international civil aviation organisation (icao). as regards bulgaria and romania, this regulation constitutes an act building upon, or otherwise relating to, the schengen acquis within the meaning of article 4 (1) of the 2005 act of accession.
