in writing. - i support the introduction of a simplified system of checks on persons at the external borders. croatia and cyprus are to recognise certain documents issued by schengen member states as equivalent to national visas and to allow third-country nationals to transit through or stay for a maximum period of 90 days. according to the international organization for migration, in 2013, the number of immigrants in croatia was 17.6% of the total population. a similar situation exists in cyprus, where the number of immigrants represents 18.2% of the total population. those member states should apply the simplified technical conditions for migrants. i support the inclusion in the report of provisions that also include romania and bulgaria in the category of schengen member states that can issue these documents. although we are not yet officially members of the schengen area, we have implemented the schengen acquis and we should be included in the category of states issuing these national visa-like documents.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision introducing a simplified regime for the control of persons at the external borders, based on the unilateral recognition by croatia and cyprus of certain documents as equivalent to their national visas for transit through or intended stay in their territories for a period not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period, and repealing decisions no 895/2006/ec and no 582/2008/ec. the objective of this decision is to introduce a regime of unilateral recognition by bulgaria, croatia, cyprus and romania of certain documents issued by other states. this objective cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states and can therefore be better achieved at union level. the union may adopt measures, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, as set out in that article, this decision does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve that objective. the simplified regime established by this decision should apply for a transitional period until a date to be fixed by a council decision.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council introducing a simplified regime for the control of persons at the external borders based on the unilateral recognition by croatia and cyprus of certain documents as equivalent to their national visas for transit through or intended stay on their territories for a period not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period and repealing decisions no 895/2006/ec and no 582/2008/ec of the european parliament and of the council. this report is a natural step in regulating the control of persons at the external borders after croatia's accession to the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and welcome the commission's proposal to amend the list of third countries whose nationals need visas to cross the external borders of the union. i believe that one of the most powerful effects of this measure will be to strengthen and deepen the relations between the union and those countries as a result of this decision based on the trust we place in those countries. while welcoming the upcoming inclusion of the uae on the positive list, i would like to draw attention to some human rights issues in the region, and the importance of effective union cooperation with the country, which will also be an example of good practice for the entire region.
in writing. - the european commission proposes to lift the visa requirement for nationals of the caribbean and pacific island states as follows: the following entries are added to the list of countries and territories in which the union is to be established: the citizens of these states pose no threat to the european union, either in terms of illegal immigration or public security. visa liberalisation will reduce the time and costs of preparing for travel to the schengen area. in addition, the visa waiver facilitates contacts between citizens, which is a key condition for ensuring the development of economic, cultural, scientific and other relations. the visa regime also strengthens contacts between peoples and gives substance to the principle of free movement, which is one of the fundamental rights of the european union. the european parliament should be involved and informed as to the status of bilateral visa waiver agreements between the european union and third countries for which visa waiver is proposed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendment of the regulation establishing the list of third countries whose nationals are subject to the visa requirement for crossing the external borders of the member states and the list of those whose nationals are exempt from this requirement. this latest amendment transfers 19 countries from the negative list to the positive list, including 16 caribbean and pacific states, colombia, peru, and the united arab emirates. i also welcome the fact that an amendment now requires the commission to carry out a case-by-case assessment of various criteria relating in particular to illegal immigration, public order and security and the union's external relations with the third countries concerned, on the basis in particular of respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the implications of regional coherence and reciprocity should also be taken into account. finally, the introduction of an obligation to inform the european parliament regularly of the state of negotiations on bilateral agreements on visa waivers is a positive development which improves the transparency of the functioning of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 539/2001 establishing the list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders of the member states and the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from that requirement. the evolving nature of the eu visa policy and the growing need to ensure greater coherence between the visa policy and other eu policies justify the consideration of additional criteria when examining the lists of countries set out in annexes i and ii to regulation (ec) no 539/2001. the determination of the third countries whose nationals are subject to or exempt from the visa requirement should be subject to a careful assessment on a case-by-case basis. this evaluation should be carried out on a regular basis and should lead to proposals for amendments to the annexes to the regulation, without prejudice to the possibility of having, in certain circumstances, country-specific amendments to the annexes, for example as a result of the visa liberalisation process or as a final consequence of the temporary suspension of the exemption from the visa requirement.

in writing. the last decade has seen an increase in the use of remotely piloted aircraft systems, so-called drones, but there has been no development of the international legal framework governing the use of drones and no development of reporting on their effectiveness. we have to make sure that the use of drones does not have a negative impact on society by traumatizing civilians, seriously injuring them or even killing them. these drones must not become weapons of terror, but must reduce the loss of human life. i believe that there needs to be more transparency about the effectiveness of drones, both in terms of their impact on civil society and on the people who operate them.
in writing. - i voted for the european parliament resolution on the use of armed drones. unfortunately, the use of remotely piloted aircraft systems (drones) in lethal extraterritorial operations has increased sharply over the last decade. we invite the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, the member states and the council to include armed drones in relevant european and international disarmament and arms control regimes; to prohibit the development, production and use of fully autonomous weapons systems that allow attacks to be carried out without human intervention; to support the work and follow-up on the recommendations of the un special rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary and arbitrary executions and the un special rapporteur on the promotion and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the fight against terrorism. we also urge the council to adopt a common eu position on the use of drones.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the state of fundamental rights in the eu, for which i voted in favour. it makes recommendations to the european commission and the member states to better guarantee citizens' rights in the union. the current political climate in many countries is characterised by the rise of xenophobic rhetoric and mistrust of foreigners, whether they are nationals of third countries or even of countries of the european union. in response, the report stresses, for example, that the right to freedom of movement is a fundamental right that must be vigorously defended, and that any attempt to revise this acquis must be brought before the court of justice of the eu, in particular in cases of violation of the principle of non-discrimination on grounds of nationality. among many other recommendations, the resolution also proposes the establishment of a new mechanism to monitor, in a regular and objective manner, compliance with the eu accession criteria ('copenhagen criteria') when they are met. this mechanism would make it possible, in particular, to set objective indicators in order to avoid a 'double standard' system.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the situation of fundamental rights in the eu. fundamental freedoms, human rights and equal opportunities must be guaranteed for all eu citizens. we call on the member states and the commission to protect, promote and implement the rights of the child in all its actions and policies, both internal and external, that have an impact on them. we stress that the principle of human dignity, equality before the law and the prohibition of discrimination on any grounds are among the foundations of a democratic society. the union and the member states must step up their action on equality and anti-discrimination. we call on member states to guarantee decent wages and pensions, reduce the gender pay gap, create high quality jobs for women, ensure women's access to quality public services and improve social protection provisions for women. we call on member states to take action to tackle the economic and social causes that foster violence against women, such as unemployment, low wages and pensions, low housing, poverty and inadequate or non-existent public services, in particular public health, education and social security services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the european arrest warrant, although in force for over 10 years, has led to unsatisfactory results. on the one hand, this instrument represents an important step towards the realisation of a genuine single area of freedom, security and justice. on the other hand, the low number of warrants issued so far shows that improvements are needed. firstly, i believe that the instrument should be applied to offences of a certain degree of risk at european level. in addition, the absence of minimum standards for pre-trial detention can lead to abuses and excessive periods of application of this measure. that is why i join those who are calling on the european commission to come forward with a proposal to improve the european arrest warrant.
in writing. - the framework decision on the european arrest warrant, adopted in 2002, entered into force on 1 january 2004 and is the eu's most important legal instrument based on the principle of mutual recognition, whereby judgments are executed on the basis of mutual trust. the objective of this mandate was to speed up and facilitate the bringing of suspects or accused persons to justice by transforming the old and burdensome extradition procedures involving the political world into a new, faster system of surrender, through communication between judicial authorities. it shall request the requested member state to execute the warrant without any assessment of the merits of the charge or conviction. the commission should facilitate the establishment and ensure adequate funding of a dedicated european arrest warrant judicial network and a network of defence lawyers working in the field of european criminal justice and extradition matters, as well as the european judicial training network. in addition, in order to ensure the effectiveness of the mutual recognition framework, the commission should examine the legal and financial means made available at union level to improve detention standards, including legislative proposals on conditions of pre-trial detention.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it proposes to close a number of loopholes in the framework decision on the european arrest warrant. this legal instrument aims at communication and cooperation between european judicial authorities, facilitating surrender by setting strict deadlines and limiting the use of double incrimination as a ground for refusal. but the fact that only one fifth of the european arrest warrants issued between 2005 and 2009 were executed reveals the flaws highlighted in this report. the recommendation sent to the european commission draws attention to deficiencies such as the non-respect of procedural rights of suspects or accused persons, the poor conditions of detention, the alleged excessive use of this type of warrant by some member states and the non-application of the principle of proportionality. at the same time, member states are encouraged to implement european criminal law, in particular the provisions on the european investigation order, the european judicial supervision order and the measures on procedural rights.
in writing. - one of the main concerns in developing a single european area of freedom, security and justice is to improve the instruments of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the disappearance of internal borders also brings freedom of movement for criminals. according to eurostat, the number of union citizens serving a custodial sentence increased from 29 832 in 2006 to over 638 000 in 2010. this worrying increase demonstrates the need to create a single, functional criminal space with adequate tools to combat crime. we need the european arrest warrant because it is the most effective union legal instrument available to member states to prevent criminals from evading justice. i support the commission's proposal to reform the european arrest warrant procedures. extradition procedures should be carried out in a shorter time frame in order to facilitate the adjudication of cases by the competent courts and to improve the administration of justice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution containing recommendations to the commission on the review of the european arrest warrant. the eu has set itself the objective of offering its citizens an area of freedom, security and justice. in accordance with article 6 of the treaty on european union (teu), the eu respects human rights and fundamental freedoms. in order to be effective, the principle of mutual recognition must be based on mutual trust, which can only be achieved by ensuring respect for the fundamental rights of suspects and accused persons and for procedural rights in criminal proceedings throughout the union. mutual trust is strengthened through training, cooperation and dialogue between judicial and legal authorities, creating a genuine european judicial culture. we call on the member states to implement in a timely and effective manner the body of union measures in the field of criminal law, given that they are complementary, including the european investigation order, the european judicial supervision order and the measures on procedural rights. we invite the commission to closely monitor the correct implementation and their impact on the functioning of the european arrest warrant and the union criminal justice area.

in writing. - the common visa policy is a natural and necessary consequence of the abolition of internal border controls within the schengen area, and the treaty of lisbon provides for the use of the ordinary legislative procedure for all aspects of the common visa policy and for parliament's consent to all international agreements in this field. the european commission and the member states should improve the implementation of the current visa acquis and, in particular, step up local schengen cooperation with a view to improving the short-term implementation of the visa code. member states should make use of the current provisions of the visa code and the schengen borders code, allowing for the issuance of humanitarian visas and facilitating the temporary shelter of human rights defenders at risk in third countries. full visa reciprocity is also an objective that the union should actively pursue in its relations with third countries, thus contributing to enhancing the credibility and consistency of the union's external policy at international level.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, the current difficult economic and financial situation requires decisive policy action, and the eib’s activity is a crucial component of our efforts to bring back growth and employment to europe. in this difficult environment it is important that the eib assumes its role as a policy-driven bank, acts as a countercyclical institution and continues to provide financing to the real economy, especially in regions and sectors where funds are not available from other sources on reasonable terms. i am convinced that parliamentʼs assessment of the eibʼs activities in the year ahead will be as supportive as its opinion on the 2012 annual report, and i look forward to continued close and successful cooperation between the commission and the bank. finally, i would like to thank you again for the excellent collaboration in the preparations for the eif capital increase. we look forward to bringing this important project to a successful outcome with you.
european investment bank. - madam president, let me start by thanking the commission for its very good cooperation. the work that the european investment bank does would not be possible without the very close and trusting cooperation between the commission and the bank. i would also like to thank all the members of the european parliament who have contributed to this debate today, as well as in the committee meetings. this has been very encouraging for us. of course, in a dynamic and vibrant parliament there will also be contradictions in the arguments that are presented. i probably cannot do justice to each and every one of you who has contributed to this debate today, but i promise that we will come back to each of you individually if there are matters that i am unable to respond to here today. let me say that i read bankwatch and publications from other institutions too. i believe that sometimes you may be misled a little and that the reinforcement of prejudices or stereotypes does not really serve any purpose. i would like to say here that it is pure nonsense that only 5[nbsp ]% of the volume of investment goes to programme countries. we will come back to this in more detail. i would also like to stress that the capital increase granted by the member states – with the support of the parliament and the commission – has also enabled us to considerably raise the risk profile of the bank’s activities. this was very helpful for us, but raising the risk profile does not mean wasting money. this is a balance sheet. the eib is not there to give grants. the eib is first and foremost a bank. this is its raison d’être and the basis for everything we do, because every cent we lend comes from the capital markets. we must have the strongest possible status in the capital markets in order to be able to do such business. i would also like to say that, when you enter upon a short-term request from the european council concerning the big challenge of youth unemployment in europe, you are under huge pressure to act quickly. time is of the essence. if we want to address the issue of youth unemployment seriously, we must speed up the process. we succeeded not only in beginning the disbursement of the pledged eur[nbsp ]6[nbsp ]billion within one month from early july to early august, but also in disbursing 50[nbsp ]% more than we had pledged. so do not expect the final analysis of the success story yet. it is simply too soon. i think we might even have to recalibrate – there is no doubt about this – after due analysis. we will do this. there have been huge developments in the bank. when this bank was founded under the treaty of rome, nobody would have thought of doing business with smes on a short-term basis. at that time, the bank was conceived of as a long-term lender for big infrastructure projects. last year, we increased the volume of sme lending by almost a hundred percent to eur 22 billion. this is a huge process that has changed the character of the bank. the developments on the capital markets and the state of affairs in banking are not such that we can assume that this pressure on smes will be reduced in the next couple of years. my concern is that, with the necessary changes in the process of achieving banking union, we might see a further credit crunch for smes in particular. we will therefore be present in this business as well. the question about blue chip companies and smes is a contradiction that reflects old thinking. we are now living in a completely different world where the dual approach between smes and large corporations has produced the global value chain. integration and interaction between companies of different sizes is therefore the name of the game in the modern world. we can see that, in some countries, additional activity in sme business is probably necessary. we will come back to that, but i do not want to contribute to speculation about developments in the banking systems of individual countries. we can do that in detail as well. i would like to express a major concern which i have for the european economy. over ten years, the european economy has seen a reduction in investment. the investment level in the european union and the member states, today and over the last couple of years, is constantly some 15[nbsp ]% below the value of 2007. what does that mean for the quality of the capital stock in the european union? it is deteriorating from year to year because we do not invest enough. in addition to that, the european union is losing ground to its global competitors when it comes to innovation, research, the promotion of technology, and education. the average contribution to innovation – the knowledge economy – in general in south korea, japan or the united states is far beyond 3[nbsp ]% of gdp per year. in europe for the last ten years, it has been consistently below 2[nbsp ]%, with huge differences among the member states. so there is not only an investment gap but also an innovation gap in europe. i wonder what our position in the world markets will be if we do not stop that trend very quickly. therefore, i fully support the idea of doing more for smes. however, i also fully support the idea of finally jumping on the innovation wagon. is our infrastructure in europe really perfect? i am rather doubtful about that. consequently, i believe that it will be very difficult to end up with a balanced portfolio in the eib. but this is something i am ready to discuss with you in detail, just as i am ready to give detailed answers to any of your questions individually if i could not give a quick response here today.

question referred under the 'blue card' procedure madam president, i would like to ask mrs delvaux whether she does not think that the gender equality report should also include equality in terms of the professional reintegration of women after long periods of absence, and i am referring here to the need for member states to increase the budget for childcare, especially for children aged 0 to 3 but even up to 7 years, in order to expand the public network of day care, nursery and services providing extracurricular services? we know that in europe there are waiting lists for kindergartens and kindergartens up to 2 years old. i believe that equal opportunities must also solve this problem.
the problem of social equality between women and men raises a number of questions, which can be analysed from several perspectives. it is essential that we can enforce the principle of equal pay for equal work, as statistics consistently show that this is a very serious discriminatory situation. i am convinced that promoting greater participation of women in decision-making, and thus increasing the proportion of women in the various bodies, would have a positive impact on our decisions. all questions require the kind of approach that is more typical of our female colleagues. the most important aspect of the problem, however, is the lack of family policy measures. we must do everything possible to ensure that women's decision to have children, the number of children, is less dependent on the economic situation of the family. when and how many children a family has should not be an economic decision. at the same time, we must help women to make reasonable compromises between raising children and building a career. the aim is to reconcile family life and the world of work, and there is still much to be done in this area.
mr president, the strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 finds that, although women represent almost half of the workforce in the european union and more than half of university graduates, they are still under-represented in decision-making processes and positions. a particular problem is rural women, who have a much lower employment rate than urban women. many rural women have never been active in the labour market; thus, they are not registered as unemployed, which leads to financial and legal problems in terms of entitlement to maternity leave and sick leave, to acquiring pension rights and social security. representation rates, family responsibilities, equal pay, introducing gender quotas for employers, representation rates in decision-making, skills and abilities doubles are important steps that can contribute to gender equality in the european union.

mr president, in the 21st century, seeking employment, working in a foreign country and living there to do that work are fundamental rights of the union. a person who wishes to work in a geographical area other than that of his country shall enjoy the same treatment as nationals of that country as regards access to the labour market, working conditions and other social and tax advantages. equally, the right to work also implies the right to strike, to draw attention in a peaceful way to the violation of fundamental rights, as romanian citizens in florence, italy, who were attacked by the authorities while peacefully protesting their rights, thought it appropriate to do. we are able, as european citizens, to show solidarity with the situation of any individual whose rights have been minimized or cancelled, guaranteed and absolutely legal in the european union.
the european commission's task is to speak to all the citizens of the union, to all its communities. romania has a hungarian community of almost one and a half million people, yet the communication of the commission's romanian representation is missing the hungarian language. i regret that the members of the hungarian community in romania do not receive information from the commission through the media in their mother tongue. the number of hungarians in romania is larger than the total population of some member states. there are as many hungarians in romania as the entire population of estonia, and we are more than the population of cyprus, luxembourg or malta. hungarians in romania have the same right to information in their mother tongue as swedes in finland, catalans in spain, germans in belgium and turks in cyprus. i would ask the european commission to introduce information in hungarian at its romanian representation.
today, in marosvásárhely, hungarians living in romania again held a peaceful demonstration demanding the autonomy of the szeklerland region, which has a hungarian majority. for decades, the nearly one and a half million hungarians in romania have been demanding that szeklerland, which is inhabited by a majority of hungarians, should be a region with a special status, with greater decision-making powers, while respecting the territorial integrity of romania. international practice shows that the various forms of autonomy greatly facilitate peaceful and harmonious cooperation between ethnic groups. the message of today's demonstration is that there are still many unanswered questions about the situation of hungarians living in romania, and the community is peacefully voicing its dissatisfaction and asking the government for dialogue. i hope that the international community will also listen to the voice of the hungarians in romania.
member of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank all those who have participated in this debate, but i would like first of all to reply to some of the criticisms regarding the eib investing in projects outside the european union. first of all, we are not an inward-looking european union. it is true that there is that english proverb which says ‘charity begins at home’, which is the most abused proverb in the english language. it does begin at home, because 90[nbsp ]% of all the funds of the european investment bank go to projects within the european union, so let us not run away with this idea that the eib is squandering money on projects outside the european union. so there is 10[nbsp ]% – and here we are dealing with 10[nbsp ]% of the funding as regards guarantees – that goes to projects outside the european union. since these are long-term projects, it is important, if the bank is to retain its aaa grading, that we give this guarantee to the european investment bank. but to say – because the criticism leads to this conclusion – that we should reduce that 10[nbsp ]% in funding for projects outside the european union would mean that we would create a european ghetto where we only do things for ourselves, and this would weaken our external action and foreign policy. let us take ukraine, for instance. right now we have this country, ukraine, which has a strong european perspective. while we have some euro-scepticism within the european union, we have people in ukraine who have died while waving european flags. should we abandon ukraine, particularly at this moment in time, when part of its territory has been invaded by another country? so what are we doing for ukraine? first of all, ukraine is one of the eligible countries under the proposed decision, so if we vote in favour of this decision today, we are indirectly also helping ukraine. the bank already has a priority project pipeline in ukraine of up to eur[nbsp ]1.5 billion for the next three years and could significantly scale this up if adequate guarantee provisions are granted and if the political and operational conditions allow it. should we diminish the 10[nbsp ]% and exclude ukraine? of course not. the bank could just provide finance in ukraine for long-term investments of up to eur[nbsp ]3 billion for 2014-2016 in support of both the local private sector and economic and social infrastructure. i disagree with those who have asked if we are doing this to bribe eastern european countries to join the european union. first of all, i take pride in the fact that there is a long waiting list of countries who want to join. if they want to join something, they must see something very good in the organisation they want to join. until now, there is no waiting list of countries which want to leave the european union, only of countries that want to join, but to say that we are bribing them – it is not bribing them, it is assisting them to fulfil the european dream for which some of them have died. the european union’s eur[nbsp ]4.8 billion ceiling for the eastern neighbourhood in the proposed decision is sufficient to cover this increase of eib operations in ukraine in the short term, and there is scope to increase this further under the flexibility to reallocate across regions. following the mid-term review, as i said in my opening speech, there is also the option to activate the optional mandate of eur[nbsp ]3 billion. my friend ms abela baldacchino, from malta, mentioned the mediterranean. the european union and the west invested so much, in the so-called arab spring, in the revolutions in three countries – egypt, libya and tunisia – where, for the first time, we have had democratic elections, in spite of the turbulence and vicissitudes of these revolutions. but we have had free elections for the first time in decades in these three countries. we have invested so much politically in north africa that we cannot abandon them to their fate, and the projects financed by the european investment bank in north africa are a way of doing politics, of doing foreign policy in our neighbourhood. in conclusion, i recommend that we adopt this decision. i would like to reiterate the commission’s support for this proposal for a decision and underline once again the value of this tool to the european union in supporting the promotion and implementation of the eu’s external policies in our partner countries.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a necessary step in a wide range of structural changes in inland waterway transport. in other words, the text voted today empowers the european commission to adopt delegated acts, in the light of economic and/or technological trends, to adapt the scope of data collection and the content of the annexes. all these measures will facilitate the development and publication of criteria and methodological requirements designed to ensure the quality of the data produced. i also support the rapporteur's view that the development of a coherent and timely inland waterway transport policy will be facilitated by the collection of data on both passengers and goods carried.
in writing. - inland waterway transport in europe for freight and passenger transport, including in urban river agglomerations, can and must play an important role in the european economy to enable the full contribution of this sector to the europe 2020 strategy. currently, there are still a number of obstacles to be overcome, such as the lack of adequate infrastructure or infrastructure charges. i support the rapporteur's proposal that an accurate picture of airworthiness in the union can only be obtained on the basis of reliable and objective statistical data. they will enable the union to develop and implement an appropriate policy in this area, which will lead to the development of an integrated, safe, environmentally friendly and competitive mode of transport (including social aspects) and the creation of new jobs at european level. i also believe that the eu should also support efforts to renew and retrain the inland waterway fleet, which would lead to more environmental benefits.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on statistics of inland waterway freight transport as regards the conferral of delegated and implementing powers on the commission to adopt certain measures. in order to take account of economic and technological developments, the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union should be delegated to the commission in respect of adapting the statistical coverage threshold for inland waterway transport, adapting definitions and adopting new definitions, and adapting the content of the annexes. in order to develop an appropriate inland waterway transport policy and to ensure consistency in the collection of statistical data for all modes of transport, both passenger and goods data should be collected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the commission's proposal because the economic crisis has shown us the need to systematically correct macroeconomic imbalances. the quality and accuracy of the statistics on them are relevant for the assessment of national economic and fiscal policies at european level before they are adopted in the member states, and beyond. effective monitoring of the statistical quality of indicators as well as of basic statistical information is therefore vital in the policy context of improving the economic governance of the union. last but not least, close cooperation with the statistical authorities of the member states will be needed for all these data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments adopted by the european parliament on 11 march 2014 concerning the proposal for a regulation on the provision and quality of statistics for the macroeconomic imbalances procedure. the detection, prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances is necessary to improve the economic governance of the union. the proposal for a regulation lays down the rules governing the way statistical data relevant for the macroeconomic imbalances procedure are provided. these rules concern the development, quality monitoring and publication of the indicators in the scoreboard for the macroeconomic imbalances procedure. the main objective of the regulation is to develop a reliable quality monitoring procedure with the aim of ensuring the best quality of data relevant for the macroeconomic imbalances procedure (mip). the relevant data for map to be transmitted by member states shall refer to the previous year (n-1) and the previous nine years (n-2 to n-10). i consider that the suspension of funds following the application of the macroeconomic imbalances procedure should only be a measure of last resort and should take into account in-depth analyses of indicators on unemployment, poverty and declining gdp.
in writing. - i voted to extend the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the united states of america for a further period of five years. this is an agreement dating back to 1998 and which benefits both parties by promoting the interest in continuing cooperation in these areas, thus bringing socioeconomic benefits. in a different vein, member states and the commission need to encourage international cooperation in global research infrastructures, and at the same time explore new ways of reducing the digital and technological gap in developing countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the extension of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the united states of america approving the extension of the agreement for a further period of five years. by decision 98/591/ec, the council approved the conclusion of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the united states of america (the 'agreement'). pursuant to article 12 (b) of the agreement, it is concluded for an initial period of five years and may be extended, subject to any amendments, for further periods of five years by mutual agreement in writing between the parties. by council decision 2009/306/ec, the agreement was extended for a further period of five years. the parties to the agreement consider that a rapid renewal of this agreement would be in their mutual interest. the content of the extended agreement is identical to that of the agreement expiring on 14 october 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european union ratifying the nagoya protocol and i think it is very important that all member states ratify it as soon as possible. such a protocol on access to genetic resources and fair sharing of benefits is, in my view, a key instrument in the service of a new vision for biodiversity. i say this because this enhanced cooperation will result in the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity and, by extension, the environment, thus contributing to the achievement of the millennium development goals.
in writing. - the nagoya protocol is a particularly important agreement for the international governance of biodiversity, as it establishes an international regime to support one of the three objectives of the convention on biological diversity, namely the fair and equitable distribution of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources to enable the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity. this agreement is all the more important as it comes in the context of a global biodiversity crisis, which is tending to worsen, threatening the extinction of more and more species and putting considerable pressure on ecosystems. the nagoya protocol can reverse this trend by mobilising the international resources needed to preserve biodiversity vital to our societies. the nagoya protocol will enter into force shortly after it has been ratified by 50 states. it is essential that the european union and all its member states ratify it as soon as possible in order to maintain its leadership and be present at the table for the first negotiations to take place at the next conference of the parties in 2014.
in writing. - scientists are drawing attention to the fact that one in three species is threatened with extinction and sounding the alarm about the pressure on ecosystems. biodiversity is vital to humanity, and ecosystems are important because of the services they provide to citizens, no matter where they live. as such, europe must be involved in order to mobilise all the necessary resources, at european and international level, mainly financial, to preserve biodiversity, and one means of achieving this is the implementation of the nagoya protocol. i therefore consider it essential that all member states and the european union ratify this document as soon as possible so that europe can maintain its leadership status and negotiate with the other partners in this position at the next conference this year.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilization to the convention on biological diversity, approving the conclusion of the agreement. in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and in particular article 191 thereof, the european union is competent to conclude international agreements and to implement the obligations resulting therefrom, contributing to the achievement of the following objectives: the conservation, protection and improvement of the quality of the environment, the protection of human health, the prudent and rational use of natural resources, and the promotion at international level of measures to address regional or global environmental problems, and in particular to combat climate change.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the adoption of the regulation on certain procedures for applying the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of serbia, of the other part. i also voted against amendment no 1, which rejects the council's position at first reading. a stabilisation and association agreement (saa) between the eu and serbia was signed in luxembourg on 29 april 2008. it entered into force on 1 september 2013. with a view to the effective implementation of the saa, the commission has proposed a regulation on certain procedures for the implementation of trade-related aspects of the saa. this regulation lays down rules and procedures for the adoption of detailed rules for the implementation of certain provisions of the eu-serbia stabilisation and association agreement and of the eu-serbia interim agreement on trade and other trade-related matters.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as i have done for all the legislative initiatives that have benefited from the experience of the financial crisis and the shortcomings of financial supervision. the changes introduced by eiopa and esma are the result of the need to redefine the financial architecture and to increase the degree of harmonisation of national and european financial policies. monitoring and assessing potential risks needs to be carried out with the utmost diligence to ensure financial stability in the face of macroeconomic and financial system developments as a whole, and all to guarantee the transparency of financial markets and products, as well as the protection of all european citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directives 2003/71/ec and 2009/138/ec as regards the powers of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority, adopting the european parliament's position at first reading. the financial crisis of 2007 and 2008 highlighted wide gaps in financial supervision both in specific cases and in the financial system as a whole. the crisis has brought to the fore shortcomings in the areas of cooperation, coordination, consistent application of union law and trust between national competent authorities. the areas for which amendments are proposed generally fall into the following categories: defining the appropriate field of technical standards as an additional tool to achieve convergence of supervisory practices and to develop a single regulatory framework; properly integrating the possibility for authorities to resolve disagreements in a balanced way in those areas where joint decision-making processes already exist in sectoral legislation; general common amendments to most sectoral legislation and necessary for the proper functioning of the directives in the context of the establishment of new authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the constant evolution of technology and the means available to potential criminals in money laundering are real challenges that need to be addressed through enhanced, cross-border and, not least, proactive cooperation. this can be done by implementing international standards in the field as a matter of priority and by continuously monitoring and evaluating their application in practice. improving the traceability of payments will also lead to greater transparency. moreover, it is an effective way of countering the current trend of money laundering moving from developed countries to the least developed, where the legislation is lax and more permissive.
in writing. - i support this report because i believe we need transparency in the transfer of funds at european level. knowledge of the originator and the beneficiary of the payment is a valuable tool for the prevention, detection and investigation of money laundering and terrorist financing. the global money laundering flow is estimated to amount to approximately 2.7% of global gdp. this figure can only be reduced by registering the owners of companies and investment funds in public registers, by making it impossible for criminals to hide behind secret accounts and offshore companies. it is important that payment service providers observe whether the information provided is complete and correct and, if this is not the case, that they can take the necessary measures to correct the gaps.
in writing. - i support the proposal for a regulation requiring the registration of the data of any payer or payee who makes or receives a transfer of funds of more than eur 1[nbsp ]000 both within the european union and between the union and other countries. the data recorded will help national and european authorities to identify money laundering attempts through transfers of funds more quickly and easily. between 2008 and 2010, an average of 15[nbsp ]000 money laundering cases were recorded at union level. of these, only an average of 3[nbsp ]000 natural or legal persons were convicted by a court decision in the same period. access to a complete and transparent database of all money transfers at union level will increase the efficiency of authorities in detecting, investigating and punishing money laundering. i call on the european commission to monitor the urgent application of the new regulation in all the funds transfer systems already in place in the european union, in order to increase the transparency of financial transfers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds. the regulation on transfers of funds lays down rules requiring payment service providers to transmit information on the payer throughout the payment chain for the purposes of preventing, investigating and detecting money laundering and terrorist financing. considers it important to improve traceability by imposing key requirements such as the inclusion of information on the beneficiary of the payment; as regards the scope of the regulation will be subject to the provisions of the regulation if used for the transfer of funds from one person to another and credit or debit cards, mobile phone or any other digital or it device; as regards the obligations of the payment service provider towards the beneficiary of the payment, to impose a requirement that the identity of the beneficiary (if not previously identified) must be verified in the case of payments from outside the eu with a value of over eur 1[nbsp000]; align the data protection requirements for the retention of information with the standards of the international financial action task force.
in writing. - i supported this report which i consider extremely important from many points of view. the financial crisis has taught us some hard lessons, but some extremely useful ones, i might add. i think the most important phenomenon that we've seen in the last few years is this revolution of transparency that we can see in the financial and banking sector. we have undertaken a series of tough policies against tax havens, money laundering and all types of financial fraud, and reforms must continue. although we have strict legislation and a specialised authority in this area, the crime of money laundering is a common practice in my country too. in the first half of 2013, the national office for the prevention and combating of money laundering suspended financial operations of almost eur 10 million. last but not least, we are talking about a fight that must be waged first at national level and then consolidated at european level.
in writing. - i welcome the vote on this report, as the new directive aims to improve the current framework to prevent the transformation of funds obtained from criminal activities into legitimate funds through the financial system. the commission proposal is drawn up to follow its review of the implementation of the current directive and to reflect changes to the non-binding recommendations issued by the international financial action task force. the rapporteurs made a number of improvements to this proposal. first, they suggest improving trade registers - it is essential in preventing money laundering and terrorist financing, identifying the beneficial owner of commercial activities or commercial transactions. secondly, the rapporteurs support the eu-wide risk assessment of money laundering in order to achieve an optimal allocation of resources. third, they propose that the approach be based on prevention and should be precise and proportionate and should not be a system of generalized control of the entire population.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to implement a directive on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing. the aim of this directive is to improve the current framework to prevent the financial system from being used for the conversion of proceeds of criminal activities into lawful funds. the new rules adopted by parliament and advocated by the socialist and democratic group will make it possible to strengthen the fight against money laundering, in particular by creating a public register of business owners in the european union. these new rules, which still need to be adopted by the member states, will extend the scope of existing legislation to include new sectors, such as the gambling sector. money laundering, with an estimated turnover of almost €600 billion a year, is often linked to major crime, terrorism, racketeering, corruption and human trafficking. it is also the cause of colossal losses for european tax regimes, and that is why it must be fought as vigorously as possible.
in writing. - according to the international monetary fund, money laundering is a widespread phenomenon, estimated at 5% of world gdp. this is why the current legal framework to prevent the proceeds of criminal activities from being 'legitimated' through the financial system needs to be improved. i therefore believe that action is needed to improve the business register system and to carefully review the risk of recycling at eu level. criminal activities undermine the integrity of the financial sector, cause governments to lose revenue, hinder competition and have a negative impact on the proper functioning of markets. for these reasons i welcome the adoption of the report today.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption of the proposal for a directive on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing; in view of the scale of money laundering, estimated at 5% of world gdp, i consider that the legal framework in force under directive 2006/70/ec needs to be improved. by registering the owners of companies and investment funds in public registers, we can prevent money laundering through the financial system, for example by hiding criminals behind secret accounts and offshore companies. the impact of the directive is all the greater as the registers will be interconnected and publicly available. they also support the legal demand that banks, auditors, lawyers, real estate agents and casinos be more vigilant about suspicious transactions of their customers. last but not least, i believe it is useful to extend the rules on politically exposed persons, whose positions expose them to acts of corruption, to politically exposed persons at the domestic level, such as persons appointed to prominent public office, such as head of state, member of the government, supreme court judge and member of parliament.
in writing. - we need to have adequate means and tools to prevent criminals from placing funds from illicit activities in the financial system. according to the un, money laundering accounts for 2.7% of global gdp, or about $1,600 billion in 2009 alone. combating fraudulent use of the financial system and money laundering is a priority. financial transfers must be made in a transparent way, and for this we need trade registers to which the real beneficiaries are entered. for greater efficiency, registers need to be interconnected and accessible to authorities so that they can check who is benefiting from commercial transactions. the new rules will improve transparency and provide a better overview of financial transactions, making it harder for dirty money to move from one account to another.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing. overcoming barriers within the internal market not only facilitates the creation or growth of businesses that operate legally within the eu, but can also provide increased opportunities for money laundering and terrorist financing. this proposal includes and repeals directive 2006/70/ec laying down implementing measures for directive 2005/60/ec, thus improving the comprehensibility and accessibility of the legislative framework on anti-money laundering (aml) for all interested parties. the main changes are: extension of the scope of the directive: two main changes to the scope are proposed: (a) lowering the threshold for high value merchants making cash payments from eur 15[nbsp ]000 to eur 7[nbsp ]500, (b) the scope of the directive includes 'gambling service providers'. the current directive, as well as the revised fatf recommendations, require that only casinos be included in the scope of the legislation on anti-money laundering/combating terrorist financing. beneficiary information: the revised directive proposes new measures to make beneciary information clearer and more accessible.
in writing. - financing operations designed to complement and support the union's external policies clearly carry a significantly higher risk than locally-developed operations. hence the need to ensure a higher level of security for these external credit operations. the bank's capital needs to be increased to the extent necessary to ensure that the bank's capital needs are met. another important aspect is that all eib investments must be properly aligned with the development strategies developed by the countries concerned. on another note, i would like to stress that the eib must stop paying loans to projects that are the subject of national or european corruption investigations.
in writing. - the eib's union external action guarantee effectively combines eu budgetary funds and own resources to achieve the 2020 external policy objectives. the objective is to focus the eib's mandate on beneficiaries for whom the use of the guarantee would bring greater added value and would gradually eliminate environmentally and economically harmful subsidies. the commission proposal therefore contains important elements concerning the general principles guiding the union's external action, information obligations, the need to assess the effects on development and public participation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision to grant an eu guarantee to the european investment bank (eib) for losses resulting from operations supporting investment projects outside the european union. the financing of the eib guarantee for the period 2014-2020 is a necessary condition for the optimal implementation of the european union's external policy and of eib investment projects in developing countries. the eur 27 billion guarantee, together with the optional amount of eur 3 billion that can be mobilised, should not become an objective in itself but should remain the ceiling for eib financing under the eu guarantee. i also believe it is very important that the european investment bank provides technical assistance to beneficiaries to prepare and implement projects, to strengthen local capacities and to encourage economic growth. the eib's technical assistance should be complementary to that provided by other eu bodies. they also believe that eib investments should be aligned with the development strategies developed by the countries concerned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council granting an eu guarantee to the european investment bank (eib) against losses resulting from financing operations supporting investment projects outside the union. the eu guarantee shall be granted as a comprehensive guarantee for payments due to, but not received by, the eib in respect of loans, loan guarantees and capital market loan instruments granted or issued for the benefit of eib investment projects, which are granted or issued by the eib for the benefit of investment projects carried out in eligible countries in accordance with the eib's own rules and procedures, including the eib's statement of social and environmental principles and standards, and in support of the relevant union foreign policy objectives, where eib financing has been granted in accordance with a signed agreement which has neither expired nor been cancelled. the eu guarantee shall cover eib financing operations signed during the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020. the maximum ceiling of eib financing operations covered by the eu guarantee for the period 2014-2020 shall not exceed eur 30[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000;
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution because the conservation of biological diversity must remain an important objective of the eu, especially in the context of the strategy we have undertaken and through which we aim to avoid the loss of biodiversity worldwide by 2020. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's climate change policy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's climate change policy. in another sense, genetic resources play a particularly important role for food and agriculture, and therefore ultimately for our food security.
in writing. - genetic resources play a significant role in the development and implementation of appropriate international strategies for restoring degraded ecosystems and recovering threatened species. genetic resources must be kept in situ and used sustainably, and the benefits arising from their use must be distributed fairly and equitably. benefit-sharing needs to be considered, as biodiversity-rich developing countries dominate the provision of genetic resources, while the majority of users are in developed countries. i believe that equitable access to benefit-sharing can contribute to poverty eradication and environmental conservation, thereby leading to progress towards the achievement of the millennium development goals, as recognised in the preamble to the nagoya protocol. today's vote ensures that european policy is brought as close as possible to the spirit and letter of this international treaty and that the mechanisms for the effective implementation of this protocol are strengthened. at the same time, we ensure that the european union maintains its leadership role in current and future international negotiations by promoting a progressive stance that can meet the challenges of conserving biodiversity and its sustainable use.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from their use in the union. the proposal for a regulation lays down rules governing access to and benefit-sharing from genetic resources and traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources in accordance with the provisions of the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilization to the convention on biological diversity (nagoya protocol). the nagoya protocol is a new international treaty, adopted on 29 october 2010 by consensus of the 193 parties to the convention on biological diversity (cbd). it applies to genetic resources over which states exercise sovereign rights and to traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources to which access is obtained after the entry into force of the nagoya protocol for the union. it shall also apply to benefits arising from the use of such genetic resources and traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources. it does not apply to genetic resources for which access and benefit-sharing are regulated by a specialised international instrument to which the union is a party.
in writing. - i voted for the legislative resolution. the whole package on vehicle safety is also extremely important for european road traffic. a well-maintained motor vehicle that meets all safety requirements is less likely to cause a road accident. regular roadworthiness tests are perhaps one of the most important precautions we can take to ensure the safety of both drivers and all road users involved. the technical compliance of motor vehicles on european roads must therefore be treated with the utmost seriousness and those who ignore these obligations must be severely sanctioned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that a minimum standard is needed for the periodic technical inspection of motor vehicles and trailers. taking into account the large number of vehicles on the roads in the union, it is necessary to regulate in such a way as to ensure adequate safety of road users. the introduction of scooters and motorcycles into the mandatory minimum inspection system is to be welcomed. this range of vehicles is increasingly common in traffic and any defect poses a maximum risk to both the driver and other road users. the re-registration of vehicles in other countries will also be much easier as the issued roadworthiness certificates will be recognised on a reciprocal basis in all member states.
in writing. - i voted for the directive on the periodic roadworthiness test of motor vehicles and their trailers and repealing directive[nbsp ]2009/40/ec. this directive establishes minimum requirements for the system of periodic roadworthiness tests for vehicles on public roads. this applies to vehicles with a design speed exceeding 25[nbsp ]km/h and belonging to a certain category of vehicles (category m1; m2 and m3, n1; n2; n3; o3 and o4). member states may introduce additional national requirements on roadworthiness tests for vehicles registered in their territory which are not covered by this directive. each member state shall ensure that vehicles registered in its territory are inspected regularly in accordance with this directive in inspection centres authorised by the member state of registration of those vehicles. technical inspections shall be carried out by the member state in which the vehicle is registered, by a public body empowered to do so by that member state or by bodies or institutions designated and supervised by that member state, including authorised private bodies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which will help to improve the mobility of european car owners, but also to facilitate cross-border sales. the measures relating to the registration procedure will also ensure that vehicles which pose an immediate risk to road safety are not used in traffic. the benefits of such harmonization do not stop there. a particular case is, for example, a change of vehicle owner or a re-registration of a vehicle in another member state. in this situation, it is evident that the technical conditions of the vehicle are not changed. it is therefore natural that the valid vehicle inspection certificate should be recognised and mentioned on the new registration certificate.
in writing. - i voted for this report because this legislative proposal improves the application of the vehicle inspection and roadworthiness regime, in particular where the technical condition of a vehicle creates an imminent risk to road safety, through measures such as temporary withdrawal or permanent cancellation of the vehicle's registration certificate. the document states that each member state is obliged to register for the first time any vehicle that has received european type-approval, on the basis of the 'certificate of conformity' issued by the vehicle manufacturer. this registration is the official authorisation for the use of a motor vehicle in traffic. compared to the existing documents, the current legislation provides for more precise definitions of the place of registration and introduces the possibility of withdrawal or cancellation of the 'registration certificate'. the certificate shall be withdrawn from motor vehicles which do not meet the standard road safety conditions and returned to the owner after passing another roadworthiness test. for motor vehicles to be registered, the 'registration certificate' shall be automatically cancelled. with regard to registrations in different member states, a motor vehicle re-registered in another country results in the automatic cancellation of the original registration in the member state in which it was originally registered.
in writing. - i voted to amend council directive 1999/37/ec on the registration documents for vehicles. the technical inspection is a component part of a wider regime which ensures that vehicles are maintained in a safe and environmentally acceptable condition during their use. that regime should provide for periodic roadworthiness tests and roadworthiness tests of vehicles used in commercial road transport activities, as well as provisions on a vehicle registration procedure to allow the suspension of the authorisation to use in road traffic a vehicle which constitutes an immediate risk to road safety. this directive should not prevent a member state from considering the electronic database managed by its competent authorities as the main source of information relating to a vehicle registered in its territory. member states should be able to use an electronic network including data from national electronic databases to facilitate the exchange of information. where a roadworthiness test has revealed dangerous deficiencies and the authorisation to use a vehicle in traffic has been suspended, the suspension should be recorded until the vehicle passes a new roadworthiness test.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because road safety on european roads needs to be improved, with over 5 people dying every day in accidents caused by technical problems. vehicle and roadworthiness tests are fundamental in this respect, as they are the only way to guarantee the compatibility of vehicles with traffic on public roads. we are talking about measures that already exist, but which have been improved and harmonised so that vehicles that pose an immediate threat to road safety are gradually but definitively removed from traffic.
in writing. - in 2010, the european commission adopted strategic amendments for road safety and to achieve the target of reducing the number of road deaths by 50% between 2010 and 2020. the security of citizens has been one of the priorities which has guided the procedures and negotiations of recent years. to this end, work has been done to improve the level of harmonisation of european legislation, to increase the number and quality of roadworthiness tests and inspections, and to establish a european electronic platform for the exchange of this information. today's vote was in favour of improving the controls on commercial vehicles in the eu to ensure the safety of all european citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on roadworthiness tests for commercial vehicles. i believe that harmonising union legislation on vehicle safety testing would increase the safety of road users and actively contribute to the commission's announced target of reducing accidents in the european union by 50% between 2010 and 2020. i agree with the introduction of vehicles under 3,5 tonnes under traffic controls because according to statistics, this category of vehicles has not seen a decrease in the number of road accidents. due to its legal status, this category of vehicles is used intensively, which makes it subject to more pronounced wear in a shorter period of time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on roadworthiness tests for commercial vehicles circulating in the union and repealing directive 2000/30/ec. a number of technical standards and requirements relating to vehicle safety and environmental characteristics have been adopted in the union. it is necessary to ensure, by means of a regime of technical checks in unplanned traffic, that vehicles remain in conformity with the technical rules applicable to traffic on public roads. in order to minimise the time lost by businesses and drivers and to increase the overall efficiency of traffic controls, the performance of technical traffic controls should be encouraged alongside controls to verify compliance with social legislation in the field of road transport. this directive develops the existing regime on technical roadside inspections, updates the technical requirements of directive 2000/30/ec and includes the rules contained in commission recommendation 2010/379/eu. directive 2000/30/ec should therefore be repealed.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the measures proposed by this directive constitute an important new step towards a public administration that does not involve paper-based documentation. this means, on the one hand, lower costs and, on the other, time savings. interoperability between systems encourages businesses to engage in cross-border public procurement, thus increasing competition and strengthening the single market as a whole. this will stimulate entrepreneurship, especially smes, leading to job creation and economic growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on electronic invoicing, which will certainly be a major step forward in the transparency of public procurement procedures, with predictable effects on the successful implementation of projects financed by european funds. this new system will bring more integration to the single market by encouraging competitiveness in cross-border auctions. by drawing up european standards in the field of electronic invoicing that are easy to understand and implement, the european union could eliminate the problems of exchanging invoices between member states, thus reducing complexity and legal uncertainty for businesses. moreover, studies show that e-invoicing would reduce public sector costs by eur 2.3 billion, which could be directed to other areas of high importance to european citizens, such as health or education.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on electronic invoicing in public procurement. according to the adopted directive, this applies to electronic invoices issued as a result of the execution of contracts to which the public procurement directives apply. i am of the opinion that the european standard on electronic invoicing should meet at least the following criteria: be technologically neutral, be compatible with the relevant international standards on electronic invoicing, take into account the need to protect personal data, allow for the creation of practical, user-friendly, flexible and cost-effective electronic invoicing systems, take into account the special needs of small and medium-sized enterprises as well as regional and local contracting authorities and contracting entities, and be suitable for use in business-to-business commercial transactions. according to the adopted directive, the main elements of an electronic invoice will be, inter alia: (a) process and invoice identifiers; (b) invoice period; (c) information about the seller; (d) information about the buyer; (e) information about the payee; (f) information about the tax representative of the seller; (g) the reference to the contract; (h) details of the delivery; (i) payment instructions; (j) information about credits or debits.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation laying down the trade arrangements applicable to certain goods resulting from the processing of agricultural products. until 31 december 2013, the main instrument of the common agricultural policy (cap) provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) was regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products (single cmo regulation). in the framework of the cap reform, regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 was replaced with effect from 1 january 2014 by regulation (eu) no 1308/2013. regulations (ec) no 1216/2009 and (ec) no 614/2009 should be adapted to take account of regulation (eu) no 1308/2013 in order to maintain the consistency of the trade regime with third countries for agricultural products on the one hand and for goods resulting from the processing of agricultural products on the other. certain agricultural products are used to produce both processed agricultural products and goods not listed in annex i to the tfeu. the regulation adopted lays down the trade arrangements applicable to imports of processed agricultural products and exports of goods not included in annex i and of agricultural products incorporated in those goods not included in annex i.
