in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which i consider to be a useful one, taking stock of how equality between women and men in the eu area has worked or not in 2012. the report highlighted the perennial failures of this principle, which should govern the world in general and the eu in particular, as it is a right enshrined in the eu treaty. the report by the european parliament's commission finds that inequality between women and men persists in most areas in 2012 and that substantial efforts are needed to reduce these inequalities. the ep plenary rejected the report: 298 votes were against and 289 for equality between women and men. this vote, which i consider emblematic of the state of women's rights in the eu, is one that leads to the idea that none of the european documents invoked in the preamble of the report, starting with the eu treaty, are functional, are obsolete in terms of gender equality. and as long as gender equality is a "separate issue" and not considered a fundamental human right, we will not solve any of the specific gender inequality issues that will persist after the may 2014 elections.
in writing. - i voted for the report on equality between women and men. although women represent almost half of the eu's workforce and more than half of university graduates, there are still many inequalities between women and men, both in terms of women's rights as human rights, career prospects, employment and wage conditions, access to education and health services, especially in rural areas, but also in terms of participation in the economy and decision-making processes, and in terms of political representation. i hope that, despite the rejection of the report, member states will include a gender perspective in their cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020 in order to meet the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, and at eu level this principle will be included in all union and member state policies, to allow for sustainable, equitable and inclusive equality conditions for men and women.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which summarises a series of proposals aimed at promoting the right of women in the eu to work, the elimination of wage discrimination against them, their right to combine work and motherhood without being penalized for it, and an adequate level of social protection. as a result of the crisis and austerity measures, millions of women in eu countries face unemployment, precarious jobs and discrimination in pay. women are more likely than men to work on part-time, fixed-term or temporary contracts, and these contracts offer much less social protection. the gender pay gap is reflected in living standards and, in the long term, pensions, which creates a higher risk of poverty for women than for men. thus, 26% of women are considered to be at risk of poverty in the eu. more effective action is also needed to prevent the root causes of poverty, social exclusion and the rise of prostitution and trafficking in women and children, as well as increased funding for organisations and institutions that provide support to women victims of violence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on equality between women and men in the european union 2012. i voted for member states to invest in affordable and high-quality childcare facilities for the sick, disabled, dependants, elderly and others, ensuring that they are flexible and compatible with full-time working hours and accessible so that as many people as possible can combine work, family and private life. i voted for the council to unblock the adoption of the directive amending directive 92/85/eec on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health of pregnant workers and workers who have recently given birth or are breastfeeding. i voted in favour of requiring member states to guarantee decent wages and pensions, to reduce the gender pay and pension gap, to create better quality jobs for women, and to provide them with high quality public services and better social protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it deals with the solutions discussed over the last few years in response to the causes of the financial crisis. the clarifications requested from the commission in relation to the european system of financial supervision are particularly useful. in addition, every aspect of the financial crisis experience needs to be harnessed and used as a basis for identifying a set of solutions. and as has been discussed many times, supervisory mechanisms should not only focus on the supervision of individual entities but also on the stability of the financial system as a whole. last but not least, i would like to draw attention to one aspect: mandatory financial contributions by member states are contrary to the independence of the european supervisory authorities and may undermine the trust placed in them.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution with recommendations to the commission on the review of the european system of financial supervision (esfs). the financial crisis has demonstrated that poor risk management and inefficient, uneven and fragmented supervision of financial markets have contributed to financial instability and insufficient consumer protection in financial services. in addition, legislation on financial markets, financial services and financial products is highly fragmented and the multitude of legal texts generates gaps, duplication of reporting obligations, institutional divergences and overlapping rules, which can have undesirable consequences and negative effects on the real economy. the european parliament has strongly advocated the creation of european supervisory authorities (esas), has conferred more coordination and direct supervisory powers on esas, and considers that they are key actors in creating more stable and secure financial markets and that the union needs stronger and better coordinated supervision at union level. we call on the commission to submit, by 1[nbsp ]july[nbsp ]2014, legislative proposals for the revision of regulations (eu) no 1092/2010, 1093/2010, 1094/2010, 1095/2010 and 1096/2010 following the detailed recommendations set out in the annex to the report, based on the experience gained since the establishment of the esas and an in-depth analysis of the legal basis and alternatives available to article 114 tfeu, including recent case law.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on public access to documents under rule 104 (7) of the rules of procedure for the years 2011-2013. article 15 tfeu establishes an institutional framework for the institutional transparency of the european union and provides for the fundamental right of access to documents of the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union for citizens of the union and for any natural or legal person domiciled in a member state. this right should be exercised in accordance with the general principles and within the limits laid down by the regulations adopted by parliament and the council. we support the need to strike an appropriate balance between transparency and data protection, as clearly indicated by the case law in the bavarian lager case, and stress that data protection should not be 'diverted', in particular to cover conflicts of interest or undue influence in the context of eu administration and decision-making. the judgment of the court of justice in the bavarian lager case is based on the current wording of regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 and does not preclude its amendment, which is necessary and urgent, in particular following the unequivocal proclamation of the right of access to documents under the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the future of the european horticultural sector growth strategies. the eu is the world's largest producer of flowers, bulbs and potted plants (44% of world production), with the highest density per hectare. according to eurostat, between 2000 and 2010, the total production costs borne by eu farmers increased on average by almost 40%, while farm gate prices increased on average by less than 25%. the increase in production costs was almost 80% for synthetic fertilisers and soil improvers, almost 30% for seeds and planting material and almost 13% for plant protection products. we underline the importance of promoting the eu horticultural sector and facilitating its efforts to compete more effectively on the world market, through innovation, research and development, energy efficiency and security, climate change adaptation and mitigation, as well as through measures to improve marketing and continuing efforts to eliminate the existing imbalance between operators and suppliers.

importantly, 15 minutes of flight time less than the average flight time of 2 hours. the consequences: comfort for passengers, less fuel burned, less carbon dioxide emissions, lower costs, lower mr president, i would stress the importance of revising the package travel legislation for millions of citizens and for the 1.8 million businesses in the tourism sector, which employ 5% of the total workforce. we need clear legislation so that those who buy package holidays benefit from appropriate measures in different circumstances. it is also important that all clauses in package travel contracts are clear, contain the coordinates of a contact point where the traveller can request information and support and lodge a complaint in relation to any non-compliance found on the spot. i regret that it is not mentioned that the telephone number must ensure the presence of an operator who will answer the call within 3 minutes, and not just a telephone robot. the amendments to this legislation will increase the quality of tourism services and increase the competitiveness of tourism businesses.
in writing. we all know that the internet has significantly changed consumer habits, and this applies also to booking holiday packages, which tourists buy very often online. the internet has opened the way to new business models, to a more varied range of offers, including dynamic package holidays, giving consumers more convenience in booking package holidays. but i firmly believe that the price to be paid for these advantages should be neither lack of consumer protection nor unfair competition. i therefore support updating and modernising the legislation, because only then can we guarantee consumer confidence and ensure conditions for fair competition. of course, the text we have before us today is a perfect one, but i believe it strikes a balance between consumer rights which have been significantly strengthened by the inclusion of linked travel packages and dynamic packages in the directive and the preservation of the competitiveness of operators in the tourism sector, a sector of particular importance to the european economy. i hope that the report will be supported by the whole of parliament and that in the autumn we will be able to resume work with the council so that this reform becomes a reality for consumers as soon as possible.
in writing. fluoride gases are the most persistent human-made greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. emissions of these gases have increased by 60% since 1990, while emissions of other greenhouse gases have been gradually reduced. it is very important to consider a phasing out of fluorinated gases that allows producers to adapt to new market conditions, to give them the time to produce viable alternatives. in this regard, it is important to encourage the development of environmentally friendly and safe technologies and alternatives with a low environmental impact at union level, while, of course, discouraging the use of those fluorinated gases with a high environmental impact. the agreement with the council is an important step in reducing greenhouse gas emissions by allowing equipment that already has less environmentally harmful substitutes to be banned from the market. it is a balanced arrangement, which allows, on the one hand, the achievement of the union's environmental objectives and, on the other hand, allows the industry to come up with feasible solutions in this direction.
i welcome the report by my colleague mrs bauer edit on the free movement of workers, which guarantees the exercise of rights by citizens of the european union who take up employment in the territory of another member state. [ french ] this document does not amend the services directive or the directives and provisions already in force within the union on freedom of movement and employment; it is intended only to simplify and facilitate their implementation. this is the last employment dossier in the current legislative cycle of the european parliament. it is particularly worthwhile to take account of and detail practical measures for implementing the regulation, but also to guarantee the enforcement of derived labour rights, such as the recognition of diplomas obtained in another eu member state, the avoidance of double taxation or the smooth exchange of information. the establishment and operation of european contact points will play a major role in this. member states should also pay greater attention to the side effects of increased mobility, as the current crisis has increased brain drain and the emigration of young people from the very regions and member states where the need to catch up with the union is greatest. the implementation of the directive could result in discrimination or obstacles to the exercise of the right to work or to remuneration for any union citizen or family member who moves to and takes up employment in another member state. member states should also ensure the mutual recognition of different legal relationships and the rights deriving from them, and the protection of the rights of workers. the scope of this regulation covers - without discrimination - not only permanent workers but also cross-border commuters and even service providers. i am very pleased that the report, on its first reading, concludes in a reassuring way the treatment of a number of sensitive issues which particularly concern the citizens of my country.
in writing. free movement of workers is one of the fundamental freedoms of eu citizens, giving every citizen the right to move freely to another member state to work and live in that state for that purpose. it shall also protect them against discrimination on grounds of nationality and against any unjustified obstacle to the exercise of that right, including double taxation, in respect of employment, remuneration and other working conditions, including dismissal, social and tax advantages, by ensuring equal treatment with nationals of the member state concerned, in accordance with national law or collective agreements. those rights should apply without discrimination to workers with a fixed-term contract, seasonal and frontier workers whose place of employment and residence are in different member states and to persons carrying out activities for the purpose of providing services. trade unions, associations, organisations or other relevant legal persons that may represent the legal or collective interests of workers should be entitled, in accordance with national law and practice, to take action on behalf of or in support of a victim, without prejudice to the procedural rules of national law on representation and defence before the courts.
in writing. in the context of the european council's discussion of the state of implementation of the country-specific recommendations addressed in the context of the european semester, a number of remarks are required, in particular as regards the way in which romania has fulfilled the requirements formulated by the commission. as regards health reform, no visible progress has been made. romanian doctors continue to leave the country, choosing to work in states that offer them a level of pay and decent working conditions. the national roma integration strategy is not being properly implemented, mainly because ongoing projects have not been approved on the basis of coherent cost-benefit analyses. european money is being spent, but not in an articulated way. the reform of the education system is stagnating, as evidenced by the catastrophic results of national examinations and their simulations. last but not least, the majority state-owned companies continue to be real 'holes' in the state budget, due to the governors' interests in not initiating a real reform of the way these companies operate and are administered. the conclusion is that, unfortunately, the commitments of the current romanian government were made only on paper, because in practice, things have not changed.
mr president, ukraine is a geo-strategic battlefield for russia and the west. to demonise russia is not a policy but an attempt to hide our lack of policy. in the long run the race of sanctions will be won by the competitor who is able to suffer the pains longer: would it be russia, as usual? everybody is keen to have the ukrainian strategic asset at his disposal, but nobody wants to undertake full responsibility towards ukraine. what remains, usually, is each side’s attempts to make ukraine unavailable for the other one. this is evil. the worst outcome would be the emergence of two ukraines hijacking each other; of new frozen conflicts which will pass on their evil consequences from one crisis to another, spilling over in the region. therefore we should negotiate, but not before ensuring equality of arms. together, with our money, we must send into ukraine our military peace-keeping forces on the ground. if crimea is lost – i do not know – let us at least rescue the rest. the eu needs courage, vision and strength to get a clear strategic deal with russia while defending ukraine’s legitimate aspirations.
mr. president, we're talking about russia invading ukraine, but moscow isn't just looking at crimea, and the methods used are pretty much the same. in february, i denounced the illegal referendum organized, with the encouragement of russia, in the gagauzia region of the republic of moldova. in crimea, something similar will be organized in a few days, which is right, after the russian soldiers have already arrived there. using plebiscite consultation outside of a constitutional framework to mark the will of a foreign power is a mockery of democracy. i do not think that under these circumstances we can consider russia a strategic partner of the union. the council must adopt very tough sanctions against putin. we have a duty to stop the russian aggressor from the kremlin, before he sends troops to the west of crimea.
mr president, the real test in the ukrainian case is whether russia keeps crimea or not. in 1994, ukraine voluntarily gave up its nuclear status against a guarantee of territorial integrity provided by three nuclear states, russia included. in the event that russia keeps crimea, other states will think twice when asked to give up their nuclear status. this will impact negatively on nuclear non-proliferation. secondly, european politics will be plunged into the 18th and 19th centuries, when turkey agreed to cede crimea to russia under specific conditions, and when russia had to give up the danube following defeat in the crimean war. consequently, while turkey could reclaim crimea, russia could again get access to the mouth of the danube, which would alter the status of the river. thirdly, and most importantly, it would mean that the european security system had failed and that a new one had to be re-negotiated with a more aggressive russia.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution on pakistan's regional role and its political relations with the eu. pakistan is one of the largest recipients of eu humanitarian and development assistance and the eu is pakistan's largest export market. the eu and pakistan have recently chosen to deepen and expand bilateral relations, as reflected in the five-year engagement plan launched in february 2012 and the first eu-pakistan strategic dialogue held in june 2012. eu-pakistan relations need to deepen and broaden through the development of political dialogue, thus maintaining a relationship of mutual interest among equal partners. in this context, we welcome the adoption of the five-year engagement plan and the start of the eu-pakistan strategic dialogue, which reflects the increased importance of political and security cooperation, including on counter-terrorism, disarmament and non-proliferation policies, as well as migration, education and culture.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the defence of the european union against possible ballistic missile attacks is of particular importance. romania will host part of the nato anti-ballistic missile system, demonstrating the commitment to ensuring the protection of the entire region. i too support the objective of ensuring the full protection of all nato countries in europe by the end of this decade. however, i would like to draw attention, as does the report, to the risk that by reducing defence funding in the member states, vulnerabilities could be created that could be exploited by possible terrorist organisations and others.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on a missile shield for europe and its political and strategic implications. we stress that eu initiatives can contribute to strengthening cooperation between member states in the field of ballistic missile defence and to joint research and development. we believe that in the long term this cooperation could lead to an even stronger consolidation of the european defence industry. we argue that with the development and deployment of ballistic missile defence technologies, a new dynamic is emerging in the field of european security, which obliges member states to take into account the implications of ballistic missile defence for their security. the ballistic missile defence measures adopted by nato are designed and constructed to protect nato member states from potential ballistic missile attacks. we call on the vice-president of the commission/high representative to pursue a strategic partnership with nato, taking into account the issue of ballistic missile defence, which should result in the full coverage and protection of all eu member states, thus avoiding the situation where they are given different degrees of security in any respect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the eu-thailand free trade agreement could have a negative impact on the eu's fishing industry. thailand is the world's leading producer of canned tuna and one of the largest importers of fresh or chilled tuna. in the context of the negotiations on the free trade agreement, therefore, a solution must be found in which the european industry is not significantly affected by the new provisions. competition must not be distorted on the european market, especially as the economic crisis has affected european producers. a balanced solution is needed that takes into account both the concerns of the industry and the interests of european consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the current situation and future prospects of the european fisheries sector in the context of the eu-thailand free trade agreement. the european fisheries and processing industry is essential for the food supply of european citizens and for supporting life in the coastal areas that rely heavily on these activities. the survival of the sector will be jeopardised if the eu liberalises trade in fishery products with developing countries that want to export their products to the union's core market, especially if they are offered zero tariffs. we therefore call for the maintenance of the current customs tariffs for access to the eu market of thai fish and seafood preserves and preparations and therefore for the exclusion of the products concerned from the tariff reduction. we recommend long transition periods and partial liberalisation commitments, including quotas for fish and seafood preparations and preserves, in order to protect the competitiveness of the european tuna industry and maintain the sector's significant activity and social dimension within the eu. we call for reciprocity in market access and the elimination of all discrimination in services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the food culture is deteriorating more and more in the european union and the consequences of this are risks to the health of european citizens. those risks can develop into diseases and pathologies that entail high costs for both patients and public health systems in the member states. that's why i believe that nutrition education for our children is essential to prevent certain diseases and to ensure their normal development. school feeding programs are very important, and physical activity is also critical to the health of our children.
in writing. - it is worrying that even in developed countries, due to lack of culture and education, food has become a fundamental cause of disease and pathology, which generates extremely high costs for the health system. poor diet has dramatic health consequences, being the leading cause of obesity, anorexia, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, gastric diseases, and so on. food habits acquired in childhood can influence food preferences and food choices, as well as food preparation and consumption methods in adulthood. therefore, childhood is a key moment for taste education, and school plays an important role in making students discover the importance of food, as well as the diversity of products and gastronomy. with today's vote, we are ensuring that food and nutrition knowledge, culinary knowledge and culinary workshops, as well as food culture and gastronomy, will be introduced into the education systems of the member states. this will help to reinforce the concept of a healthy lifestyle based on a balanced diet among schoolchildren and will contribute to improving the health and well-being of the population in the long term.
in writing. - perhaps not coincidentally, the cuisine and culinary traditions of an eu member state are also included in the unesco world heritage list, demonstrating that gastronomy is a powerful cultural export for the eu and its member states. i support the proposal to support the initiatives of the member states and their regions to promote and preserve the territory, the landscape and the range of local, regional and national handicrafts products that make up the european gastronomic heritage. in addition, it will be beneficial for the union regions to promote local and dietary gastronomy in school and collective canteens in association with local producers, in order to preserve and enhance the regional gastronomic heritage, to stimulate local agriculture and to strengthen short circuits.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the european gastronomic heritage. i believe that an appropriate approach is needed to this problem, since from an educational point of view the health and well-being of the population is closely conditioned by the type of diet and the environment, and therefore by the methods used in agriculture, fisheries and animal husbandry. from a cultural point of view, gastronomy is part of our identity, it is an essential element of the european cultural heritage and an essential part of the cultural heritage of each member state of the european union. i encourage the initiation of exchange of information and practice projects in the field of gastronomy and nutrition through programmes such as comenius or erasmus+, through which students and professionals participate in intercultural exchanges based on vocational training in the field of food and gastronomy.
in writing. - in today's society we face two worrisome situations related to nutrition. on the one hand, there are the poor countries, where the population does not have the means to eat well. on the other hand, we find that in rich countries the population is poorly fed, due to insufficient information on dangerous substances added to food, but also due to the lack of gastronomic culture. given the importance of proper nutrition for health, i support introducing nutrition courses in the school curriculum from an early age. i also support stricter control of the information conveyed to consumers through advertising. as a member of the committee on regional development, i appreciate the efforts made at european level to protect geographical indications and traditional products internationally, which help to preserve the rituals and customs of local and regional gastronomy. in this context, i would also like to recall the role of gastronomy as a form of cultural exchange and a means of encouraging tourism. in the light of the economic crisis, which has significantly affected disadvantaged groups and young people, i call for a reassessment of the role of school canteens, which provide balanced nutrition to pupils, thus allowing them to develop harmoniously and improve their school performance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the european gastronomic heritage: cultural and educational aspects. gastronomy is part of our identity and is an essential element of the european cultural heritage and an essential part of the cultural heritage of the member states. we call on member states to include in the education of children from an early age the study and sensory experience of food and knowledge of nutrition and healthy eating habits, including historical, geographical, cultural and empirical aspects, as a means of contributing to the improvement of the health and well-being of the population. we welcome the gastronomic education programmes in schools in certain member states and stress the importance of combining education with healthy eating. the school curriculum needs to be enriched with information on the gastronomic culture, in particular the local one, the process of preparation, production, preservation and distribution of food, its socio-cultural influences and consumer rights. we suggest that member states include in their educational programmes workshops based on the development of the senses, especially taste, combining information on the nutritional benefits of food and on the regional and national gastronomic heritage. we also suggest that european cities apply for the title of unesco city of food within the creative cities network.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because respect for privacy and the protection of personal data are fundamental rights of every european citizen, enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. in particular, in the light of the recent scandals concerning telephone tapping and access to electronic mailboxes, there was a need to strengthen legislation in this area. of course, we must not forget that in certain situations involving national security, exceptions to these fundamental principles are necessary. but we are talking about exceptions and exceptional situations here, because our objective must be to protect the privacy of european citizens. i want to welcome the introduction of minimum standards for data processing in the workplace. this will enable the employee to know from the moment he takes up a job what his rights are, whether his employer can check his e-mails or whether he can use the work phone for personal purposes.
in writing. - in its current form, and particularly in the area of employee data protection, this regulation can only provide a minimum level of protection. each member state should continue to be able to set more favourable standards for employees. it should be possible to set such standards in collective agreements. it is necessary to lay down certain minimum european standards concerning the level of protection. the data protection officer has a very important role. it must therefore be clear that he can exercise his duties without fear of external pressure or influence and for the benefit of the employees. special protection against dismissal and the prohibition of discrimination are therefore appropriate. the requirements for data transfers within a group of undertakings in the eu should also be sufficiently specified. the processing of personal data by the controller should be carried out in accordance with the law of the member state where the controller is established. it is therefore important that consent is possible even in situations of imbalance, if it confers legal and economic benefits on the employee. in addition, delegated acts should be used only where non-essential elements of this regulation need to be adapted in a rapid and flexible manner to technical and safety innovations.
in writing. - the report by mr albrecht is in favour of strengthening the right to the protection of personal data, while ensuring a unified legal framework which reduces the administrative burden on data controllers. i have therefore supported this report in order to promote the use of technological measures to protect personal data and to provide incentives to controllers who take such measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data because there is a need to harmonise the legislation in force to guarantee a high level of protection for all data processing activities within the union. directive 95/46/ec has been applied differently in the member states, which has hampered the development of the single market due to differences in data protection requirements. i hope that the improvements to the regulation will increase the level of protection of this data and at the same time create an environment conducive to the economic development of the european union.
in writing. - in an era where technology has reached such a high level of development, it is important that personal data is only collected legally, under strict conditions and for a legitimate purpose. every day, at union level, public authorities and businesses transfer personal data both nationally and across borders. according to a 2008 eurobarometer survey, two thirds of respondents across the union (65%) indicated that their firm had transferred personal data via the internet. the proportion of companies making such transfers ranged from 13% in germany to 59% in slovakia. these figures demonstrate the need for a uniform legal framework to effectively protect personal data of individuals.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (general data protection regulation). i consider that the data protection principles should apply to any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. in order to determine whether a person is identifiable, all means that can reasonably be used, either by the controller or by any other person, for the purpose of identifying or highlighting that natural person, directly or indirectly, should be considered. they argue that consent should be given explicitly, by any appropriate method that allows the free, specific and informed expression of the will of the data subject, either by a statement or by an unequivocal act that is the result of a choice made by the data subject, ensuring that the natural person is aware that he or she is giving consent to the processing of personal data. the unequivocal act could include ticking a box when the person visits a website or any other statement or action which clearly indicates in this context the consent of the data subject to the proposed processing of his or her personal data.
in writing. - i voted today in favour of the data protection regulation, as adopted by the libe committee, because some progress on clarifying the commission proposal has been achieved. the libe committee has taken steps in the right direction on better definitions, more flexible certification and the deletion of a large number of delegated acts. however, many issues are still not solved, ranging from unreasonably heavy administrative and financial burdens for small and medium-sized enterprises, to obstacles in health research and hindrances to much-needed research cooperation at global level. by maintaining a negative perception of profiling, the report is hampering innovation in the digital economy and the usage of big data for increasing efficiency in all activity sectors. as shadow rapporteur for the alde group in the industry committee, i believe that a much wider debate and a longer period of time for negotiations is needed to arrive to a reasonable and workable regulation for all eu citizens and companies.

in writing. - in 2013 a total of 670[nbsp ]000 counterfeit euro banknotes were withdrawn from circulation. around 75[nbsp ]% of these counterfeit notes concerns eur[nbsp ]20 and eur[nbsp ]50 banknotes. also in 2013 a total of 175[nbsp ]900 fake euro coins were withdrawn resulting in a counterfeit ratio of 1 for every 100[nbsp ]000 genuine coins. the pericles 2020 programme is vital to maintaining the integrity of the euro by assisting member state authorities in their efforts to fight counterfeiting and fraud, and by fostering cooperation between relevant stakeholders. with a budget of eur[nbsp ]1.1 million per year, the programme has already financed 135 projects both within and outside of the eu. for instance, it has strengthened anti-counterfeiting cooperation particularly within the vulnerable regions of eastern europe and south america. i must insist that the pericles 2020 programme also be applied to member states that have not yet adopted the euro. the programmeʼs greatest potential lies in being applied across the whole of the euʼs territory.

in writing. - today's armed conflicts involve one or more non-state armed actors fighting against states or other armed groups, while civilians become the main victims of wars, and many of these victims are children. the international community has a duty to ensure that all parties to the conflict, both states and armed non-state actors, commit to the protection of these children. there is a need at european union level to include in policy dialogues with third countries, for example in the framework of the cotonou agreement, the objective of preventing and stopping the recruitment and forced recruitment of children under 18 years of age and ensuring their release and reintegration into society. i support supporting humanitarian organisations engaging in dialogues with non-state armed actors to promote compliance with international humanitarian law in armed conflict and, in particular, the protection of children through political, diplomatic and financial means. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the problem of children involved in armed conflict tends to be accentuated. we're already talking about over 250,000 children involved in these events, and the impact on them is not just physical, but mostly emotional and psychological. very often, they are scarred for life by the atrocities committed around them, and there is a risk that they themselves will later be directly involved in such situations. the union therefore has a duty to promote legal rules at international level applicable both to states and, in particular, to non-state actors. these rules shall provide for the prohibition of the recruitment of minors and for their protection in the context of conflicts.
in writing. - i am in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the humanitarian engagement of non-state armed actors in the field of child protection. few people know that a significant number of children are used in armed conflict every year, with devastating consequences for their physical and mental development for the rest of their lives. we need to acknowledge this and get involved as much as possible in eliminating this practice. it is against human rights for children to be recruited as soldiers, forced to kill and subjected to sexual exploitation and, moreover, it is against any rights to be maimed or killed by landmines.
in writing. - i voted for the european parliament's recommendation on the humanitarian engagement of non-state armed actors in the field of child protection. most current armed conflicts involve one or more non-state armed actors fighting against states or other armed groups, while civilians and especially children become the main victims of wars. unfortunately, armed conflict has a devastating impact on children's physical and mental development, with long-term consequences for human security and sustainable development. the international community has a moral duty to ensure that all parties to conflict, both states and non-state armed actors, commit to the protection of children. we recommend that the commissioner for development and the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy support humanitarian organisations engaging in dialogues with non-state armed actors with the aim of promoting compliance with international humanitarian law in armed conflict and, in particular, the protection of children through political, diplomatic and financial means. we also recommend that they call on eu member states to join international efforts to prevent attacks on schools and their use by armed actors by endorsing the draft lucens guidelines on the protection of schools and universities against military use during armed conflict.
