in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the commission delegated regulation of 12 december 2013 amending regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers as regards the definition of 'manufactured nanomaterials' objecting to the commission delegated regulation. we consider that the commission delegated regulation is not compatible with the purpose and content of regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 and exceeds the delegated powers conferred on the commission by the latter act. we call on the commission to present a new delegated act which takes into account parliament's position. article 18 (3) of regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 on consumer information on food provides that all food ingredients present in the form of manufactured nanomaterials are to be clearly specified in the list of food ingredients to ensure consumer information. the commission delegated regulation excludes all food additives included in the union lists from the new definition of 'manufactured nanomaterials'. this general derogation cancels the labelling provisions for all food additives that are manufactured nanomaterials and this is contrary to the fundamental objective of the directive to pursue a high level of protection of the health and interests of consumers by providing final consumers with a basis to make an informed choice.
in writing. - i voted against the report because, in my view, the objective of the proposed directive should have been to strike a balance between the protection of personal data and the fight against crimes such as terrorism. there are a number of provisions aimed at reducing the risk of misuse and use of personal data for purposes other than lawful ones. however, the version approved by the libe committee introduces a number of bureaucratic procedures which will make it difficult to apply the directive. this increases the risk that, if necessary, competent authorities may not be able to intervene or may act too late against threats to national security. i hope that if adopted, the directive will not create a climate of impunity for several categories of potential offenders and will not pose a risk to the security of the member states.
in writing. - an effective data protection framework in europe can make a significant contribution to ensuring a good level of data protection for all european citizens. any processing of personal data must be lawful, fair and transparent in relation to the natural persons concerned. the specific purposes for which the data are processed must be explicit and legitimate and determined at the time of the collection of the personal data. the data shall be adequate, relevant and limited to the minimum necessary for the purposes for which the data are processed. personal data should be processed only where the purpose of the processing could not be fulfilled by other means. in order to ensure that data are not stored for longer than necessary, the operator should set deadlines for deletion or periodic review. the transfer of personal data to other authorities or private entities in the union shall be prohibited unless the transfer complies with the law and the recipient is established in a member state. the controller must inform the recipient of the purpose of the processing and the supervisory authority of the transfer, and the recipient must be informed of the processing restrictions and ensure that they are respected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and on the free movement of such data. ensuring a uniform and high level of protection of personal data of natural persons and facilitating the exchange of personal data between the competent authorities of the member states is essential to guarantee the effectiveness of judicial cooperation in criminal matters and police cooperation. i consider it important that any processing of personal data is lawful, fair and transparent in relation to the natural persons concerned. in particular, the specific purposes for which the data are processed should be explicit and legitimate and determined at the time of the collection of the personal data. personal data should be adequate, relevant and limited to the minimum necessary for the purposes for which they are processed. this shall in particular entail limiting the data collected and the period for which they are stored to the minimum necessary. personal data should be processed only where the purpose of the processing could not be fulfilled by other means.
in writing. - i voted in favour of reforming the single sky implementation regulation, which aims to accelerate the implementation of the air navigation services reform, without departing from the original objectives and principles of the regulation. the implementation of the single european sky should play a positive role in terms of growth, employment and competitiveness in europe, in particular by stimulating the demand for highly skilled jobs. i believe that this proposal has the potential to accelerate progress in this area by preventing another setback of the european aviation industry caused by external competition and a new wave of airline failures. i believe that a synergistic approach to network configuration, network management and technology deployment can lead to the creation of an integrated operational european airspace, to the benefit of both citizens and european industry.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and i would like to point out that, unfortunately, the major objectives of the single european sky have not yet been achieved. and this costs both the airlines and, by implication, the european passengers. whether we are talking about higher pollution, higher ticket prices or even flight safety problems all are effects of improper implementation of initiatives in this area. what is even more worrying is that the implementation delays will have even more serious effects in the context of the fact that the number of flights in europe will increase by more than 50% in the next 10-20 years. i think we should put aside the political sensitivities that are blocking progress on this issue and put the interest of european citizens first.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the implementation of the single european sky. this regulation shall apply to the airspace of the icao eur and afi regions where member states are responsible for the provision of air traffic services in accordance with this regulation. member states may also apply this regulation to the airspace under their responsibility in other icao regions, provided that they inform the commission and the other member states thereof. in order to avoid the expected increase in air traffic exacerbating or generating congestion in european airspace, with all the economic, environmental and safety costs that this entails, the fragmentation of that airspace should be ended and this regulation should also be implemented as soon as possible. i voted for amendment no 146 which calls on member states to take all necessary measures to ensure that air navigation service providers, when drawing up their business plans, take into account offers from different assistance service providers in order to choose the most financially appropriate provider and one which meets the appropriate operational, social and safety standards.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, when it comes to air transport, passenger safety must come first. that is why i am also in favour of introducing a mandatory certificate for organisations involved in the design or manufacture of air traffic management systems. but i also want to stress the importance of training air traffic controllers and the need for continuous specialisation. the role of the aviation safety agency will be essential to ensure compliance with the new rules. i also think it is welcome to clarify certain aspects of its functioning, such as the role in issuing certificates that i mentioned earlier. the ultimate objective must be to extend the agency's remit and strengthen its role, not only at european level but also at international level.
in writing. - within the european economy, an important component is the european aviation sector, which makes a strong contribution to promoting trade and tourism and has a significant employment rate. the desire to create new services in this field at member state level has led to the inefficient fragmentation of european airspace, with effects on air traffic control services at european level. each country has created its own air traffic management system, which results in reduced responsiveness to customer requirements airlines and the travellers who pay for these services. i support the idea that the implementation of the ses and the related reform of the european system must be accelerated, in order to help users cope with a fierce global competitive environment and to improve the overall efficiency of the way european airspace is organised and managed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 216/2008 in the field of airports, air traffic management and air navigation services. this regulation is part of the same legislative package as the single european sky and addresses the issue of aviation safety and the competences of the european aviation safety agency (easa). the regulation is very important for two reasons: firstly, to adapt to the new rules imposed by the single european sky, and secondly, to reform governance in order to implement the provisions of the interinstitutional agreement on european agencies. the main objective of this regulation is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe and to establish the structure (governance) of the european aviation agency. easa, at the heart of the union aviation system, should also play a leading role in the union's external aviation strategy. easa, in close cooperation with the commission, should make a major contribution, given its expertise, to the export of union aviation standards and to the promotion of the movement of union aviation products, specialists and services worldwide, thereby facilitating their access to growing markets.
in writing. - i supported and voted in favour of this report because, as in most european countries, tourism plays an extremely important role in my country's economy. the development of the internet has made it easier for us to access many services and information. however, their regulation is still in its infancy, given their novelty. in addition, fair competition issues in the online environment are more difficult to monitor and implement. i believe that before making payment, the consumer must be able to know all the elements of the offer he is buying, including the possibility of a refund within a reasonable period of time. in addition, the possibility to cancel the package or reserved offer in the event of unjustified or unexpected price increases seems to me to be extremely useful for consumer protection.
in writing. - the development of new communication technologies is making a major contribution to ensuring travellers' access to information for booking travel and tourist packages, and is also contributing to the growth of online travel package bookings. in the context of the european single market, travellers should enjoy uniform protection and clear rights, regardless of the country in which they reside, and i support the proposal that member states should not be able to maintain or introduce in their national legislation provisions different from those laid down in this directive, unless this directive contains other provisions to that effect.
in writing. - mr mayer's report concerns the revision of directive 90/314/eec on all-inclusive travel to include online trade. the aim of the directive is to ensure compliance, effectiveness and an adequate level of protection for consumers/travellers in the event of insolvency, and to provide for penalties in the event of breaches of obligations by undertakings. the main issues are therefore pre-contractual information and withdrawal procedures, changes to the journey, price reductions or price increases, the protection of travellers in difficulty and objective liability.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on package travel and assisted travel arrangements because tourism plays an important role in the union's economy and package travel, holiday and tours (packages) represent a significant proportion of this market. given that travel services are currently combined not only in the form of traditional pre-arranged packages but also often in a personalised way, many of these travel products fall either in a legal grey area or are not expressly covered by directive 90/314/eec. this directive aims to adapt the scope of protection to those developments and to increase transparency and the level of legal certainty for the benefit of travellers and traders. i welcome this initiative and hope that both at the european union level and at the level of romania this directive will ensure a favourable environment for the development of european tourism.
in writing. - i voted for the directive on package travel and assisted travel arrangements, amending regulation (ec) no [nbsp ]2006/2004 and directive [nbsp ]2011/83/eu and repealing council directive [nbsp ]90/314/eec. tourism plays an important role in the economies of the union and packaged travel, leisure and touring represent a significant proportion of this market. in addition to traditional distribution chains, the internet has become an increasingly important medium for the provision of travel services. travel services are now combined not only in the form of traditional pre-arranged packages but also, often, in a personalised way. this directive aims to adapt the scope of protection to those developments and to increase transparency and the level of legal certainty for the benefit of travellers and traders. member states may implement the provisions of this directive in respect of packages and associated travel arrangements offered or combined on an occasional basis by natural or legal persons for whom no direct or indirect financial income is derived from the sale of those packages or from the facilitation of the associated travel arrangements concerned, as well as of packages and associated travel arrangements covering a period of less than 24 hours and not including accommodation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it deals with a matter of general interest, with repercussions both for us and, above all, for future generations: climate change. emissions of fluorinated gases, which have a climate-warming effect up to 23,000 times greater than carbon dioxide, have increased by 60% since 1990, while all other greenhouse gases have decreased. therefore, we need an appropriate legal framework in place through which eu consumers and business users of equipment can drive change and drive technological development in all sectors that currently use f-gases. this will result in higher market shares for companies that take advantage of the opportunity and develop climate-friendly products and equipment.
in writing. - the montreal protocol has succeeded in mandating the worldwide phasing out or reduction of most ozone depleting substances, including chlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. the substitution substances used, such as hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons and sulfur hexafluoride, have however been shown to have a very large influence on climate and a global warming potential up to 23[nbsp ]000 times greater than that of carbon dioxide and can remain for thousands of years in the atmosphere. the european union has called for greenhouse gas emissions to be reduced, but while all other greenhouse gases have been reduced, the eu's fluorinated gas emissions have increased by 60% since 1990. today's vote by the european parliament has given the green light to pass new legislation now to prevent emissions from rising in the coming decades. i believe that phasing out hfcs will strengthen sustainable development, stimulate innovation and reward european companies that have invested in green technologies. by taking on an ambitious global leadership role, europe can maintain its competitiveness in innovative refrigeration, cooling and heating technologies in an environmentally responsible way.
in writing. - in the context of the economic and social crisis, job protection is and remains a priority for the european union, but i believe that the implementation of the proposal to reduce the use and production of fluorinated gases requires a socially equitable transition period. this period is particularly necessary for small and medium-sized enterprises, which also need to reduce the financial and administrative burden in order to be able to contribute to the implementation of the various aspects of the regulation. on the other hand, it will be beneficial to increase support for industrial research and innovation, in particular in terms of the design of technologies alternative to fluorinated greenhouse gases, and for the design of appropriate training programmes to train workers in alternative technologies to fluorinated greenhouse gases, but taking into account the specific situation of smes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on fluorinated greenhouse gases. the fourth assessment report of the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) of the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc), to which the union is a party, states that, on the basis of existing scientific evidence, developed countries should reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80% to 95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels in order to limit global climate change to a 2 ̊c increase in temperature, thereby preventing undesirable effects on climate. the aim of the adopted regulation is to protect the environment by reducing emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases. it (a) lays down rules on the containment, use, recovery and destruction of fluorinated greenhouse gases and related ancillary measures; (b) imposes conditions on the placing on the market of specific products and equipment containing or relying on fluorinated greenhouse gases; (c) imposes conditions on specific uses of fluorinated greenhouse gases; and (d) sets quantitative limits for the placing on the market of hydrofluorocarbons.
in writing. - the free movement of workers is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union and a basic element of eu citizenship, which every citizen must be able to enjoy. however, at present, a large number of citizens who want to move or have moved to another eu country for work have expressed their grievances about their rights not being respected. the better functioning of the internal market therefore requires a more efficient and uniform application of the rights conferred by union rules on the free movement of workers. member states need to take appropriate measures to protect citizens against discrimination on grounds of nationality and any unjustified obstacle to the exercise of the right to work abroad. i welcome the provision that member states designate one or more structures or bodies to promote, analyse, monitor and support equal treatment for all workers and members of their families, without discrimination on grounds of nationality or citizenship, and adopt the necessary provisions for the functioning of such bodies. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, after the debate in january, in which i sent a strong political signal to all those who believe that freedom of movement is optional, i am pleased to see that we are now legislating a number of the principles discussed two months ago. freedom of movement in the european union is therefore non-negotiable and is a pillar of the community's construction. and european workers who choose to work in another country must enjoy the same rights as those in that country. after all, they are subject to the same rigors, even some more stringent ones, so why not enjoy similar benefits? especially since, in general, the productivity of foreign workers is higher than the national average, regardless of the state we're talking about. as i come from romania, and many of my fellow citizens have chosen to seek a better future in other member states, i know exactly what problems they face. either they are discriminated against when they try to get a job or they cannot even enroll their children in school thus violating the fundamental right to education. these are problems faced by any romanian citizen who goes to work in the west.
in writing. - the free movement of workers in europe is and must remain a political priority of the european union and i hope that the directive will contribute to fair and balanced mobility, especially as only 3% of european workers exercise their right to mobility in the eu. on the other hand, the exercise of the right of free movement of workers without obstacles or discrimination, equal treatment and the fight against discrimination on grounds of nationality of european workers exercising their right to free movement are elements that will help protect fundamental rights, improve eu competitiveness, business productivity and the quality of workers' jobs, and remain a pillar of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which calls on eu countries to ensure equal treatment of workers and adequate protection of labour rights. member states should ensure that free movement is not a source of exploitation, in view of the unequal treatment and vulnerability of migrant workers to possible abuse. i consider it essential that the member states work together to improve the framework for combating discrimination and to ensure that employees are better aware of their rights. at the same time, stronger action is needed to counter the discriminatory and xenophobic tendencies that are gaining ground in the context of the worrying social and economic crisis. in order to reduce inequalities between migrant and indigenous workers, i support the proposal on access of union citizens to public sector posts, in accordance with eu law as interpreted by the court of justice of the european union, which has stressed that the limitation of access to certain posts in the public administration to nationals of a member state should be interpreted restrictively and only for posts involving direct or indirect participation in the exercise of authority conferred by public law and in tasks aimed at protecting the general interests of the state or other public authorities.
in writing. - i voted against this report on the free movement of workers. the proposal as it stands does not provide adequate answers to the needs of workers, particularly those relating to an immediate solution to the problem of unemployment. we cannot allow macroeconomic imbalances and different conditions of access to the labour market, particularly at this time of severe economic crisis which threatens to undermine the credibility of the european union as such.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because we cannot talk about a more integrated european union in the context of an increase in discrimination against workers in the union on grounds of nationality over the last year. this discrimination has been manifested by the elimination of certain benefits, the provision of jobs not adapted to their skills and the provision of a net wage lower than that of nationals of the member state concerned. the free movement of workers shall not adversely affect nationals of the member state concerned by reducing their wages or benefiting from social advantages. free movement provides workers in sectors where there is a shortage, and these workers actively participate in economic growth by paying taxes to the state and producing goods and services needed by the domestic economy. i believe that we need better information in this area, by making conclusive studies available to european citizens and by immediately sanctioning states that deliberately obstruct the free movement of workers within the union.
in writing. - i support the commission's proposal for a directive on measures to facilitate the exercise of the rights of workers in the context of freedom of movement, as provided for in article [nbsp ]45 tfeu. every citizen of the union, regardless of his place of origin, must have the right to move and work in another member state. free movement cannot be separated from the single market. you cannot have free movement of services and capital in the single market without free movement of people. you cannot have the right to establish companies in bucharest or sofia, to benefit from reduced production costs, without accepting romanian and bulgarian labour in your country. free movement is not negotiable as long as you are a member of the union and the single market.
in writing. - the free movement of workers is a milestone in the process of european integration and plays a crucial role in countering the effects of the economic crisis, developing social cohesion and reducing disparities between european regions. however, eu workers face difficulties in exercising their rights when moving from one eu member state to another. the proper functioning of the internal market requires that the gap between the rights that union citizens enjoy in theory and those that they enjoy in practice be narrowed. i therefore believe that member states and the eu must make sustained efforts to ensure that the rules on free movement guarantee the full exercise of the rights conferred on union citizens. it is essential that those rules guarantee both the protection of workers against exploitation and the protection of host countries against abuse in relation to national social protection systems. by my vote in favour, i welcome the lifting of restrictions on the labour market in all eu member states for romanian citizens. this decision will have beneficial effects both for romanians and for the economies of the host countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on measures to facilitate the exercise of the rights of workers in the context of freedom of movement for workers. the free movement of workers is one of the fundamental freedoms of union citizens and one of the pillars of the internal market in the union, enshrined in article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). the adopted directive lays down provisions to facilitate the application and ensure uniform enforcement of the rights conferred by article 45 tfeu and articles 1 to 10 of regulation 492/2011. the adopted directive applies to the following aspects: access to employment, working and employment conditions, in particular as regards remuneration, dismissal, occupational safety and health and, where union workers are unemployed, reintegration and re-employment, access to social and tax benefits, membership of trade unions and the right to be elected to workers' representative bodies, access to training, access to housing, access to education, apprenticeships and vocational training for the children of union workers and assistance from the employment offices. i voted against amendments nos 65, 66, 67 and 68, which sought to restrict the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe it will strike a very good balance between protecting the environment and stimulating economic growth in the european union. the new provisions will remove a number of fears of public opinion and professional organisations when environmental impact assessments of projects are carried out. the elimination of bureaucratic procedures will also facilitate the carrying out of these assessments, allowing for timely and safe implementation of projects. europe needs jobs and growth, and large-scale projects can deliver these goals.
in writing. - directive 2011/92/eu harmonised the principles for assessing the effects of projects on the environment by introducing minimum requirements and has contributed, in its 28 years of application, to ensuring a high level of protection of the environment and human health. however, in order to remedy certain recent problems and to align the text of the directive with the new political priorities of the union, including the soil protection strategy, i consider it necessary to amend directive 2011/92/eu. the review will enhance the quality of the environmental impact assessment procedure, simplify the various steps of the procedure, align the procedure with the principles of smart regulation and improve coherence and synergies with other union legislation and policies, as well as with strategies and policies developed by member states in areas of national competence. the main objective is to ensure better implementation at member state level by simplifying burdensome administrative procedures that have generated additional delays and risks in environmental protection. i consider that, in order to ensure harmonised application and equal protection of the environment throughout the union, the commission should ensure qualitative as well as procedural compliance with the provisions of directive 2011/92/eu, including those on public consultation and participation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment. directive 2011/92/eu harmonised the principles for the assessment of the impact of projects on the environment by introducing minimum requirements as regards the type of projects assessed, the main obligations of project promoters, the content of the assessment and the participation of competent authorities and the public, and contributes to ensuring a high level of protection of the environment and human health. member states are free to adopt more stringent protection measures in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). i consider that, in order to ensure a high level of protection of the environment and human health, the environmental impact assessment and the prior verification procedures should take into account the impact of the whole project, including, where appropriate, the surface and underground phases and during the construction, operation and, where appropriate, demolition phases. i support the need to review directive 2011/92/eu in a way that ensures improved environmental protection, increased resource efficiency and support for sustainable growth in the union. to that end, the procedures provided for in that directive should be simplified and harmonised.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, in order to ensure legal certainty and accuracy in the statistical data, there was a need to align the existing regulations to the regime of implementing and delegated acts. a distinction should be made between situations where delegated acts are adopted and cases where the variant of implementing acts is chosen. i would stress the importance of the european parliament's scrutiny of the acts adopted by the european commission under this regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics relating to external trade with third countries as regards the conferral of delegated and implementing powers on the commission to adopt certain measures. this proposal aims at aligning regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics relating to external trade with third countries with the regime for implementing and delegated acts established by the treaty of lisbon (articles 290 and 291 tfeu). at present, most of the legislative acts in the field of the common commercial policy have been aligned to the new constitutional regime through the omnibus acts on trade i and ii and a few other subsequent individual alignments. i voted to limit the delegation of powers to the commission to five years. such a limitation allows for greater parliamentary scrutiny by requiring the commission to draw up a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the period laid down. on the other hand, the tacit extension of the delegation of powers for identical periods of time avoids imposing an excessive burden on legislators and facilitates the implementation of the common commercial policy. this amendment reflects the outcome of the trade omnibus i and ii negotiations, where the same approach was supported.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i consider it particularly useful to further develop this european earth observation system. the benefits of copernicus are manifold, whether we're talking about preventing natural disasters or humanitarian crises. the programme provides more complete information and enables informed decisions in the field of environment, climate, civil protection and security at national and community level. however, i would like to point out that the reduction in the programme budget compared to the commission's original proposal is not welcome, especially in the context of copernicus generating a profit of eur 3.2 for every eur spent.
in writing. - the european union must continue to pay particular attention to european space programmes, and the implementation of programmes such as galileo and copernicus will allow the union to maintain its leading position internationally, contributing to creating an environment conducive to the development of quality jobs at european level. i believe that it is beneficial to involve european companies in order to increase investment, jobs and growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it was necessary to align the legislation on gsa with the common approach on decentralised agencies. i would point out, however, that there are concerns about the level of funding for the agency, which may not be sufficient. for example, the salaries of the agency's staff are at the general level of income in the czech republic, but in the metropolitan area of prague, where the agency is located, the levels are much higher, both in terms of income and especially in terms of expenditure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 912/2010 establishing the european gnss agency. the european gnss agency is to ensure the accreditation of the european satellite navigation systems (the systems) and, to this end, initiates and monitors the implementation of security procedures and the performance of security audits. these systems are complex and their establishment and operation involve numerous stakeholders with different roles. in this context, it is of crucial importance that eu classified information is processed and protected by all stakeholders involved in the implementation of the galileo and egnos programmes, in accordance with the basic principles and minimum standards laid down in the commission and council security rules on the protection of eu classified information. the stakeholders involved in and affected by the security accreditation process are the member states, the commission, the relevant union agencies and the european space agency (esa). given the specific nature and complexity of the systems, the different bodies involved in their implementation and the diversity of potential users, security accreditation should be facilitated through appropriate consultation of all relevant parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, seeing what is happening in ukraine, i think it is obvious to all of us that the time for statements of support and encouragement to our eastern neighbours has passed. it is time to take action and support them in a concrete way, especially financially. i draw attention to the fact that while the entire international community is focused on russia's invasion of crimea, there is potential for instability in the republic of moldova as well. already the russian occupation forces in the separatist transnistrian region have raised the alert level. this is despite the fact that the foreign ministry in moscow said after the adoption of the european parliament resolution on the situation of transnistrian schools that russian soldiers in the area have an exclusively peacekeeping role. i wonder what kind of peace is being maintained, because it seems that russia sees the concept of peace differently than we do.
in writing. - the eu must focus on citizens of the eastern partnership countries, on policies that will deliver concrete results, such as visa liberalisation. the eu should focus on youth and energy security and cooperate with its eastern partners on this issue. i welcome the 2013 allocations under the 'eastern partnership integration and cooperation programme' of the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument, distributed between moldova, georgia and armenia, representing the additional funding for eastern partnership countries making progress on reforms for a strong democracy and human rights. i also welcome the commission's proposal to allow moldovan citizens to travel visa-free within the schengen area, to which the romanian authorities have made a key contribution. more efforts are also needed, in particular on promoting cooperation in the fields of education, science, culture and sport. the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, vocational training, paid and unpaid training, voluntary service and au pair work is an instrument that will have a major impact on education and culture.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the evaluation and prioritisation of eu relations with the eastern partnership countries. now more than ever, eastern partnership societies that are in favour of integration into the european union need strong, proactive and immediate support from the eu, which should be provided through different methods and in different policy areas, ranging from financial assistance to visa facilitation schemes. we recommend the flexible use of the instruments available to the eu, such as macroeconomic assistance, facilitation of the exchange regime, projects to strengthen energy security and economic modernisation, and the rapid application of visa liberalisation, in line with european values and interests. we underline that cooperation in the field of energy security is a priority within the eastern partnership and the european neighbourhood policy. we believe that further progress on the integration of the gas and electricity networks in the region, including reverse flows, is essential to achieving the energy community objectives. projects such as south stream increase the eu's dependence on russian gas and therefore support the need for member states and the commission to accelerate projects that can help alleviate the eastern partnership countries' energy dependence on russia.
in writing. - i voted for the report. i have to admit, the sheer scale of the nsa's surveillance program has taken the public by surprise. what is even more surprising is that in some member states, national authorities themselves have provided certain information to the nsa illegally. we must admit that the confidence of many europeans has been shaken. the bases for cooperation between the union and the united states should be redefined in relation to data protection in order to prevent similar situations in the future. but i don't think we should resort to emotional decisions, let alone irrational ones. after all, we are talking about the union's most important partner, which not only helped to rebuild our continent after the second world war, but has consistently supported and even defended us in the decades since.
in writing. - the revelations of the last half year have seriously jeopardised the trust that has underpinned transatlantic relations, as well as the confidence of eu citizens in the ability of their own governments and european forums to defend their rights. the european parliament therefore condemns the widespread and indiscriminate collection of strictly personal data, which violates not only the right to privacy but also notions that are at the foundation of a democratic society, such as the presumption of innocence, freedom of the press or the non-use of information in political confrontations. in this context, the position of the european parliamentary forum is very clear: the us must ban secret mass surveillance activities. otherwise, bilateral relations will deteriorate rapidly, as already reflected by the partial suspension of the transatlantic trade and investment partnership. a thorough investigation of past abuses is also needed, a reform of the european cybersecurity and data protection framework, and a review of the national framework in each member state for the democratic control of intelligence activities. as the report on which i voted points out, national competence in matters of espionage and national security does not preclude a parallel, eu-specific competence in matters of internal security.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the surveillance programme of the us national security agency, the surveillance bodies in the various member states and their impact on the fundamental rights of eu citizens and on transatlantic cooperation in justice and home affairs. we condemn the widespread, systematic and secret collection of personal data of innocent people, including many times strictly personal and private information. we consider it essential to protect the privilege of professional secrecy of lawyers, journalists, doctors and other persons exercising professions regulated by mass surveillance activities. we stress that any uncertainties related to the confidentiality of information communicated in the lawyer-client relationship could have a negative impact on citizens' right to legal advice, access to justice and the right to a fair trial. i voted for amendments nos 27 and 28, which call for an end to the mass interception and processing of webcam images by any secret service outside the legal framework for the protection of personal data and call on the member states to establish mechanisms to hold those responsible to account for this abuse of power.
in writing. - i supported this report because i believe that the justice dashboard could be extended to criminal cases. the deepening of the area of freedom, security and justice implies greater cooperation and a delegation of competences to the european union also in criminal matters. the commission's monitoring of the judicial system in the member states is essential to ensure that the judicial systems of the member states function as efficiently as possible.
in writing. - the 2013 justice scoreboard covers only civil, commercial and administrative justice, but should also include criminal justice, as the functioning and integrity of criminal justice have important implications and fundamental rights are also closely linked to the rule of law. the establishment of a criminal cases scoreboard will be a fundamental contribution to the creation of a common understanding of eu criminal law among judges and prosecutors. the commission should establish a separate scoreboard covering the judiciary, which should assess, using objective indicators, the independence, efficiency and integrity of magistrates, the careers of judges and the respect of procedural rights. the commission should propose an effective mechanism for regular assessment of member states' compliance with the eu's fundamental values as set out in article 2 teu, providing a basis for an early warning tool and a crisis mechanism with appropriate forms of intervention, more effective infringement procedures and the possibility of sanctions in case of systematic violation of the principles of democracy and the rule of law and in case of failure of appropriate checks and balances in a member state.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the evaluation of justice in terms of criminal justice and the rule of law. in the field of criminal justice, evaluation enhances mutual trust, and mutual trust is key to the effective implementation of mutual recognition tools. also, in the stockholm programme, evaluation is listed as one of the main tools for integration in the area of freedom, security and justice. the 2013 justice scoreboard covers only civil, commercial and administrative justice but should also include criminal justice, as the functioning and integrity of criminal justice also have important implications for fundamental rights and is closely linked to the rule of law. we stress that the establishment of a criminal scoreboard will be a fundamental contribution to creating a common understanding of eu criminal law among judges and prosecutors, thus strengthening mutual trust. we call on the commission to gradually extend the scope of the scoreboard to become a separate scoreboard covering the judiciary, which assesses, using objective indicators such as the independence, efficiency and integrity of magistrates, the careers of judges and the respect of procedural rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because there is a significant fragmentation of the audiovisual markets in the european union. the existence of a uniform legal framework guaranteeing equal access of users to the services offered by providers is essential. i also stress the importance of respecting the principle of net neutrality, especially in the context of the increasing number of audiovisual services being transmitted over the internet. last but not least, i believe that greater convergence will also be able to stimulate innovation in the field, which will contribute to further development of the audiovisual services market.
in writing. - in the face of the development of information technology, the internet and social networks and their use by an increasing number of citizens, the traditional linear audiovisual service offerings continue to represent an important part of the media consumption habits of european citizens. i also support the idea that maintaining information pluralism, promoting cultural and linguistic diversity and preserving the structural role of the public service media in the european media ecosystem are values of public interest. these values must be maintained and promoted as part of the european social model. a debate at european level on audiovisual convergence would be beneficial, which should have as its central objectives the protection of european cultures and the inseparable protection of the interests and fundamental rights of citizens, in particular minors and other vulnerable audiences.
in writing. - the digital market has brought with it new business models, which are currently little or not regulated. the placing on the market of unauthorised audiovisual content may, in some cases, pose a threat to quality journalism. in addition, the preferential transmission of media content to the detriment of others affects the diversity of opinion and the right of users to be informed in a non-discriminatory manner. if we also take into account the new advertising strategies that rely on these technologies - screen capture, consumer profiling, multi-screen strategies, etc. - the question of consumer protection, privacy and personal data arises. in this context, i am convinced that we need uniform standards and more effective regulation for the digital sector, which at the same time supports innovation and technological progress. i also believe that ensuring product and opinion diversity, and the search and discovery of audiovisual content should not be driven by economic interests. i therefore call on the european commission to identify ways of financing and producing high-quality european audiovisual content that will stand the test of time and offer a testimony to the cultural excellence specific to our continent.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on preparing for the full convergence of the audiovisual world. we stress that regulation is necessary when there is a control of 'content converters' over access to the media and a direct or indirect impact on opinion formation. we invite the commission and the member states to monitor developments in this regard and to make the most of the opportunities offered by european competition law and antitrust law and, if necessary, to introduce measures to protect diversity and to develop a regulatory framework for convergence that is adapted to these developments. we believe that, in the context of electronic communications, all data packets should in principle be treated equally, regardless of their content, application, origin and purpose (the 'best effort' principle) and we call for the maintenance and safeguarding of a free and open internet, in particular with regard to the development of specialised services. we emphasise that network neutrality, in the sense of an internet operating on the basis of the principle of best effort and non-discriminatory access and transmission of all audiovisual content, is a guarantee of a pluralistic supply of information and of the diversity of opinion and culture and thus constitutes an element analogous to the 'must-carry' principle of the convergent media world.
in writing. - i welcome the commission's eu citizenship report 2013 which announces new actions in 12 areas aimed at strengthening the rights of eu citizens. at a time when european citizens are losing confidence in the european construction, measures are needed to ensure that they can enjoy all the rights inherent in european citizenship. citizens need to be able to make informed decisions on the exercise of their treaty rights and should therefore be provided with easily accessible practical information on the economic, social, administrative, legal and cultural issues they face. this requires national, regional and local authorities to promote a better understanding of european citizenship and explain its concrete benefits to citizens. i believe that more needs to be done to promote that citizens residing in a member state other than their home member state can exercise their right to vote in european and local elections, just like citizens of the country in which they have chosen to reside.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the rights of european citizens must be strengthened. although european law guarantees equal treatment for european citizens, regardless of the country they are in, there are still gaps in implementation. the global economic crisis has accentuated certain xenophobic tendencies in some european countries, leading to a backsliding in the guarantee of equal rights for eu citizens. i therefore believe that the role of national administrations will be both to rigorously enforce european legislation that guarantees the protection of eu citizens and non-discriminatory treatment, and to facilitate dialogue and information.
in writing. - with the concept of european citizenship and the rights derived from it as its backbone, the report reviews a number of specific issues, starting from concrete situations of non-application or misapplication of the idea of european citizenship. such situations, which are invoked mainly by citizens through petitions to the ep's specialised committee, are considered to be incompatible with the idea of european citizenship and therefore to be criticised. of particular interest to romanian european citizens are a number of issues identified in the report as common in the eu area: discrimination on grounds of nationality, de facto differences between the rights of european citizens, which should be equal, the maintenance of derogations from the right to free movement or the invocation of criteria other than technical ones for the access of member states to the schengen area, criteria of the nature of violating the same right to free movement. in this context, the report highlights the need to better inform european citizens about their rights, and underlines the role of the ep, as the only directly elected body representing european citizens, which must take a clearer stand towards respecting the right to free movement, a fundamental right of the european citizen.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2013 eu citizenship report eu citizens: your rights, your future. we call on the commission to play an active role in ensuring that the procedures implemented by the member states fully respect the values and human rights recognised by the european treaties. we stress that labour mobility is one of the main pillars of the single market and we also highlight the positive benefits of eu migrant labour to the economies of the member states. in this regard, we call on the commission to closely monitor the situation and take appropriate measures to remove potential obstacles, such as excessive bureaucracy, to this fundamental freedom at national level. we invite each member state to set up, as soon as possible, a one-stop shop in each state for the coordination of projects with cross-border impact. we consider that the nomination of candidates for the post of president of the commission by european political parties at european level is an important step towards creating a genuine european public space and we argue that the prospect of a europeanisation of the electoral campaign can only be realised through pan-european activities and through local and national media networks, in particular public companies, in the fields of broadcasting, television and the internet.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, despite the more or less justified concerns that some national parliaments, including the chamber of deputies in romania, have expressed, i believe that the emergence of the european public prosecutor's office is a positive thing. we are talking, however, about investigations into the use of european money, and the union must have the right to protect its financial interests. that is why i cannot fully understand the negative opinions expressed by several parliaments on the proposal. if in the case of some, the justifications were pertinent and raised questions of common sense, in the case of the lower chamber of the parliament of romania it is clear that the motivation had a different substrate. perhaps the fear of a 100% independent prosecutor who could expose possible fraud led the representatives of power to reject such an institution. but i am glad that we in the european parliament are expressing our full support for commissioner reding's proposal, and i commend her for her tenacity and determination. one thing must be clear to all of us: we are in a time of crisis and now, more than ever, we must use european and national money as rationally and legally as possible.
in writing. - the creation of a european public prosecutor's office is an important step in the process of cooperation between member states in the field of criminal justice. the report aims to improve the fight against crossborder crime, cooperation between states, the protection of european values, european funds, etc. coordination with eurojust, olaf and europol would be functional and complementary to criminal prosecution, with a view to full judicial cooperation in criminal matters, bringing together significant national experiences in a single body, with the participation of all member states wherever possible. it is necessary to review the remedies for determining the court with jurisdiction for offences of the prosecutor's office's subsidiary competence, for investigative measures, for the admissibility of evidence and for the closure of investigations. in addition, as regards procedural safeguards, a set of principles and rights is necessary to strengthen the protection of suspects without thereby weakening the prosecution and punishment of offences. it is also important to create a responsive and rapid structure that ensures high standards of independence, experience and professionalism, balancing the need for rapid decisions with the accuracy of investigations and knowledge of the national realities in which the offences occur.

madam president, we are fully entitled to talk here about more transparency, more democratic control over the work of the institutions, which has actually saved several member states of the european union from financial, economic and social collapse. but in discussing these things, let's not forget the fundamentals, namely responsibility and solidarity. a country that is over-indebted -- that is in danger of not being able to pay its debts -- such a country has no choice but to restructure its economy. we expect solidarity from the creditors. creditors will always seek to give a respite to distressed countries, having faith, confidence that those countries are carrying out the necessary structural reforms and, of course, accommodating the revenue potential of that country with payment obligations. from this point of view, i consider that the troika has done its duty, even though there have been many complaints about the troika's activity. in difficult conditions, the troika did a good thing. the european union lacked the financial resources, financial instruments and experience to devise complex structural adjustment programmes for a number of troubled developed eu member states.
in writing. it has been almost four years since the first troika-imposed adjustment programme was launched in greece. unfortunately, the austerity measures dictated by the tripartite organization have brought recession and increased public debt and unemployment in the countries that have gone through such a program. today, unemployment in spain is over 25%. at the same time, greece's public debt stood at around 172% of gdp at the end of 2013, compared to 148% of gdp in 2010. the international monetary fund itself admitted in june last year that it had underestimated the negative effects of the austerity measures imposed on greece. however, the troika cannot be held accountable for its actions as it is not vested with democratic legitimacy. i therefore believe that it is necessary to replace the troika with a new, democratic and european law-based body, the european monetary fund, and to reform policies for countries in difficulty by including economic recovery and public debt support measures.

rapporteur. - mr president, the international financial reporting standards and the international standards on auditing are the bedrock for the comparability and transparency of company accounts throughout the union. this is about the quality of financial information in the decision-making process. public money – eur[nbsp ]43 million – will be used to co-finance three non-profit organisations which deliver public goods: the international financial reporting standards foundation, which, through the international accounting standards board, develops international financial reporting standards; the public interest oversight board, which oversees international audit, ethics and education standards for the accounting professions; and the european financial reporting advisory group (efrag), the technical adviser of the european commission, which assesses whether or not an ifrs standard complies with eu company law as part of the endorsement process in the european union. during our work on this report, important questions have arisen: the question of the prudence principle versus the neutral one included in the conceptual framework, and the principle that accounts should give the true and fair value; the question of independence of the standard issuers and the governors of these organisations; the need for convergence and the differences between the ifrs standard and the us accounting standards; and the effectiveness, proactivity and governance of efrag. answering these questions is not an easy task. we found ourselves in an academic debate, a professional debate and a political debate. during the negotiations, we finalised a good compromise on this report together with the council and commission. we have clear commitments regarding annual assessments of the work done by these three organisations; the commission's report by 31[nbsp ]march this year on efrag’s implementation of the maystadt recommendation; the commission report by 31[nbsp ]december[nbsp ]2014 on eight years of experience of ias regulation implementation; and, where appropriate, proposals for ias regulation changes. this report will also refer to governance arrangements for the ifrs foundation and the icb. the ifrs foundation and the icb will take measures for interest disclosure in order to avoid conflicts of interest. as rapporteur for this dossier, it is my duty to thank the shadows for their contribution and support: säid el khadraoui, wolf klinz, sven giegold, syed kamall and our assistants. i also thank commissioner barnier for his understanding of our concerns and for the right decision which he took.
mr president, i would stress that for the effective functioning of capital markets and the achievement of the integrated financial services market in the union, a common financial reporting framework is needed that functions properly. bodies active in the field of accounting and auditing in the union play important and decisive roles for the functioning of the internal market and obviously depend heavily on funding. this regulation should provide for the possibility of co-financing the activities of certain bodies pursuing objectives which are part of the union policy on the development and approval of standards or the supervision of standard-setting processes relating to financial reporting and auditing and which support that policy. i stress the importance of hiring top experts as well as the efficient use of financial resources, including for the training of experts to meet the union's policy objectives in financial reporting and auditing. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that perhaps, unfortunately, the current crisis is partly due to the fact that these standards could be made more stringent.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the european asylum system is not working at optimum parameters, and this is because there is no full solidarity between member states. it is clear to me that the southern states of the union are more exposed to waves of illegal immigrants or asylum seekers. this is why i welcome the fact that the financial allocations from the asylum, migration and integration fund will be given priority to those countries. i think the money should be used primarily for the construction of accommodation centers, because in many places the current facilities are overcrowded. the union should also provide support to the member states in the implementation of the union's external borders policy. this could give a chance of social integration to those who come to europe because their lives and safety are threatened in their countries of origin.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the asylum, migration and integration fund. this new financial instrument, covering the period 2014-2020, has a budget of around €3.1 billion over seven years, an increase of around 50% compared to the three funds from the 2007-2013 period that it now merges and expands. i welcome its adoption, as parliament has succeeded in strengthening the rights of migrants, in particular by giving priority to the financing of asylum and integration policies. the main improvements achieved by parliament's efforts include the fair and transparent distribution of funding between the different objectives of the fund (asylum, integration and return), with a minimum of 20%[nbsp ] of available funds allocated to asylum and integration policies respectively, the involvement of ngos and relevant international organisations in the development, implementation and monitoring of the fund at national level, the strengthening of a results-based approach that would not only take account of actions but also focus on a qualitative assessment of their achievements, and finally increased coordination and coherence between actions in countries.
in writing. - welcomes the adoption by the european parliament of the regulation on general provisions for the european asylum and migration fund; i agree with the agreed funding structure, namely the grants, but also with the co-financing rate of 75%. in addition, i welcome the flexibility of the regulation to allow the co-financing rate to be increased to 90% for strategic priorities and in exceptional circumstances. i believe that before the preparation of the multiannual national programmes, there should be a dialogue between the member states and the european commission to ensure the coherence of the strategies developed. i also believe that the european parliament should be regularly informed about the outcome of the political dialogues, but also about the preparation of the national programmes and their implementation. last but not least, i support the usefulness of providing technical assistance at the initiative of the european commission for the preparation and evaluation of projects, the strengthening of institutional capacities, the carrying out of evaluations, expertise and studies, as well as for the updating and interconnection of information systems at european level.
in writing. - i voted for the proposal for a regulation establishing the asylum and migration fund. the union's objective of an area of freedom, security and justice should be achieved, inter alia, through common measures to shape an asylum and immigration policy based on solidarity between member states and fair towards third countries and their nationals. the fund should reflect the need for increased flexibility and simplification, while respecting the requirements related to predictability and ensuring a fair and transparent allocation of resources to meet the general and specific objectives set out in this regulation. the general objective of the fund is to contribute to the effective management of migration flows and to the implementation, strengthening and development of the common policy on asylum, subsidiary protection and temporary protection, as well as the common immigration policy, while fully respecting the rights and principles enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the fund shall be established for the period from 1[nbsp ]january[nbsp ]2014 to 31[nbsp ]december[nbsp ]2020 and the overall resources for the implementation of this regulation shall be eur 3,137 million in current prices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the hong kong international convention on the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships should be ratified as soon as possible. the act is an important step worldwide towards safer and greener ship recycling. however, it should be borne in mind that stricter rules exist at eu level in this area, which means that ratification of the convention will not have a significant impact on member states. however, as regards third states, the application of the provisions of the convention will generate a greater degree of responsibility and safety when it comes to ship recycling.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation to ratify the hong kong international convention on the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships. although it was adopted in 2009, only norway has acceded to it. the recycling of ships is a very important process, given the pollution hazard it poses. due to the large number of hazardous materials carried on board, any ship to be dismantled poses a potential risk to the environment. even if the convention allows for the beach-failing method, globally it brings significant improvements over the current situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft decision on the ratification by member states of, or accession to, the hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships (2009) in the interests of the european union. the hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships was adopted on 15 may 2009 under the auspices of the international maritime organisation. in order to enter into force and take effect, it will need to be ratified by the main flag states and recycling states. on 9 january 2014, the convention was signed by five parties and only one of the parties (norway) acceded to it. in 2013, regulation (eu) no [nbsp ]1257/2013 on ship recycling was adopted. the purpose of this regulation is to ensure the environmentally friendly recycling of eu ships. this regulation also aims to facilitate the ratification of the hong kong international convention on the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships of 2009. the new regulation will not apply before 31 december 2015 and not later than 31 december 2018. it will legalise the recycling of eu ships in non-oecd countries provided that the recycling is carried out in facilities included in a european list.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. even if we are dealing with a controversial text, we cannot ignore the contributions made by the troika, in a context where the financial crisis has generated a serious economic and social crisis throughout the european union. each member state has experienced negative effects ranging from employment levels to access to credit or decreased income. my country, which is not yet a member of the eurozone, has faced the same problems as the rest of europe, and the negative effects could have been much worse without the tough but particularly useful measures taken by the former right-wing government in bucharest.
in writing. - i welcome the criticisms in the report of the ecb's unclear role in the troika and the specifics of the troika's decision-making process. the troika's mandate was perceived as unclear, lacking in transparency and democratic control. i therefore believe that more transparent procedures are needed with regard to the adoption of macroeconomic adjustment programmes and the respect of the control rights conferred on the european parliament. it is also necessary to focus after the first phase of intervention, which led to macroeconomic stabilisation on policies to boost growth, create jobs and improve the social situation, in order to alleviate the tensions caused by troika pressures.
in writing. - i welcome the european parliament's report on the role and activities of the troika in the four euro area countries covered by the adjustment programmes. it should be noted that the trigger factors for the crisis were fundamentally different in greece, portugal, ireland and cyprus, and their public finances were in a vulnerable situation even before the crisis. although the structural deficits of the four eu countries have been reduced since the start of the financial assistance programmes, it is regrettable that a reduction in the public debt-to-gdp ratio has not been achieved. i believe that too little attention has been paid to the economic and social impact of adjustment strategies. there was also uncertainty about the role of the european central bank (ecb) in the adjustment programmes and a lack of transparency and democratic control over the troika's activities. it is regrettable that the former eurogroup president admitted before the european parliament that the troika's recommendations were agreed without the political implications being analysed in detail. they also question the dual role played by the european commission in the troika, namely both as an agent of the member states and as an institution of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the inquiry into the role and activities of the troika (ecb, commission and imf) in the euro area countries participating in the programme. the troika was composed of the european commission, the european central bank (ecb) and the international monetary fund (imf) and was established following the adoption of the decision of 25[nbsp ]march[nbsp ]2010 by the euro area heads of state or government to establish a joint programme and to grant conditional bilateral loans to greece, a decision also based on the recommendations of the ecofin council, which has since become operational for portugal, ireland and cyprus. the troika and its role are laid down in regulation no [nbsp ]472/2013 of 21[nbsp ]may[nbsp ]2013 and are mentioned in the treaty on the european stability mechanism (esm). we stress that the recommendations in the memoranda of understanding are in contradiction with the modernisation policy developed in the form of the lisbon strategy and the europe 2020 strategy. we stress that the memoranda of understanding need to be adapted to take account of the wage-setting practices and systems and the national reform programme of the member state concerned in the context of the union strategy for growth and jobs, as provided for in regulation (eu) no [nbsp ]472/2013 article 7 (1).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, especially as i fully agree that once the economic and budgetary sustainability of the four countries is guaranteed, efforts must focus on social aspects, with particular attention to job creation. we are witnessing unprecedented levels of unemployment in europe and all our efforts must be focused on remedying this dangerous situation in which we find ourselves. however, it is worrying that, when looking closely at the growth prospects and unemployment levels, these countries, which have gone through the imposed austerity programme, have not improved their situation considerably.
in writing. - the report has two main objectives: to be strictly limited to the economic and social realities in greece, ireland, portugal and cyprus, before and after the adjustment programmes, and to integrate the problems and solutions needed into reality. the adjustment programmes and the economic crisis have led to an increase in unemployment and job losses, with a significant impact on public social protection systems. the troika and the member states should establish crisis management mechanisms to increase transparency in decision-making. the commission and the member states should consider public health and education expenditure as an investment in the future, not as a cost that can be cut, and should treat social aspects on an equal footing with economic ones. member states should consider that future labour sector reforms take into account the principle of flexicurity and enhancing the competitiveness of enterprises and do not overlook other key reforms, such as those related to the cost of energy, social dumping, unfair competition, fair and efficient financial systems and tax policies that favour growth and employment. it is also important to develop a social recovery and job creation plan as a matter of urgency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on employment and social aspects of the role and work of the troika (ecb, commission and imf) in the euro area countries participating in the programme. the unprecedented economic and financial crisis has exposed the fragility of public finances in some member states. measures under the economic adjustment programmes adopted in response to the situation in greece (may 2010 and march 2012), ireland (december 2010), portugal (may 2011) and cyprus (june 2013) have had a direct and indirect impact on employment levels and living conditions of many people. we recommend that the commission and the member states consider health and education spending not as deductible expenditure but as a public investment in the country's future, which should be respected and increased in order to accelerate economic and social recovery. we invite the commission and the council to give social imbalances and measures to correct them the same attention as they give to macroeconomic imbalances and to ensure that adjustment measures aim at achieving social justice and fostering a balance between growth and employment, implementing structural reforms and fiscal consolidation.

in writing. - european parliament legislative resolution of 13[nbsp ]march[nbsp ]2014 on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security in the union (com (2013) 0048 c7-0035/2013 2013/0027 (cod)). networks together with information systems and services play a vital role in society. their reliability and security are essential for the freedom and general security of the citizens of the union, as well as for economic activities and social well-being and, in particular, for the functioning of the internal market. the directive adopted at first reading lays down measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security (nis) in the union. to this end, the directive: (a) lays down obligations for all member states with regard to the prevention, management and response to risks and incidents affecting network and information systems; (b) establish a cooperation mechanism between member states to ensure uniform application of this directive throughout the union and, where necessary, coordinated, efficient and effective management and response to risks and incidents affecting network and information systems, with the participation of the relevant stakeholders; (c) lay down the security requirements for market operators.
