in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because one of the advantages of the lisbon treaty is that it gives increased powers to the european parliament. after all, meps are the only elected representatives of the european citizens. i must point out, however, that the new powers which the treaty gives us give parliament a certain degree of control over the european commission's acts, but not over its composition. in practice, parliament votes for the commission, but the chances of sanctioning it, or even dismissing it in exceptional cases, are reduced to a minimum. the treaty also does not require that the vote of european citizens be respected when nominating a candidate for the presidency of the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the implementation of the lisbon treaty strengthens the democratic prerogatives of the eu, in particular by regulating more precisely the interinstitutional relations between the european parliament and the european commission. there is a need to deepen european integration and protect the community method, and to enhance the democratic legitimacy of the eu institutions, in particular the commission. i therefore support the proposal for the nomination of the candidates for president of the commission by european political parties, thus creating a closer link between the vote of the citizens and the election of the president of the commission by the european parliament. in addition to the need for democratic legitimacy of eu fora in the context of the identity crisis of the european project, it must be borne in mind that the treaty of lisbon has considerably strengthened the role of the european parliament, conferring on it important new powers with regard to eu legislation and international agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, in my opinion, the right to property is a fundamental right that should be guaranteed at the universal level. as the report shows, over a billion people live on property to which they have no official right. what's even more worrying is that in some regions, even those who theoretically have such rights could lose them, especially in the context of abuse by the authorities. the existence of customary rules that often replace legal regulations creates a climate of legal uncertainty, especially for right-holders, and thus inhibits economic growth, because, for example, a farmer will only be incentivised to cultivate his land if it has legal stability and legal predictability.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the role of property rights, property regimes and wealth creation in eradicating poverty and promoting sustainable development in developing countries. property rights can be defined as the rules of conventional or customary law governing the conditions under which individuals, communities, public and private actors acquire and retain access to tangible and intangible assets. the commission notes that the land use rights of the beneficiaries are not limited to the land use rights of the beneficiaries, but are also limited to the land use rights of the beneficiaries. the obligations of investors should be defined in clear terms and should be enforceable, for example by including sanctioning mechanisms in cases of human rights violations. all land transactions should also include a legal obligation to sell a certain minimum percentage of the produced crops on the local market. we stress that land policies must guarantee secure land rights for different ethnic, social or generational groups in a fair manner.

the author. - mr president, i was the one who proposed that this item be placed on the agenda. i have received the support of the epp and then of the other political groups and i would like to take this opportunity to thank them. why did i bring this up? because while our attention is now focused on the russian invasion of crimea, i think we also need to be aware of the serious violations of human rights and the rule of law that are taking place in russia. the latest example is the very verdict on february 24th regarding eight of the bolotnaya square protesters, protesters who took to the streets in may 2012 along with tens of thousands of russians, to simply express their dissatisfaction with putin's re-election. the whole process is revolting. the charges were clearly politically motivated, as an expression of contempt for difference of opinion, the procedural rights of the accused were not respected, and the sentences handed down are clearly disproportionate. a new wave of arrests followed, in fact, after the verdict. opposition leaders boris nemtsov and alexei navalny were again thrown in jail for ten days. navalny is now under house arrest and an electronic bracelet monitors his movements. another accused in connection with the events of may 2012, mikhail koshenko, was sentenced last year to forced psychiatric treatment. all of these are practices of silencing dissent, reminiscent of the soviet period and the treatment of political dissidents, and therefore have nothing to do with democracy. i think we need to redefine our strategy with russia. i personally don't think, as i've said here, that at this point, under putin, russia can still be considered a strategic partner of the european union. these practices take it out of the realm of some frequented democracies.
in writing. – the actions of the russian authorities in the bolotnaya square case are absolutely unacceptable. following this protest, which was held in may 2012 in response to alleged irregularities in the 2011 parliamentary elections, 400 people were detained. eight people have now received prison sentences. amnesty international called these cases ‘politically motivated show trials’ and indicated that the bolotnaya protesters had suffered abuse at the hands of the russian police. stepan zimin, one of those recently convicted, was accused of throwing stones at police; however, there is no video evidence of this, nor is there any reliable witness testimony to corroborate the story. mikhail kosenko, who was convicted in october 2013, was sentenced to indefinite forced psychiatric treatment. though he suffers from a psychiatric disorder, he has been living normally for many years; yet, the court inexplicably decided that he was not mentally sound. additionally, the policeman who was the supposed victim of kosenko could not identify him during his trial. politically motivated abuses by the russian judiciary and police cannot be condoned. if this trend continues, it could have major repercussions for russia’s relations with the eu. as such, i strongly urge the russian government to take all necessary steps to promptly fulfil its legal and humanitarian obligations.

member of the commission. - madam president, let me first thank ms ayala sender for her work on this report. i am glad to see that parliament recognises the progress that we have made in the fight against fraud. i agree that there is always room for further improvement and that this further improvement needs to encompass two aspects. we need to improve as far as our actual measures to protect taxpayers’ money are concerned, but we also need to continue improving our reporting on fraud. on the first point, i am convinced that the key instrument is the european public prosecutor’s office that the commission proposed in july last year. if we want to make tangible progress we must make sure that this office is being set up as an independent european structure with the right competences. parliament’s support on this, in this report and in your recent interim report, is crucial and much appreciated. on the second point, i would like to remind members that we have already taken on board several of the requests that parliament has made in the past. this includes, for example, the detailed analysis of fraudulent irregularities. but we will look into additional possibilities to make our reporting even more meaningful in the future. this is the last anti-fraud report by this parliament and the last one to be published under the mandate of this commission. i therefore would like to take the opportunity to take a brief look beyond this report at what we have achieved over this last four and a half years. i think i can say that during this period we have taken unprecedented legal and legislative measures to improve the protection of our taxpayers’ money. this series of measures was kicked off in 2011 when the commission adopted its multiannual anti-fraud strategy. initially addressed to the commission services, the strategy was pivotal in raising fraud awareness, including among managing and audit authorities. moreover, based on the strategy, specific anti-fraud provisions were introduced into the new spending programmes for 2014-2020. a second milestone in stepping up our fight against fraud was marked by the reorganisation of olaf in 2012 and the adoption of the new olaf regulation in 2013. both have streamlined olaf procedures and increased the effectiveness of the office. at the same time, they reinforced the procedural guarantees for the persons concerned. in 2012 and 2013, the commission addressed the criminal law side of the protection of the eu’s financial interests. apart from the proposal on the european public prosecutor’s office that i have already mentioned, we also proposed a directive on the fight against fraud by means of criminal law. this directive should remove loopholes in member states’ anti-fraud legislation that impair the effective prosecution of fraudsters. i therefore count on members’ support when they vote on this proposal. finally, we have also taken a number of important measures to protect specifically the revenue side of the eu budget. these were in particular the directives on a quick-reaction mechanism against vat fraud and the reverse charge mechanism, the signature of the fctc protocol on illicit trade in tobacco and our 2013 communication on the fight against tobacco smuggling. cigarette smuggling is a complex phenomenon and we appreciate parliament’s support in our fight. with all these measures, the commission has indeed shaped a new landscape for anti-fraud policy at eu level. i am confident that we will soon be able to reap the benefits of the efforts we have made.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, as rapporteur of the group of the european people's party, i support the prosecution of cases of fraud against european funds and the recovery of the money. however, there are shortcomings, particularly in the member states, which need to be addressed urgently. i'll just mention a few of them. a first shortcoming is the collection of credible and comparable statistics at european level, which is still a difficult process because member states use different criteria for analysis and collection. secondly, the rate of criminal prosecutions initiated by member states on the basis of investigations carried out by olaf is in any event low and, moreover, uneven across member states. thirdly, in the absence of dialogue between olaf and the directorates-general, the financial indicators for rural development excluded 99,83% of cases from the selection procedure for investigations. so, practically all rural development cases went uninvestigated when there was a suspicion of fraud. in addition, i am deeply concerned about the attitude of some member states, which deal with fraudulent irregularities only by applying financial corrections and do not investigate possible crimes. this is unacceptable and encourages fraudsters and endangers the entire european anti-fraud strategy. finally, i asked the commission to publish on its website the beneficiaries of european funds from all member states, given that greater transparency is needed, which is crucial to see fraudulent schemes and to deter, identify and catch them.

in writing. - due to the ageing of the population, changing working conditions and production patterns and above all the financial crisis, strong action is needed to enable older workers to remain active in the labour market. the use of an older workforce and the extension of working life can make a positive contribution to recovery and future growth, although this must be mitigated by the necessary opportunity to secure jobs for our young people. the measures under the european social fund (esf) are therefore more important than ever for the implementation of the new programmes starting in 2014.
in writing. - i welcome the conclusions and recommendations of the european court of auditors, which i hope the member states and the european commission will take into account. older workers are a vulnerable category; it is regrettable that there is no data at the level of operational programmes on the effectiveness of the european social fund expenditure for this category. it is of concern that in some member states there is no consistency in the definition of age groups at the level of the different operational programmes. in general, i think we need more transparency when we talk about spending european funds, but also better defined impact indicators, in order to have a correct measure of how efficiently and effectively the european social fund is spent for each social category and target group.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on special report no 25/2012 of the european court of auditors: are there instruments in place to monitor the effectiveness of the european social fund funding for older workers? in 2012, the employment rate in the eu in the 55-64 age group was below 50% (54.4% for men and 41.8% for women). we call on the commission to put more emphasis on combating age discrimination against older workers and to use its powers under existing legal instruments to combat age discrimination. we call on the member states to apply and complement the common esf indicators in the next programming period accordingly, in order to establish the number of older workers, men and women, who have taken part in esf-funded projects, with a focus on adapting to the workplace, acquiring new skills, improving the labour market situation of workers or finding a job, and how many of them have gained new qualifications, improved their labour market situation or found a job after benefiting from esf-funded projects.
in writing. - i voted for the report. i consider the statements made by the italian mep to be a form of insult to the roma community. at the same time, i do not believe that such statements are directly related to the mandate of the mep, especially since they were not made in the plenary of the european parliament. that is why i think it is right that the judiciary should rule on this case and that the mep's immunity should not be defended by parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament decision on the request for the defence of the immunity and privileges of mario borghezio. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of prosecution, detention or legal proceedings for opinions or votes expressed in the performance of their duties. the purpose of this provision is to ensure in principle the freedom of expression of members of the european parliament, but this right to freedom of expression does not authorize slander, defamation, incitement to hatred or insult to the honour of other persons. statements made by deputy mario borghezio refer to alleged characteristics of the roma ethnic group. at the same time, the statements he is accused of exceeding the tone that generally characterizes political debate and, moreover, are deeply anti-parliamentary in nature. they are contrary to article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and therefore cannot be considered to have been made in the exercise of the duties of a member of the european parliament. this decision therefore decides not to protect the immunities and privileges of mr mario borghezio.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and its recommendations because i believe that all those involved in the death of sergei magnitsky must be held accountable. if the russian judiciary has chosen not to clarify things, it is necessary that at least the european union takes a series of measures to sanction the guilty. the freezing of financial assets or travel restrictions are very useful tools to put pressure on the russian judiciary. it must shed light on this case.
in writing. - i voted for the recommendation to establish common visa restrictions for russian officials involved in the sergei magnitsky case. the arrest of sergei magnitsky, followed by his death in custody, is a well-documented and significant case of human rights and fundamental freedoms violations in russia. russia, as a member of several international organisations, is committed to the protection and promotion of human rights, fundamental freedoms and the rule of law. at the same time, the eu has repeatedly provided additional assistance and expertise to help russia modernise and comply with its constitutional and legal order in line with council of europe standards. however, there is a growing need for a firm, coherent and comprehensive eu policy towards russia, coupled with unhesitating and fair criticism, including sanctions and restrictive measures. the visa restrictions for russian officials involved in the sergei magnitsky case and other restrictive measures do not constitute in themselves judicial sanctions in the traditional sense, but are nevertheless a political signal of eu concern addressed to a wider public and thus continue to be a necessary and legitimate foreign policy instrument.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that at the level of international organisations, especially those with political relevance, the union must speak with one voice and that the priorities must be common. only then can we become more credible, and only then can we count internationally when major decisions are made. i welcome the fact that these priorities include the eradication of torture, the principle of the responsibility to protect, and post-2015 development assistance. last but not least, i am pleased that climate change continues to occupy a particularly high place on the political agenda of the european union. it is clear that without a global commitment, the achievement of carbon reduction targets is impossible.
in writing. - i voted for the ep recommendation on the 69th session of the united nations general assembly. as the world's leading donor, the eu supports both stepping up efforts to meet the 2015 deadline for the millennium development goals (mdgs) and a common approach to poverty eradication and sustainable development. i support the recommendations to the council such as: • to promote the integration of human rights and fundamental freedoms into all aspects of un activity; • to call on the un general assembly members to make full transparency in corporate reporting and the fight against corruption, money laundering, tax havens, illicit financial flows and harmful tax structures a top priority on the agenda of international financial and development institutions; • ensure that poverty eradication remains a priority in the new single and integrated framework, alongside the fight against inequality and the promotion of sustainable development, food security and gender equality; • work towards a single, comprehensive and integrated framework for the post-2015 mdgs with clear benchmarks, including the key aspects of development and sustainability; • ensure that this framework is universal and global, promoting prosperity, human rights and well-being for all.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because the role of the media in promoting common values and principles of the european union on a global scale is essential. the establishment of a european radio service worldwide can act as a means of promoting democratic values and universal human rights. despite the cultural differences in the world, a number of principles should be among the priorities of any state. the role of the european union is therefore to promote and strengthen them, including through the media.
in writing. - an internationally-present european broadcaster can play an important role in communicating the values of democracy, freedom of the press and human rights throughout the world. it will also play an active role in explaining different national perceptions, communicating eu policies, shaping a genuine european perspective and providing the public with reliable and high-quality information. in the light of the above, i believe that we need a coherent and substantive eu broadcasting strategy in the context of its external relations, thus promoting freedom of expression and media pluralism and upholding and strengthening democracy and human rights in europe and in third countries.
in writing. - european broadcasting with an international presence can play an important role in communicating the values of democracy, press freedom and human rights worldwide, in explaining different national perceptions, in communicating eu policies, in shaping a genuine european perspective and in providing the public with reliable and high-quality information, mainly through a firm, ongoing commitment to journalistic objectivity. any threat to media independence through government intervention, intimidation of journalists, lack of transparency of ownership structures or superior commercial interests affects the overall situation of media freedom and pluralism in any country. it is important to establish a coherent and substantive eu broadcasting strategy in the context of its external relations, thus promoting freedom of expression and media pluralism and upholding and strengthening democracy and human rights in europe and in third countries. it is essential to target eu project-related funding from external aid towards broadcasting services that already comply with and act in accordance with the highest standards of independence, accuracy and journalistic balance and promote eu values, as well as towards projects that would enable broadcasting services that lag behind in terms of independence, accuracy and sustainability to achieve those standards.
in writing. - the watson report, adopted on april 2nd, calls for media bodies to be editorial independent. that means not being dependent on a partisan political interest. when i worked on the text, as rapporteur for the epp group, i asked myself a few questions: is there any country in the union where a tv station is 100% the voice of a political party? would a european socialist party accept as its political-media satellite a creation of someone convicted of collaborating with the political police of a former communist country? is it acceptable for a media outlet to stigmatize the opponents of the socialists without giving them the right to reply? are european values respected when a tv channel is the one that robs the public of the right to information? is it normal for such manipulators to enjoy impunity, since their sanction is decided - by vote - by a body (cna) whose members are as politicized as the station that should be stopped from committing abuses? is there on european soil a political-media success based on blackmail and intolerance? can we accept the operation of a media institution that, if it were registered as a political party, would be banned? can we just be indifferent? all these are rhetorical questions for a romanian who has at least once looked at antena 3.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the role of broadcasting in promoting the eu and its values. i support the importance of a specific approach to broadcasting without prejudice to the independence of the media and the competence of the member states to confer, define and organise the mission of public service broadcasting. they should adhere to a broadcasting charter that requires the broadcasting of fair and objective news and a balanced and comprehensive presentation of the diversity of the eu and its member states, adhere to a journalistic code with a particular focus on policies to guarantee journalistic independence, accuracy and balance, and to this end, establish their own independent codes of conduct and define their editorial lines. i also believe that euronews, with its wide network of national stations and its wide distribution, can play an important role in the media landscape and in stimulating the debate on europe, including in third countries. they argue that euronews should have the means to continue to operate in several languages and to promote opportunities for education and training of journalists on european issues.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that we must not overlook the impact of noise on health. studies show that in addition to the stress associated with noise pollution, it also has effects on the human body, possibly even contributing to high blood pressure or nervous system dysfunction. noise pollution should not be a necessity in highly industrialized areas or a certification of a powerful machine, on the contrary. that is why i support this proposal, which will have the beneficial effect of reducing ambient noise, firstly by clearly defining limit values.
in writing. - today's vote is a step forward in protecting public health and the environment through measures to reduce vehicle noise. labelling and consumer information are important issues and therefore i consider it necessary and appropriate that the commission should consider an impact assessment on the labelling conditions applicable to noise and air pollution levels and the correct information of consumers. manufacturers, in turn, must provide complete and adequate information on the sound level of vehicles at the point of sale and in technical promotional material. it is of particular importance that the protection of blind and other vulnerable persons be ensured by the installation of appropriate audible warning systems in electric vehicles and, to this end, the parliament and the council have agreed that such systems should be made mandatory.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the adoption of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the noise level of motor vehicles and of silencers, because i believe that reducing the noise level of motor vehicles is in the interest of public health. given the increasing number of motor vehicles on european roads, i believe that a reduction in the limit value for noise pollution is needed. annex iii is a good step in this direction, as it not only provides for a limitation of values, but it provides for this limitation to take place in three phases, thus reducing economic efforts. they also agree to install an audible warning system in electric cars to ensure adequate protection for blind people.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution of the house on the adoption of the regulation on the sound level of motor vehicles and replacement silencers. the proposal aims to protect public health and the environment through measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. the main elements of the agreed text are as follows: the commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the technical specifications for the vehicle categories m1 to m3 and n1 to n3 and the technical specifications for the vehicle categories m1 to m3 and n1 to n3 as referred to in article 7 of regulation (eu) no 167/2013. implement an impact assessment on the labelling conditions applicable to noise and air pollution levels and inform consumers: manufacturers will provide information on vehicle noise levels at the point of sale and in technical promotional material; ensure the protection of blind and other vulnerable persons by installing appropriate acoustic warning systems in electric vehicles. this provision will apply to new types of vehicles within three years of the date of application of the regulation, and within five years for all electric and hybrid vehicles; road surface issues and their contribution to reducing vehicle noise - the commission will develop information and best practice guidelines on technological development of road quality and road classification, based on information provided by member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the proposed amendments concerning the electronic identification of bovine animals and the abolition of the provisions on the optional labelling of beef and veal involve a number of changes to the electronic databases which form part of the surveillance networks in the member states. this is a simple adaptation because until now the electronic databases set up in the member states contained information on bovine animals located on their territory but not data on the electronic identification of bovine animals.
in writing. - i voted against the parliament's resolution on the proposal for a directive on electronic databases forming part of the surveillance networks in the member states. food safety is one of the main concerns of european citizens and this was seen last year in the case of horse meat fraud. the technology is available and therefore member states need to increase their efficiency in identification and traceability methods. the more information citizens receive about the food they consume, the more confident they become as consumers. the s&d group supports the need for a mandatory system for electronic identification of animals, within a transitional period of 10 years. this will give member states the time needed to introduce this system, which will reduce administrative costs, simplify registration and guarantee traceability of animals. the s&d group also supports the maintenance of the voluntary labelling system, which is working well and provides manufacturers with additional tools to promote their products and customers with the necessary information. we regret that the agreement reached did not take into account the s&d group's view.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the application and compliance of international trade rules by all state actors is essential for the stability and predictability of the system. there are many countries that do not comply with international rules in this area and the union must have measures in place to counter any adverse effects of breaches of international rules. i also believe that services should be included in the range of trade policy measures available to the union, to the extent that international or bilateral bodies for the settlement of trade disputes allow this.
in writing. - the eu currently lacks a horizontal legislative framework to ensure the exercise of its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. in the context of the increasing number of retaliatory measures worldwide, the proposed instrument is legitimately intended to strengthen the exercise of eu trade rights and eu credibility and ultimately to convince our economic partners to respect the rules of the game set out in trade agreements. in recent years, there have been few cases where the eu has had to resort to retaliatory measures; however, an important factor in ensuring a positive solution is the existence of a credible threat. it should be noted that in the absence of a horizontal framework, each decision should now be adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, which takes on average between 15 and 31 months.
in writing. - the european union does not currently have a state-of-the-art legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. the question of international trade agreements has always been a thorny one, involving a number of issues, including the protection of our products and the respect of the principle of reciprocity. in a global context such as the one in which we operate, the new strategy is designed for the legitimate purpose of enforcing the eu's trade rights, to strengthen its credibility and to enforce the rules of trade agreements on our trading partners.
in writing. - i support the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the exercise of the union's rights to apply and enforce the rules of international trade. i consider it imperative to create a legislative framework to ensure the exercise of the union's rights in international trade agreements. the european union's rights in international trade are currently enforced through the ordinary decision-making procedure, which is very time-consuming and entails high economic losses for the union. the european union needs credible threats that give it negotiating power, thus avoiding retaliation. i support extending trade policy to the services sector, as it is a fast-growing economic area that could be severely affected if a third country fails to respect union rights.
in writing. - i voted for the regulation on the exercise of the union's rights to enforce and enforce international trade rules. this regulation lays down rules and procedures to ensure the effective and timely exercise of the union's rights to suspend or withdraw concessions or other obligations under international trade agreements with a view to responding to breaches of international trade rules by third countries affecting the interests of the union, to rebalancing concessions or other obligations in trade relations with third countries, when the treatment of union goods is altered in a way that affects the interests of the union. it is essential that the union has adequate instruments to ensure the effective exercise of its rights under international trade agreements in order to protect its economic interests. member states should ensure that commercial policy measures in the field of public procurement are applied in their territories in the manner that best corresponds to their administrative structures and practices, while respecting union law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it required full alignment of the acts regulating trade in rice from bangladesh with the lisbon treaty and the omnibus regulations. the use of delegated or implementing acts is necessary to allow the commission to take decisions in a timely manner. however, the european parliament's scrutiny of these acts is essential.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on imports of rice originating in bangladesh. in the context of the uruguay round, the union committed itself to offering preferential import arrangements for rice originating in the least developed countries. one of the countries to which the offer was addressed, namely bangladesh, expressed an interest in developing its rice trade. the preferential import arrangements shall involve a reduction of import duties up to a certain quantity of husked rice. the equivalent quantities of rice at processing stages other than the husked rice stage should be calculated in accordance with commission regulation (ec) no 1312/2008. the preferential import arrangements shall be limited to a quantity equivalent to 4 000 tonnes of husked rice per calendar year. the quantities of rice at processing stages other than husked rice shall be converted using the conversion rates laid down in article 1 of regulation (ec) no 1312/2008. we consider it important to recognise the right of small farmers and rural workers to a decent income and a safe and healthy working environment as a fundamental objective in granting trade preferences to developing countries and in particular to the least developed countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that all aspects of health, and therefore of medical devices used for this purpose, must be treated with the utmost seriousness. with regard to the safety of medical devices and their free movement within the internal market, the interpretation and application of the rules should be uniform and should not leave room for interpretation or uncertainty. high quality standards and, most importantly, the safety of patients and healthcare professionals must take precedence in this area. i therefore welcome the amendments made by this regulation which will ensure the proper functioning of the internal market in this area.
in writing. - in recent years, there have been substantial shortcomings in the conformity assessment procedure, such as lack of transparency, rapid approval and placing on the market of medical devices despite insufficient patient investigations and therefore insufficient clinical data, which have put patients at risk. medical devices that could pose the greatest risks to patients should be subject to a stricter procedure than conformity assessment. this category should include medical devices listed in class iii, those implanted in the body, those incorporating a substance considered to be a medicinal product, those intended for the administration of a medicinal product or those using non-viable tissues or cells of human or animal origin or derivatives thereof. for such devices, it was proposed to introduce the possibility to assess on a case-by-case basis the robustness of the clinical data and the evidence that the device can be placed safely on the eu market. a category of special notified bodies has been created. the provisions concerning the staff of the authorities responsible for the designation and monitoring of notified bodies should be strengthened also to ensure that those authorities have the necessary qualifications to audit the notified bodies for which they are responsible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on medical devices, which classifies medical devices into four classes according to the level of risk to patients. i consider that medical devices which could present the greatest risks to patients should be subject to a stricter procedure than conformity assessment. a medical device evaluation committee (mdec) shall be established to provide case-by-case evaluation when its members consider it necessary for the review of clinical data. the acmd shall be formally placed under the aegis of the commission, which shall provide its secretariat and its smooth functioning. the acmd will be composed of the best specialists in different medical fields. patient representatives and a representative of the european medicines agency should be part of the mca and contribute to the case-by-case assessments. i also consider that the provisions concerning the staff of the authorities responsible for the designation and monitoring of notified bodies should be strengthened to ensure that those authorities also have the necessary qualifications to audit the notified bodies for which they are responsible. in addition, they should ensure that notified bodies have in-house competent staff on a permanent basis, with the exception of subcontracting.
in writing. - i supported this report because the regulation of in vitro diagnostic medical devices must be clear and uniform. this regulation also appears in the context of scientific and technological developments in the field in recent years, which have led to substantial differences in the interpretation and application of the rules. the new clear and transparent regulatory framework will address all these shortcomings and will by default lead to an increased level of safety for patients as well as for healthcare professionals. another important aspect is that such unitary legislation has the potential to support and encourage innovation, thus increasing the competitiveness of the in vitro diagnostic medical device industry.
in writing. - ivd medical devices are medical devices for in vitro (out of the body) diagnosis, which can be performed in the laboratory or in close proximity to the patient, for example at the bedside. this term encompasses a huge variety of tests, such as self-testing for blood sugar, hiv testing, and dna testing. the notified bodies need to be substantially improved and the monitoring of notified bodies by the member states needs to be strengthened. strengthening the vigilance and market surveillance system is very important. unannounced inspections of undertakings will be compulsory. in addition, the commission proposes the introduction of a network of european reference laboratories, which have an important role in the control of high-risk medical devices and will considerably improve patient safety. the commission will also be able to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of personal data, in particular the rules on the protection of personal data and the rules on the protection of personal data. the protection of minors and other persons who are not in a position to give informed consent should be regulated in the same way as in the 2001 clinical trials directive; the deadlines should be moderately extended to give the ethics committee and the authorities the time to assess the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices. ivd medical devices are medical devices for in vitro (out of the body) diagnosis, which can be performed in the laboratory or in close proximity to the patient, for example at the bedside. this term encompasses a huge variety of tests, such as self-testing for blood sugar, hiv testing, and dna testing. ivd medical devices are products which can circulate freely in the common market and therefore the european union is obliged to ensure the highest possible level of safety. the commission proposal includes major improvements to address the current shortcomings of the system for ivd medical devices, similar to those for other medical devices. the notified bodies will be substantially improved and the monitoring of notified bodies by the member states will be strengthened. it is very important that the vigilance and market surveillance system be strengthened. in addition, the commission proposes to introduce a network of european reference laboratories, which play an important role in the control of high-risk medical devices. the parliament amended the commission proposal to take account of the capacity and needs of smes, such as the possibility to provide information also by electronic means, and the information accompanying the product must be provided in an official language of the union.
in writing. - identifying the links between the environment and the economy and measuring the impact of the economy on the environment became needs to which the european institutions responded promptly by adopting the regulation on environmental economic accounts in 2011, when the first three modules were introduced. since then, the european parliament has called for the gradual adoption of new accounts that would lead to improved policymaking. today we adopted three new modules on environmental protection expenditure, the environmental goods and services sector and the accounts for physical energy flows, which have the potential to contribute to the development of more comprehensive indicators, thus improving both the quality of european policy-making and public debate. what is really important in this file is that member states can really fulfil their obligations to collect, compile, transmit and evaluate data specific to each of the accounts. therefore, as rapporteur, i proposed that the first reference year be the year following the year of entry into force of this regulation, giving member states time to adapt their statistical systems to the reporting needs established by the regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that over time environmental accounting, recently introduced to the european union agenda, will have a strong impact on analysis and forecasting. it will be used both for the preparation of policy proposals and for reports on the implementation of policies and their impact. the most important aspect i think is the one that relates to measuring the effects of economic activity on the environment, but also the contribution that the environment makes to the economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the proposal for a regulation on european environmental economic accounts. the current pace of developments and uncertainties about likely future trends require further measures to ensure that union policies continue to be based on a sound understanding of the environmental situation, the possible response options and their consequences. new tools should therefore be developed to ensure the preparation of data and indicators of a guaranteed quality and to improve their accessibility. the environmental protection expenditure accounts present data, in a manner compatible with the data reported in the european system of accounts (esa), on environmental protection related expenditure, namely the economic resources allocated by resident units to environmental protection. these accounts allow the compilation of national environmental protection-related expenditure which is defined as the sum of the use of environmental protection services by resident units, gross fixed capital formation for environmental protection activities and transfers for environmental protection which are not a counterpart of the previous items, less the financing by the rest of the world. the accounts of environmental protection expenditure should use information already existing in the national accounts, structural business statistics, the business register and other sources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, given that the deadline for achieving the millennium development goals is 2015, the commission's decision to declare this year the european year of development is welcome. in 2015, a reflection at european level will be needed on the direction development assistance policies should take. there is certainly a need for continued global commitments to poverty reduction. increasing literacy is also imperative. last but not least, promoting respect for human rights as a condition for achieving economic prosperity is another priority.
in writing. - the european year for development should raise awareness of all forms of gender discrimination faced by women and girls in different regions, especially in access to education, employment and healthcare, as well as in cases of forced marriage, sexual exploitation, genital mutilation and other harmful practices. combating poverty and all forms of discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression should be the main objective of the european union's development policy. the allocation of financial assistance for development should respect these universal values. the eu should ensure, by making development aid conditional, that third countries protect women and girls from torture. the council should suspend aid to countries that practice torture and direct this aid to support victims. the fact that women and girls are the most vulnerable to poverty, hunger, illiteracy, disease and all forms of exploitation should be taken very seriously in eu development assistance programmes. promoting gender equality and women's empowerment are considered effective ways to combat poverty, hunger and disease and to encourage sustainable development.
in writing. - the declaration of 2015 as the european year of development is a very important signal from the european parliament at a time when financial difficulties around the world are diverting attention to other issues, often wrongly considered as priorities. the existence of a close link between development and the right to human dignity should, however, remind us of the importance of the desire to combat poverty, which goes beyond the borders of the european union and is, in the end, the ultimate goal of development as a process. through the tools that will be made available to the eu under this project, 2015 will allow us to engage as many people as possible in achieving our goals. the more than 100 million europeans who unfortunately live on the poverty line remind us that, while we act abroad, we cannot ignore what is happening on the european continent, where we will have to continue to fight to reduce the gap between states. as vice-president of the committee on development, i welcome this initiative and will unconditionally join the european union's efforts in this regard.
in writing. - 2015 is a testbed for highlighting and making visible the development policies implemented by the european union. the european parliament has, in the legislature which is about to end, fought hard for funds and policies dedicated to reducing the differences between the different member states. we must continue to work in this direction to meet the major challenges of cooperation policy by advancing the achievement of the millennium development goals and the post-2015 agenda.
in writing. - welcomes the report of the european parliament on the declaration of 2015 as the european year of development; this initiative will facilitate european awareness of the development challenges faced by the world's poorest states and draw attention to the importance of respecting democratic principles and human rights worldwide. these are the fundamental principles on which all societies, regardless of their geographical position or economic power, must be built. i also hope that, through the activities carried out as part of the european year for development, public opinion in the european union will become aware of the long-term benefits of development cooperation for both third countries and eu states. even if the budget foreseen for the european year of development actions is limited, it is important that it allows for the presentation of impactful projects and actors from developing countries, including ngos and young people.
in writing. - under the millennium development goals, 189 un member states in 2000, but also the european union itself, under articles 209 and 210 of the treaty, committed themselves to, among other things, ending extreme poverty and hunger by 2015, achieving universal primary education, promoting gender equality and the empowerment of women, reducing child mortality, improving maternal health, combating hiv/aids, malaria and other serious diseases, ensuring environmental sustainability and building a global partnership for development, to name just a few of the key commitments. the european year for development is a good opportunity to reflect on how to pass on the achievements, since the eu provides more than half of the world's development funds, meaning that it has played a responsible role at the global level, yet the average citizen knows little about it. the european year for development also serves to mobilise citizens and civil society, by highlighting the possibility, in the context of globalisation, of helping millions of people living in extreme poverty to avoid being forced to leave their communities and homelands, and to create more decent living conditions for themselves and their families locally, partly on their own initiative. the development contribution also relieves the union of migratory pressures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the proposal for a decision on the european year of development, which designates 2015 as the 'european year for development' under the motto 'our earth, our dignity, our future'. development cooperation policy shall have as its primary objective the reduction and, in the long term, the eradication of poverty, as set out in article 21 of the treaty on european union (teu) and in article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the year 2015 should be a landmark and pivotal year, as it is the last year in which the collectively agreed millennium development goals (mdgs) can be achieved, thus providing a unique opportunity to review international commitments. the year 2015 will also be the year in which major international decisions on the development framework to replace the mdg framework in the coming decades will have to be taken. the european year should therefore act as a catalyst for public awareness-raising, including through public policy debate and development education, and for the promotion and exchange of good practices between member states, local and regional authorities, civil society, the private sector, social partners and international entities and organisations involved in development issues.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because in recent decades space, at the edge of our atmosphere, has become increasingly 'populated' by various types of space infrastructure. whether we're talking about satellites, space debris or other vehicles, there is a major risk of collision between these objects, which could have negative consequences, including for those on earth. improving general knowledge in this area is the first step towards a concrete action plan to reduce the risk of collisions between these objects.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution of the parliament on the proposal for a decision establishing a support programme for space surveillance and tracking. the european union recognises the need for a future space situational awareness capability (ssa) as a european-level activity, which develops and exploits existing national and european civil and military means. in general, the ssa covers three main areas, which aim at protecting space infrastructure, namely space surveillance and tracking (sst), space weather forecasting and monitoring, and near-earth objects. activities in these areas aim to protect infrastructures in and from space. in order to reduce the risks of collision, the union will also seek to find synergies with initiatives for the active disposal and passivation of space debris, such as the initiative developed by the european space agency (esa). the sst support framework should contribute to ensuring the long-term maintenance of european and national space infrastructure and services that are essential for the security of europe's economies, societies and citizens. the osh support framework should consist of the creation of networks and the use of national osh assets for the provision of osh services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which will replace the financial provisions in several legal acts with a single, transparent and clear financial framework capable of streamlining the implementation and, in particular, the operation of the management of expenditure in the food and feed sector. i believe that this proposal will serve the eu's overall objectives of ensuring a high level of human, animal and plant health throughout the food chain. it will also increase consumer protection and information, competitiveness and job creation. last but not least, i think we need clear strategies in support of food security.
in writing. - the regulation voted on today in parliament's plenary is part of the legislative package 'smarter regulation for safer food'. this package provides for sectoral legislation on animal health, plant health and plant reproductive material and official controls, and the regulation on the management of related expenditure. as the proposal rationalizes funding rates, it is important that the union ensures that funds are spent appropriately and takes measures to simplify its spending programmes. i consider it important to introduce precise indicators to better assess the effects of food supply chain security policies. in addition, pest epidemiological surveillance programmes will be established to prevent growing plant health threats.
in writing. - i voted for the regulation laying down provisions for the management of expenditure on the food chain, animal health and welfare, plant health and plant reproductive material. this regulation lays down provisions for the management of expenditure from the general budget of the eu in the areas covered by union rules. it covers food and food safety at all stages of production, processing, distribution and disposal of food, including rules aimed at ensuring fair trade practices and protecting the interests and information of consumers, and the manufacture and use of materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. it also regulates feed and feed safety at all stages of production, processing, distribution and disposal of feed and its use, including rules aimed at ensuring fair trading practices and protecting consumers' interests and information. it also lays down rules on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms and on the protection of intellectual property rights in plant varieties and the conservation and exchange of plant genetic resources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, whether we are talking about logging in the european union or in other countries, it is our duty to combat and discourage illegal logging and the trade in it. the consistency of the rules in this area with the provisions relating to delegated or implementing acts was necessary to reinforce the measures in this area.
in writing. - the forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt) licensing scheme has a particularly important role to play in combating illegal logging and related trade. by voting today, the european parliament does not seek to change the essential features of the flegt licensing regime, but only to align the provisions on comitology in council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts provided for by the treaty of lisbon. the proposal thus empowers the commission to adopt implementing acts for the assessment and approval of existing mechanisms guaranteeing the legality and reliable traceability of timber products exported by partner countries, in order to provide the basis for obtaining a flegt licence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 establishing a flegt licensing scheme for imports of timber into the european community. regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 confers powers on the commission for the implementation of certain provisions of that regulation. as a consequence of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it is necessary to align the powers conferred on the commission under regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). for the purpose of implementing certain provisions of regulation (ec) no 2173/2005, the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu should be delegated to the commission in respect of amending annexes i, ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 2173/2005. it is of particular importance that the commission carry out appropriate consultations during its preparatory work, including at expert level. in order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of regulation (ec) no 2173/2005, implementing powers should be conferred on the commission to allow it to assess and approve existing systems ensuring the legality and reliable traceability of timber products exported by partner countries with a view to becoming the basis for a forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt) licence.
in writing. - the european union has enormous potential to be exploited in the medical field. we have the expertise, infrastructure and funds to excel globally. but to attract foreign investment and stimulate innovation we need a single set of laws and as little bureaucracy as possible. on the one hand, the procedures for authorising and reporting clinical trials should be accelerated and simplified. however, the highest standards of safety and transparency for patients must also be maintained. on another note, i regret to note that romania is at the top of the ranking in europe for investments in medical research and development. i hope the ponta government realizes that the benefits of innovation in medicine are enormous: both for patients and for the economic impact on the country.
in writing. - in a clinical trial, the safety, rights, health and well-being of the subjects should be protected and the data generated should be relevant, reliable, robust and reflect the diversity of the population in terms of age and gender balance. the interests of the participants should always take precedence over other interests. the regulation will ensure consistency in the implementation of the legislation across the eu. this will be of particular benefit to those carrying out research in the field of rare diseases, as the small number of patients targeted makes cross-border studies indispensable. it is also important to create national compensation systems. currently, the insurance costs associated with certain clinical trials are astronomical and can discourage many sponsors from conducting these trials. academic clinical trials, especially those on rare diseases, are often the ones excluded from the market because of the high cost of insurance. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, in particular through the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni). at present, most of the public funds invested in medical research are devoted to insurance expenditure. the costs of operating an indemnity system would be relatively low for the member states.
in writing. - given that clinical trials conducted in a single member state are also indispensable for european clinical research, the procedure laid down in this regulation should also cover those clinical trials. i consider that for these clinical trials the application file should also be submitted through the single european portal.
in writing. - progress in medicine is conditioned by innovation. to ensure access to innovative and effective medicines for patients, there is clearly a need for a legislative framework that encourages the pharmaceutical industry to invest in research and innovation in europe and to bring new treatments to the market. the agreement on the modernisation of clinical trial legislation is good news for both patients and the competitiveness of the european pharmaceutical industry. the number of clinical trials has been declining so far, partly due to the administrative obstacles created by the 2001 directive, especially for multinational clinical trials, which are very important for rare disease treatments. the new regulation adopted today will encourage clinical trials in the eu by providing faster and simpler common procedures for their approval. as regards the deadlines for approval, they could have been more ambitious, but even those provided for in the agreement are progress compared to the current situation. it also brings more transparency to clinical trial results, increased protection of subjects and a system for reporting on drug safety issues. all of this will make the eu more attractive for clinical trials, while increasing the quality of the results and ensuring trust in the system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on clinical trials of medicinal products for human use and repealing directive 2001/20/ec. this regulation shall apply to all interventional clinical trials conducted in the union. a clinical trial may be conducted only if the rights, safety, dignity and well-being of the subjects are protected and take priority over all other interests and if it is designed to generate reliable and robust data. interventional clinical trials shall be subject to scientific and ethical review and shall be authorised in accordance with this regulation. the ethics review shall be carried out by an ethics committee in accordance with the law of the member state concerned. member states shall ensure that the time limits and procedures for the review by the ethics committees are compatible with the time limits and procedures laid down in this regulation for the assessment of the application for authorisation of an interventional clinical trial.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because tragic events in the past have shown us the seriousness of the damage caused by accidents in the nuclear sector. the effects on the environment, but especially on human health, may be irreversible. the commission considers that the measures provided for in this decision are in line with the principle of proportionality, numerous studies and research show that the use of this type of energy can be a viable solution in the diversification of energy sources. in the context of the union's presence of around one third of all operational nuclear reactors worldwide, strengthening the regulatory framework for nuclear safety is vital.
in writing. - by voting today, parliament has voted in favour of the proposal to amend, strengthen and supplement the nuclear safety directive. a major improvement is the introduction of the requirement of effective independence of the competent regulatory authorities. i consider that judicial independence and the exercise of jurisdiction in an impartial and transparent manner are crucial factors in ensuring a high level of nuclear security at european level. the negative consequences of the lack of independence were evident in the case of the fukushima accident. the provisions of directive 2009/71/euratom on the functional separation of the competent regulatory authorities should therefore be strengthened in order to ensure the effective independence of the regulatory authorities and to guarantee that they have the appropriate means and competences to properly discharge the responsibilities entrusted to them. i would like to stress the importance of preventing incidents and accidents, and of responding effectively in the event of an incident or accident. i therefore believe that it is necessary to develop common strategies at european level on accident preparedness measures and to establish rules on on-site emergency preparedness.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directive 2009/71/euratom establishing a community framework for the nuclear safety of nuclear installations. the proposal requires measures to minimise the risks of nuclear accidents and to improve nuclear safety, and also refers to 'stress tests' carried out to obtain comprehensive risk and safety assessments of eu nuclear power plants. the main elements of the proposal are: to ensure the avoidance of radioactive releases at all stages of the life cycle of nuclear installations; criteria and requirements to ensure the independence of regulatory bodies, adequate budgetary own funds and autonomy in their execution; requirements for the appointment and dismissal of staff, the avoidance and resolution of conflicts of interest and the provision of staff with the necessary qualifications, experience and knowledge; the introduction of general objectives on the safety of nuclear installations and the provision of detailed provisions for the various stages of the life cycle of nuclear installations, including on site selection, design, construction, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of nuclear installations; the existence of an on-site emergency response centre for nuclear installations; a self-assessment of nuclear installations and joint assessment of safety-related functions by the commission and the member states, in close cooperation with the commission and the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it an important part of the efforts to close the existing fiscal gaps. we must not lose sight for a second that the loss of public money recorded at eu level amounts to some 1 000 billion euro annually. so the unjustified costs faced by eu citizens are worrying, undermining their trust in national and eu institutions. that is why i welcome all measures against double taxation and aggressive tax planning. in this respect, for example, the member state in which the parent company is situated and the member state in which its permanent establishment is situated should tax the part of the profits which is deductible by the subsidiary of the parent company.
in writing. - in the union, around eur 1 000 billion of potential tax revenues are lost each year through tax fraud and evasion or aggressive tax planning, representing an annual cost of around eur 2 000 for each union citizen. it is therefore essential to take the necessary measures against tax fraud and to amend council directive 2011/96/eu to ensure that the application of that directive does not impede effective action against double taxation in the field of hybrid lending structures. the benefits of directive 2011/96/eu should not lead to situations of double non-taxation or extreme forms of under-taxation and therefore should not generate unintended tax advantages for groups of parent companies and subsidiaries in different member states, compared to groups of companies in the same member state. this directive shall not prevent the application of domestic or agreement-based provisions necessary to prevent tax evasion or to permit the taxation of activities at the place of production or consumption, in so far as they are compatible with this directive.

in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishing a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, intermediation and transit of dual-use items. the european parliament, the council and the commission recognise the importance of continuously improving the effectiveness and coherence of the eu control regime on strategic exports, as well as ensuring a high level of security and adequate transparency, without harming competitiveness and legitimate trade in dual-use items. the three institutions consider that the modernisation and increased convergence of the system is necessary to keep pace with new threats and rapid technological change, to reduce distortions, to create a genuine common market for dual-use goods (fair and uniform conditions of competition for exporters) and to continue to be a model of export control for third countries. to this end, it is essential to streamline the process of updating the checklists (annexes to the regulation), to better assess risks, to intensify information exchange, to develop improved standards for the use of the relevant industry and to reduce implementation gaps.

in writing. - in romania, interbank card transaction fees are among the highest in europe. i know opinions are divided on the margins of the file, and the banks are obviously the most vocal. they cite huge losses, but they forget the losses that public systems had to suffer because of their greed during the economic crisis. interchange fees act as a minimum price, determining the amount paid by merchants for accepting the card. inevitably, the price is also passed on to consumers. the capping of fees will bring benefits to traders, consumers and the economy. small traders will pay low commissions, sales volumes will increase and final prices for consumers will fall. in addition, card payments will be encouraged over cash, and tax evasion will be reduced.
in writing. - the adoption of union-wide ceilings on interchange fees for domestic and cross-border transactions is an important step in the process of improving the functioning of the internal market and in implementing the principle of the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital in the eu, with a specific focus on the consumer. this regulation should apply to card-based payment transactions, irrespective of the medium in which the payment transaction takes place, including transactions carried out through small-value payment instruments and services that may be offline, online or transactions executed using commercial cards.
in writing. - to benefit from the internal market, it is necessary to remove barriers to the integration of new card payment solutions, including mobile and internet payments, which rely on card transactions. i support the need to facilitate the smooth functioning of the internal market for card, internet and mobile payments for consumers and retailers. card payment transactions are generally based on two main business models, namely tripartite card payment systems (cardholder issuing and accepting system - merchant) and quadripartite card payment systems (cardholder issuing bank accepting bank merchant). this regulation shall apply to cross-border and national card-based payment transactions. the adopted amendments provide for the possibility for merchants to opt for an acceptor outside their own member state ('cross-border acceptance'), which is facilitated by the imposition of the same maximum level of domestic and cross-border interchange fees for accepted transactions and the prohibition of territorial licences, which will provide the necessary legal clarity and prevent distortions of competition between card payment systems.

in writing. - i voted for the regulation on reducing or eliminating customs duties on goods coming from ukraine. ukraine is a priority partner state within the european neighbourhood policy and the eastern partnership. the union shall pursue the development of an increasingly close relationship with ukraine, beyond mere bilateral cooperation, which implies gradual progress towards political association and economic integration. to this end, an eu-ukraine association agreement including a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) was negotiated between 2007 and 2011. under the provisions of the dcfta, the union and ukraine have provided for the establishment of a free trade area during a transitional period of up to 10 years from the date of entry into force of the association agreement, in accordance with article xxiv of the general agreement on tariffs and trade 1994. in view of the unprecedented political, economic and security challenges facing ukraine, and in order to support its economy, it is appropriate not to wait until the entry into force of the provisions of the association agreement relating to the dcfta, but to anticipate its implementation through autonomous trade preferences and to start the unilateral reduction or elimination of union customs duties on goods originating in ukraine.
