in writing. - the european union needs to make rapid progress on the coherence of external action in areas and on global issues such as development, trade, energy or migration. coherence can also be facilitated by the powers introduced by the treaty of lisbon, namely by creating the triple role of high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, vice-president of the european commission and president of the foreign affairs council. it is regrettable that this prerogative is not being exploited to its full potential. further progress is also needed in synchronising and sharing the responsibilities and actions of member states in developing countries, under the leadership of a head of delegation to coordinate between eu states, the host government, civil society, and other international donors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's global approach and its consequences for the coherence of its external action. we believe that the eu has recently acquired new instruments of external action through the lisbon treaty, which enable it to develop a more active and unified foreign policy. the eu must maintain and promote its values, interests and stability on the world stage and protect the security and prosperity of its citizens. we stress that this requires a new approach to shaping, in cooperation with our strategic partners, a new multipolar world order that is inclusive, credible, fair and cooperative, based on respect for human rights, the rule of law and democracy, and that seeks to resolve disputes without resorting to armed conflict. we also stress that the eu's external policy can only be effective if member states are willing and able to formulate common policies, especially in the framework of multilateral organisations such as the united nations. we urge member states to fulfil their treaty-based commitments to actively support the union's external relations in a spirit of mutual solidarity and to align their policies with the union's action in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because financial resources in the union remain limited and budgetary discipline and the efficient allocation of funds must be treated with the utmost seriousness. the commission's discharge is the most important, as a large part of the union budget is its responsibility, together with that of the member states. after reading the european union's report on combating corruption, i found that there is no assessment of corruption at the level of the european institutions. in an appeal to the commission i raised this issue. the answer was not clear, with the commission saying it would return to the issue in future anti-corruption reports. i suggest that the future european parliament should insist on such an assessment at the level of the community institutions.
in writing. - in addition to a number of relevant observations on how the european commission implemented the 2012 budget and recommendations for improving management and reducing the error rate, this report also contains paragraphs on the impact of the situation in romania and bulgaria on the implementation of european funds. as for romania, although the country is indeed subject to the cooperation and verification mechanism in order to combat corruption and guarantee the independence of the judiciary, i think it is superfluous to say that, because of this, it is almost impossible to spend european funds according to the legal provisions. without pretending that there were no implementation problems and without ignoring the other positive aspects, i cannot however support a report that seems to give a negative and almost definitive verdict to romania in terms of european funds. romania still has a long way to go, but i remain hopeful about my country's ability to make progress towards a fairer and more widespread use of european funds.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section iii commission and executive agencies. i voted for amendments nos 29, 2, 3, 30, 32, 33, 41 and 42. i voted for amendment no 16 tabled by the s&d group and against the original text of paragraph 296, which states that bulgaria should receive less european funds. the court of auditors has drawn up, for the financial year 2012, a statement of assurance on the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. the council also recommended on 18 february 2014 that the commission be given discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012. parliament therefore gives the commission discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, and sets out its observations in its resolution forming an integral part of its decisions on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section iii commission and executive agencies and in its resolution of 3 april 2014 on the court of auditors' special reports in the context of the commission's discharge for the financial year 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and support the conclusions of the court of auditors in the context of its special reports carried out in 2012. the court of auditors' conclusions will not only help to ensure better management of european taxpayers' money, but also constitute an action plan for the future to address identified shortcomings. the effectiveness of european union action in certain areas is primarily determined by the added value of the funds used. achieving the best possible results in the context of limited resources must therefore be the objective of each european institution in managing community money.
in writing. - i voted for the court of auditors' special reports for the 2012 financial year. parliament considers that, given the complexity and diversity of agricultural structures within the union, it is necessary to maintain the specific form of aid granted to the modernisation of farm associative systems, as it has been objectively demonstrated that it can solve the problems posed by insufficient economic size and/or generational change. parliament regrets that there is currently no comprehensive regulatory framework at union level on conflicts of interest, which ensures comparable basic requirements on independence and transparency and which are applicable to all union agencies. finally, i voted for paragraphs 141, 144 and 147, in which parliament asks the commission to monitor the case of reconstruction work and the construction of social housing in the abruzzi region and in the city of l'aquila. parliament expressed its concern about the eight people detained by the italian police who are suspected of tampering with building permits for reconstruction work taking place in the abruzzi region and in the city of l'aquila and called on the commission to monitor the development of this situation and to report to parliament on this, including on criminal cases.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the european development fund contributes to the achievement of some key foreign policy objectives of the european union. the court of auditors' analysis has shown very clearly that the revenue operations and the commitments of the accounts are in line with the regulations in force. however, i would also point out that the court of auditors' assessment has shown that the supervisory and control systems at europeaid's headquarters and within the union delegations are partially effective in ensuring the legality and regularity of payments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2012, giving discharge to the commission in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2012. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution containing the observations forming an integral part of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2012. the overall commitments, the individual commitments and the level of payments were eur 3[nbsp ]745 million, eur 3[nbsp ]817 million and eur 3[nbsp ]292 million respectively for the financial year 2012. we encourage transparency and the fight against corruption and fraud as these are essential for the success of budget support operations initiated by the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the cooperation between the council of the european union and the european parliament on budgetary management is still weak. however, there are some improvements compared to 2011, in particular as regards the low level of errors in the payments for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies for the year ended 31 december 2012. i also consider it useful to set up an audit committee at the level of the general secretariat of the council. the european parliament should be informed of the work of this committee. last but not least, i too would like to deplore the council's decision to appoint a member of the court of auditors, despite the negative opinion of parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section ii european council and council. in its 2012 annual report, the court of auditors included observations to the european council and the council on the existence of errors in the design of procurement procedures: one error relates to the conduct of a negotiated procedure and another to the application of one of the selection criteria. in 2012, the european council and the council had an overall budget of eur 533[nbsp ]920[nbsp ]000 (eur 563[nbsp ]262 480 in 2011), with an implementation rate of 91,8%. parliament is concerned that the unused appropriations rate remains high and suggests that a number of key performance indicators be drawn up for the most critical areas, such as funds for delegation travel, logistics and interpretation services. in 2012, eur 44[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000 of commitment appropriations were cancelled due to insufficient implementation of the funds and reduced use of programmes. parliament reiterated that the budget of the european council should be separated from that of the council in order to improve the transparency of the financial management of these institutions and their accountability.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the role of the european external action service is particularly important, especially in the light of recent developments in the union's neighbourhood. the strengthening of the eeas is imperative to enable the european union to have a coherent position in the dialogue with external partners. however, i would like to express my regret at the geographical imbalance in the eeas staff, especially in view of the under-representation of new members. for the next financial year of the union, the role of the eeas in the management of union resources will be all the more important as it will have a budget of eur 96 billion for union external assistance funds, for which it shares responsibility for implementation with the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section x european external action service. we welcome the fact that in the second financial year the european external action service (eeas) continued to implement its budget without significant errors being identified by the court of auditors and that most of the problems identified in the 2011 annual report of the court of auditors as a result of the constitution process have not reappeared. we support the objective of one third of the eeas staff being national diplomats by the mid-2013 deadline and take note that the eeas is not inflexible and that staff selection is based on applications and merit. we regret, however, that a better geographical balance has not yet been achieved in terms of appointments to senior management positions and urge the eeas to take the necessary measures to have a better and more balanced representation of all member states. we also call on the eeas to strengthen the geographical balance of the posts of heads of union delegations and reiterate the need to ensure greater geographical balance among member states at all levels of the administration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which deals with a problem which unfortunately we have been facing quite often lately and which is undermining the confidence of european citizens. i believe that electronic identification systems for cattle will considerably improve their traceability and, most importantly, minimise the risk of possible fraud. and i don't think the benefits stop there, because the management of direct payments to farmers per head would be more efficient and thus even possible payment errors could be reduced. however, i believe that it will take some time to achieve the expected results, in particular with regard to the recognition of electronic identification as an official means of identifying bovine animals.
in writing. - one of the main concerns of the citizens is security. european legislation must therefore ensure their optimum protection by means of updated and stricter provisions, whenever this proves necessary. the electronic identification of bovine animals allows for more reliable data, strengthening the traceability system and at the same time food security. it also allows for faster registration of cattle, automation of certain tasks and more effective management of herds. it is also essential to ensure the harmonisation of technical rules in order to avoid a possible anarchic development of this method of identification and to achieve interoperability between national devices. given the wide diversity of european bovine breeders, i consider that electronic identification should remain optional for breeders, unless the member state concerned decides to make it mandatory on its territory.
in writing. - this commission legislative proposal provides for greater clarity and improved applicability of legislation on the identification and traceability of bovine animals, thus contributing to consumer protection and public health, and promoting consumer confidence. i consider that such general rules at european union level are absolutely necessary for the correct electronic identification of bovine animals, for the simplification of the provisions on the labelling of beef and veal and for the protection of consumers by providing objective information which can be verified by the competent authorities and which is understood by consumers. in addition, the expansion of the electronic devices market through this regulation will lead to lower prices and to the future generalisation of this identification method in line with ongoing developments worldwide.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the amended proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 as regards the electronic identification of bovine animals and the abolition of the provisions on the optional labelling of beef and veal. regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 provides that each member state is to establish a system for the identification and registration of bovine animals in accordance with the provisions of that regulation. in view of technological advances in the field of electronic identification of bovine animals (eid), several member states have decided to start implementing optional eid of bovine animals. these initiatives are likely to result in different systems being developed in individual member states or by stakeholders. such a development would prevent further harmonisation of technical standards at union level. i believe that they should ensure that the systems introduced in the member states are interoperable and comply with iso standards. member states have very different livestock systems, farming practices and sectoral organisations. therefore, i consider that member states should be allowed to introduce mandatory bse on their territory only if they consider it appropriate, after taking into account all factors, including any negative effects at the level of small farmers, and after consulting the representative organisations of the bovine sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and for the discharge to be given to the court of justice, in particular because of the extremely important role that this institution plays in ensuring that european law and values are respected in all the member states. i would like to reiterate the idea that in order to make the work of the court of justice more efficient, additional judges will be needed in the near future. a further argument in favour of such a decision is the lower number of closed cases compared to 2011. however, i would also like to express my support for the rationalisation of the translation services at the court of justice, as the staff employed in such posts represents approximately 47% of the total.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section iv court of justice. the number of cases pending and closed by the general court decreased slightly in 2012 compared to previous years (e.g. 1[nbsp ]308 cases pending in 2011 and 1[nbsp ]237 cases pending in 2012). we regret, however, that the number of closed cases has decreased and we consider that the proposal for the creation of the possibility of appointing additional judges to the general court, currently under consideration by the council, could contribute to an effective reduction in the number of pending cases. we request clear information on the productivity of each chamber of three or five judges of the court of justice and the general court and of each chamber of three or one judge of the civil service tribunal. we also request information on the number of cases dealt with as rapporteurs by the president and vice-president after the reorganisation of the court of justice. calls on the court of justice, the general court and the civil service tribunal to provide an overview of the number of cases pending for more than 24 months;
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the court of auditors has a vital role in assessing the way in which european finances are managed by the community institutions. i would like to point out, however, that as far as translation services are concerned, there are very large differences in costs for different languages. finally, i would like to welcome, as does the report, the fact that the average time for preparing a special report has been reduced from 25 to 20 months since 2008. this allows for the shortcomings to be remedied in a shorter time and for significant savings to be made.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, according to the independent external auditor who audited the court of auditors' annual accounts, the financial statements give a true and fair view of the court's financial position for the financial year 2012. however, the court of auditors should reduce differences in substantial variations between translation costs for different languages and apply the same method of calculation as in other institutions to allow a comparison of translation costs between institutions. the court of auditors should also include in its annual report the results of cases closed by olaf and reported by the court of auditors and the results of cases where the investigation concerned the institution or a person working for it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section v court of auditors. we support the court of auditors' assessment of the quality and impact of its work and welcome the results achieved. we support the court's efforts to allocate more resources to performance audits and analyses aimed at determining whether the principles of economy, efficiency and effectiveness have been respected. it is recalled that for the budgetary and legislative authority, it is necessary for the court of auditors to issue not only a statement of assurance on the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, but also reliable and viable opinions on the results achieved by the various union policies. we would point out that some member states are over-represented at management level, while member states that have joined in the last 10 years are still under-represented at the level of heads of unit or directors. we reiterate the need to ensure greater geographical balance at all levels of government.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section vi european economic and social committee. the eesc's budget for 2012 was eur 128 816 588 (eur 128 600 000 in 2011) with an implementation rate of 96,8%. the eesc budget is purely administrative, with a large part going to the people who work in the institution, and the remainder going to buildings, furniture, equipment and miscellaneous running costs. the 2012 execution rate of 96.8[nbsp ]% is higher than that of 2011 which was 95.4[nbsp ]%, but lower than that of 2010 which was 98[nbsp ]%. parliament calls on the eesc to ensure an even higher rate of implementation for future periods. takes note of the council decision on the level of the allowances for eesc members of september 2013 and welcomes the fact that the eesc has implemented the new rules on the reimbursement of travel expenses of members on the basis of actual costs, as recommended by parliament; parliament also welcomes the fact that the decision to make the declarations of financial interests of eesc members public was implemented in 2012.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, section vii committee of the regions. in 2012, the committee had an approved budget of eur 86503000 (eur 84059000 in 2011), of which eur 85000000 was in commitment appropriations, with a utilisation rate of 98,2%, an increase from the rate of 97,5% in 2011. the budget of the committee shall be purely administrative. parliament welcomed the establishment of a subsidiarity coordination group to strengthen the political governance of the committee and to implement the committee's new strengthened role, as provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. we welcome the committee's internal organisation projects, which aim to promote cooperation between services and to create synergies in the framework of joint activities and actions. we ask the committee to continue to monitor the staff structure to ensure maximum efficiency in the organisation of posts and its contribution to better use of the budget allocated. parliament considered that the administrative cooperation agreement between the committee and the eesc is an effective mechanism and recommended that the committee keep this mechanism in an updated form.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and for the discharge to be given to the european ombudsman. i am very familiar with the role of this institution because, as vice-chairman of the committee on petitions of the european parliament, i have often worked with this structure and its representatives. the european ombudsman has a particularly important role to play in protecting the interests of union citizens. the commission's investigations have on several occasions led to the initiation of infringement proceedings by member states. i therefore believe that the role of the institution must be strengthened and its powers extended in order to better protect the rights and interests of the citizens of the european union.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency for the financial year 2012. we recall the key role played by the agency in the safety and interoperability of rail systems in europe. the agency's competences are currently being reviewed under the fourth railway package and we stress the need to provide the agency with the financial, material and human resources to enable it to successfully fulfil the tasks entrusted to it. we regret that the use of two sites (lille and valenciennes) for the activities generates additional costs for the agency and we request that a decision be taken on a single site for the agency, located in a place easily accessible by public transport, in order to save limited resources and ensure more efficient operation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to close the accounts of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2012. as one of the three european economic and financial supervisory authorities, and therefore still in the establishment phase, the authority benefited from an increase of around 20% over the 2011 budget. however, the funding will remain inflexible and liable to jeopardise the independence of this authority if the blended funding system is not abandoned in the near future. given the role of the authority in promoting the stability and security of financial markets, it is very important that the results and impact of its work are made public and accessible to european citizens.
in writing. - the european securities and markets authority has a strategic role in relation to the european economy as it promotes the stability and security of financial markets, ensures the stability of the european financial system and ensures the safe functioning of european stock markets. having found no concerns or errors in the documentation submitted and voting in favour, parliament grants the executive director of the european securities and markets authority discharge in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the discharge report for the european securities and markets authority as the court of auditors stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability and legality of the annual accounts and the regularity of the underlying transactions of the authority for the financial year 2012. the authority implemented in 2012 a stricter management budget implementation monitoring to ensure timely corrective action on the low execution rates of commitment appropriations. the recruitment forms have also been revised to improve recruitment procedures and a new conflict of interest policy is to be adopted by the management board to ensure a neutral and transparent decision-making process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament decisions on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european securities and markets authority (esma), granting discharge to the executive director of esma and approving the closure of the accounts of the esma for the financial year 2012. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution containing the observations forming an integral part of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2012. the budget of esma for the financial year 2012 was eur 20279000, representing an increase of 19,53% compared to the 2011 budget, and the overall union contribution to the budget of esma for the financial year 2012 was eur 6408000, representing a decrease of 5,54% compared to 2011. according to the court of auditors' annual audit report, eur 2[nbsp ]800[nbsp ]000 (14[nbsp ]%) of the total appropriations were cancelled and eur 4[nbsp ]200[nbsp ]000 (21[nbsp ]%) of the committed appropriations were carried over in 2013. the high level of cancellations is mainly due to the fact that the budget was drawn up on the basis of a staff scheme completed in full at the beginning of the financial year 2012 and as a result of delays affecting procurement procedures in the it field.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i consider that there are no grounds for postponing the closure of the accounts of the european training foundation for the financial year 2012, especially as we can observe that the corrective measures adopted in response to the observations relating to the previous financial year have been implemented. in addition, the total level of committed appropriations was 99,9%, so it can be seen that the commitments were made in a timely manner and overall the budget planning was effective.
in writing. - the important role that the foundation has played in contributing to improving human capital development in partner countries is noteworthy; we welcome the achievement of the work programme objectives, as demonstrated by the increase in the number of institutional outputs in 2012, detailed in the annual activity report, as well as the emphasis in the foundation's work on the important aspects of youth employment and a renewed focus on education and training, the sme skills aspect and migration processes. the court of auditors has found the operations underlying the annual accounts of the foundation for the financial year 2012 to be legal and regular and its financial position as at 31 december 2012 is clearly presented. the overall level of committed appropriations remained high (99,9%) in 2012 and was implemented in a timely manner, indicating proper budgetary planning. the foundation's annual accounts reflect the problematic situation of the foundation's headquarters, which remained unresolved in 2012 despite the preventive and mitigation actions undertaken. i welcome the conclusion of an agreement with the regional authorities in 2013 which ensures the continuation of the foundation's activities in the period 2013-2015.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament decisions on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the euratom supply agency (eaa), granting the director-general of the eaa discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget and approving the closure of the eaa accounts for the financial year 2012. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution containing the observations forming an integral part of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european atomic energy community for the financial year 2012. according to the court of auditors, between 2008 and 2011, the aae did not benefit from its own budget, with the commission directly financing and paying all the expenditure. the court of auditors considers that this situation was contrary to the agency's statute. we note with concern that in 2012, although the commission granted the agency an own budget of eur 98[nbsp ]000[nbsp ] (eur 104[nbsp ]000[nbsp ], if financial revenues from own investments are included) following the court's observations, and although article 54 of the treaty establishing the european atomic energy community and article 6 of the agency's statute provide for the agency to have financial autonomy, the bulk of the agency's expenditure continued to be directly financed by the commission. we ask the commission to provide an explanation for this situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of closing the accounts of the european foundation for the improvement of living and working conditions for the financial year 2012, as there are no grounds for postponing it. in addition, the foundation's work is important, especially in the current context, where the effects of the financial crisis are felt at the social level, with working conditions in many member states steadily deteriorating. finally, the court of auditors found the operations underlying the foundation's annual accounts for the financial year 2012 to be legal and regular and its financial position as at 31 december 2012 was clear.

in writing. - the court of auditors has concluded that the annual accounts of eurojust, which has an annual budget of eur 33,3 million for 2012, present fairly, in all material respects, its financial position as at 31 december 2012, as well as the results of its operations and its cash flows for the year ended on that date, and that the transactions underlying the annual accounts of eurojust for the financial year 2012 are legal and in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, in all material respects. the court of auditors considers that improvements are needed in recruitment procedures. in general, more emphasis should be placed on auditing eurojust's sound financial management, that is, on the economy, effectiveness and level of performance with which eurojust has used the appropriations allocated to it for the exercise of its responsibilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the discharge decision in respect of the implementation of eurojust's budget for the financial year 2012. the annual audit of the court of auditors did not identify any significant issues with regard to the level of carry-overs in 2012 and we congratulate eurojust on adhering to the principle of annuality and on the timely execution of its budget. in accordance with the annual activity report and the court of auditors' audit findings, the level and nature of transfers in 2012 remained within the limits of the financial rules; we congratulate eurojust on its efficient budget planning. we call on eurojust to improve the transparency of recruitment procedures. i also note that there was no evidence to show that the questions to be used for the tests and interviews had been set before the candidates were examined by the selection board and that there is no evidence that the corresponding weight of the written tests and the corresponding weight of the interviews had been set before the candidates were assessed. we request eurojust to monitor the evolution of this issue in the report on the state of play of the 2012 discharge.
in writing. - i voted in favour of discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european police office for the financial year 2012, in the light of the fact that the court of auditors has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the office's annual accounts for the financial year 2012 and the legality and regularity of the operations. however, it should not be overlooked that the office had two postponements which did not correspond to the legal commitments assumed, as such situations should not be repeated in the future. therefore, while i support closing the accounts of the european police office for 2012, it is important that it improves its financial planning in the future.
in writing. - the court of auditors has found that the annual accounts of the european police office (europol) present fairly, in all material respects, its financial position as at 31 december 2012. the court of auditors found that the level of carry-overs of commitment appropriations is still high (19,64%), compared with the level of carry-overs of over 40% in the previous year. europol referred to the establishment of the european cybercrime centre, which was decided only in june 2012 and for which new budgetary resources were made available only towards the end of the 2012 financial year. according to the agency, the carry-over of appropriations was necessary to cover this new burden in 2013, for which no additional resources were provided. it is necessary to continue to focus on the verification of the sound financial management of europol, in particular as regards efficiency and performance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the discharge decision for the implementation of the budget of the european police office for the financial year 2012. the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2012 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 98,8[nbsp ]% and the payment appropriations execution rate was 79,7[nbsp ]%. the office made 19 budgetary transfers amounting to eur 4[nbsp ]500[nbsp ]000 affecting 82 of the 115 budget lines. the amount of assigned revenue in accordance with article 21 (3) of the financial regulation is estimated at eur 100000. we note with concern that the recruitment procedures examined showed three shortcomings, namely: the questions to be used for the written tests and interviews were developed after the selection board examined the applications, there was no evidence that the weighting of the selection criteria used for the shortlist was established before the examination of the applications, and the selection boards did not properly document all the meetings that took place and all the decisions they took. we ask the office to rectify this situation and to provide information on the progress of the actions to be undertaken following the 2012 discharge procedure.

principle is maintained and supported by the agreement reached by the european parliament and the council in january this year, facilitating not only the reduction of aircraft noise at source, but also land-use planning and management measures, operational procedures for noise abatement and operating restrictions, without prejudice to existing obligations and agreements. the measures envisaged in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation no 515/97 on mutual assistance between the administrative authorities of the member states and cooperation between the latter and the commission to ensure the correct application of the law on customs and agricultural matters. actions to combat customs infringements are an integral part of the protection of the financial interests of the union and the development of customs cooperation. customs legislation may be infringed by various practices, such as misrepresenting imported goods to take advantage of lower customs duties, misrepresenting declarations of origin to circumvent anti-dumping duties and/or to avoid import restrictive quotas or abusing the transit system, where goods actually imported are declared as being in transit in order to avoid payment of the applicable customs duties. to combat such breaches of customs legislation, a wide exchange of information is necessary in the framework of cooperation both between member states and between member states and the commission. the regulation improves customs fraud detection, investigation and prevention operations by enhancing the exchange of information and increasing the volume of evidence available, as well as by improving the functioning of the system in place, thereby increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of the action concerned.

considerable negative impact on employment and the local economy and aggravate the already fragile economic situation in the affected region. the spanish authorities submitted the application for a financial contribution from the egf in may 2012 and regret that its evaluation was only submitted by the european commission in march 2014. we regret the long evaluation period and consider that this delay is contrary to the purpose of the european globalisation adjustment fund to provide rapid assistance to workers made redundant. we welcome the fact that training courses are offered and that these will be complemented by on-the-job training activities and we also welcome the fact that the training will be tailored to the skills and qualifications needs of the companies establishing themselves in the industrial park, which is part of the measures taken in addition to the package of measures financed by the egf.
in writing. - in addition to their direct function of protecting depositors, deposit guarantee schemes are also essential for the stability of the financial system, especially in times of crisis. if the banks' customers lose confidence in their credit institutions and attempt to withdraw their deposits simultaneously, this crisis phenomenon may lead not only to the collapse of the already unstable institution, but may also spread to other credit institutions and other countries as a result of a growing and general loss of confidence. the level of liquid assets required to guarantee deposits is so high that no credit institution can keep such an amount available.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading on deposit guarantee schemes, as it proposes to reduce payment terms in the event of insolvency to 7 working days, which means a reduction to less than half under the current provisions. i believe that the principle of risk-based contributions will increase depositors' confidence and strengthen financial stability by discouraging institutions from taking too much risk. depositors must be given clear information about the account opened and the deposit guarantee schemes available so that disadvantaged persons are not put at risk should the institution become insolvent.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the council's first reading position with a view to adopting a directive on deposit guarantee schemes, which approves the council's first reading position. parliament adopted its position at first reading in plenary on 16 february 2012. after three rounds of trilogue negotiations, the negotiating team of the parliament and the council reached an agreement on this file on 17 december 2013. following the legal and linguistic review, the council adopted its position at first reading on 3 march 2014, thus confirming the agreement of 17 december 2013. the compromise thus lays down for the first time eu-wide rules on the financing of deposit guarantee schemes. member states shall ensure that credit institutions affiliated to deposit guarantee schemes establish a deposit guarantee fund, which shall amount to at least 0,8% of the deposits covered by the scheme within 10 years. the payment deadlines in the event of insolvency are also reduced from 20 working days under the current provisions to 7 working days. member states will have the possibility to introduce a transitional period until the end of 2023.
in writing. - i believe that a new union strategy on alternative fuels should be implemented without prejudice to national and union efforts to influence travellers' behaviour and promote a modal shift towards more sustainable modes of transport and efficient logistics solutions, particularly in urban areas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on alternative fuels infrastructure because a union strategy on alternative fuels should be implemented without prejudice to national efforts and without influencing travellers' behaviour. in addition to alignment with the regime of delegated and implementing acts, the essential purpose of this proposal is to introduce a legal basis for future grants, in the form of lump sums and without call for proposals, for the benefit of national statistical institutes. a strategic approach is needed to meet the long-term energy needs of all modes of transport. in particular, policies should be based on a broad mix of alternative fuels, with a focus on the specific needs of each mode of transport. the needs of transport modes with limited alternatives should be properly integrated into national policy frameworks. i welcome this initiative and hope that both at the european union level and at the level of romania, this directive will ensure a favourable environment for the development of alternative fuels.
in writing. - i voted for the directive on the installation of alternative fuels infrastructure. this directive establishes a common framework of measures for the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure in the union with the aim of minimising the dependence of transport on oil and mitigating its impact on the environment. this directive lays down minimum requirements for the establishment of alternative fuels infrastructure to be implemented through member states' national policy frameworks, including common technical specifications for recharging points for electric vehicles and for refuelling points for natural gas (lng and cng) and hydrogen, as well as requirements for user information. in order to develop alternative fuels infrastructure and promote alternative fuels, national policy frameworks may be composed of several plans, strategies or other planning documentation developed separately or integrated, or in another form, including at administrative level, as decided by member states. the development and implementation of member states' national policy frameworks should be facilitated by the commission through the exchange of information and good practices between member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive amending directive 96/53/ec of 25 july 1996 laying down for certain road vehicles circulating within the community the maximum authorised dimensions in national and international traffic and the maximum authorised weight in international traffic. this directive aims to improve road safety and working conditions for drivers in the field of international freight transport. i have supported all the amendments which provide for increased ergonomics of the cab and space available to the driver. i think it is important that the flaps that help improve the aerodynamics of a truck can also be automatically manipulated by the driver. they also support the mandatory introduction of the weight sensor and its interoperability with the new generation digital tachograph. the weight sensor can contribute both to the protection of transport infrastructure and to the compliance with social legislation in the field of transport. therefore, i believe that the use of the weight sensor should be mandatory and not voluntary. as regards the use of 'mega-trucks' in cross-border situations, i consider that the current legislation is clear and sufficient and the tran committee has repeatedly criticised the various misinterpretations of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms and amending directives 77/91/eec, 82/891/ec, 2001/24/ec, 2002/47/ec, 2004/25/ec, 2005/56/ec, 2007/36/ec and 2011/35/ec and regulation (eu) no 1093/2010. the financial crisis has demonstrated that there is a significant lack of appropriate tools at union level to effectively manage the situation of credit institutions and investment firms that are not viable or are in difficulty. those instruments are necessary in particular to prevent insolvency or, if insolvency occurs, to minimise the negative consequences by maintaining the systemically important functions of the institution concerned. during the crisis, these challenges were a major factor forcing member states to bail out institutions using taxpayers' money. the objective of a credible recovery and resolution framework is to avoid as far as possible the need for such a measure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend directive 2009/65/ec on the coordination of laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) as regards depositary functions, remuneration policies and sanctions. directive 2009/65/ec should be amended to take account of market developments and the experience gained so far by market participants and supervisory bodies, in particular to address discrepancies between the provisions of national law concerning the obligations and liability of depositaries, the remuneration policy and penalties. in order to counter the potential negative impact of poorly designed remuneration structures on the sound management of risks and the control of risk-taking behaviour by individuals, there should be an explicit obligation for collective investment undertakings (ucits) management companies to establish and maintain, for the categories of staff whose professional activities have a material impact on the risk profile of the ucits they manage, remuneration policies and practices compatible with sound and effective risk management. those policies and practices should apply proportionately to any third party that takes investment decisions that affect the risk profile of ucits.
in writing. - i voted for this european directive because it requires the financial systems of the member states to ensure that people with low incomes or in poverty can open bank accounts. many banks now charge fees for maintaining bank accounts that are prohibitive for low-income or poor individuals.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the comparability of payment account fees, switching of payment accounts and access to payment accounts with basic functionalities. the smooth functioning of the internal market and the development of a modern, socially inclusive economy increasingly depend on the universal provision of payment services. i support this directive which provides for rules on the transparency and comparability of fees charged to consumers for payment accounts held by them in the union, rules on switching payment accounts within a member state and on facilitating the cross-border opening of accounts by consumers. this directive also defines a framework of rules and conditions under which member states guarantee the right of consumers to open and use payment accounts with basic features in the union. in order to facilitate effective and smooth financial mobility in the long term, it is essential to establish a uniform set of rules addressing the issue of low customer mobility and, in particular, to increase the comparability of services and fees related to payment accounts and to motivate switching payment accounts, and to avoid discrimination on grounds of residence of consumers intending to purchase a cross-border payment account.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on key information documents relating to investment products. the range of different types of insurance-based retail investment products (priips) available to retail investors when they intend to make an investment is increasing. improving the transparency provisions of priips offered to retail investors is an important measure to protect investors and a prerequisite for restoring their confidence in the financial market, in particular in the context of the consequences of the financial crisis. the regulation adopted at first reading provides for uniform rules on the format and content of the key information document to be drawn up by manufacturers of packaged retail insurance-based investment products and uniform rules on the making available of that document to retail investors. the aim is to provide retail investors with the opportunity to understand and compare the key features and risks of the priip.
in writing. - i voted to amend the protocol on the statute of the court of justice of the european union by increasing the number of judges in the general court. as a result of the progressive extension of its powers since its establishment, the court of first instance is now seised of a steadily increasing number of cases. the number of cases brought before the general court has been increasing steadily over the years, which in the long run has the effect of increasing the number of cases before it and lengthening the duration of proceedings. in accordance with article 19 (2) of the treaty on european union, the court of first instance shall have at least one judge per member state. since this arrangement already ensures a geographical balance and a representation of the respective national legal systems, additional judges should be appointed solely on the basis of their professional and personal merits, taking into account their knowledge of the legal systems of the european union and of the member states. however, there should be no more than two judges per member state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision on the implementation of the interoperable eu-wide ecall system. ecall will be based on the installation of type-approved equipment for the single european emergency number 112, starting with certain vehicle categories, on all vehicles, and on a framework for the management of ecalls in telecommunications networks and in emergency call centres (psap). according to the commission, an ecall to 112 can reduce the time needed for emergency response by 40% in urban areas and by 50% in rural areas (with a net gain of around 10 minutes), thus saving lives and reducing the severity of personal injuries. the decision is addressed to the member states and addresses the infrastructure side of the psaps of the commission's ecall strategy, based on a triple regulatory approach covering the in-vehicle system, telecommunications networks and emergency call centres. member states shall implement the psap infrastructure necessary for the proper reception and management of all ecalls from their territory by 1 october 2015 at the latest. it is obviously necessary that the location of the caller for 112 calls be precise and reliable.
in writing. - while i welcome the adoption of the deployment of ecall for a better safety for our citizens, i deeply deplore that my amendment requiring an extension of the caller location obligation to mobile terminals has not been accepted by the council. ecall will represent only 1.7% of the annual number of emergency calls in the eu. the technology is available to cover the other 90% of emergency calls (290 million) originated from mobile terminals. i believe that all citizens, and not only car drivers equipped with ecall technology, should benefit from the already widely deployed gnss location technologies. we need to ensure our citizens an equal right to emergency services for all, not only for drivers or car users. at least eur[nbsp ]4 billion could be saved annually if accurate caller location information targets were to be deployed. the european parliament has strongly supported and called for caller location for years. i hope the next commission will show determination in its next mandate, in order to avoid more dramatic accidents like the one in romania where people who survived a plane crash died for not having been attended earlier on time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on measures to reduce the cost of installing high-speed electronic communications networks, because the digital economy is bringing profound changes to the single market. due to its innovative nature, speed and cross-border dimension, it has the potential to bring single market integration to a new level. the union aims at a digital economy that produces sustainable economic and social benefits, based on modern online services and fast internet connections. a high-quality digital infrastructure underpins virtually all sectors of a modern and innovative economy and is of strategic importance for social and territorial cohesion. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the european schools in the member states and the european schools in the union. i believe that a proper approach to the problem of reducing the cost of deploying high-speed electronic communications networks is needed as a large part of these costs can be attributed to inefficiencies in the expansion process related to the use of existing passive infrastructure, bottlenecks related to the coordination of civil works and on the installation of networks inside buildings, cumbersome administrative procedures for granting permits, significant financial obstacles and the absence of feasible business plans for the installation of broadband in rural areas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on measures to reduce the cost of installing high-speed electronic communications networks. the regulation proposes to reduce the cost of deploying high-speed and ultra-fast electronic communications networks by providing tools for cost-effective deployment of new physical infrastructure, by reducing administrative burdens, by sharing existing infrastructure and by harmonising civil works. the regulation proposes to maximise synergies between networks, addressing not only providers of electronic communications networks but any owner of physical infrastructure suitable for hosting elements of electronic communications networks such as electricity, gas, water and sewerage, heating and transport services. access to civil infrastructure facilitates the expansion of high-speed broadband networks by any operator. the development of ict services, both in the public and private sectors, should be used as a means of improving public services such as healthcare, state education and culture, public safety, social services, and can revitalize the economic activity of smes and stimulate their development. particular attention should be paid to encouraging private investment in rural and remote areas, thus ensuring convenient access to broadband services also in areas where the market fails to provide it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on a community fleet capacity policy to promote inland waterway transport. regulation (ec) no 718/1999 lays down measures to support structural improvements in the waterway sector, in particular as regards the capacity of the fleet of member states with inland waterways linked to those of another member state. reserve funds were thus set up, financed by the inland waterway transport sector from the surplus of funds from the structural improvement programmes administered until 28 april 1999 and from the special contributions received under the 'old for new' rule. over the years, the funds have grown to a current cumulative value of approximately eur 35 million. the inland waterway sector and the member states tried to use the funds, but the commission considered that the applications did not fall within the scope of the regulation. welcomes the extension of the scope of the current regulation so that the reserve funds can be used to support the inland waterway sector more effectively and to create a favourable environment for innovation and increased safety and environmental performance. i regret that the logistics of intermodal freight transport are not mentioned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on information measures for agricultural products on the internal market and in third countries. under council regulation (ec) no 3/2008, the union may carry out information and promotion actions on the internal market and in third countries for agricultural products and their production methods, and for foodstuffs based on agricultural products. the objective of these actions is to increase the competitiveness of european agriculture, to contribute to the manufacture of more profitable products, to create greater competitive equity both on the internal market and in third countries and to increase consumer awareness of the qualities of agricultural products and foodstuffs based on union agricultural products, as well as by developing and opening up new markets. those actions shall complement and usefully reinforce the actions of the member states, while ensuring equal access for all member states at all times and promoting positive discrimination in favour of the outermost regions in accordance with article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the participation of the union in the research and development programme on assisted living arrangements jointly undertaken by several member states. i believe that the european union needs to take urgent action to address the challenges of an ageing population. the european horizon 2020 programme can provide concrete solutions in this regard, including funding activities related to active ageing, independent living and assistance for autonomy. i give you as an example the solutions provided by information and communication technologies (icts), which can substantially improve the quality of life of the elderly. in addition, taking into account the long-term budgetary pressures associated with an ageing population, at the budgetary level, ict solutions also allow for the efficiency of social welfare systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the participation of the union in the research and development programme on assisted active driving (aaa) jointly undertaken by several member states. the research and innovation activities carried out under the aaa programme should be fully in line with the general principles of horizon 2020, in particular with regard to gender equality, open access and ethical principles. research and innovation activities should also comply with ethical principles and relevant national, international and union legislation, including the charter of fundamental rights of the eu and the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and its additional protocols. particular attention should be paid to the principle of proportionality, the right to privacy, the right to the protection of personal data, the right to the physical and mental integrity of the person, the right to non-discrimination and the need to ensure high levels of protection of human health. in line with the objective of sme participation in indirect actions of horizon 2020, the aaa programme should aim to allocate 20% of its budget allocated to indirect actions to smes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the participation of the european union in a research and development programme jointly undertaken by several member states to support small and medium-sized enterprises carrying out research activities. i welcome the european commission's proposal to continue the european union's participation in the eurostars 2 programme, which promotes market-oriented research activities by smes. the experience of the predecessor programme has shown that it responds to the real needs of r&d performing smes, which is evidence that the number of eligible projects exceeded the budget originally allocated. however, i believe that we need more transparency in procedures and a reduction in bureaucracy, in particular reducing the time from evaluation to signing of contracts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the participation of the union in a research and development programme jointly undertaken by several member states to support small and medium-sized enterprises carrying out research activities. the adopted decision lays down the rules and conditions for the participation of the union in the second research and development programme jointly undertaken by several member states to support small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) carrying out research and development activities (eurostars-2). the union shall participate in eurostars-2, which is jointly conducted by austria, belgium, bulgaria, cyprus, croatia, denmark, estonia, switzerland, finland, france, germany, greece, ireland, iceland, israel, italy, latvia, lithuania, luxembourg, malta, norway, poland, portugal, the united kingdom, the czech republic, romania, slovakia, slovenia, spain, sweden, turkey, the netherlands and hungary, in accordance with the conditions laid down in this decision. the union's financial contribution to eurostars-2 is up to eur 287000000. the union financial contribution shall be paid from the appropriations in the general budget of the union allocated to the relevant parts of the specific programme implementing horizon 2020.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the participation of the union in a european programme for innovation and research in the field of metrology jointly undertaken by several member states. the union shall participate in the european programme for metrology innovation and research (empir) jointly conducted by austria, belgium, bosnia and herzegovina, bulgaria, croatia, denmark, switzerland, estonia, finland, france, germany, greece, ireland, italy, norway, poland, portugal, the united kingdom, the czech republic, romania, serbia, slovakia, slovenia, spain, sweden, turkey, the netherlands and hungary, in accordance with the conditions laid down in this decision. the union's financial contribution to empir shall be up to eur 300[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000[nbsp]. the union financial contribution shall be paid from the appropriations in the general budget of the union allocated to the relevant parts of the specific programme implementing horizon 2020, established by decision 2013/743/eu, in accordance with article 58 (1) (c) (vi) and articles 60 and 61 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 966/2012, and in particular part ii 'leadership in the industrial sector' and part iii 'society-wide challenges'.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the participation of the union in a second eu-developing countries partnership programme on clinical trials, jointly conducted by several member states. the union is a major funder of research in poverty-related diseases and neglected infectious diseases. the commission and the member states contribute to around a quarter (22%) of government investment in this area worldwide. the union is also a particularly important player in global health. the commission and the member states provide around half of the global fund to fight hiv/aids, tuberculosis and malaria. supporting the fight against poverty-related diseases would also help to protect union citizens against these diseases, as increasing global mobility (including tourism), migratory movements and changes in the geographical distribution of these diseases mean that europe could face new or recurring challenges from these diseases. unfortunately, only 10 percent of the world's research funding goes to diseases that account for 90 percent of the world's diseases. it is essential that the acquisition of informed consent for clinical trials conducted in developing countries should always be on a voluntary basis and following adequate information.
in writing. - currently, both consumers and businesses, especially smes, face difficulties when trying to recover amounts of money across borders. i consider it unacceptable that some debtors can avoid paying debts just because they are not resident in the same country as the creditor or simply by moving their money to another account. the european account preservation order will facilitate cross-border debt recovery, which will help to increase consumer and business confidence in cross-border trade. the new instrument will be pragmatic, effective and easy to apply for when the circumstances of the dispute warrant it, while ensuring a balance between the rights of the parties to the dispute. in this respect, i am pleased that we were able to obtain the maintenance of the ex parte procedure and, at the same time, to ensure the precise identification of the bank account concerned. another important aspect in my view is the enforceability of the order issued, which will increase the chances of recovering the debt. i do think that the system for obtaining information on the debtor's bank account could have been simpler, without requiring an enforceable court order, but overall i think this instrument will bring benefits to europeans.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the union has set itself the objective of maintaining and developing an area of freedom, security and justice, in which the free movement of persons is ensured. in order to progressively establish such an area, the union shall, inter alia, adopt measures on judicial cooperation in civil matters with cross-border implications, in particular where they are necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. this regulation establishes a union procedure concerning a protection measure allowing a creditor to obtain a european account preservation order to prevent the withdrawal or transfer of funds held by the debtor in a bank account within the union. the preservation order shall be available to the creditor as an alternative to existing protection measures under the national law of the member states. this regulation shall apply to claims in civil and commercial matters having cross-border implications as defined in article 3, irrespective of the nature of the court seised. in particular, it does not apply to tax, customs or administrative matters.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive amending council directives 78/660/eec and 83/349/eec as regards disclosure of non-financial and diversity information by certain large companies and groups. in order to enhance the consistency and comparability of non-financial information disclosed across the union, it is necessary for certain large undertakings to draw up a non-financial statement containing information on at least environmental, social and human resources aspects, respect for human rights, the fight against corruption and bribery. such a statement should include a description of the policies, results and risks related to those aspects and should be integrated into the management report of the undertaking concerned. the non-financial statement should also include information on the undertaking's due diligence policies and, where relevant and proportionate, its supply and subcontracting chains, in order to identify, prevent and mitigate existing and potential adverse impacts. member states should be able to exempt undertakings subject to this directive from the obligation to draw up a non-financial statement in cases where they present a separate report corresponding to the same financial year and with content covering the same subjects.
in writing. - i voted for the new directive on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals in the context of a transfer within the same company because it is necessary to regulate labour migration from non-eu countries. however, i believe that the use of non-eu labour should not be to the disadvantage of european citizens. european legislation must be clear: third-country nationals can only be called upon for certain jobs if there are no european workers to fill them. workers from third countries are a factor of development and growth for the european union. as a result, the european commission has proposed several directives over the past seven years to facilitate employment contracts for highly skilled workers, seasonal workers, paid trainees and workers transferred within the same company. i reiterate the need to include the principle of community preference in the labour migration directives. i am pleased that this principle is also reflected in the directive voted today, the latest in a series of regulations on legal migration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals in the context of a transfer within the same company. i voted for amendment 6, which states that, whatever the law applicable to the employment relationship, persons transferred within the same undertaking are entitled to equal treatment with nationals of the host member state as regards: the terms and conditions of employment as laid down in the laws, regulations and administrative provisions and/or in arbitral awards and collective agreements applicable to the place of employment in the member state in which they are currently employed; the freedom of association, affiliation and participation in a workers' or employers' representative organisation or any organisation whose members are engaged in a specific occupation, including the benefits and rights conferred by such organisations, without prejudice to the provisions of national law on public policy and the recognition of public security; the award of diplomas, certificates and other evidence of formal qualifications, as laid down in article 3 (3) of regulation (ec) no 883/2004, without prejudice to the existing national procedures for the award of diplomas and certificates, as laid down in article 3 (3) of regulation (ec) no 648/2004.
in writing. - i welcome the request for further transparency included in the report on the clean sky 2 joint undertaking. however, i would have gone further. the joint undertaking should make public the professional details of its managerial staff members, the management board members and the experts it employs. in addition, declarations of interest should be available on the joint undertakingʼs website. i call therefore on clean sky 2 to remedy the situation as a matter of urgency. moreover, i request that the joint undertaking publishes on its website its policy on conflicts of interest. this is the only way to offer full transparency, limit the risks of conflicts of interest and protect taxpayersʼ money invested in research projects. i ask the commission to closely monitor the system through which the joint undertaking chooses the projects and institutions which will receive funding from the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on the clean sky 2 joint undertaking. the commission has followed up many of the recommendations made in the first interim evaluation of the clean sky joint undertaking, in particular with regard to: - significant leverage in terms of private funding and commitment by the sector to additional activities; - improvement of the governance structure of the joint undertaking; - increased openness of the public-private partnership through competitive tendering. we believe that funding for the horizon 2020 transport challenge should be increased in view of the huge budgetary constraints it will probably face when it has to finance not only clean sky 2, but also sesar and shift2rail. the states representatives group and the scientific committee should be empowered to fulfil their role as advisory bodies in addition to the joint undertaking. they should meet at least twice a year and their representatives should have the right to attend and speak at meetings of the governing board. at the same time, openness and transparency should not be limited to the internal functioning and governance procedures of the joint undertaking.
