madam president, i thank the rapporteur for this very good result achieved after a long time. it is a fact that in the european union public pension systems, that is, those in which those who are currently working pay contributions to a pension fund from which the pension of those who are old is paid, are becoming increasingly unsustainable as the share of the elderly increases and the share of the active population decreases. therefore, in many member states, supplementary occupational pension schemes are increasingly being introduced, whereby persons participating in such schemes constitute their own pension fund. i shall vote for this directive because it comes to specify much better and guarantee the rights of people who work in different member states, move from one to another, as well as the obligations of those who manage these supplementary pension funds. i believe that this directive strengthens the right of european citizens to free movement and i would like to point out that in my country, romania, some 3 million romanian citizens work in other member states of the european union and will benefit from this directive.
in writing. the proposal for a directive brings a significant improvement by providing greater protection for posted workers. considers it important to have a clear and closed list of criteria to avoid different application of these criteria by member states, a clear list of administrative and control measures to be used by control bodies in a member state when checking a company that posts workers, and a common set of clear rules that benefit companies by providing them with a stable legal framework and preventing the authorities of a member state from imposing arbitrary measures. the addition of new administrative and control measures by a member state will only be possible under strict conditions, with the european commission, member states and service providers informed. we need to combat abuses against posted workers by establishing a system of individual and collective liability, generally on a voluntary basis, and a mandatory system in the field of construction, as well as effective and proportionate sanctions against the contractor where workers have difficulty in obtaining their rights. also, a very important thing to consider is the cross-border enforcement of fines which allows the recovery of fines in the home state of the posting company.
the effectiveness of the directive on the return of unlawfully removed cultural objects, which has been in force since 1993, has left a legacy to be desired, according to experts, and the current revision is therefore certainly justified. the extension of the scope of the directive, the application of the return procedure to all cultural objects considered to be national treasures is a welcome step, since the extreme diversity of similar objects makes it pointless to maintain the annex to the directive. the extension of the time limits for enforcement and initiation of the return procedure also serves to increase the number of goods returned. the most important revision proposal, however, is to place the burden of proof on the owner. as a result, the owners of the objects will have to prove that they have exercised due care and have done everything possible to ensure that the objects are of legal origin. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the eu's return policy, which aims to improve the quality of return procedures and to improve the efficiency of judicial procedures. this effectively restores the obligation of member states to inform each other of return. it is important to note that, in the absence of a commonly agreed definition of national treasures, i believe that member states are free and unrestricted to decide what they consider to be national treasures. there is no need to regulate this issue any further. i support the rapporteur's proposal to continue to have a monitoring committee to monitor the implementation of the directive, as this will guarantee the effectiveness of the current revision of the document.
in writing. the regulation on the surveillance of the external maritime borders proposes new rules that will contribute to a more effective surveillance of our external borders and to the fight against all forms of cross-border crime. the new regulation will require member states to fulfil their obligation to provide assistance to people and vessels in distress at the eu's external border. the regulation sets out a clear obligation for participating units to engage in life saving and to cope with search and rescue situations in the context of operational cooperation coordinated by frontex. this new legislation is a step forward in addressing the problems that arise at the eu's external borders, in particular with regard to the assistance to be provided to those who are intercepted or rescued in the maritime border area. through this regulation, the eu regulates and provides the necessary guarantees for unaccompanied minors, vulnerable persons and those in need of international protection who are victims of trafficking.
in writing. the 1919-1923 treaty of trianon, which ended the first phase of the great war with 15 million casualties, anticipated the second wave of world warfare in the last century by adopting the plans of the paris peace conference in unaltered form. their failure was partly due to the general fatigue and weariness of several years of work, and partly to the efforts of the allies - incomprehensible to me - to carry out the ambitions of the peoples of the austro-hungarian monarchy seemingly without any consideration, while it was always the responsibility of the victors to create a lasting peace. despite all this, it is still often the majority who have a one-sided view of multiculturalism, multilingualism, human and minority rights. of the countries concerned, hungary and the hungarian community suffered the greatest loss: according to the peace treaty, every third hungarian-speaking person became a citizen of a foreign country, even though he did not leave his native land. i am convinced that history can provide the european union with the means to deal with the consequences that are still being felt today, including by recognising the rights of minorities and ensuring their autonomy.
in writing. this year marks 100 years since the start of the first world war, in which more than 10 million people died. world war ii also claimed more than 70 million lives, many of them civilians. in both wars, technological progress and new technical discoveries were used for destructive purposes. the schuman declaration of 9 may 1950 paved the way to a united europe, since 'the contribution to civilization which an organised and active europe can make is indispensable to the maintenance of peaceful relations. robert schuman stressed that 'the pooling of coal and steel production will immediately ensure the establishment of common bases for economic development, a first step towards the realisation of a european federation and will change the destiny of those regions which in the past were dedicated to the manufacture of munitions of war but which have been, at the same time, the most constant victims of conflicts'. today, more than ever, we need to learn from the lessons of the past and look to the future. the eu needs all its energy, creativity, resources and diplomacy to ensure the well-being and development of its members and to contribute to world peace. united in diversity, the peoples of europe must use technological progress and scientific discoveries only in the service of peace and social progress.
mr president, first we have to make up our minds: do we want war or do we want peace? if we want war we must prepare for war; if we want peace we must prepare for war too. secondly, a war could be fought with economic weapons. if we choose to use those weapons we must calculate in advance their precise effectiveness, making sure that they will not backfire. so far the therapy of gradual and personalised sanctions has been unconvincing. thirdly, if we cannot beat them let us join them. in other words, let us negotiate. the true problem is not ukraine but the lack of multilateral strategic dialogue on a global scale. global order could only be consensual. we do not like russiaʼs views on it but we cannot achieve it without russia. fourthly, since the peace of westphalia every major war in europe has ended with a peace conference and a peace treaty. this was the case in 1815, 1856, 1878, 1920 and 1946. the cold war ended without a peace treaty. we assumed that everything was clear and settled. this was not the case; now is the time to do it. tomorrow’s geneva meeting could be a first step in that direction. fifthly, it is obvious that international law and the international institutions do not function. we might deplore it but we would do better to negotiate new covenants adapted to the post-bipolar realities. the helsinki act might have died in crimea but it was mortally wounded in kosovo. lastly, if we want to be successful we must stop approaching international relations from an ideological perspective whilst consolidating and deepening eu integration. if we want peace, stability, security and freedom within our borders as well as in our neighbourhood, if we want russia to respect our standards, then we need a true power in europe, be it a soft power, but a power nevertheless.
mr president, the domino effect, appeasement and the doctrine of protecting nationals in foreign countries all played a crucial role in the outbreak of the last two world wars. alas, they are all present today in the crisis created by russia’s military actions against ukraine and its increasing pressures on the eastern partnership countries. the stakes are very high. this is not just another crisis which will fade away like the one in georgia in 2008. the current european order – based on the helsinki final act, the conventional armed forces in europe (cfe) treaty signed in paris – the eu’s credibility and article 5 of the washington treaty on which nato rests will all be called into question if what is happening in ukraine does not get the right answer. if we let ourselves be lured by the siren song of the executioner playing victim, by the appeals to stand tall to the warmongering americans or by the fata morgana of endless riches provided by lucrative contracts, or let ourselves be scared by the accompanying threats, then we stand to lose much more than money. those contracts, our energy dependence and the iranian and syrian dossiers are now simply instruments through which russia hopes to get our acquiescence to its military actions, destabilisation and pressure on the eastern partnership countries. moldova and georgia, along with ukraine, deserve full support to resist those pressures and provocations in order to continue and accelerate the reform process they engaged in on entering the eastern partnership, thus getting rapidly more substance to their european perspective.
mr president, for a month now we have been busy putting big words in public statements to show our concern for the people of ukraine, our condemnation of moscow’s actions or our indignation at russia’s soviet-style behaviour. resolution after resolution we have shouted out loud our worries when russia bluntly goes about annexing bits and pieces of ukraine. at the same time, president schulz is talking about eu-russia common interests. well, not all of us are willing to sell our souls for russian gas. it might be easy for some to talk that way – the ones who did not feel the destructive might of soviet russia – but it is insulting to all those people from romania, poland or east germany who died fighting for freedom and democracy, and these are the values the ukrainian people are fighting for today. we should not repeat the same mistakes with moldova. we cannot end up debating resolutions when it is too late. we must give them a european membership perspective and sign the association agreement as soon as possible.
mr. president, what's happening in the ukraine is unacceptable. a sovereign state is being attacked from outside, and from within it is losing, against all international rules, territory. the russian federation takes advantage of the economic situation and the legitimate desire of the european union for the absence of armed conflict and acts without hesitation outside of any international rules and treaties. we cannot accept the annexation of crimea. statements that it's a fait accompli are not helping to resolve the situation in the area. the lack of reaction has led to the extension of the process to kharkov and dombas and may reach as far as transnistria. moldova has shown a lot of will, resisted pressure and made important steps on its european path. we cannot accept that moldova is subjected without its will to a loss of territory. the union must support ukraine. firm positions and measures are needed. the sanctions applied so far have not had the expected effects. economic sanctions are needed to make a difference. the gas is needed by the beneficiary, but the producer also needs to sell. economic sanctions can create short-term problems for member states, but they are absolutely necessary if we want to avoid much worse consequences in the long term. the russian federation must be stopped from these actions directed against a sovereign state and which endanger the peace of the whole of europe.

in writing. - the directive provides that workers moving to another member state will not lose their state pension rights. there are currently no similar rules at eu level for supplementary pension schemes, so eu citizens who move between member states risk losing their acquired rights over a period of time if it is not considered long enough by the country they move to. the period of active membership of a pension scheme required for a person to retain his supplementary pension rights must not exceed three years. a clause was also included that crossborder workers should benefit from the same level of protection, which member states must implement for four years. the text also provides that member states may allow the social partners to lay down other provisions in collective agreements, provided that those provisions offer equally favourable protection and do not create obstacles to the free movement of workers.
in writing. - i supported the adoption at first reading of the directive on minimum requirements for increasing the mobility of workers between member states by improving the acquisition and retention of supplementary pension rights. it lays down rules aimed at facilitating the exercise of the right of workers to freedom of movement between member states by reducing the obstacles created by certain rules governing supplementary pension schemes linked to the existence of an employment relationship. member states shall take the necessary measures to ensure that: where a period of vesting of pension rights or a waiting period, or both, applies, the total combined period shall in no case exceed three years for workers who cease to work; where a minimum age for vesting pension rights is stipulated, that age shall not exceed 21 years for workers who cease to work; where a worker who ceases to work has not yet acquired pension rights acquired at the time of termination of the employment contract, the supplementary pension scheme shall refund the tax contributions paid by or on behalf of the worker under the internal taxation agreement or, where the amount of the tax contributions is the investment or risk resulting from the investment, the amount of the tax contributions or risk incurred by the worker in the case of the investment or risk resulting from the employment contract.
in writing. - ensuring a high level of human, animal and plant health throughout the food chain is a key objective of the treaty on european union and can only be achieved through the correct application of complex legislation in this field. today's vote will bring about a general harmonised legal framework at eu level and will allow the process of a thorough review of existing provisions to begin. this will allow for the removal of any overlapping regulations and a proportionate and flexible approach to be able to react more effectively in preventing and tackling risks as well as in emergency situations. as regards the financing of official controls, i consider it necessary to ensure that in particular the provisions for setting fees are clear and unambiguous, as this is the only way to achieve uniform application in the member states. it is also important that the bureaucratic burden of collecting fees is minimised when setting fees.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on official controls and other official activities carried out to ensure the enforcement of food and feed law, animal health and welfare rules, plant health, plant reproductive material and plant protection products. this regulation shall apply to official controls performed to verify compliance with the following rules, established either at union level or by the member states for the purpose of applying union legislation in the following areas: food regulation, food safety, quality and hygiene at all stages of food production, processing and distribution; regulation of the deliberate release of gmos into the environment; prevention and minimisation of antimicrobial resistance in animals and humans as well as in the environment; regulation of feed and feed safety; establishment of animal health and welfare requirements; prevention and minimisation of risks to human and animal health arising from animal by-products and derived products, etc.
in writing. - i voted for the proposed animal health regulation. this regulation lays down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases which are transmissible to animals or humans, tools and mechanisms to facilitate progress towards the declaration of disease-free areas and territories, and prioritises actions and the sharing of responsibilities in relation to animal health. the impact of transmissible animal diseases and of the measures needed to control those diseases can be devastating for individual animals, animal populations, animal holders and the whole economy and can have a major influence on public health and food safety. as recent experience has shown, transmissible animal diseases can also have a significant impact on public health and food safety, as for example in the case of avian influenza and salmonella. in order to ensure that the legislation is as clear as possible and is therefore applied correctly and fully, it is necessary to identify a criterion and a principle for the organisation of the delegated and implementing acts to be adopted pursuant to this regulation.
in writing. - i believe that the proposed measures for protection against plant pests must be taken in such a way as to ensure that all operators apply the precautionary principle and that the eradication of pests is carried out in a sustainable manner in order to protect the health of the food and agricultural chain, the population and, by implication, the environment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on measures to protect against organisms harmful to plants. this regulation lays down rules for the carrying out of phytosanitary inspections and other official activities by the authorities of the member states for the purpose of identifying the phytosanitary risks posed by any species, strain or biotype of pathogenic agents, animals or plants harmful to plants or plant products (hereinafter referred to as 'pests'), including invasive plant pests and the necessary phytosanitary measures to prevent the introduction of pests from other member states or third countries. member states should take measures to raise awareness of the potential economic, social and environmental impact of plant pests, the key principles relating to their prevention and spread, and the responsibility of society as a whole to ensure plant health in the union. at the same time, the commission should maintain an updated, publicly accessible list of emerging harmful organisms in third countries that could pose a risk to plant health in the union.
in writing. - i voted to amend the regulation on the safety of consumer products and to repeal directive 87/357/eec and directive 2001/95/ec. the objective of this regulation is to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market while maintaining a high level of health, safety and consumer protection. the provisions of this regulation are based on the precautionary principle. this regulation should apply and prohibit the marketing, import and manufacture or export of consumer products which, although not being foodstuffs, resemble foodstuffs and may mislead certain persons, in particular young children. products that are attractive to children should also be assessed in terms of their level of risk and appropriate measures should be taken to reduce that risk. i voted for amendment 60, which supports the introduction of the eu safety tested marking. this marking may be applied only to consumer products covered by this regulation and may not be applied to other products. the eu safety tested mark shall be applied after testing on representative samples of the products for sale, selected at random under the control of a judicial officer, an authority or any other third body.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on product market surveillance. the european single market is based on the free movement of goods, which is why there must be close supervision in the european union of goods traded within the eu, including products imported from outside the union. while the rapex alert system has already proven its effectiveness, better and more transparent cooperation between member states is needed to accurately identify problem goods, including their place of origin. i'll give you just two examples to illustrate this point: the 2011 e-coli outbreak, when responsibility and blame was passed from one country to another, and the 2013 horse meat scandal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on product market surveillance. the market surveillance activities covered by this regulation should not be exclusively concerned with the protection of health and safety, but should also apply to ensuring compliance with union legislation aimed at protecting other public interests, for example by regulating measurement accuracy, electromagnetic compatibility, energy efficiency and applicable environmental legislation. this regulation should apply to all forms of supply of products, including distance selling. member states and the commission should develop a common approach to market surveillance of products sold online and, where necessary, provide guidance on the roles and responsibilities of operators in the e-commerce supply chain with a view to strengthening the enforcement of rules on products sold online. in order to facilitate the work of market surveillance authorities, economic operators should make available to those authorities all documents and information necessary for the performance of their activities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on markets in financial instruments and amending the regulation on otc derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories. the financial crisis has brought to the fore a number of deficiencies in the transparency of financial markets that can contribute to negative socio-economic effects. in order to increase transparency and improve the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, it is necessary to establish a new framework laying down uniform requirements as regards the transparency of transactions in markets for financial instruments. the regulation adopted at first reading lays down uniform requirements in relation to: (a) the publication of transaction data; (b) the reporting of transactions to competent authorities; (c) the trading of derivatives on organised venues; (d) non-discriminatory access to clearing and non-discriminatory access to trading of benchmarks; (e) the responsibilities of competent authorities, the european securities and markets authority (esma) and the european banking authority with regard to product intervention, and the responsibilities of esma with regard to position management controls and position limits; (f) the provision of investment services or activities by third country companies following an applicable equivalence decision adopted by the commission, with or without a branch.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the markets in financial instruments directive, repealing directive 2004/39/ec. the evolution of financial markets has highlighted the need to strengthen the regulatory framework for markets in financial instruments, including over-the-counter (otc) trading in those markets, in order to increase transparency, investor protection, trust, address unregulated areas and to give supervisors adequate powers to fulfil their tasks. it is appropriate to include in the list of financial instruments commodity derivatives and those that, by their constitution and trading, involve regulatory issues comparable to those applicable to classical financial instruments. the adopted directive applies to investment firms, market operators, data reporting services providers and third-country firms providing investment services or performing investment activities in the union by establishing a branch. it lays down requirements relating to the following: the conditions of authorisation and operation applicable to investment firms; the provision of investment services or activities by third-country firms through the establishment of a branch; the authorisation and operation of regulated markets; the authorisation and operation of data reporting services providers; and supervision, cooperation and enforcement by competent authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 638/2004 on community statistics relating to the trading of goods between member states as regards the conferral of delegated and implementing powers on the commission to adopt certain measures, the communication of information by the customs administration, the exchange of confidential data between member states and the definition of the statistical value. i consider that, in order to satisfy the needs of users of statistical information without imposing excessive burdens on economic operators, to take into account changes required for methodological reasons and the need to set up an efficient system for data collection and statistics, the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union should be delegated to the commission in respect of adopting different or specific rules applicable to specific goods or movements, adapting the coverage rates of intrastat, specifying the conditions for the definition of the thresholds referred to in article 10 (4) of regulation (ec) no 638/2004, specifying the conditions for the simplification of the information to be provided for small transactions and defining aggregated data. in order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of regulation (ec) no 638/2004, implementing powers should also be conferred on the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on improving the settlement of financial instruments in the european union and on central securities depositories (csds) and amending directive 98/26/ec. by playing an important role in financial instrument holding systems, whereby participants report financial instruments held by investors, financial instrument settlement systems managed by csds function as an essential tool for checking the integrity of a given issue, thereby preventing the unjustified creation or reduction of issued financial instruments and thus playing an important role in maintaining investor confidence. in addition, the financial instrument settlement systems managed by csds are closely involved in the collateralisation of monetary policy operations as well as in the collateralisation process between credit institutions and are therefore important players in the collateralisation processes. the adopted regulation provides for uniform requirements for the settlement of financial instruments in the union as well as rules on the organisation and operation of central securities depositories in order to promote the safety, efficiency and soundness of settlement. it shall apply to the settlement of all financial instruments and activities of csds, unless otherwise provided for in this regulation.
in writing. - i voted for the report on relations between the european parliament and the national parliaments. the european parliament (ep) has paid particular attention to the role of national parliaments (np) in responding to the accusation of a 'democratic deficit' in the eu and finding valuable allies in building a european conscience. we welcome the treaty provisions which confer on national parliaments a number of rights and obligations which enable them to contribute actively to the proper functioning of the union. these rights and duties relate to: (a) active participation in eu affairs (power to ratify treaties, participation in the convention referred to in article 48 teu, control of national governments, control of subsidiarity, exceptional possibility of opposition, transfer of european law into national legislation); (b) political dialogue (interparliamentary cooperation and mutual exchange of information with the european institutions, in particular the european parliament). i believe that in order for member states to be represented unitedly and fully democratically in the eu, the position taken by national governments in the council should take account of the views of national parliaments, thus reinforcing the democratic nature of the council. we call on the commission to respond promptly and fully to the reasoned opinions and contributions submitted by the national parliaments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of pressure equipment. this directive concerns pressure equipment and assemblies which are new to the union market when they are placed on the market, namely either new pressure equipment or assemblies produced by a manufacturer established in the union or new or second-hand pressure equipment or assemblies imported from a third country. the directive should apply to all forms of supply, including distance selling. this directive applies to the design, manufacture and conformity assessment of pressure equipment and assemblies with a maximum allowable pressure exceeding 0,5 bar. pressure equipment subject to a pressure of 0,5 bar or less shall not present significant pressure related risks. therefore, their free movement within the union cannot be impeded.
in writing. - i voted for the amendment of regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 as regards the rules applicable to the unified patent court and the benelux court of justice. the amendments to regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 provided for in this regulation as regards the unified patent court are intended to establish the international jurisdiction of that court. as courts common to several member states, the benelux unified patent court and the benelux court of justice are not, unlike a court of a member state, able to exercise jurisdiction under national law in respect of defendants who are not domiciled in a member state. the rules laid down in regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 should, as regards matters falling within the competence of the unified patent court and the benelux court of justice respectively, also apply to defendants domiciled in third countries. the existing rules on jurisdiction in regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 ensure a close link between the actions to which that regulation applies and the territory of the member states. it is therefore appropriate to extend those rules to actions against all defendants, irrespective of their domicile.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 577/98 on the organisation of a labour force sample survey in the union. labour force survey is a key tool for collecting statistical data on the labour market situation in the european union, which can be used in european policy-making. i welcome the new provisions of the regulation, in particular those on alignment with the regime for delegated and implementing acts. given the important role that national statistical institutes play in labour force survey surveys, i welcome the introduction of a legal basis for granting grants in the form of lump sums and without a call for projects to statistical institutes operating in the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 577/98 on the organisation of a labour force sample survey in the community. in order to effectively combat discrimination in accordance with article 10 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), to contribute to ensuring compliance with article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and to pursue the objective of full employment and social progress in accordance with article 3 of the treaty on european union (teu), and to monitor progress towards the achievement of union policy objectives, such as the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, comparable, reliable and objective statistics on the situation of workers, the unemployed and persons out of work are necessary, while respecting statistical confidentiality, privacy and the protection of personal data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the multiannual financing of the european maritime safety agency's actions in the field of combating pollution caused by ships and marine pollution caused by oil and gas installations. considers it necessary to renew the multiannual funding for the period 2014-2020 in order to ensure the proper performance of the maritime safety agency's activities. i am pleased that consensus has been reached both on the agency's budget, with a view to increasing it, and on clarifying the issues relating to the definition of oil and gas installations. i believe that the agency plays an important role in tackling pollution from ships and gas and oil installations and that the benefits are both ecological, socio-economic and financial.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on the multiannual financing of the european maritime safety agency's actions in the field of combating pollution caused by ships and marine pollution caused by oil and gas installations. the agency shall provide a network of oil spill response vessels to supplement the response capacity of member states in such situations. the agency shall provide a satellite oil spill detection and monitoring service, cleanseanet, as well as information on chemical spills, through the mar-ice network. since january 2013, the agency has been given new tasks such as: responding to 'marine pollution caused by oil and gas installations'; monitoring by cleanseanet of marine hydrocarbon pollution caused by oil and gas installations and its impact on the environment. the geographical area covered (member states and acceding states) also extends to the european neighbourhood policy partner countries and the countries participating in the paris memorandum of understanding on port state control. the amount of eur 160,5 million allocated by the commission for the reference period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020 is therefore considered to be insufficient.
in writing. - unemployment is the greatest social challenge facing europe today. in july 2013, the unemployment rate in the eu as a whole was 11%, and for some member states it was above 20%. smes, micro-enterprises, entrepreneurs and innovators are job creators, currently providing 90 million jobs in the private sector in the eu, where there is huge potential for job creation, growth and innovation. given that 85% of all new jobs in the last 10 years have been created by smes, we need to ensure that the needs of smes are placed at the heart of policy-making. the commission and the member states should fully exploit the job creation potential of the green economy by developing a rise for sustainable europe (rise) industrial recovery strategy, which aims at technological, social and business innovation towards a third industrial revolution, including a low-carbon modernisation offensive. rise will create new markets, new business models and creative entrepreneurship, new jobs and decent work, producing an industrial renewal characterised by dynamism, confidence and economic competitiveness.
in writing. - i support the promotion of non-bank financing methods for businesses in the european union. in the period 2009-2011, 64% of enterprises preferred bank loans as their main source of financing. in 2013, that number jumped to 68 percent. however, also during 2013, 29% of all enterprises that applied for a bank loan did not receive the financing they needed. the european union provides non-bank financial support through the european regional development funds (erdf), the european investment bank (eib) or through the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) and the horizon 2020 programme. i call on the european commission to provide member states with a good platform to inform them about the non-bank financing opportunities offered by the european union to support the development of small and medium-sized enterprises that have not been able to obtain bank loans.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on how the european union can help create a favourable environment for businesses, companies and start-ups to create jobs. we underline the job creation potential of the green economy, which the commission estimates could create 5[nbsp ] million jobs by 2020 in the energy efficiency and renewable energy sectors alone, provided ambitious climate change and energy policies are put in place. we call on member states to ensure sufficient levels of investment in these sectors, to anticipate future skills requirements of workers and to guarantee the quality of 'green' jobs. education and training systems should be better adapted to and converged with the skills required by enterprises in the future. we stress that free and fair competition in the single market, underpinned by common social standards, is vital to stimulate growth and innovation and therefore increases employment in the union. we also support better coordination of eu corporate tax systems through the introduction of a harmonised tax base, accompanied by measures to combat tax evasion and aggressive tax planning.
in writing. - i voted for the motion on new technologies and open educational resources. in 2012, 15,8%[nbsp ] of young people in the eu were not in employment and were not in education or training, and were thus at risk of being excluded from the labour market as a result of the growing skills mismatch. also, by 2020, 90% of jobs will require digital skills, and by 2015 there will be around 900000 unfilled vacancies in the field of information and communication technologies (ict) in the eu. we invite member states to ensure coordinated and progressive education on safe internet use in schools. we underline the commission's role in encouraging the exchange of good practice between member states and between educational institutions, building on existing projects and experiences, and ask the commission to promote and extend the european schoolnet network and actions. we also welcome the commission's initiative to develop indicators for the close monitoring of ict integration in education and training institutions.
in writing. - the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), signed in 1973, guarantees that international trade in wild fauna and flora does not endanger their survival. at eu level, regulation (ec) no 338/97 ensures the protection of species of wild fauna and flora through a series of provisions on their import, export and re-export, and trade. the reform of that regulation is necessary and justified by the need to update it under the treaty of lisbon in order to allow for further amendments related to delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the protection of species of wild fauna and flora by controlling trade in them. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) aims to ensure that international trade in wild fauna and flora does not endanger their survival. it contains provisions on the import, export and re-export and on trade within the union of specimens of the species listed in its four annexes. the amendments to regulation (ec) no 338/97 are justified by the need to update the proposal under the treaty of lisbon to replace the old obsolete provisions with new provisions, in particular as regards the comitology rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the eu, of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of seychelles. the economy of the republic of seychelles is based mainly on fishing and tourism. the seychelles have signed fisheries agreements on the catches of migratory species with the eu, japan, south korea and taiwan. the eu-seychelles agreement is one of a number of fisheries agreements signed by the eu with countries in the indian ocean, and must be approached from a regional perspective. the first eu-seychelles fisheries agreement dates back to 1984 and has since evolved into a fisheries partnership agreement (fpa). the agreements could initially be renewed every three years, while the fpa is automatically renewed, except in cases where the protocol is suspended or terminated at the request of one of the parties. in 2013, a new protocol to that fisheries agreement was initialled, covering a period of six years from its provisional application. given that the current protocol expired in january 2014, the new protocol should be applied provisionally as from january 2014 in order to ensure the continuity of the eu fleet's activities in seychelles.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the conclusion of the protocol between the eu and the union of the comoros setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement in force between the two parties. the main objective of the protocol to the agreement is to provide eu vessels with fishing opportunities in the union of the comoros's fishing zone within the limits of the available surplus. the overall objective is to enhance cooperation between the eu and the union of the comoros with a view to establishing a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the union of the comoros' fishing zone, in the interest of both parties. the total annual financial contribution shall be eur 600 000 per year over the entire reference period. this contribution shall be based on: a reference tonnage of 6 000 tonnes for an access charge of eur 300 000. however, the total annual amount paid by the european union may not exceed twice that amount. this support shall meet the objectives of the national fisheries policy and, in particular, the needs of the union of the comoros in the fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the conclusion of the protocol agreed between the eu and the republic of madagascar setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement in force between the two parties. the fisheries partnership agreement agreed between the eu and madagascar allows european fishing vessels to fish in madagascar's waters and is part of the series of tuna fisheries agreements concluded with countries in the indian ocean region. the protocol, which grants fishing opportunities to eu vessels and sets the amount of the financial contribution, will expire on 31 december 2012. a new protocol should therefore be concluded which better corresponds to the actual capabilities and requirements of the fleet of the member states. the new protocol proposed by the european commission, which must be approved by the european parliament, applies for two years (2013-2014) and provides for fishing opportunities for 96 vessels (40 purse seine tuna vessels and 56 floating parachute vessels). the total financial contribution of the protocol is eur 3 050 000 (i.e. eur 1 525 000 per year), an increase of eur 328 000 per year compared to the previous agreement (2007-2012).
