in writing. - the stabilisation and association agreement between the union and montenegro, signed in 2007 and entered into force in 2010, represents an important step in supporting montenegro in its prospects of joining the european union. i have always supported the stabilisation and association process of the balkan countries by developing economic relations with them, by providing financial assistance, assistance for democratisation, civil society, education and institutional development. we have always promoted cooperation in the field of justice and home affairs and the fight against corruption. the inclusion of croatia among the signatories to the agreement further symbolises the union's commitment to bringing the western balkan countries closer to the member states and democratic values. we must continue to fight for the political and economic stability of the states in this region and demonstrate in this vital region that europeanization remains the safest bet for the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of montenegro, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union. negotiations for the conclusion of the protocol started on 22 november 2012, following earlier technical consultations with montenegro on this subject. subsequent rounds of negotiations took place on 25 january 2013 and 7 march 2013. the protocol was initialled by the commission and the government of montenegro on 16 may 2013. the commission proposes to the council to decide on the signing and provisional application of the protocol on behalf of the european union and to conclude the protocol on behalf of the union and its member states. as regards the conclusion of the protocol on behalf of the european atomic energy community, the commission proposes that the council approve the conclusion of the protocol in accordance with the second paragraph of article 101 of the treaty establishing the eaec.
in writing. - i support the participation of neighbourhood countries in the work of union agencies and european programmes. it is important to provide these countries with an opportunity to further promote cultural, educational, environmental, technical and scientific links with the union and the member states. participation in union programmes will enhance people-to-people contacts and sectoral cooperation, promote reform and modernisation in the union's neighbourhood and strengthen regulatory and administrative convergence. according to a progress report published by the european commission as part of the 2014 neighbourhood policy package, the political dialogue between the union and the georgian government was intense in 2013. it is important to continue to support georgia on its path towards the rule of law and to provide it with support to cope with pressure from the russian federation. the protocol signed in december 2013 between the european union and georgia is an important step for georgia and needs to be implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and georgia, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and georgia on the general principles for the participation of georgia in union programmes by which the european parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of the protocol. the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) between georgia and the european communities entered into force on 1 july 1999. georgia has actively participated in the european neighbourhood policy since 2004 and in the eastern partnership since its launch in 2009. i support the protocol to the apc that was signed on 12 december 2013. the objective of the protocol is to lay down the financial and technical rules enabling georgia to participate in certain union programmes. the horizontal framework established by the protocol constitutes a measure of economic, financial and technical cooperation, which allows access to assistance, in particular financial assistance, to be provided by the union under union programmes. this framework shall apply only to programmes for which the relevant constituent legal acts provide for the possibility of participation by georgia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision to apply a reduced rate of excise duty to rum and liqueurs produced and consumed locally in the autonomous region of madeira and to liqueurs and spirits produced and consumed locally in the autonomous region of the azores. in accordance with the explanatory memorandum of the commission proposal, portugal was authorised until 31 december 2013 to apply a reduced rate of excise duty in the outermost regions of madeira and the azores to liqueurs and spirits produced and consumed locally, taking into account the small area, fragmentation and low degree of mechanization of agricultural holdings and to compensate for the additional costs of transporting raw materials and installing equipment in these remote island areas. portugal requested the renewal of this authorisation until 31 december 2020 and the commission considered that the renewal is justified in order to avoid holding back the development of these outermost regions and to avoid distortion of competition in the internal market, while limiting the tax benefits to what is strictly necessary to compensate for the additional costs. this measure aims to further stimulate economic activity in the outermost regions and has no disruptive effect on the internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision on the aiem tax applicable in the canary islands. decision 2002/546/ec authorises spain to apply, until 30 june 2014, exemptions or reductions from the 'arbitrio sobre importaciones y entregas de mercancías en las islas canarias' (referred to as 'aiem') for certain products locally manufactured in the canary islands. the purpose of this exemption is to strengthen competitiveness, to compensate for the additional production costs generated by isolation, dependence on raw materials and energy, the obligation to build stocks, the small size of the local market and the low level of exports. spain may apply exemptions or reductions from the aiem tax for certain products locally manufactured in the canary islands for the period 2014-2020. the specific features of the canary islands are holding back their development and are responsible for the additional costs borne by local operators and it is justified to maintain the exemption or reduction of the aiem for a list of locally manufactured products, given that this measure is necessary and proportionate and does not undermine the integrity and consistency of the union legal order. this measure aims at continuing to stimulate economic activity and competitiveness in an outermost region, without prejudice to the union legal order.
in writing. - i voted to amend the period of application of council decision 2004/162/ec on the dock dues in the french overseas departments. decision 2004/162/ec authorises france, until 1 july 2014, to apply exemptions or reductions to 'anchorage duties' for a number of products manufactured in the french outermost regions (except saint martin) in order to increase competitiveness and compensate for additional production costs due to isolation, dependence on raw materials and energy, stockholding, the small size of the local market and the low level of export activity. france has requested that a differentiated charging system similar to the current system be maintained until 31 december 2020. this measure is justified and aims to further stimulate economic activity and competitiveness in an outermost region.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the rules of procedure as regards the provisions relating to parliamentary questions. i voted for amendments nos 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11. each part-session thus includes a 90-minute question-and-answer period for the commission on one or more specific horizontal topics decided by the conference of presidents. the conference of presidents shall invite commissioners whose portfolio is linked to the specific horizontal theme or themes on which they will be asked questions. no more than two commissioners shall be invited to each part-session, with the possibility of inviting a third according to the specific horizontal theme or themes chosen for the question time. the questions are submitted electronically. each member may table no more than five questions per month. exceptionally, a member may submit additional questions in the form of a paper document, signed by the member himself and deposited with the competent department of the secretariat. each member may also put a maximum of six questions for written answer to the european central bank per month, in accordance with the criteria set out in an annex to these rules of procedure. questions shall be published, together with the answer, on parliament's website.
in writing. - i voted to amend rule 90 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament on international agreements. at present, the rules of procedure do not provide for the other committees to deliver an opinion on resolutions on international agreements, although, in view of the increasing number of comprehensive agreements with a significant trade component, it has become indispensable to give the international trade committee the opportunity to contribute to shaping parliament's position. the objective of allowing for the issuing of opinions in the context of parliament's examination of international agreements can be achieved by amending rule 90 (4) of parliament's rules of procedure. by extending the period of application of that provision, which currently equals the duration of the negotiations, to cover the entire procedure from the start of the negotiations to the conclusion of the agreement, parliament could therefore intervene at any time to clarify its position with a view to the approval it must give. at the same time, other committees could participate in the procedure as committees called upon for an opinion or as associated committees in a consolidated form.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the rules of procedure of the european parliament to allow the use of electronic signatures. i therefore voted for the introduction of a new article 148 entitled 'electronic processing of documents' and which states that parliament's documents may be prepared, signed and distributed in electronic format. the office shall decide on the technical specifications and the presentation of the electronic format. also, in rule 156 paragraph 1 the interpretation following paragraph 2, the text which stated that amendments could be signed electronically in a pilot project involving a limited number of parliamentary committees is deleted, provided that, on the one hand, the committees participating in the project had given their consent and, on the other hand, that appropriate measures had been taken to ensure the authenticity of the signatures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation establishing the shift2rail joint undertaking. the shift2rail joint undertaking ((s2r) will be a public-private partnership aimed at stimulating and better coordinating union investment in research and innovation in the railway sector, while creating new employment opportunities, with a view to accelerating and facilitating the transition towards a more integrated, user-friendly, efficient, sustainable and attractive eu railway market, in line with the overall objective of achieving a single european railway area. the s2r joint undertaking will contribute to the achievement of the specific objectives set out in the 2011 white paper and the fourth railway package, such as improving the efficiency of the railway sector for the benefit of public finances, significantly expanding or upgrading the capacity of the rail network to enable rail transport to compete effectively and to take a significantly higher share of passenger and freight transport, improving the quality of rail transport services by meeting the needs of passengers and freight forwarders, removing technical barriers affecting interoperability across the sector and reducing the negative externalities of rail transport. the progress of the s2r joint undertaking towards meeting those objectives should be measured on the basis of key performance indicators.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution adopting the regulation on the introduction of noise operating restrictions at airports in the union. the regulation harmonises, clarifies and strengthens common rules on noise-related operating restrictions at eu airports, such as the prohibition of night flights. the rules, which are based on principles agreed by icao and known as the 'balanced approach', cover in particular the assessment and management of aircraft noise and aim to identify the most effective way of reducing aircraft noise at each airport. the regulation applies only to large airports with more than 50 000 aircraft movements per year and does not set specific noise thresholds, which remain the responsibility of national or local authorities. at parliament's initiative, local authorities will retain the power to decide on noise reduction measures at airports, such as measures to ban night flights. moreover, the commission is obliged to come up with solutions to the health problems caused by noise at airports by revising the environmental noise directive 2002/49/ec.
in writing. - i support the commission's proposal to continue this programme for the years 2020-2033. the union must support an ambitious cultural policy and defend cultural diversity in the member states. in 2007, the romanian city of sibiu was the european capital of culture together with luxembourg city. the big gain for sibiu after this year was certainly the increased visibility it benefited from. the number of tourists in 2007 reached 700 000, double the number in 2006 and triple the number in 2005. of the total number of tourists, 40% were foreign tourists. at the same time, the investments in the city's infrastructure made for 2007 benefited the inhabitants of sibiu. this is just one example of the benefits this programme brings to a city, providing opportunities for issues of social inclusion and cohesion, education, tourism, heritage and urban regeneration at all levels.
in writing. - welcomes the parliament's approval of the agreement reached by the committee on culture in its negotiations with the council, in particular on the divergent position on the designation of the winning cities of the european capital of culture; the cultural capitals initiative is of great importance to the union, since 1985 it has been one of the projects best known to citizens, a true symbol of community programmes. today, we are taking a step forward by adopting the regulatory framework for the period after 2020, giving cities a green light to present their cultural applications and programmes. i hope that the new programme will provide more funding for the cultural capitals, given the possibility of accessing additional resources from the eu, especially from the structural funds, but also from national administrations. the leverage effect is to make infrastructure investments sustainable in the long term, with the effects of the cultural capital title being maintained in the years to come. i also express my confidence that the member states, who will designate the city as the cultural capital on the basis of the recommendations of the expert jury, will choose the best candidate, strictly according to objective criteria.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution adopting the decision on the union action on european capitals of culture for the period 2020-2033. the existing rules for the designation of european capitals of culture from 2006 expire in 2019. the commission proposal maintains the structure and content of the current procedure and includes a calendar setting out the order in which member states will host a european capital of culture. the selection will be based on a presentation by the candidate cities of their cultural programmes throughout the year. candidate cities will be able to include in their proposal also a neighbouring region. the main changes to the proposal concern: (i) the designation of cities (by the commission and not by the council); (ii) the members of the selection and monitoring panel; and (iii) the opening of the initiative to candidate and potential candidate countries. the agreement reached aims to: increase national representation in the selection and monitoring panel the host member state will appoint two persons; strengthen the european dimension of the annual cultural programmes; ensure the long-term sustainability of infrastructure projects; facilitate access to other sources of european funding (in particular the structural funds). the host member state will also designate a city, based on the recommendation of the expert panel, and the commission will publish the name of the city in the official journal of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 812/2004 laying down measures concerning incidental catches of cetaceans in fisheries. in view of the shortcomings of regulation (ec) no 812/2004, the relevance and effectiveness of the provisions of that regulation with regard to the protection of cetaceans should be reviewed before the end of 2015. on the basis of that review, the commission shall, if necessary, draw up a comprehensive legislative proposal, to be submitted to the european parliament and to the council, to ensure effective protection of cetaceans, including through regionalisation. the commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to update the technical specifications and conditions of use of acoustic intimidation devices, in particular the signal characteristics and the corresponding implementation characteristics, with a view to adapting the regulation to technical and scientific progress. the commission will provide for a sufficiently long period for the implementation of these adjustments. the power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the commission for a period of not more than four years.
in writing. - freedom of movement for workers is one of the basic conditions for the proper functioning of the european free market. the number of workers transferred annually is significant and growing, making a visible contribution to reducing unemployment and strengthening the employment sector. we must take into account that the posting of workers and the free provision of services, particularly in cross-border areas, is an opportunity with bilateral benefits. perhaps for the first time in romania, the industrial platform of their hometown, chisinau-cris, employs workers from the neighboring state, hungary. it is necessary to establish common standards for posted workers also in the field of the provision of services, within a well-regulated legislative framework that establishes the legal status and the categories of workers and services covered by the posting. the alignment of the laws of the member states is therefore a priority for the effective functioning of the internal market. the establishment of measures aimed at applying non-discriminatory treatment will ensure equal opportunities for participation by companies in host states. the measures will also aim to combat discrimination on grounds of nationality between employees.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive implementing directive 96/71/ec on the posting of workers in the framework of the provision of services, adopting the directive at first reading. the adopted directive aims to ensure that an adequate level of protection of the rights of workers posted for the purpose of cross-border provision of services is respected, in particular ensuring that the terms and conditions of employment applicable in the member state where the service is to be provided are applied, in accordance with article 3 of directive 96/71/ec, while facilitating the exercise of the freedom to provide services for service providers, promoting fair competition between them and thus supporting the functioning of the internal market. the directive does not in any way affect the exercise of fundamental rights as recognised in the member states and at union level, including the right or freedom to strike or take other actions which are part of the specific labour relations systems of the member states, in accordance with national law and/or practice. it shall also not affect the right to negotiate, conclude and enforce collective agreements and to bring collective actions in accordance with national law and/or practice.
in writing. - in the context of free movement within the european area, the protection of cultural property belonging to the national heritage becomes a concern of the authorities of all member states. this is in the light of the alarming increase in the trafficking of such goods in recent years. the average number of crimes against national cultural heritage is alarming. it is estimated that there are about 8 000 such cases every year. the european legislation that has been in place until now had to be amended, given its limited effectiveness in returning cultural goods. this inefficiency is partly due to the short time-limits for initiating restitution actions and partly to the related costs and to the non-uniform definitions given to cultural goods of national interest in each of the member states. i believe that the reform should aim at increasing the number of cultural objects returned by extending the time limit for the implementation of the return action and by approximating the laws of the member states as regards the conditions for compensation to the holder of the object of the return. i also support the need to regulate the situation of cultural goods placed on the market as a result of illegal archaeological excavations in many eu countries. i also stress the obligation of the member states to inform each other on the matter of return in order to streamline the whole process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state. the internal market comprises an area without internal frontiers in which the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital is ensured in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in accordance with article 36 tfeu, the relevant provisions on the free movement of goods do not preclude prohibitions or restrictions on imports, exports or goods in transit justified on grounds relating to the protection of national heritage objects of artistic, historical or archaeological value. the adopted directive applies to the return of cultural objects defined or classified by a member state as belonging to the national heritage as referred to in article 2 (1) of that directive which have left the territory of that member state unlawfully. cultural objects which have left the territory of a member state unlawfully shall be returned in accordance with the procedure and under the conditions laid down in this directive.
in writing. - nearly 100 billion plastic bags are consumed each year, and this number is projected to increase to 111 billion plastic bags by 2020 if no action is taken. this means that on average each european uses 200 plastic bags in a year. this excessive consumption of single-use plastic bags is not only very resource-inefficient, but also has negative consequences for the environment. every year, eight billion plastic bags are dumped into the environment in the eu, including the seas. despite rising resource prices, the current recycling rate for plastic bags is estimated to be only 6.6% and is unlikely to increase significantly in the coming years. for these reasons, i believe that a european approach to this problem is necessary to achieve the desired results.
in writing. - the consumption of plastic bags in the european union is excessive and has significant negative consequences for the environment. each year, eight billion plastic bags are thrown into the environment in the eu, and the current recycling rate for plastic bags is only 6.6%. i therefore consider the commission's proposal to be a key initial step in the adoption of important legislative measures against the irrational use of plastic carrier bags. consumer information plays a decisive role in achieving any objective of reducing the consumption of plastic bags. i therefore believe that efforts at institutional level are needed to raise awareness of the environmental impact of plastic bags and to remove the current perception of plastic as a harmless, cheap and worthless commodity in itself. in addition, carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to reproduction substances and substances that are endocrine disruptors should be removed from packaging material in order to avoid unnecessary exposure of humans to such substances and to avoid these substances entering the environment as waste.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directive 94/62/ec on packaging and packaging waste to reduce the consumption of thin plastic carrier bags. it is estimated that in 2010, over 8 billion plastic carrier bags were discarded in the eu. they are not included in waste management systems and accumulate in the environment, especially in the form of marine litter, which is increasingly recognised as a major global problem. once discarded, plastic carrier bags can last for hundreds of years, mostly in a fragmented form. also, from a resource-efficient perspective, the very high and continuously increasing consumption of such bags is not optimal. i support the objective of this proposal on plastic carrier bags to limit negative environmental effects, in particular in terms of waste generation, to encourage waste prevention and more efficient use of resources, while limiting negative socio-economic effects.
in writing. - in recent years, the mediterranean region has been affected by a number of international geopolitical and economic developments, which have contributed to political instability. as a result, migratory flows and asylum pressure from the southern shores of the mediterranean sea have increased on the northern shores, especially on the southern eu member states on the geographical periphery of the eu, such as greece, italy, spain, malta and cyprus. the number of people crossing europe's southern maritime borders using unsafe ships rose to about 10 000 in 2010, rose to over 70 000 in 2011, to fall again to about 20 000 in 2012, with the majority of these crossings organised by smugglers. i believe that responsibility-sharing and solidarity have become indispensable factors in ensuring that the fundamental rights of asylum seekers and refugees are fully respected in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation laying down rules for the surveillance of the external maritime borders in the context of operational cooperation coordinated by the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union. the objective of the union's external border policy is to ensure the effective monitoring of the crossing of the external borders, including through border surveillance, while contributing to ensuring protection and saving lives. border surveillance aims to prevent unauthorised border crossings, to combat cross-border crime and to detain or take other measures against persons who have crossed the border irregularly. this regulation shall apply to border surveillance operations carried out by member states at their external maritime borders in the context of operational cooperation coordinated by the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union. measures taken for the purpose of a maritime operation shall be carried out in such a way as to guarantee, in all situations, the safety of persons intercepted or rescued, the safety of participating units or that of third parties. coercive and investigative measures shall be governed in accordance with national criminal law and the existing instruments on mutual legal assistance in the field of judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework for the management of financial liability relating to investor-state dispute settlement tribunals established by international agreements to which the european union is party. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, foreign direct investment has been included in the list of areas covered by the common commercial policy. in accordance with article 3 (1) (e) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the union has exclusive competence in respect of the common commercial policy and may be a party to international agreements containing provisions on foreign direct investment. without prejudice to the division of competences established by the tfeu, this regulation applies to investor-state dispute settlement proceedings conducted under an agreement to which the union is a party or to which the union and its member states are parties and initiated by a third-country complaining party.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community and regulation (ec) no 597/2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community. in order to improve the transparency and predictability of anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations, parties affected by the imposition of provisional anti-dumping and countervailing measures, in particular importers, should be informed of the impending imposition of such measures. in the case of investigations where the imposition of provisional measures is not appropriate, it is also desirable that the parties should have known this sufficiently in advance. a short period should be allowed for exporters or producers to verify the calculation of their individual dumping or subsidy margin before the imposition of provisional measures. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry did not suffer material injury within the meaning of article 3 (5) of the basic regulation.
in writing. - the existence and development of european political parties is essential to generate public interest in eu affairs. welcomes the development of a reform package for european political parties as a means of mobilising the democratic energies of individual citizens and their organisations. i believe it is absolutely necessary that european political parties and foundations respect in their programmes and activities and those of their members the values on which the european union is founded, namely respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the statute and funding of european political parties and european political foundations. the european union must operate on the basis of the principle of representative democracy as set out in article 10 (1) of the treaty on european union. european political parties and european political foundations will have special rights, obligations and responsibilities under this regulation and should therefore conform to compatible organisational models. membership of a european political party and voluntary participation in its political activities should not be regarded as payments or benefits in kind, but as dedication to volunteering. technical assistance to be provided by the institutions of the european union to european political parties should be based on the principle of equal treatment, should be provided on an invoice and payment basis and should be the subject of a periodic public report by the relevant institution. we also believe that european political parties should be able to finance campaigns in the context of referendums in one or more member states directly related to issues concerning the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 966/2012 as regards the financing of european political parties. the contributions may only be used to reimburse a percentage of the running costs of european political parties which are directly linked to the objectives of the parties concerned. these reimbursable costs include administrative costs and those relating, inter alia, to technical assistance provided, meetings, events, including cross-border events and joint events with political groups in the european parliament, information, publications, research and studies, campaigns in the context of elections to the european parliament and referendum campaigns organised at european level. the costs of campaigns in the context of elections to the european parliament shall be reimbursed in accordance with the rules laid down in article 17 of the regulation (eu) on the statute and funding of european political parties and european political foundations. exceptionally, contributions may also be used to finance campaigns for national, regional or local referendums, provided that the subject of the referendum concerned is union law, the functioning of an institution of the union or the ratification of amendments to the treaties of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 966/2012 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the union and repealing regulation (ec, euratom) no 1605/2002. the commission proposal amends article 13 of the financial regulation to include carry-over rules in the case of the emergency aid reserve and of projects financed under the cef, in accordance with article 9 (2) of the cfm regulation as regards the emergency aid reserve and with the explanatory statement of the proposal for a council regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014 to 2010 as regards the cef. as the commission proposal was submitted before the adoption of the common provisions regulation, it could not provide for certain necessary adjustments in the light of the text of the final political agreement. it is therefore appropriate to include in the financial regulation specific provisions on the establishment of a performance reserve and on the sme initiative in the current revision of the financial regulation, as required by the new mff. this report also endorses a specific joint statement agreed in the negotiations on the commission delegated regulation on the model financial regulation for public-private partnership (ppp) bodies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the monitoring, reporting and verification of carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport and amending regulation (eu) no 525/2013. shipping has an impact on the global climate and air quality through emissions of carbon dioxide (co2) and other emissions, including nitrogen oxides (nox), sulphur oxides (sox), methane (ch4), particulate matter (ps) and black smoke. this regulation lays down rules for the accurate monitoring, reporting and verification of greenhouse gas emissions and other relevant information from ships arriving in, or within, or departing from ports under the jurisdiction of a member state, in order to promote the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from maritime transport in a cost-effective manner. this regulation applies to ships of more than 400 gross tons in terms of emissions generated during their voyages from the last port of call to a port under the jurisdiction of a member state and from a port under the jurisdiction of a member state to their next port of call, as well as within ports under the jurisdiction of a member state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive alien species. the appearance of allogeneic species, whether animals, plants, fungi or micro-organisms, in new environments is not always a cause for concern. a significant subset of allogeneic species may become invasive, causing serious adverse effects on biodiversity, related ecosystem services, and other economic and social effects, which should be prevented. approximately 12 000 species occurring in the environment in the union and other european countries are allogeneic, of which approximately 10 to 15% are estimated to be invasive. this regulation lays down rules on the prevention, minimisation and mitigation of the adverse effects of the introduction and spread, both intentional and unintentional, of invasive alien species on biodiversity in the union. it is important to ensure that priority is given to addressing the sub-group of invasive alien species considered to be of union interest. a list of invasive alien species of union concern should therefore be established and regularly updated. a harmful invasive species should be considered to be of union interest if the damage caused by it in the affected member states is so significant that special measures with a union-wide scope are justified.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (eu) no 525/2013 as regards the technical implementation of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change (cconusc). the conference of the parties to the cconusc, serving as the meeting of the parties to the kyoto protocol, adopted the doha amendment, which established the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, beginning on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020 (the doha amendment). the adoption of the doha amendment, the implementation of related decisions of the conference of the parties to the unfccc serving as the meeting of the parties to the kyoto protocol and a joint fulfilment agreement require the establishment of rules to ensure the technical implementation in the union of the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, including the transition from the first to the second commitment period, in order to allow the effective functioning of a joint fulfilment agreement and to ensure its alignment with the functioning of the european union emissions trading scheme established by directive 2003/87/ec and decision 406/2009/ec.
in writing. - as epp rapporteur on the 2012 report on the protection of the union’s financial interests, i expressed my concerns regarding the attitude of some member states which deal with fraudulent irregularities only through the application of financial corrections instead of investigating fully the potential criminal offence. in this respect, i welcomed the commission’s proposal for a directive on the fight against fraud to the union’s financial interests by means of criminal law. this directive must represent a strong step forward in the protection of the union’s financial interests and the taxpayers’ money. in order to achieve this ambitious goal, we need a strong legal basis for the directive. criminal procedures will be better unified and therefore more efficient and effective, and at the end of the day this will mean a higher degree of protection against fraudsters. in addition, we need the full participation of the european parliament throughout the entire legal procedure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the fight against fraud against the union's financial interests by means of criminal law. in order to ensure the consistency of union law with regard to the protection of the financial interests of the union, it is appropriate to introduce certain minimum levels of penalties in relation to the offences defined in this directive. this directive lays down minimum rules. member states should remain free to maintain or introduce more stringent penalties for those offences. i voted against amendment no 42, which excludes vat revenue from the scope of this directive. i voted for amendments nos 43 and 44 tabled by the s&d group which lower the damage threshold from eur 100 000 to eur 50 000. the court of auditors, the national audit bodies and the auditors entrusted with auditing the budgets of the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies set up by the treaties or the budgets managed and audited by the institutions shall inform olaf of any criminal offence of which they become aware in the course of their duties. the union's officials shall also inform olaf of any criminal offences of which they become aware during their duties.

in writing. the european union needs a budget based at least 75% on own resources and only 25% on a resource mechanism linked to the economic strength of each member state. the negotiations for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework have once again demonstrated the need for a european union budget based on own resources. if we don't reform the eu budget, on own resources, then we will keep the negotiations of any eu budget in the area of how much a member state contributes and receives from the eu budget and leave the size of that budget to governments.
the council president-in-office of the council. - madam president, the council is fully aware of the problems of payment appropriations in the context of the european union's external aid and of the concerns expressed by mrs barbarella, the president of the council, and the president of the commission, mr delors, in the context of the european union's external aid. joly and mr. lamassoure, on behalf of the committee on budgets and the committee on development. parliament, the council and the commission have already had an opportunity to discuss this issue at the budgetary trilogue which took place on 2 april. this meeting enabled us to identify possible ways of coping with the financial problems flagged by the commission. the commission was able to give an initial response to the shortage of payment appropriations concerning humanitarian aid and the european instrument for democracy and human rights by presenting two transfer proposals. the council went to considerable lengths to ensure that both of these transfer proposals were processed as quickly as possible. i am very pleased to inform you that since the beginning of this week, following adoption by the agriculture and fisheries council on monday, the commission is in a position to move the requested funds to the budget lines in need. should these additional appropriations prove insufficient to cover the needs of the budget lines later this year, the commission is invited to present further proposals for reallocation of appropriations or, if not sufficient, a draft amending budget. i would like to assure you that the council will fully respect the wording and content of the joint statement on payment appropriations which was agreed by our three institutions in november last year in the context of the conciliation on the 2014 budget. in line with that statement, the council will swiftly process any possible request for the transfer of payment appropriations, including across financial framework headings. it will also reach a position on any possible draft amending budget as quickly as possible in order to avoid any shortfall in payment appropriations. at the same time, you will of course understand that i am not, at this moment, in a position to prejudge at this stage the position that the council will take on any specific transfer request. allow me to say a few words on the proposed eu support package to ukraine which is currently an issue on which the media have particularly focused. the council is determined to support the ukrainian people and the ukrainian government in its efforts to stabilise the country and undertake reform. the council therefore welcomes the comprehensive assistance package presented by the commission and is committed to ensuring its implementation. we acknowledge that this might create additional pressure on the issue of payment appropriations in the eu budget this year. the budgetary trilogue on 2[nbsp ]april was an opportunity for our three institutions to have an exchange of views on this question as well. the commission has meanwhile taken a first set of measures to tackle the problem, and the council has promised to react swiftly. i would like to conclude by recalling that it is the commission which has the power of initiative. it is therefore for the commission to present any proposals for budgetary redeployment or for a draft amending budget. the council for its part is committed to examining any such proposal rapidly and to reaching a position on them as soon as possible.
member of the commission. - madam president, the management of budgets today, both at national and european level, is a management of shortage. this is a fact of life and is due to systematic under-budgeting and the level of payments available being below what is a forecast for payments needed for 2012-2013 and now 2014. we are now familiar with a kind of two-step approach – implementing the budget but then asking for the amending budget, on the basis of perhaps more hard data, to convince the member states to deliver, because even in austerity you need to pay your household bills, such as electricity bills. 2014 will be a difficult year on many fronts, as we have a level of payments which is eur[nbsp ]9[nbsp ]billion lower than that executed last year. so we can expect shortages, unfortunately across the budget and not only for the external obligations of the european union. for example, we have more than eur[nbsp ]20 billion in unpaid bills for cohesion from last year and this is a major headache in the implementation of the 2014 budget. but of course, reacting to the letter and oral questions from ms joly and mr[nbsp ]lamassoure, we need to react in the area of external aid programmes, also having recourse to the tools we have under the financial regulation and under the treaty. this was announced in our joint declaration on payment appropriations. i quote, ‘the global level of payments would be managed through the use of a global margin for payments. if needed, the commission may also have recourse to the flexibility instrument and the contingency margin agreed upon in the ... mff regulation.’ therefore, in this context the commission intends to propose correcting measures in light of implementation, using to the extent possible all the tools offered by the new mff as it was in 2012 and 2013. in 2013 we already mobilised an additional 54% for humanitarian aid, so this is now repeating the exercise with even more dramatic needs. what is our toolbox in this respect? first, there is monitoring, but monitoring is a diagnosis of what the shortages are. this is not enough. secondly, there are precautionary measures. we are taking precautionary measures, for example two tranches for humanitarian aid, and reducing the pre-financing rates to international organisations’ crisis management under the same logic this year. the third tool in our toolbox of course relates to transfers. there are two of these already coming up, one to the advantage of so-called bridge financing and humanitarian aid, and the second to the european instrument for democracy and human rights. mr lamassoure was right. this is exploiting the profile of payments. some budgetary lines need a payment late in the year, but we need to replenish. we are borrowing money somehow to frontload them now, but we need to find compensation by the end of the year. the next tool is the emergency aid reserve. if there is no possible alternative, we have the emergency aid reserve. later in the year, this is a global transfer for redeployment, as far as possible, because we have better knowledge in the second half of the year about what could be redeployed under this management of shortage. last but not least, there is budget amendment. this will come late this year, but will probably not be enough. margins are not enough, so we also need the flexibility instrument and contingency margin. this is the reality of budgets. however, regarding humanitarian aid – and i can agree with the oral questions that these are sometimes lifesaving actions – we need to respond and we to exploit all the possibilities. regarding ukraine, there is additional frontloading – additional monies that were not agreed in the 2014-2020 budgets. as for the profile of this eur 11 billion, eur 1.4 billion relates to grants and the rest to loans, partly under the guarantee of european budgets. this is manageable and i think we need to react as quickly as possible now, given the dramatic, even tragic, developments in eastern ukraine.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, i would like to welcome today's debate on the payment deficit for financing the external aid granted by the european union this year. it is indeed vital that we find a solution to this problem, because from tomorrow until july we will not meet again. or, in the meantime, the european union must honour its commitments and at the same time be able to respond to any humanitarian crises that may arise. i would therefore like to return to the magnitude of this problem. this is a payment deficit of eur 400 million, which is therefore about half of the union's annual humanitarian aid budget. according to the directorate-general for humanitarian aid and civil protection, €150 million needs to be found by the summer to avoid a real crisis of payments. this means that humanitarian projects that are vital for people affected by crises in third countries are at this point in time at risk. it is true that during the crisis the entire union budget had to be reduced and that the problem of payment appropriations affects other budget lines, not just our external action. but i want to mention a few things that i think are very important. first, humanitarian aid is different from other types of union expenditure. these are short-term financing, projects that last 12 to 18 months and often need to be activated immediately if we want our action to be effective in contexts such as armed conflict, drought or floods. secondly, the directorate-general for humanitarian aid and civil protection has helped 120 million people through its actions in 2013. beyond the numbers, it is a payment deficit affecting vulnerable people in syria, south sudan, the central african republic and, here, ukraine, which counts, relying on our help. finally, in opinion polls, humanitarian aid has consistently emerged as one of the union's most popular actions among citizens. it is therefore a matter of responsibility to european citizens and of the credibility of our external action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation laying down detailed rules for the exercise of the european parliament's right of inquiry and repealing decision 95/167/ec, euratom, ecsc of the european parliament, the council and the commission. the treaty of lisbon has created the conditions for a renewed and stronger institutional balance within the union, allowing its institutions to function more efficiently, more openly and in a more democratic way. the european parliament's powers of political control have been strengthened and extended. therefore, in accordance with national parliamentary practice and the requirements of the treaties, the committees of inquiry of the european parliament should be strengthened by conferring on them specific, real and clearly delimited powers which are more in line with its powers and political status, while respecting the principle of proportionality as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. the powers of committees of inquiry, which are exceptional instruments of political control, should be without prejudice to the responsibilities of other institutions. committees of inquiry should fully respect the rights of the persons they summon to testify in accordance with the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council regulation (eu, euratom) laying down implementing measures for the system of the european union's own resources, approving the draft council regulation. the implementing regulation is part of the wider package on the reform of the own resources system presented by the commission in june 2011 (and revised in november 2011). it contains provisions on the determination of own resources, control and supervision and reporting requirements for national authorities. as indicated in the draft council decision on the system of own resources, the implementing regulation contains provisions of a general nature applicable to all types of own resources and requiring appropriate parliamentary oversight. the council adapted the commission's 2011 proposal to the outcome of the negotiations on the mff/own resources, except for the sections on the reform of the vat own resource and the introduction of an own resource from financial transaction tax (ftt), which did not receive the council's support. unfortunately, the council also decided to transfer the provisions on the calculation of gni-based resources back into the own resources decision, as is currently the case, thus missing the opportunity to bring all the implementing provisions together in a single legislative text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council decision on the system of the european union's own resources, approving the council's draft as amended by the european parliament (ep). i voted for amendment no 2 because the current system of union funding, whereby some 74% of resources come from gni-based contributions and 11% from existing statistical vat-based contributions, has led to the introduction of complex and opaque reductions and other correction mechanisms, contributing to the recurrent problem of insufficient payments in the annual budgetary procedure. i voted for amendment no 3 because i support the need for a fundamental reform of the own resources system which should return to a clear, simple and fair own resources system. the ep considered that the commission's legislative proposals on own resources of june 2011 were a step in the right direction, which is why they were supported from the outset by an overwhelming majority of the ep. we also regret that the final political agreement of the european council of 8 february 2013 did introduce new reductions and exceptions.
in writing. - i congratulate my colleagues for their work in this vital dossier for our citizens. a complete reform of the current own resources system is imperative if we want the budget of the eu to be a transparent and equitable one. nevertheless, i deeply deplore the reluctant position of the council which refused any reform of the vat contribution system. how can we expect our citizens to trust the investments made through the eu budget, if its structure remains as undemocratic and opaque as ever. vat contributions remain to this day unevenly distributed among member states, with some being blessed by rebates, preferential quotas and lump sum payments, while the others are only entitled to carry the burden of these exceptions. therefore, i expect and wish for a thorough review of the own resources system to be finalised by the high level working group by the end of this year, in order to be able to put an end to the current imbalances at the post-electoral revision in 2016.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council regulation on the methods and procedure for making available traditional own resources and own resources based on vat and gni and on measures to meet the needs of the treasury (reform) approving the draft council as adapted to take account of the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission. the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considers that the commission proposal does not contain any substantive amendments other than those identified as such in the proposal and that, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the previous acts with those amendments, the proposal is limited to a mere codification of the existing acts without any substantive amendments to them. we invite the council to inform parliament if it intends to depart from the text approved by the ep. we also ask the council to consult it again if it intends to substantially amend the text approved by the ep.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the measures to implement the european union's own resources system. we welcome the council's agreement to establish measures for the implementation of the union's own resources system as provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. they argue that, because of austerity measures, member states are reluctant to increase their contributions to the eu budget, despite the undeniable benefits they receive through programmes funded by the eu budget. the only viable solution is to set up a system of direct own resources for the eu. we regret that the council has not been able to make progress on reform of the own resources system on the basis of the legislative proposals put forward by the commission.
in writing. - in the context of the economic crisis and the accompanying unemployment, but also due to the transformation of national labour markets due to technological developments, changing labour needs or career transformation (geographical or cross-sectoral mobility, interruptions and resumes of professional activity), the missions and modes of operation of public employment services have changed. given the commitment of the member states to better coordinate their economic and employment policies within the union, all available means should be mobilised to support this transformation by the union. the european commission's initiative to officialise the already existing network of representatives of these national public employment services so that they can compare, on the basis of precise data, the effectiveness of the measures they have to implement in the labour market in their respective member states is to be welcomed. this cooperation can be enhanced by: including in the objectives a particular focus on combating youth unemployment, promoting sustainable jobs and combating social dumping; involving social partners and national labour administrations and respecting the organisation of competences in the various member states.
in writing. - the high level of unemployment is one of the most important challenges facing european society. there are currently 26 million unemployed in europe, of whom over five million are young people. the adoption of the decision on strengthening cooperation between public employment services (spofm) sends a strong signal that the european union is using all its instruments to counter the effects of unemployment. the decision will improve the functioning of public services in the european union and strengthen the coordination of employment policies at european level. the modernisation of the spofm will also contribute to the development of innovative measures in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. this will facilitate the implementation of labour market projects funded by the european social fund. however, in order to bring the joint work of public employment services as close as possible to the reality of the labour market, it is necessary that authorities at local, regional and national level be involved in the work of the spofm network.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on enhanced cooperation between public employment services (pepes) adopting the ep's position at first reading. a network of fmcss (the 'network') is hereby established at union level for the period from the date of entry into force of this decision to 31 december 2020. the network shall be composed of spofm designated by the member states and the commission. member states with autonomous sub-national mapps shall ensure that they are adequately represented in the specific initiatives of the network. the objective of this decision is to encourage cooperation through the network between member states in the field of employment, in the areas falling under the responsibility of the spofm, in order to contribute to the europe 2020 strategy and the implementation of relevant union policies, thus providing support, inter alia, to: • the most vulnerable social groups, facing high unemployment rates, in particular older workers and young people who are not in a professional capacity and are not following any education or training programme; • decent and sustainable working conditions; • better functioning of eu labour markets.
in writing. - the european union solidarity fund is the clear expression of solidarity with citizens in eu regions affected by disasters. the amendment of the eu solidarity fund regulation creates the necessary conditions for simplifying the rules in force so that aid can be paid more quickly than at present. the union's action must be directed to the benefit of its citizens by improving its response capacity, in particular in the event of disasters having direct consequences for people. i therefore welcome the introduction of the rapid advance payment system, at the request of the member state concerned. this facility will allow local and regional authorities in affected european states to access the fund immediately after natural disasters have occurred. as a member of the committee on regional development, i strongly support the introduction of clearer rules on eligibility in the event of regional disasters. these will simplify the current rules, while helping to speed up the decision-making process and the payment of aid. congratulations to my colleague, mrs. ferragut, on her work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 2012/2002 establishing the european union solidarity fund. under the regulation adopted at first reading, at the request of a member state or a state which is in negotiations with a view to accession to the union, hereinafter referred to as 'eligible state', aid from the fund may be mobilised where, in one or more regions of that eligible state, serious repercussions on living conditions, the natural environment or the economy arise as a result of a major or regional natural disaster that has occurred in the territory of that eligible state or of a neighbouring eligible state. direct damage caused as a direct consequence of a natural disaster shall be considered as part of the damage caused by that natural disaster. for the purposes of this regulation, a 'major natural disaster' means any natural disaster which causes direct damage in an eligible state estimated at either more than eur 3[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]000 in 2011 prices or more than 0,6[nbsp ]% of the gni of that state. the fund may also be mobilised for any natural disaster in an eligible state which is also a major natural disaster in a neighbouring eligible state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the european union's participation in the capital increase of the european investment fund (eif). under decision 94/375/ec, the eif was set up in 1994 to 'promote sustainable and balanced development within the community'. following an increase in the eif's subscribed capital in 2007, the authorised capital of the eif amounts to eur 3 billion, divided into 3 000 shares of eur 1 million each, with a paid-up capital ratio of 20%. the union, represented by the commission, participated in the previous increase of the fund's subscribed capital in accordance with decision 2007/247/ec. the decision adopted aims to increase the support from the eif to certain actions which complement the actions undertaken by the member states in favour of enterprises, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises. in addition to its current participation in the capital of the eif, the union shall subscribe for up to 450 shares, each with a nominal value of eur 1 million. the subscription of shares and the annual payments shall be made in accordance with the terms and conditions to be approved by the eif general assembly. the union shall purchase new shares in the fund over a period of four years starting in 2014.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on fees payable to the european medicines agency for the performance of pharmacovigilance activities in respect of medicinal products for human use. the revenue of the european medicines agency shall consist of a contribution from the union and fees paid by undertakings for obtaining and maintaining union marketing authorisations. this regulation shall apply to fees for pharmacovigilance activities concerning medicinal products for human use authorised in the union pursuant to regulation (ec) no 726/2004 and directive 2001/83/ec and which are levied by the european medicines agency on marketing authorisation holders. this regulation also lays down the union-wide pharmacovigilance activities for which fees are due to the agency, the amounts and modalities of payment of those fees, and the levels of remuneration paid by the agency to rapporteurs and, where appropriate, co-rapporteurs for the services provided. micro-enterprises shall be exempt from any levy provided for under this regulation. the fees provided for in this regulation should be transparent, fair and proportionate to the activities carried out. information on those fees should also be public.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the decision to grant macro-financial assistance to the republic of tunisia. eu-tunisia relations are developing within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy (enp). under the eu-tunisia association agreement, which entered into force on 1 march 1998, tunisia completed the elimination of tariffs on industrial products in 2008, becoming the first south mediterranean country to enter a free trade area with the union. bilateral political dialogue and economic cooperation have also continued to develop through the enp action plans, the most recent under discussion covering the period 2013-2017. the union shall make available to tunisia macro-financial assistance of up to eur 300 million to support tunisia's economic stabilisation and reforms. the assistance shall contribute to meeting tunisia's balance of payments needs as identified in the imf programme. the union's macro-financial assistance shall be provided in full to tunisia in the form of loans with a maximum maturity of 15 years. the union's macro-financial assistance shall be provided for a period of two and a half years. a precondition for macro-financial assistance is that tunisia respects genuine democratic mechanisms, including a multi-party parliamentary system and the rule of law, and guarantees respect for human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 302/2009 on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. the amendment of regulation (ec) no 302/2009 is necessary in order to implement the recommendation of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat 12-03) in union law in order to ensure the effective conservation of bluefin tuna stocks, to provide legal certainty as regards the fishing seasons concerned and to allow member states to properly define their fishing, capacity and inspection plans and to fulfil their reporting obligations. it is also important to implement in union law iccat recommendation 13-08 on the use of stereoscopic camera systems in the context of caging operations and on the possible establishment of a different start date of the fishing season for purse seiners and trawlers and for trawlers in the eastern atlantic ocean.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro and other currencies against counterfeiting by means of criminal law measures and replacing council framework decision 2000/383/jha. since the introduction of the euro in 2002, counterfeiting of the euro as a currency that is constantly under the spotlight of organised crime groups active in the field of counterfeiting money has generated financial losses of at least eur 500 million. it is in the interest of the union as a whole to oppose and to criminalise any activity that has the potential to jeopardise the authenticity of the euro coin by counterfeiting. the directive adopted at first reading lays down minimum rules on the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in the field of counterfeiting the euro and other currencies. the directive also introduces common provisions to strengthen the fight against and the investigation of such offences and to ensure better cooperation against counterfeiting.
in writing. - i voted against the report on the proposal for a directive amending council directive 2001/110/ec on honey. the commission proposal amends the honey directive to clarify that pollen is a natural constituent and not an ingredient and to align the directive with the provisions of article 190 of the lisbon treaty on delegated acts. the s&d group considers that the definition of pollen as a natural component allows the application of the provisions of the gmo regulation to honey to be avoided, to the detriment of beekeepers and consumers, who need to have accurate and complete information about the products they buy or consume. the rapporteur entered into negotiations with the council on the basis of a commission proposal and the agreement reached provides that pollen is a natural component of honey. aware of the cost of additional labelling, the s&d group proposed a compromise amendment which proposes the obligation of additional labelling only for genetically modified pollen. thus, only pollen from areas where gmo contamination is possible would require the necessary testing and labelling. i believe that every consumer has the right to know whether the honey they buy contains genetically modified organisms.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amended proposal for a regulation on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). this regulation lays down the union financial measures necessary for the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp); the relevant measures relating to the law of the sea; the sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture and inland fisheries; and the integrated maritime policy (imp). this regulation shall apply to operations carried out within the union. the emff shall contribute to the following objectives: to promote competitive fisheries and aquaculture, to encourage the implementation of the cfp; to promote territorial development conducive to the inclusion and balanced development of fisheries and aquaculture areas; to encourage the development and implementation of union mff in a manner complementary to cohesion policy and the cfp. the resources available for commitments from the emff for the period 2014-2020 under shared management shall be eur 5 749 331 600 in current prices. the european maritime and fisheries fund shall contribute to the europe 2020 strategy and to the implementation of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending decision 2005/681/jha establishing the european police college (cepol). pursuant to article 4 of council decision 2005/681/jha, cepol is to have its seat in bramshill, united kingdom. the united kingdom informed cepol that it had unilaterally decided that it no longer wished to host its headquarters on its territory. in view of the obligations of sincere cooperation under the treaty on european union (teu), and in particular the obligations arising from article 4 teu, the union and its member states should provide each other with mutual assistance for the maintenance of cepol's operational activities. to this end, the united kingdom is in particular requested to ensure a smooth transition of cepol to the new location without jeopardising cepol's regular budget. cepol shall have its seat in budapest, hungary.
mr president, throughout this mandate we have frequently addressed various violations of religious freedom and defended religious communities in many countries, especially in our emergency resolutions, which we debate every thursday afternoon. many times, we have had to condemn acts of violence against religious communities, whether it was christians, muslims, jews, buddhists or the baha'i community. members of these communities have been denied fundamental rights simply because they are members of religious communities. we also condemned attempts to close or destroy places of worship in many countries. in this very last session we will discuss, at my suggestion, the persecution of christians in pakistan because of the blasphemy laws. beyond these one-off reactions, however, it is very important to have a coherent strategy of action at european union level to deal with the proliferation of intolerance. that is why i think my colleague marietta giannakou's report is very timely. our reflection on the construction of the union's foreign policy in a world of cultural and religious differences has proved to be a very sensitive issue, which has divided the members of the committee on foreign affairs to a great extent. i believe, however, that the text to be put to the vote will allow us to come together around some fundamental ideas and very clear principles of action. i fully agree with my colleague, giannakou, that cultural and religious differences have been far too often used globally as a pretext for gross human rights violations. they are increasingly a source of polarization, conflict and extremist violence. just look at what is happening right now in nigeria - the bloody bombing in abuja on monday has again claimed many lives. these are in addition to the more than 1[nbsp ]500 people who have lost their lives since the beginning of this year alone as a result of boko haram violence. it's something we can't obviously accept. in our strategy we must be consistent and determined, we must systematically underline that intolerant interpretations of any religion, which allow violence and repression of those of other faiths, are not compatible with the values of the union and with the universalism of human rights.

mr president, this draft european regulation responds to a real requirement, both of the economy and of the financial market, namely the formation of long-term european investment funds. in europe, banks, which dominate financial markets, are reluctant to engage in long-term investment financing because they mobilise credit resources, usually for the short term. we need such investment funds that allow the mobilisation of resources not only from professional investors but also from small investors who, as a rule, invest their savings, and for these small investors to have the confidence to put their savings in such european investment funds in the long term, they need to have the faith that these funds are managed correctly, apply prudential rules, both in terms of the distribution of the investment portfolio and in terms of how the rules on the avoidance of conflicts of interest are respected. the report contains such prudential rules and i consider it a very good step forward, so i will vote for this report.
