in writing. - i voted in favour of the council decision on the eu-albania: protocol to the stabilisation and association agreement (accession of croatia). the council decision authorises the commission to open negotiations with albania, on behalf of the european union, its member states and the republic of croatia, with a view to concluding a protocol to the stabilisation and association agreement with the republic of albania to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu. the eu-albania stabilisation and association agreement was signed in luxembourg in june 2006 and entered into force in april 2009. in accordance with article 36 (3) of the stabilisation and association agreement, this act ensures that the mutual interests of the european union and albania are respected. the signature and conclusion of the protocol shall be subject to a separate procedure as regards matters falling within the competence of the european atomic energy community.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council decision on the agreement with the kingdom of norway on the modalities of its participation in the european asylum support office. the council decision refers to article 49 of regulation (eu) no 439/2010, which provides that, in order to fulfil its mission, the european asylum support office should be open to the participation of countries which have concluded agreements with the eu under which they have adopted and apply eu law in the field covered by this regulation, in particular iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland, hereinafter referred to as 'the associated countries'. norway has concluded agreements with the eu under which it has adopted and applies eu law in the field covered by this regulation, in particular the agreement between the european community and the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway concerning the criteria and mechanisms for establishing the state responsible for examining a request for asylum lodged in a member state or in iceland or norway. norway will participate fully in the activities of the support office and benefit from support actions by the support office. under this agreement, norway will be present in the support office's management board as an observer without voting rights. norway shall contribute to the support office's revenue by an annual amount calculated on the basis of its gross domestic product (gdp).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council decision on the agreement with the principality of liechtenstein on the modalities of its participation in the european asylum support office. the council decision refers to article 49 (1) of regulation (eu) no 439/2010, which provides that, in order to fulfil its mission, the european asylum support office should be open to the participation of countries which have concluded agreements with the eu under which they have adopted and apply eu law in the field covered by this regulation, in particular iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland, hereinafter referred to as 'the associated countries'. liechtenstein has concluded agreements with the eu under which it has adopted and applies eu law in the field covered by this regulation. the principality of liechtenstein will participate fully in the activities of the support office and benefit from its support actions. under this agreement, liechtenstein will be present in the support office's management board as an observer without the right to vote. liechtenstein shall contribute to the support office's revenue by an annual amount calculated on the basis of its gross domestic product (gdp).
in writing. - under the europe 2020 strategy for better competitiveness and employment, long-term financing is an important tool used to put the european economy on a path to steady and sustainable growth. the need has therefore arisen to adopt uniform rules at union level for european long-term funds in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and a high level of investor protection. i agree that complementing bank financing with a wider variety of financing sources that better mobilise capital markets could help to address financing gaps.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds. european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing to a diverse range of infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or long-listed small and medium-sized enterprises that issue equity and debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. by providing funding for such projects, the efsi contributes to the financing of the real economy and the implementation of union policies. as regards demand, eltifs can provide a steady and secure stream of income to pension administrators, insurance companies, foundations, municipalities and other entities facing regular and repeated obligations and pursuing long-term cash flows within well-regulated structures. the regulation adopted at first reading provides for uniform rules on the authorisation, investment policies and operating conditions of eu alternative investment funds (aifs) marketed in the union as european long-term investment funds (eltifs).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the estimates of revenue and expenditure of the european parliament for the financial year 2015. the 2015 budgetary procedure will take place in an electoral year at european level, in which the parliament's estimate for the financial year 2015 will be adopted by the current parliament and the final budget will be approved by the new parliament in the autumn. the ceiling for heading v (administration), established by the new multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020, shall be eur 9 076 million for the 2015 budget. the ceiling for the institutions' overall administrative expenditure was set at eur 7 351 million. the secretary-general proposed to continue and further strengthen the four areas of work adopted after consultation of the joint bureau working group and the committee on budgets in 2014, namely strengthening independent scientific advice and control capacity, and improving logistical and local support for members. the ep approved the draft estimate of the 2015 budget at eur 1 794 929 112, corresponding to an overall growth rate of 1.8% compared to the 2014 budget, and agrees to include in it the 0.4% extraordinary compulsory expenditure resulting from the new agreement on the adjustment coefficient for remuneration and pensions.
in writing. - the enforcement of the treaty on the functioning of the european union's provisions on competition at public level is also carried out by national authorities. this directive reaffirms the union acquis on the right to compensation for damage caused by infringements of competition law, in particular as regards capacity and the definition of damage. in order to remedy some of the difficulties in quantifying the damage caused by the breach of antitrust rules, national courts should have the power to establish the existence and estimate the amount of the damage taking into account the evidence submitted by the parties.
in writing. - the damage caused by anti-competitive practices can be huge, amounting to billions of euros each year. an impact study commissioned by the european commission in 2004 showed that the direct costs to consumers and other affected persons range from around €13 billion to over €37 billion annually. the study also found that the enforcement of competition rules through compensation actions is poorly developed in europe and that victims face substantial obstacles when seeking to obtain damages in court for infringements of these rules. the fines imposed by the european commission or national competition authorities do not go back to the injured party, as they have only a sanctioning and preventive purpose, not a remedial function. i support the introduction of a procedure at union level to facilitate the effective implementation of this type of action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on certain rules governing actions for damages under national law for infringements of the competition law of the member states and of the european union which adopts the ep's position at first reading. this directive lays down certain rules necessary to ensure that any person who has suffered damage caused by an infringement of competition law by an undertaking or association of undertakings can effectively exercise his right to claim full compensation from that undertaking or association of undertakings for that damage. it also provides for rules which promote undistorted competition in the internal market and remove obstacles to its proper functioning by ensuring equivalent protection throughout the union for any person who has suffered such damage. the adopted directive also lays down rules for coordinating the enforcement of competition rules by competition authorities and the enforcement of those rules through actions for damages brought before national courts.
in writing. - i voted for the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1013/2006 on shipments of waste. in order to protect the environment, regulation (ec) no 1013/2006 lays down requirements for shipments of waste both within the union and between member states and third countries. divergences and shortcomings have been identified in the enforcement of the regulation and in the controls carried out by the authorities involved in the controls in the member states. therefore, appropriate planning of waste shipment controls is needed to determine the capacities required to carry out such controls and to effectively prevent illegal shipments. control plans should also be established for the controls carried out in accordance with those provisions. illegal shipments of waste frequently originate from uncontrolled collection, sorting and storage facilities. the systematic checks of shipments of waste should therefore help to identify and address those uncontrolled activities, thereby promoting the implementation of regulation (ec) no 1013/2006. in order to allow member states sufficient preparation time, it is appropriate that the first control plans are adopted by 1 january 2017.
in writing. - i voted for the proposed new psychoactive substance regulation. the increasing number of new psychoactive substances available on the internal market, their increasing diversity, the speed with which they appear on the market, the various risks they may present when consumed by humans, all call for the capacity of public authorities to provide effective solutions to protect public health and safety without obstructing the functioning of the internal market. given the different conditions and circumstances in the member states with regard to psychoactive substances, restrictive measures vary accordingly from one member state to another, which means that economic operators using new psychoactive substances in the production of different products have to fulfil, for the same substance of this kind, different requirements, such as pre-export notification, export authorisation or import and export licences. this regulation should provide for the necessary exceptions to ensure the protection of human and animal health, to facilitate scientific research and development and to allow the use of new psychoactive substances in industry, provided that they are not liable to cause adverse effects and cannot be misused or recovered.
in writing. - i voted for the amendment of council framework decision 2004/757/jha laying down minimum provisions on the constituent elements of criminal offences and penalties applicable in the field of illicit drug trafficking, as regards the definition of the term 'drug'. this directive respects the fundamental rights and observes the principles recognised by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and in particular the right to an effective remedy and to a fair trial, the presumption of innocence and the rights of the defence, the right not to be tried or convicted twice for the same criminal offence, the principles of legality and proportionality of criminal offences, the right to access to preventive healthcare and the right to medical treatment. for the purposes of this directive, 'drugs' means any of the following substances: (a) any of the substances covered by the 1961 united nations single convention on narcotic drugs and the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances; (b) any of the substances listed in the annex; (c) any mixture or solution containing one or more of the substances in points (a) and (b); the establishment of minimum common rules on the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in the field of drug trafficking should ultimately contribute to the protection of public health and the reduction of the harmful effects of drug trafficking and drug use.
in writing. - i voted for the council decision on the negotiation of the eu-japan strategic partnership agreement. japan has been a strategic partner of the eu since 2003 and the two share a special responsibility for promoting peace, stability and prosperity in a rapidly changing world. the eu and japan already cooperate in a number of areas, such as science and technology, internet security, academic and research cooperation, peaceful uses of nuclear energy, business community contacts and the promotion of direct people-to-people links. we call on the council, the commission and the european external action service to include a broad framework of cooperation in science, technology, business and research to increase the potential for innovation and to cooperate in finding innovative solutions to transport issues. we also call for the promotion of bilateral cultural and academic exchanges, as well as exchanges between young people, direct exchanges between people and sports.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the eu's foreign policy in a world of cultural and religious differences. the eu is founded on the principles of human rights, the rule of law and democracy, principles enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and has the will and the legal and moral obligation to promote and defend these values in its external relations with all other countries. i voted for paragraph 7 which calls on the institutions and member states to maintain and strengthen their commitment and political will to try to abolish the death penalty worldwide. the eu must promote respect for freedom of expression, freedom of religion or belief, freedom of the press and freedom of access to the media and new information technologies in its external actions, and actively protect and promote digital freedoms. we also call for a consistent eu human rights policy based on common fundamental standards and a constructive, results-oriented approach.
we must firmly and unanimously condemn the aggression of one state against the territorial integrity of another state. that's why we created the united nations after world war ii and a dense network of international organizations to help resolve disputes between states. the events of the last few weeks have disregarded these very principles. on the margins of the international crisis, many are asking whether europe and the united states could have acted differently when maidan protesters took to the streets to demand a radical change in social conditions. if the west hadn't been silent when one of the first acts of the new power was to suspend the language law. i am convinced that the new ukraine needs an example from the european union first and foremost. it must be seen that in europe it is unthinkable that citizens who speak a language other than the majority should be discriminated against in various areas of life. that in the union, by means of an exemplary minority policy, harmonious relations can be established with all national communities. i don't know if ukraine has received these signals from us, but i am quite sure that we still have a lot of work to do in terms of setting an example.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the joint resolution on the pressure exerted by russia on the eastern partnership countries and in particular on the destabilisation of eastern ukraine. i voted for paragraph 9 which underlines the urgent need for russia to engage in constructive dialogue with the current legitimate government of ukraine and by which parliament supports the eu's active involvement in diplomatic efforts to escalate the crisis. i voted for paragraph 23 where parliament encourages ukraine to continue its current political reform efforts, especially with regard to constitutional reform, which should be the subject of broad and deep discussions among all elements of ukrainian society. we welcome the willingness of the government of ukraine to implement its commitments to ensure the representativeness of government structures reflecting regional diversity, to ensure full protection of the rights of persons belonging to national minorities, to align national anti-discrimination legislation with eu standards, to investigate all human rights violations and acts of violence and to combat extremism. i also voted for paragraphs 29, 31 and 32. i voted for amendment no 2 by which parliament recalls that the so-called 'referendum' which took place in the autonomous territorial unit of gagauzia did not respect the constitution of the republic of moldova and was therefore illegal.
in writing. - i voted for the council decision on the eu-vietnam free trade agreement. the commission's mandate for the eu-vietnam fta negotiations is attached to the council's authorisation of 23 april 2007 to open negotiations for an fta with the association of southeast asian nations (asean) countries and follows the approval by the council of a preparatory document setting out the common objectives of both sides of the negotiations, namely the intensification of existing bilateral trade relations. the initial objective was to negotiate an fta with the asean region. over the past 10 years, the eu has maintained a negative trade balance with vietnam, reflected again by the second quarter 2013 figures indicating a total trade volume of eur 13,4 billion. this represents a sharp decrease from the total trade volume in 2012 of eur 23,871 billion, of which eur 18,52 billion in imports from vietnam to the eu and eur 5,351 billion in exports to vietnam from the eu. we call for the establishment of a transparent and effective interstate dispute settlement mechanism and, where appropriate, the inclusion in the free trade agreement of applicable provisions on investor-state dispute settlement to ensure adequate protection of investments and to discourage investors from entering into fanciful claims.
in writing. - since increasing the competitiveness of smes is a horizontal effort, which intersects different policy areas, and taking into account that almost a third of the administrative burden of eu legislation results mainly from disproportionate and inefficient implementation at national level, i believe that it should be considered that these enterprises can create jobs if the appropriate conditions are met, such as access to a skilled workforce and minimisation of administrative burdens.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the measures adopted by the commission following the consultation of the 'top 10' of smes on european regulations. 20.7 million smes account for over 65% of the private sector workforce and smes are among the most innovative enterprises, leading the way in terms of job creation and growth. i voted for amendment no 16, which stresses that simplification of eu regulations should be done in a way that fully respects eu requirements on health and safety at work, the rights of eu workers, and the principles and objectives of eu legislation on the environment, health and consumer protection. i voted against paragraph 21 which argues that in order to reduce the burden of employment legislation, the working time directive should be fundamentally revised, as it is inflexible for micro-enterprises and smes. i also voted against paragraph 22 which recommends that, in order to reduce the burden of health and safety legislation, companies with reduced risk should not be required to carry out written health and safety assessments.
author. - mr president, it is difficult to summarize in two minutes the absolute horror of the human rights situation in north korea. i shall therefore be content to mention a few facts which are more than eloquent. i would first recall that the pyongyang regime runs at least four large concentration camps containing between 80 000 and 120 000 political prisoners. in addition to these, the usual prisons and other forms of short-term detention, so that the total number of north korean political prisoners is estimated to be between 150[nbsp ]000 and 200[nbsp ]000. the united nations commission of inquiry likened the daily horrors of these gulag camps to the atrocities of the totalitarian camps in the second half of the last century. between 2005 and 2012 alone, 510 public executions could be documented, but the real numbers are likely to be much higher. we all remember, on the other hand, the famines that occurred in the 1990s, which caused between 200,000 and 3,000,000 deaths. starvation is systematic, and today, the north korean terror state has arrogated to itself the right to distinguish between citizens who can be kept alive and those who can be dispensed with. more than 200,000 people were abducted from neighboring countries, mainly japan and south korea. forced abortion and infanticide are common practices that target, in the vast majority of cases, north korean women who are forcibly repatriated from china. this is, unfortunately, the picture of north korea today.

president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank all the members who have spoken. the debate was certainly an important and welcome debate because we need to inform. we need measures that have been taken and also inform about the operations during the whole period of the dismantling process. so from this point of view, it is certainly good that there is this debate, it is good that there is this dialogue between the presidency, representing the high representative, and parliament. there were specific points which merited a more specific answer. first of all, i confirm that this is an operation that is taking place under a un resolution and under the supervision of the un. secondly, why could these operations not be carried out in syria? because because of the conflict, because of the insecurity situation, it was absolutely impossible to take such an important initiative in the midst of the syrian conflict. why hydrolysis at sea, as mr pedicini asked, i think, also invoking history - recent history i would not invoke, because it could lead to different results from those to which you referred. because there was no way to do it on land. there was no fact that this operation is now under way should be widely appreciated, because at the time international, european and italian public opinion was calling on all governments to intervene precisely to prevent the terrible suffering of the syrian people from being compounded by the unacceptable and odious use of chemical weapons. and this is the operation that is responding to that demand of the citizens, to that demand of public opinion. it has been said that hydrolysis is experimental. it has been used, according to the information i have been given, in the united states for many years for the destruction of their chemical weapons stockpiles. as regards the question of chemical weapons, the material involved will be stored on the cape ray ship and, as one of the honourable members has also mentioned, will be transported to germany and finland to be burned. so there will be no sea or air missions during this operation. in reply to mr grammatikakis and mr pedicini, i would also like to say that all the necessary measures have been taken by the cape ray staff, who have been trained to deal with any problems that may arise during this process. the last point was about hypocrisy in what i said about the european union. but it is not hypocrisy. mr sakorafa is no longer here, but i will answer you anyway. the european union is simply not a party to the chemical weapons convention, it is not a member, it is not even an observer member, and therefore the european union as such does not participate in the executive council which takes the decisions of this organization. as i said, 28 european countries are participating, which are also member states of the european union. in conclusion, madam president, we are convinced that the programme for the destruction of syrian chemical weapons has been a success and must continue because it is a very important commitment that the international community has made and must continue to make, and it is also essential to prevent the reuse of these illegal weapons against the syrian people, to which we must not add any more suffering to that which they are already suffering. we have received, as i said, specific information, which i have shared with you in this debate, as to why this operation is being carried out on the american ship and also how it is being carried out. i can confirm to mr salini in conclusion the peacekeeping nature of this operation. i have no doubt that this operation is a contribution to peace, which has been preceded and which will be followed by many other contributions, because we are talking about a situation in which a real humanitarian tragedy is taking place. madam president, i thank all members again for their contribution to this debate.

in writing. - youth unemployment is a major issue that should be of growing concern to every eu member state, given that almost a quarter of young europeans are currently out of work. i voted in favour of the resolution on combating youth unemployment because i am aware of the need to create new jobs, the need to bring together the requirements of employers and the knowledge acquired in school by young people, and to stimulate job-creating investment and entrepreneurship among young people. all of this is an investment in a competitive and prosperous european future to which we can successfully contribute. in concrete terms, there are instruments at european level to prevent and reduce youth unemployment. we need a european framework to encourage temporary employment that could help young people to enter the labour market. increased youth mobility should be extended to programmes targeting unskilled labour. i am convinced that programmes such as the young farmer facility or erasmus for young entrepreneurs can play a multi-faceted role. at the same time, they contribute to employment growth, improve performance and support free enterprise.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution on youth employment because young people, especially those under 25, are the most affected by the effects of the crisis, but they are also the most confident in the european ideal. more than 5 000 young people gathered in strasbourg in may to put their ideas together in a document entitled 'ideas for a better europe'. i am glad that i was able to encourage and support 50 hungarian young people from transylvania to participate in the eye 2014 and in the preparation of this document. they are sounding the alarm that they are a "stopped generation" not only because of the crisis but also because of the huge gap between the educational supply and the demand in the labor market. i believe that the most important priority for the next five years is to find ways to help the millions of young unemployed people to find a job, but also to support the education systems in the member states to match reality. convinced that only by working for young people, you are really working for the future of your community, i collaborate with the hungarian youth organization in transylvania - miért and yepp - the youth organization of the epp, and support their initiatives.

in writing. - i join my colleagues in expressing our full support to the work of the international criminal court and to the promotion of peace through criminal justice. the definition of the crime of aggression as stated during the kampala conference in 2010 reflects a compromise made by many states with the aim to ensure a high efficiency of the icc in cases when armed force is used by one state against another state, without the justification of self-defence or without authorization by the security council. these cases are the current reality if we look at the horrific violence in ukraine or moldova. i encourage all the member states to align their national criminal legislation with the kampala amendments' definitions in order to achieve the goal of having the dispositions on the crime of aggression entered into force and in order to have the possibility to hold account the responsible persons. i further urge all nations to put aside political or commercial interests and ratify and implement the amendments. it is thus critical to make every effort possible to ensure that we have the legal framework to condemn such deplorable cases.

commissioner, congratulations on the way you have handled the difficult issue with russia, but i would like to raise the question of the real impact of the russian embargo on food products from the european union and in this context, the question of compensation and how it will be calculated and paid must obviously be discussed. not only was the inability to deliver these goods to russia a loss, but also a large number of orders were cancelled on the intra-community market. in effect, the european foodstuffs rejected by russia and left in europe saturated the internal markets and made it impossible to conduct normal trade as had been the case in previous years. for example, a romanian producer that traditionally sold on the german market finds this year a market that is oversaturated, as do other european markets. as a result, huge stocks have built up in warehouses, and the goods are spoiled. in fact, romanian producers have lost half of their harvest so far. if other countries lost the russian market, romania lost the markets to which food destined for russia was redirected. we can't think in simplistic terms. we have to accept that all the states lost because the markets were upset. therefore, any aid granted must take into account this aspect of the crisis: the blocking of intra-community agricultural and food trade and not just actual sales to russia. that is why, commissioner, i am asking for a point of view on this matter.

in writing. today in strasbourg, the european parliament voted by a majority to approve the eu-ukraine association agreement, including the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement (dcfta). it was a historic moment, as at the same time the agreement was ratified by the ukrainian parliament. the agreement implies a political association and liberalised trade. the political component brings ukraine one step closer to the eu, while the economic component provides mutual, free market access, substantially integrating the two parties' markets, abolishing import duties and prohibiting other trade restrictions. as a member of the european parliament, on behalf of romania, ukraine's neighbour, i would like to underline the importance of this agreement, which is a clear sign of the eu's solidarity and appreciation for the ukrainian people in their struggle for democracy, for a prosperous future in a country where the principles of democracy are respected. ukraine needs good neighbourly relations with both western and eastern europe. following the vote in the european parliament and in ukraine, the agreement will be applied provisionally, but the exact date will be confirmed by the council. the agreement must be ratified by all 28 member states to enter into force.

in writing. - we voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-ukraine association agreement and welcome the simultaneous ratification of the agreement by the european parliament and the ukrainian parliament in kiev. taking into account the close historical relations between the eu and ukraine, as well as the current political situation, we support the desire to strengthen and extend relations in an ambitious and innovative way through this association agreement. the main object of the agreement is to accelerate political and economic relations between ukraine and the eu, as well as ukraine's gradual access to parts of the eu internal market, including through the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area. the overall objectives of the association are to promote a progressive rapprochement between the two parties on the basis of common values; to intensify political dialogue; to promote, maintain and strengthen peace and stability both regionally and internationally; to create conditions for improved economic and trade relations, with the ultimate objective of ukraine's gradual access to parts of the eu internal market. the agreement will be applied provisionally, but the date will be confirmed by the council. the agreement must be ratified by all 28 member states to enter into force.
the cutting of payment appropriations has become a structural problem, which threatens to create an impossible budgetary situation at the end of this framework programme, if current trends are not corrected. if the commission were to receive the necessary level of payment appropriations for horizon 2020 in the coming years, then the payment appropriations for research and technological development would be eur 7 billion. unfortunately, given the limited budget that the directorates-general for research and development face each year, the estimated budget required for the r & d part will be around 16 billion, nine billion more than normal. in practice, 20% of the budget for horizon 2020 is deferred to the next mff. in order to meet the ceiling in the mff, the commission significantly reduced the budgetary request for 2014 from horizon 2020 and the council introduced further reductions. to cope with this situation, all directorates-general implementing r & d programmes have introduced important measures. the level of project funding has been reduced and in a number of cases project calls and deadlines have been postponed to move more payments to 2015. for 2015, the draft budget has already been reduced to the minimum. the commission would be able to cover the outstanding payment obligations only with the above measures. however, in july the council proposed a further cut to the 2015 budget of a further eur 1 billion for the entire research budget. if this reduction is adopted, the r&d directorates-general will no longer be able to meet their contractual obligations regarding payments on time, and in any event, their future obligations. as already mentioned above, if we continue to push payments for the next few years, the situation will worsen.
europe's main problem is to maintain its global competitiveness. this desire cannot be achieved without the necessary financial resources. a reduction in funding for research and innovation is not just a few cuts, as the council has noted. there are cuts that lead to job losses and a decrease in the role played by the council, but also by the governments represented on the council at the global research level. we have to understand that the decline of these funds will not only affect us now, but for years to come and for generations to come. horizon 2020 is a key project for what we want the european union to look like in 2020. in doing so, researchers and innovation will bypass europe, and our projects, the projects that could have made our continent a leader in innovation, will disappear. it is important that we keep these amounts for this project, but at the same time i ask the commission and the council to make a concrete and transparent assessment of the amounts allocated and the projects financed.

thank you, madam president. the efficient digital single market cannot exist without reliable and high-speed infrastructures. a functioning digital single market needs connected european citizens everywhere in europe, but unfortunately the reality shows that europe has lagged behind in the development of 4g networks. unfortunately, according to the commission's latest high-speed broadband data, only a small proportion of european households have a subscription above 100 mbps. i would remind you that the digital agenda 2020 targets are 30 mbps for all citizens of the european union and that at least 50% of european households have internet connections above 100 mbps by 2020. what can the union do to connect all its citizens, wherever they live, so that we have a true digital society? as regards the ongoing negotiations, i would like to ask the commission what timetable it envisages for the completion of the telecoms package, as the council is still very divided. i would stress that the s&d group will firmly defend the european parliament's first reading position, particularly on roaming, consumer protection and net neutrality. even if member states are very reluctant, increased harmonisation of spectrum, combined with the application of common principles for spectrum rights within the european union, is a key remedy to address the problem of unpredictability in spectrum availability. this would allow for innovative uses of wireless broadband while protecting transmission times and preventing interference. on 5g: what is the current state of 5g development and in particular of the 5g public-private partnership launched by the commission to provide solutions, architectures, technologies, standards for next generation communications infrastructures in the last decade? what can the european union do to avoid 4g errors and delays in europe?
mr president, the completion of the digital single market means more growth and more jobs for the people of europe without putting more debt on the shoulder of the people of europe. therefore, it is high time to address the existing barriers that hinder the development of a digital single market and unleash the potential of our digital products and services. commissioner, you have rightly pointed to the impressive potential gdp increase coming from the digital single market in europe, but the question is: why were nokia and ericsson pioneers of the mobile era which then lost their supremacy to apple and samsung over the past 15 years? twenty-eight national digital markets regulated at national level are a competitive disadvantage and a considerable burden for investors and consumers in europe. we cannot afford fragmented regulation if we want to unleash the potential of our digital products and services. we have to remove the remaining fiscal and legal barriers. we need european regulators, pan-european operators and a truly europe market. we also need an integrated online and mobile payments market. it is also high time to have fast fibre european networks in every household in europe. a slow internet connection is a competitive disadvantage for a company, and we see that especially in rural areas. we should set ambitious targets and respect them. we should aim to connect most european households, even in rural areas, with 100 megabytes of internet connections by 2020. my last point: we should also push forward with the digitalisation of the public sector. supply and demand of public services should meet online. too often it is human interference which is a source of imperfection and even corruption in delivering high-quality public services to the people of europe.
mr president, while i am very pleased to see that the digital single market has been a top priority for the outgoing commission, as it is for president juncker’s new team, we do need an online market flexible enough for businesses to grow and secure enough for citizens to make use of it. cross-border purchases are still rare in europe. standards for electronic signatures and contracts still vary from one member state to another. corporate legislation is far from being harmonised, while the data protection regulation is nowhere near implementation. too many barriers hamper companies’ investment in the use of ict as well as cross-border and internet-based economic activity. we want to encourage innovative entrepreneurship among our youth. we all want to see a digital market where goods and services flow freely among member states, where competition drives knowledge forward and prices down, but that requires a shift in approach from a national market mindset towards a european one. if we want a pan-european digital market, we need investment in infrastructure, and therefore we need to provide the appropriate regulatory framework and stability for electronic communication providers. we should also take a closer look at our competition rules. we know what the hurdles are and what we want to do. we therefore expect the commission to define a concrete action plan with clear policy targets and a viable timetable. we must also understand that the digital single market is not something we politicians are going to build. we must always involve and consult all the relevant stakeholders. i am thankful to the outgoing commission for its work and i very much look forward to working with the new commission to make the digital single market a reality.
in writing. according to a study by the european parliament, the creation of a digital single market would generate €260 billion at european level. this could represent thousands of new jobs both horizontally and vertically, considering that the internet creates five jobs for every two jobs lost. it is important, however, to set out as clearly as possible the priorities for investing european funds in the coming years and actions to make their use more efficient at european level. it should be borne in mind that europe is part of a highly competitive global economy, including in the digital sector, which is also constantly evolving and very fast, and some member states need support to close the infrastructure gap. in this context, one of the keys to the successful unification or completion of the digital single market in the european union is the establishment of strong legislative and administrative safeguards to boost citizens' and business confidence in the digital economy, including through a legal framework for strong data protection, but also increasing the participation rate of small and medium-sized enterprises in e-commerce to 50%.

member of the commission. - madam president, first of all i would like to thank parliament for this very important debate and i also want to thank those who expressed some personal messages about my work and the commission’s work in this area. it is the duty of the commission to inform parliament about every step which is taken in the area of youth employment. i will be brief because of the shortage of time but i would like to respond to some of the key points of today’s discussion. first of all i would like to clarify very clearly that the youth guarantee is a reform. it is about a reform agenda; it is about reforming vocational training; it is about reforming, if necessary, how the public employment services work in various eu member states because it is public action that is needed to help young people who might be looking for a job or who might not even be registered as unemployed in many cases. obviously the purpose is that young people gain skills that are relevant to the labour market and information and experience which will help them in their future careers. let me also clarify that the youth guarantee is not a one-size-fits-all project. it allows for a lot of flexibility – for example integrating measures to boost entrepreneurship; it allows for demand-side measures but also supply-side investment; and it calls for an innovative approach at member state level and also within regions. concerning current trends, i think it is clear – and clear too from the discussion – that recently unemployment, including youth unemployment, has been falling faster outside the euro area than inside the euro area. that just highlights how important the macroeconomic background is in making progress. nevertheless in those countries where there has been progress in reducing the youth unemployment rate, i would like to underline three important criteria which also need to be observed at the same time. one of them is the quality of the new jobs and the new employment. the second one is outreach to their needs because it is not enough just to reduce the number of registered unemployed; the youth guarantee is also about reaching out to those who are not in education, employment or educational training. and the third, to monitor something very important in our scheme – and it is actually uniform – namely the four-month deadline, the actual guarantee that young people can count on this safety net. another observation concerning current trends is that there is indeed no conflict between labour mobility and reducing youth unemployment. countries that have either been performing well or making progress in the recent period, like germany or the united kingdom, have experienced a relatively significant inward mobility but, at the same time, falling or low unemployment. why? because they have been on the better side of the eu in terms of economic growth and this has allowed new jobs to be created in this period. so the contradiction or the trade-off which some people assume to exist cannot be observed in reality. fourthly, regarding money: more money is of course always better than less money but the important thing is that we take advantage of the existing budget. the eu budget is not the only source. it was never meant to be the only source for the youth guarantee, especially in countries and regions that are not eligible because their performance has already been relatively better. so it is also important to rely on national resources and combine the european social fund plus the top-up fund – the famous eur 6 billion – in regions where the youth unemployment rate has been extremely high in the past period. it is also important – if members are concerned with the flow of eu funds – to take the lead in council in order to refill the eu budget with the payment credits needed to enable the commission to pay the bills in time under the european social fund and other financial instruments. a very good starting point for this would be to agree on the third amending budget for 2014 and the draft budget for 2015 without any cuts to the commission proposal. we need to reduce the accumulated backlog of payment claims and not to increase it further. finally, my fifth point is about the evaluation. i agree with those who stress the importance of a serious fact-based evaluation of progress – or, in some cases, the lack of it – and this evaluation has to be inclusive. it has to include the social partners, the parliaments – the european parliament as well as the national parliaments – and, most importantly, the youth organisations themselves. this is what i have been doing in my capacity – meeting as much as possible representatives of the youth forum and various youth organisations. this is what we are acknowledging also at member state level.
president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, a few words in conclusion. first of all, thank you for the discussion today. the debate was extremely stimulating, frank and emphasized the urgency of action to tackle one of the most alarming problems facing many member states today. there's just one point i want to say a few words about. the fact that the youth guarantee mechanism has been strongly criticised in some speeches has led to speeches of hypocrisy. we have never claimed that the measures we have discussed today can provide a solution on their own. the youth employment initiative provides the seed capital to stimulate national initiatives and the scope for action at eu level is relatively limited and the initiatives are mainly aimed at coordinating, promoting new initiatives and supporting funding mechanisms. the council provides guidance to the member states and strongly encourages them to take action to tackle the problem of youth unemployment and, on behalf of the council, i can assure you that the italian presidency will do everything possible to help create the conditions for the worrying situation of youth unemployment in europe to be alleviated. let me express my sincere hope that the excellent cooperation we have had on this subject up to now will continue with the new parliament and the new european commission. i am convinced that our joint efforts to combat youth unemployment in europe will soon bear fruit.
in writing. with a youth unemployment rate in the eu of 23.6%, twice the adult rate, and with 7.5 million europeans aged 15-24 not in employment and not in education or training, the €6 billion 'youth jobs' initiative is an excellent tool. unfortunately, there are member states which have not yet approved the programmes submitted by their governments to the commission. these countries include romania. according to a study by the academy of economic studies, in romania, although last year the youth unemployment rate was below the european average, in the first quarter of 2014 this rate reached 25.7%, after a continuous increase in the last three quarters. in this context, and given that the youth employment rate has declined considerably, i ask the european commission to assist member states and to be actively involved in finding solutions for programmes already submitted for approval. i also call on those member states which have not yet started implementing this programme to make efforts to do so.
in writing. sleeping among young people has increased alarmingly recently at european level. statistics show that in most member states unemployment is the main problem facing the population. in fact, today one in four young people are not working, even though they should be the main active workforce. at member state level, there are still very large discrepancies between youth unemployment rates: from almost 8% in germany to over 50% in greece, spain and croatia. a series of common measures at european level is needed to encourage employers to recruit young graduates and unemployed people up to the age of 29. i also propose the establishment of committees to monitor very closely the use of european funds allocated to tackling youth unemployment. there are countries, like romania, where you don't see any results at all. that is why i insist once again that we look very carefully at the problem of youth unemployment, because they are the future of europe and the way the eu will develop depends on them.
in writing. youth unemployment is twice as high as for other categories. today, unemployment is over 23%, compared to 9% in 2012. over 70% of young people in employment have fixed-term or part-time contracts. 13% of young europeans are not registered as unemployed or in some form of education. i come from a country, romania, where the government has done a lot for young people, even being the fourth european country to implement the european youth guarantee. however, i do not think that either the council or the commission understand the gravity of the situation. 6 billion euros for 6 million unemployed under 25 years old is not enough! but what about the 25- to 40-year-olds? i repeat the information in such a way that the gravity of the situation is understood: - 6 million unemployed young people in europe - 6 million young people without a future in europe - 6 million young people who have nothing to live for in europe. these aren't just numbers, we're talking about people!

acting president of the council (on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy). - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the ceasefire of 26 august, which brought to an end 50 days of terrible violence between israel and palestinian groups in the gaza strip, was welcomed by the european union and the entire international community. by ending a cycle of violence which has caused over 2 100 palestinian deaths and 71 israeli deaths, this ceasefire has allowed a much needed humanitarian aid operation to begin which is now facing considerable difficulties. the ceasefire agreement, however, did not guarantee the overcoming of the previous status quo. this is of fundamental importance and the various conclusions adopted by the foreign affairs council and the european council in recent weeks clearly underline this. what is needed is a lasting solution to the gaza question, one that addresses decisively both the problems of the people of gaza and those of israel. a comprehensive political agreement is needed, which will place the question of gaza within the framework of a peaceful and comprehensive solution to the israeli-palestinian conflict. the european union has never had any doubt that gaza should be part of a future palestinian state. efforts are continuing to build on the progress made with the ceasefire agreement of 26 august. on 20 september within the agreed one-month deadline egypt is expected to invite the parties back to cairo for important negotiations on key issues that were left unresolved in august. these include demands on the palestinian side for the opening of a seaport and the reopening of the airport; the european union is also committed to the peace process in the gaza strip. at the same time, the members of the un security council are seeking consensus on the adoption of a resolution establishing an international framework for the normalization of the situation in gaza. there is no denying that there is great uncertainty about the outcome of all these negotiations, but one thing is certain: the eu and its member states spare no effort to try to achieve a satisfactory outcome for all parties concerned. the eu is also mobilising to make a concrete and substantial contribution to the reconstruction of gaza. of course, the eu's ability to provide concrete assistance is closely linked to the political process i have just described. political stability will be crucial to delivering humanitarian assistance and to continuing to provide stable support. to this end, it will be essential that the palestinian authority re-establishes itself in gaza and regains control of security. the eu missions already on the ground (eubam rafah and eupol copps) could provide a good starting point, provided that the parties reach an appropriate agreement and that the situation in gaza improves from the point of view of conflict and security. the european union calls on israelis and palestinians to choose peace and to resolve the conflict which has opposed them for too many years. it is time for the leaders of both sides to take the courageous decisions necessary to end the spiral of violence and resume negotiations. the european union, with your support, will do everything possible to help achieve this objective.

seven weeks of conflict. i hope that both sides will remain committed to finding a lasting solution and that egypt will continue to play a positive role in the future negotiations on a permanent ceasefire. i deplore, on the other hand, the fact that the recent conflict has again caused loss of life and suffering to the civilian population. my condolences to the victims and their families. it and i adopted amendments to that effect. the issue of reconstruction in gaza is also important. i therefore welcome yesterday's agreement to establish an interim mechanism to speed up, under un to a sustainable and comprehensive solution that enhances the security, well-being and prosperity of palestinians and israelis. we must not lose sight of our common goal of achieving a just and lasting peace in the middle east.

in writing.– i welcome the annual report on human rights and i am proud of the role played by the european parliament as a champion of democracy and human rights. it is encouraging that almost 150 human rights country strategies were adopted and, at a civil society level, more than 530 new eidhr 1 initiatives were launched. it is important that all actors should continue to promote human rights, democracy and the rule of law, and in particular to abolish the death penalty, combat torture, and fight racism and other forms of discrimination. however, the challenge remains for the newly agreed country human rights strategy papers to be fully implemented and to uphold human rights through the eu’s trade, investment and development actions. we see everyday stories and images of great suffering which lead us to realise that further urgent action is needed. the action plan will help us to ensure continued progress and we should make all the efforts to implement the eu strategic framework on human rights and democracy, with adequate flexibility so as to respond to new challenges as they arise. we should continue to step up our efforts and provide help to peoples in need around the world.
madam president, in the last two years we have discussed bangladesh four times in our emergency resolutions. this shows that there is an interest in the european parliament in developments in this country with which the european union has cooperative relations, especially, as is well known, in the framework of a partnership and development agreement. and the fact that we're interested means that we're looking at both what's happening positively and what's happening negatively. bangladesh, for example, has made significant progress in recent years in achieving the millennium development goals and, most recently, in legislation on the prevention of child marriage. on the other hand, serious concerns remain, as amnesty international's report earlier this month demonstrated, regarding enforced disappearances, the new policy adopted in august on the press, or the persistence of ethnic and religious violence. it is precisely because we are partners with bangladesh that we must ask that country to address seriously and urgently these human rights violations.
member of the commission. - madam president, i welcome the parliament’s resolution on human rights violations in bangladesh. as part of bilateral relations, the european union has consistently engaged with bangladesh to support the consolidation of democracy. it has repeatedly called on all parties to create favourable conditions for transparent, inclusive and credible elections. the eu regretted the fact that such conditions did not materialise in the elections of 5 january of this year. this means that the people of bangladesh were not given the opportunity to express fully their democratic choices. since then we have been closely monitoring developments, which unfortunately remain a cause for concern. we are in a situation where the main opposition party is not represented in parliament, which would help to ensure democratic accountability and meaningful oversight. this leaves the country without proper checks and balances. we are concerned about the situation of human rights and those of minorities and indigenous people. the space for civil society appears to be narrowing. we recognise the strong support of bangladesh for women’s empowerment. however, violence and discrimination against women and child labour still exist and demand further efforts. overall, as the parliament has rightly stressed in its resolution, the situation remains worrying. the eu is closely following key human rights issues, notably allegations of excessive use of force by law enforcement agencies and discrimination against minority groups and indigenous people, including the lack of implementation of the peace accord for the chittagong hill tracts region. we are monitoring the recent policy guidelines on broadcasting. this policy is likely to limit and restrict freedom of speech and have a chilling effect on media freedom. the eu opposes the death penalty as a matter of principle. the eu is also closely following the situation of the rohingya minority in myanmar and bangladesh. we encourage both countries to discuss the issue and to address the humanitarian situation. the eu remains committed to continuing to help the government of bangladesh in the implementation of its national strategy on myanmar refugees and undocumented myanmar nationals, whilst seeking to improve the conditions of operation of humanitarian service providers. after the rana plaza disaster, the eu launched the global sustainability compact to improve working conditions, labour rights, and safety conditions and to foster corporate social responsibility. the signature of the sustainability compact has permitted bangladesh to continue benefiting from the duty-free, quota-free tariff preferences for exports into the european union, which are key to sustaining exports and a major instrument of stability and poverty alleviation. we very much value the commitment of bangladesh to pursuing the implementation of the sustainability compact and we call on the government to make real progress in meeting compact commitments. while progress has been significant, much remains to be done and we must keep up the momentum. human rights and governance dialogue between the european union and bangladesh is in place within the framework of the eu-bangladesh joint commission. the next meeting will take place in the coming month. when preparing for it we will remain in close contact with and give support to civil society partners and human rights defenders in bangladesh. we will continue to work with the european parliament to monitor the situation and encourage the political parties to engage in genuine dialogue to strengthen democratic accountability and to hold transparent, inclusive and credible elections as soon as possible. let me finish by saying that only a genuinely democratic set-up can guarantee the fulfilment of the wishes and aspirations of the people of bangladesh, going along with economic progress and development.

in writing. – in violating ukraineʼs sovereignty, territorial integrity and freedom of choice, the russian federation has embarked on a new chapter of relations with the european union, drifting away from the common path of mutual responsibility for, and shared commitment to, ensuring peace on the european continent. in light of such developments, and thus as a result of the deliberate choice made by the moscow authorities, the eu can no longer maintain its previous stance towards the russian federation and the strategic partnership thereof. however, there can be no peace and stability without an act of responsibility and political maturity on the part of russia. its role remains a necessary factor for de-escalation of the conflict and a political, sustainable, long-term solution. with this assumption in mind, the inclusion of our amendments was a precondition for a yes vote. while condemning strongly russian actions, they emphasised the crucial need to support initiatives on dialogue with moscow, keeping open all available channels of communication. they also reiterated the full reversibility of the current eu position and its readiness to overturn its stand and to re-engage with russia as soon as it contributes genuinely and without ambiguities to a fair and negotiated settlement.

in writing. - i think it's time for the european union to speak with one voice and act in a coordinated way in relation to russia. after half a year of hesitation and ineffective staged sanctions, the ukrainian conflict is about to enter a winter favorable to russia. faced with the specter of a gas crisis in europe and the possible occupation of eastern ukraine, the eu needs to do more than make symbolic gestures. ukraine has already paid a painful blood toll for its european aspiration. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution calling on member states to act together to improve the eu's energy security and its ability to counter asymmetric challenges from russia. more firmness is needed in the face of russia's violation of international borders and norms. the eu can no longer afford to hesitate and take steps, because there is a danger of fuelling the kremlin's aggressiveness towards the former soviet states. in this context, i would like to draw attention to the risk that the eu-ukraine association agreement will remain a mere symbolic gesture if it is not swiftly ratified by the member states of the union and if its entry into force is delayed until the end of 2015.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. i welcome the signing of the minsk ceasefire. it is necessary that this agreement be fully and in good faith implemented in order to lead to a genuine peace process. i support the commitment to ukraine's independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, inviolability of its borders and its european option. significant improvements in energy security, ensuring the eu's independence from external pressure, by strengthening the energy sector, developing energy infrastructure in the eu's neighbouring countries and developing energy interconnections between these eu countries are needed. i believe that the only viable eu response to russian threats is to be united, to send a unified message, to abandon the concept of strategic partnership and to identify a new unified approach.

in writing. - the joint resolution on the situation in ukraine and the current state of eu-russia relations clearly expresses the european parliament's position on the situation created east of the eu border and also refers to maintaining the european perspective for ukraine. in this document, meps strongly condemn the russian federation for waging an undeclared hybrid war against ukraine, using russian regular forces and supporting illegal armed groups. i also voted for the resolution because it reiterates the view that the eu-ukraine association agreement, recently approved by the european and ukrainian parliamentarians, is not the ultimate goal of eu-ukraine relations. the resolution stresses that, in accordance with article 49 of the treaty on european union, ukraine - like any other european state - has a european perspective and can apply to become a member of the european union, provided that it embraces the principles of democracy, respects fundamental freedoms, human and minority rights and ensures the rule of law.
in writing. – the ebola outbreak was officially declared on 22 march 2014 in guinea. it has reached four other countries (liberia, nigeria, sierra leone and senegal), affected almost 4 000 people, caused more than 2 000 deaths, and is the largest recorded outbreak in terms of cases, deaths and geographical coverage. information and communication are important tools in fighting the ebola outbreak and it is essential to facilitate trust and popular cooperation with anti-ebola measures. it is essential that the eu member states have the capacity to mobilise immediate response teams to ensure early diagnosis, monitoring of contact persons and tracing of transmission chains, measures for burials, education and local support. i voted for the eu to support and encourage the african union in regard to the need for a holistic action plan, as the situation is continuing to deteriorate rapidly; and for control systems to be put in place to ensure that the whole of the budget allocated to stopping the ebola outbreak is actually directed at fighting the epidemic in countries affected by the virus. furthermore, the member states and the commission should coordinate and strengthen medical research and the production of effective medicines and vaccines against ebola.
in writing. - i believe that the current crisis following the ebola outbreak cannot be solved by health systems alone, and that a concerted approach involving different sectors such as health, education and training, sanitation and food aid is also needed to address critical deficiencies affecting all essential services.

in writing. - the recent war between israel and palestine has brought significant loss of life and property. but i think we need to put aside the statistics and take concrete action to achieve peace. i think this conflict has no real winner. the recent hostilities have weakened israel's economy. the figures show a decline in consumption, especially in the south of the country, and tourism, which accounts for 7% of gdp, has been hit hard, given the peak mid-summer period. at the same time, hamas claims its so-called victory for the simple fact that it still exists today, considering that the victims and material damage justify its actions. unfortunately, it is the civilian population that suffers most and wants the situation to stabilise. the european union must play a more active role in resolving the israeli-palestinian conflict. i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that we have the capacity to intervene with diplomatic action to restore the necessary balance in the region. i would remind you that funding through the peace iii programme for peace and reconciliation in northern ireland has contributed significantly to creating a stable climate in the region.

in writing. – the recent war between israel and palestinian militants in the gaza strip has been the third of its kind in the past six years, and possibly the most gruelling of all. although it lasted for 50 days, it claimed the lives of more than 2000 palestinian, mostly children, and 70 israelis. in reaction to the 4500 rockets and mortars fired at israel by palestinian militants, the 5226 air strikes carried out by the israeli air force left gaza in ruins and in humanitarian need. the ongoing cycle of violence must be broken. although israel has the legitimate right to defend itself against militant attacks, the death of children and innocents is simply unacceptable. the only way to break this vicious circle is to find a sustainable agreement that will address all the root causes of the conflict. such agreement should restore fundamental freedoms to the people in gaza and at the same time provide security for israel. the eu has a prominent role to play in the resumption of the middle east peace process, with the objective of a two-state solution. i strongly urge the union to take a more active role in the efforts aimed at achieving a just and lasting peace.

member of the commission. - mr president, i will limit myself to addressing some important points which have been made. let me first make it clear: the solidarity fund exists to pay compensation for damage after the fact. under the current legal framework, the solidarity fund cannot be used to prevent something; it can only be used ex-post facto, and even then it has to be activated by an application from the country concerned. as to the question: is it true that different funds have been allocated to different countries? there is no pre-allocation of funds. it depends on the type of disaster; it depends on the type of damage. for instance, one of the conditions is that the damage must exceed 0.6% of the region’s gdp: in the case of liguria, for example, that means damage in excess of eur 660 million. then, assistance is dependent on proof of the damage. there are so many factors which can differ from one country to another that i cannot give a straight answer except by enunciating the main principles. to take italy, for example: so far there has been no application by italy to activate the funds, but once that happens and once it is determined that the damage exceeds 0.6% of the gdp of liguria then, of course, the solidarity fund will pay for part of the damage. i must add, however, that the compromise struck by the european council in february this year has reduced the maximum annual allocation from the solidarity fund from eur 1 billion to eur 500 million: a 50% decrease. so no one can perform miracles – one can only do, perhaps, something approaching the impossible with the funds available. i had a question from ms moi, if i remember rightly, about allegations of irregularities in the use of the funds, and whether the commission checks their use. of course we check their use: there are a number of financial regulations which have to be followed and, more than once, when it has turned out that funds were used for the wrong purpose, or for purposes other than that for which they were allocated, a request has been made for the recovery and collection of those funds. as regards prevention – and i made it clear in my statement how cost effective prevention is – there is no specific fund in the european union just for floods. there are the structural funds, on which all the member states can draw, and particularly those states which are liable to natural disasters. i mention italy, in particular, because italy has experience of volcanic eruptions, mud slides, floods and earthquakes, so it is a country with one of the best-developed civil protection systems. because of the realities on the ground, italy can use the structural funds for purposes of prevention. i would like to finish by saying that funds are important, and government intervention is important, but i was impressed recently by seeing how volunteers – the so-called angeli del fango – also gave their assistance in genoa. we had seen them before: i was still young but i remember them in 1966-1967 at the time of the floods in florence. even then they were called the angeli del fango, which literally translates as ‘the mud angels’. the commission will continue its emphasis on coordinating the efforts of member states for prevention. that is why we have the floods directive which, although it is not a financial instrument in itself, is a legal instrument for coordination and cooperation between member states in response to natural disasters of this kind.
, in writing. floods are natural phenomena with major impacts on people's lives and the environment. human intervention in the environment through urban expansion, agricultural development, but especially through uncontrolled deforestation has considerably changed the situation of watersheds. a complete response to this problem involves, in addition to the flood response mechanism, a medium- and long-term risk prevention management. the strategy in this regard should go beyond coordination actions limited to flood response capacity. structural measures shall focus on the protection and safety of citizens, the environment and essential food sources. there are instruments at member state level that can deliver concrete results. funding programmes such as 'first afforestation' aim to increase the area of forest with a protective role against natural factors. unfortunately, in romania, interest in financing projects under measure 221 was particularly low, with only 26 projects contracted with a value of eur 1,55 million out of a total allocation of eur 230 million. the commission and governments need to do more to develop a coherent eu-wide flood prevention programme.
in writing. according to the world health organization, 4,447 people have died of ebola as of 14 october, making the epidemic a growing threat to global security. although the european centre for disease prevention and control maintains that the risk of transmission of the disease in europe is extremely low, i believe that this crisis should not be underestimated. rapid and coordinated action at european level is needed to limit ebola contamination, and european health systems must be prepared to diagnose and treat ebola if necessary.
madam president, it is obvious that young people have been a victim of the economic crisis of the past years without having caused that crisis, and that is why it falls upon us to look at the problem of youth unemployment and creating employment opportunities for youth as an utmost priority. so what shall we do to improve the situation of youth and bring youth back to the labour market? my first answer is labour market reform. all of those countries which have dared to make labour market reforms, even if difficult, even if unpopular ten years ago, their economies are stronger and more resilient and more competitive now. all of the countries which have postponed labour market reforms are in a more difficult situation. too often youth is the victim of a rigid labour market which protects those who are already employed but takes away the opportunities for young people to enter the labour market. my second answer is that we need to provide a framework in which the private sectors feel confident to invest, through competitiveness, innovation, research, solid public budgets and most notably structural reforms, because it is the private sector which mainly creates the jobs. thirdly, commissioner, i am a supporter of the youth guarantee scheme because i think unemployment levels are so high in europe that every measure which leads to bringing youth unemployment down is good. but we need to improve the youth guarantee scheme. we need to tailor it to member states, because we have it now in practice, and we have been talking about it for one, almost two years but we see that young people in europe are not really finding many more jobs. what i would like to ask you is to make sure that you get the public employment services which are already meeting at european level more involved in tailoring the youth guarantee scheme so that it responds to the needs of the people in various eu member states.
