mr president, as prime minister, the commissioner of course pioneered the youth guarantee at national level in his home country – a successful project which has now also been introduced at european level. this will not solve youth unemployment as a whole, but it clearly helps. there are many good employment and youth unemployment policy ideas at national level which can be applied in other eu member states as well, not necessarily one-to-one – not all of them – but obviously a country in which youth unemployment is 50% or above might want to implement some of the successful measures from countries in which youth unemployment is 10% or below. therefore, i propose to establish a european mechanism for the exchange of best practices for job creation and especially for youth unemployment. parliament’s report on the european semester also contains my proposal to create such a european mechanism. i look forward to working with you, commissioner, in your new capacity as vice-president for jobs, to transpose this into reality. the second point i would like to make is linked to labour mobility. we are, of course, working on making transnational european labour mobility a reality in europe, but labour mobility is also too low within many eu member states. we often see in the same member states unemployment levels of below 5% and employers having a hard time filling vacancies, while in other regions in the same country unemployment is above 30%. therefore, we need also to include this and highlight it in the country-specific recommendations and work together on basically making labour mobility work within member states too.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank honourable members very much for a very valuable debate and ideas. i will just take up a few issues which i would like to comment on briefly. one of the issues which we seem to more or less agree on is the implementation of country-specific recommendations. we can recognise that this has not happened as efficiently as it should have done and there we all must carry our own responsibility. the issues are, of course, in the hands of member states and governments and national parliaments, but we can also encourage them to do what they had promised to do and what is good for the countries themselves as well as for europe as a whole. my second point: mr cofferati and ms gall-pelcz mentioned the internal market and the country-specific recommendations concerning the single-market-related issues. we all know that there are also lots of shortages in this field. for instance, in the implementation of the services directive there are lots of shortages. this is quite amazing because we – the parliament, commission and council – have already decided on the services directive, for instance, and it has not been implemented yet. so we are lacking economic growth because of poor performance in various member states in this field as well, so we need to pay more attention there in the future. the third point is about the structural reforms. mr eickhout said that the commission has historically represented structural reforms that are too one-sided and our idea has been just to use structural reforms as a tool to reform austerity policy. of course, it depends on the country as to what the problems are, but i would just like to raise a few issues and a few examples of non-austerity structural reforms. the first one is tax reform, for instance lowering labour tax and raising environmental tax, or raising dividend tax and at the same time lowering corporate income tax. another issue is pension reform, which is necessary in many countries because the population is ageing – municipality reform, labour reform and things like that. so it is not only about austerity, but a change to society so that it is stronger and more sustainable. the next point is gender equality. many members also raised this issue. i am very happy about this because it is a question both of equality and labour supply. so at the same time as we are reforming our societies to be more sustainable, they can be more growth-oriented. gender equality – the finnish labour party is based on this – is very crucial in this sense. my final point: mr pirinski and mr cofferati mentioned the role of research and development. this is one of the issues on which we have to concentrate more during the next european semester – what we could do in order to strengthen r&d activities in our member states because this is the way to improve the potential growth of the member states. there are good examples in various member states where the universities and small- and medium-sized entrepreneurship have been combined in a very fascinating way and the universities have become a hub of entrepreneurship. so in something like this we could learn from each other, and they could be added to country-specific recommendations.
president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, just two concluding remarks, after thanking all those who have spoken and having found a passionate debate here too, with many common views, although certainly not unanimous. the coming weeks and months are crucial in many respects and we hope to be able to examine soon the first annual growth analysis to be presented by the new commission. we need to review the economic governance provisions in the six-pack and two-pack review. and we must complete the europe 2020 mid-term review to ensure that the strategy and its implementing instruments remain valid and effective. cooperation between all the institutions of these processes will be essential to achieve positive results. as we embark on these revisions at european level, we are well aware that what matters to citizens is the result at national or regional or local level and their need to see improvements in their everyday lives. we have identified the policies that can bring about these improvements and implementing them is our common challenge.
the european semester has become an effective instrument of the european union and the member states for coordinating economic policies. the experience gained in recent years in using this tool is beginning to bear fruit. however, i believe that two problems still visible which affect the effectiveness of the european semester need to be removed. first, in some member states, the draft national reform programmes and those of the convergence or stability programmes are not presented to national parliaments before being sent to the european commission. secondly, the recommendations made to each member state by the european commission and adopted by the council are not transposed into programmes and measures at national level, so as to ensure that identified problems are addressed and trends are corrected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in the sector of redundancies in the manufacturing of metal products in the comunidad valenciana, driven by similar problems in romania, where the metal sector has lost over 200,000 jobs in the last 20 years. some of the combines were privatised, but in most cases they disappeared altogether, being privatised by liquidation. the metal industry has become a jobless industry. and it will remain so for some time to come, as the big combined companies continue to reduce their spending. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question were necessary to restore the viability of the company. i consider that the european globalisation adjustment fund, through the measures provided for and the financial support provided, is an effective instrument for employment in the eu and an indispensable measure for the retraining of redundant employees. through such programmes, the european union is once again demonstrating its support for the workforce.
in writing. - spain submitted application egf/2014/004 es/comunidad valenciana metal for a financial contribution from the egf, following the 633 redundancies that occurred in spain between april and december 2013 in 142 enterprises active in the manufacture of metal products. i would point out that the redundancies in the 142 metal products companies are linked to the global economic and financial crisis. in spain, the production of metal products decreased by 23,3% in 2009 compared to the previous year and by 36,6% between 2008 and 2013, and the number of jobs in the metal products sector decreased by 43%. the processed metal products sector is an important supplier of raw material to a whole range of manufacturing industries, in particular the shipbuilding, construction and automotive sectors, all of which have been considerably affected by the economic crisis in the union. as s&d coordinator for industry, research and energy, i stress the need for a union strategy on european industry. viable solutions are needed for both the steel industry and the metal products sector to maintain competitiveness and jobs in the eu.
in writing. - i have voted for this egf project because as a shadow rapporteur from the s&d group i have contributed to the elaboration of the report and i support the need for an egf contribution. i believe that the european globalization adjustment fund is an excellent instrument capable in offering the support needed by the redundant persons but also in directly creating new jobs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the application egf/2013/012 be/ford genk - belgium. belgium has applied for a financial contribution from the egf following the redundancies of 512 workers, 479 of whom were targeted for participation in the measures in question, at the ford-werke assembly plant in genk and at 10 suppliers of ford genk between july and november 2013. the disposals are linked to major changes in the structure of world trade, as well as to the rapid decline of the eu's share of the global market for passenger car production and the steady decline in sales of new cars in the union. as there were less than 500 redundancies during the reference period, the requirements of the regulation are partially met as regards the minimum number of redundancies. the commission has declared the application for an egf contribution admissible as redundancies have a strong impact on employment and the local economy. in the present case, two other waves of redundancies expected in 2014 (approximately 4 340 redundancies at ford genk and 2 820 redundancies at suppliers in the same geographical area) are taken into account. these will have a strong impact on the entire flemish region, with the loss of 11 000 jobs expected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund: for the application egf/2013/002 be/carsid belgium. belgium has applied for a financial contribution from the egf following the dismissal of 939 workers, of whom 752 were targeted for participation in the measures concerned. the redundancies occurred after the closure of the carsid s.a. production plant in the reference period september 2012 and january 2013. the disposals at carsid are linked to the major structural changes in the world due to globalisation, the rapid decline in the union's global market share in the production of crude steel obtained by continuous casting and the constant decrease in the production of crude cast steel in the union due to the reduced demand for steel in the automotive and construction sectors. the production of continuous casting crude steel in the eu-27 decreased by 13,4% between 2006 and 2011 and the market share of the eu-27 decreased by 30,7% in the same time period. unfortunately, the steel sector in europe is facing serious economic difficulties and as the s&d coordinator for industry, research and energy, i stress the need for investment in this sector to revive steel production in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the request made by france following the 6120 redundancies at peugeot citroën automobiles. the company is active in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers. of the total number of redundancies, 2357 workers are covered by measures co-financed by the egf in the october-january 2014 reference period. between 2000 and 2012 world production of cars increased by 44%, although production in western europe decreased by 25% and, in addition, production in third countries (south korea, china, turkey, indonesia, iran, malaysia, thailand and south america) increased considerably, currently constituting 47% of world production of cars (compared to 15% in 2000). to date, the automotive sector has been the subject of 21 egf assistance requests, 12 of which were based on trade-related aspects of globalisation and 9 on the global economic and financial crisis. as s&d coordinator for industry, research and energy, i stress the need to identify solutions that strengthen the competitiveness of the automotive sector. in view of the significant difficulties faced by the european automotive industry, these solutions need to take into account economic, social and environmental aspects.
in writing. the barroso commission's mandate has been marred by a constitutional, geo-political and financial crisis. the constitutional crisis was resolved by the treaty of lisbon. the geo-political crisis remains to be resolved. an important step has been taken by ratifying the association treaty with ukraine, but the next commission will have to finalise the agreement with moldova. the financial crisis was a difficult time for member states: the barroso commission has proposed several legislative packages to achieve a balance of fiscal responsibility, access to the european single market and initiated a deep structural reform in the countries concerned. a banking union has been created. as a result, the financial sector is equipped to supervise banks. the barroso commission has drawn up a long-term plan for modernising the european economy. multiannual programmes will aim to improve competitiveness by focusing on research, innovation and infrastructure development. it ensured that horizon 2020 was the largest european research programme and was endowed with an eu budget 30% larger than the previous programme. it wants to connect europe in the transport, energy and digital sectors. all these 2020 targets, agreed by the previous commission, will set a framework for competitiveness, sustainability and security in the eu.

mr president, the geopolitical climate at our eastern border is still frozen in limbo and, as the approaching winter becomes the main negotiation tool for our eastern supplier, pragmatism appears to be the word on everyone’s lips. but i beg to differ and this is why. for the completion of the single energy market we need to fill in the missing links in the infrastructure. we need to get smart and we need direct access to the global energy market through multiple entry points. a fully functioning internal energy market connected to the global market is the key to security of supply and to the long-term competitiveness of our industry. the resources we need for infrastructure cannot be covered by public money. we need to attract private investment, making better use of the financial instruments we have put in place. focussing on a co2 emissions reduction target that will keep our air clean is good, but we must also allow member states to decide themselves how they want to streamline their efforts on renewables and energy efficiency because each competitiveness pole in europe needs different policy tuning and a different energy mix. that is why a general emissions reduction target with flexible implementation is the choice to make. keeping our industry competitive and creating a real european market in energy with low prices and numerous supply sources is not a pragmatic choice; it is a choice for growth and this is what should be in our leadersʼ minds at this upcoming summit.

in writing. - the resolution we voted on today represents a financial package of eur 142.1 billion in payments appropriations and eur 145.6 billion in commitments appropriations. although a modest budget, the council took the approach of making further cuts in payments, representing a reduction of -0.18% in comparison to 2014. these cuts were reversed by the ep, which also called on the use of the flexibility mechanism to generate an additional eur 4 billion for the 2015 budget. these funds are essential for investment in programmes such as horizon 2020, erasmus and cosme, which help to promote job creation and growth. but a discussion on the 2015 budget cannot take place without addressing the shortage in payments for 2014. even if the draft amending budgets for 2014 are successfully adopted, we are still facing a roll-over of bills from 2014 into 2015 of eur 18 billion eur. this situation is unacceptable. this resolution, which i voted in favour of, reminds the council that the eu budget is an investment, not a burden. the longer the council takes to address the shortage in payments, the longer it continues to make further cuts to what is already perceived as a limited-size budget, the longer it delays europe’s economic recovery and growth.
in writing. - the 2015 union budget is designed to meet future challenges, to promote initiatives for growth, jobs and investment in the general interest, but not least to strengthen areas of weakness or priority. unfortunately, the proposed reduction in the commitment appropriations of operational funds for producer organisations contributes to widening the development gap. i would remind you that in some member states the level of organisation of producer groups is very low. they also draw attention to the fact that the application of the 'financial discipline' mechanism may create difficulties for farmers with regard to direct payments exceeding eur 2000. the abolition of quotas for milk in april 2015 and for sugar in 2017 will create major imbalances in the internal market. it is therefore necessary to create as a matter of priority a fund for the identification of new markets for distribution in third countries. the commission recently allocated eur 30 million for exploring new markets under temporary emergency aid following the russian embargo. we still need concrete action plans backed by a robust budget to reduce the dairy and sugar surpluses.
in writing. - i believe that additional support is needed to mitigate the impact of the ban imposed by russia on the import of certain agricultural and fishery products from the union and the emergency support measures taken by the european commission as a first response to this crisis.
in writing. - the council's position on the 2015 budget is contrary to the european parliament's resolution of 13 march 2014 and the european council conclusions of june and august 2014. the reduction of payment appropriations from the competitiveness and growth fund is of particular concern, in breach of the council's commitments to act to overcome the crisis and its effects. instead of a strategic investment programme to boost competitiveness and sustainable jobs in key areas such as transport, telecommunications and energy infrastructure, the council has put forward a proposal that ignores the eu's role in coordinating growth initiatives and supporting them through its own funding instruments. i am referring in particular to the programmes under the europe 2020 strategy, such as eures, which are designed to promote cross-border labour mobility. in this regard, i consider it appropriate to launch the pilot project for the introduction of the european worker's electronic card, which will include workers' occupational and social security data card distinct from the european health insurance framework. i also support the call for increased subsidies for smes and cooperatives to support them in the face of rising production costs, continuing technological progress and the market dominance of large companies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft general budget of the european union because, through the efforts of the committee on budgets of the european parliament, of which i am a member, we have succeeded in creating a budgetary architecture that focuses on the needs of young people, innovation, smes and social policies. the draft budget also includes the pilot project i initiated on increasing access to health services in rural areas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015. the union budget plays an important role in achieving objective policy objectives such as: investments in transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure at union level (including the completion of the digital single market by 2015), energy efficiency, innovation and research. unemployment is the eu's top concern and the recovery of member states' economies and the creation of new jobs require a review of the eu's austerity policies, allowing member states to apply the most appropriate policy options to their specific situations. the eu budget should therefore focus in particular on decent job creation and sustainable economic growth. in addition, instruments such as the esf, the european regional development fund, the cohesion fund or the youth employment initiative are particularly important in times of crisis. as 2015 will be the second year of implementation of the new cycle of the european structural and investment funds, we stress the need to allocate sufficient commitment and payment appropriations to ensure that programmes reach the desired number of beneficiaries and thus produce the expected impact.
mr president, i was glad to see that my amendment expressly pointing to the issue of roma poverty, social marginalisation and discrimination in europe, was accepted in the final report on the european semester. this is proof of the fact that here in the european parliament we are aware of and agree on the need to implement long-term targeted and integrated measures aimed at reducing the social and economic marginalisation of roma communities. i believe that these measures should also be included and followed through in the european semester recommendations for all countries facing challenges in this field. drawing the roma into the regular labour market would provide them with social benefits. on the one hand it would alleviate the burden of social welfare systems and on the other hand would lead to increases in tax revenues. in the long term, however, i found that it is imperative that we increase school attendance by roma children and that we take more targeted measures against early school leaving.
in writing. - high debt levels, high unemployment, especially among young people, and almost non-existent economic growth in the euro area are some of the current challenges and priorities of the european semester. labour market recovery is hampered by the lack of competitiveness of some sectors, which contributes to the fragmentation of the labour market at community level. economic growth is closely linked to the existence of a functioning labour market, based on the exploitation of vocational skills, favourable to inclusion, encouraging mobility and guaranteeing equal treatment for all workers. the economic crisis has hit the sme sector hard, making it difficult to access finance. consistent programmes are needed to increase competitiveness, to create new jobs, and the european semester can make a real contribution to this by coordinating budgetary policies. the particularly low level of implementation of the country-specific recommendations indicates a lack of confidence in these recommendations and confirms the lack of coherence between community commitment and the actual implementation of policies at member state level. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the commitment of member states' governments to the community is an essential condition for economic growth, financial stability and employment.
in writing. - fragmentation of the labour market is currently one of the causes of unequal access to jobs, differentiated pay or unfavourable working conditions in the eu. all this translates into high youth unemployment, insufficient standards of living, and an increasingly pronounced polarization between low-skilled and high-skilled work. ending this fragmentation requires structural reforms that focus on sustainable policies that are pro-growth and ultimately create jobs and combat poverty. i believe that these reforms should focus on increasing the capacity of labour markets to integrate young people into the workforce, or to be able to provide opportunities to vulnerable groups. another objective of structural reforms should be the medium- and long-term sustainability and equity of social security, healthcare and pension systems.
in writing. - i believe that, after years spent following a model of austerity that has proven unsuccessful, leaving us in an unacceptable economic and social situation (higher percentage of unemployment, extremely low inflation rate) we have successfully pushed for the change that europe is waiting for. parliamentʼs report calls for a strong social pillar to be the priority of the european semester. parliament calls for more investment in research and development and recalls that investments should come mainly from the public sector. it highlights the importance of socially sustainable structural reforms, enhances the fight against social exclusion, against gender inequality in the labour market and the difficulties smes experience in accessing finance. moreover, it enacts the use of automatic stabilisers as a way of fighting against macroeconomic unbalances and removes the concept of macroeconomic conditionality, a rule that would punish underdeveloped regions which, on the contrary, need more support from the eu financing system. it is in my hope that with the support of mr junkerʼs eur 300 billion investment plan, we can finally recover from this crisis and put an end to social suffering that threatens the cooperation and solidarity of the european union.
in writing. - i support the draft resolution calling on the new european commission to launch, as a matter of urgency, a european investment programme to restore economic growth in the eu in the short term. it is a key support of parliament for president juncker's proposal to allocate €300 billion to boost the still fragile economic recovery in many member states. the european commission must give priority to public investment in infrastructure, research and innovation and human capital, as it committed to do during the european parliamentary hearing. i would like to draw attention in this connection to the need for measures to facilitate access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises, as a fundamental element of the european economy. the full implementation of the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme 2014-2020) must be accompanied by measures to reduce costs and simplify procedures affecting the ability of smes to access funds. the current fragmentation of national digital services regulations also needs to be overcome in order for the digital single market to become a significant driver of economic growth. in this respect, i advocate better coordination against tax evasion, in particular by multinational companies, in order to strengthen the conditions for fair competition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the european semester for economic policy coordination: implementation of the priorities for 2014. recovery from the financial crisis, sovereign debt and competitiveness cannot be achieved through a loose monetary policy alone. we stress the importance of continuing the process of deep, balanced and socially sustainable structural reforms in order to achieve growth, create jobs and combat poverty. the eu cannot increase its competitiveness again by reducing spending alone, but must increase investment in research and development, industrial development, education and skills, and the efficient use of resources at both national and european level. we call on the commission and the member states to strengthen eu industry through a more flexible competition policy that promotes competitiveness and employment, and through a green and digital transition plan. we reiterate the call on the commission to draw up, after consulting the social partners, a legislative proposal on the information and consultation of workers on restructuring planning and management, in order to ensure an economically and socially responsible adaptation to changes in eu industry.

president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, hong kong is an important partner for the european union: we share values such as freedom of expression and the rule of law and we have flourishing trade and economic relations. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. in order to fulfil the commitment made to the european parliament in 1997, the commission and the eeas publish annual reports on the political and economic developments in hong kong since the transfer of sovereignty to china. while adhering to the 'one china' policy, the european union is keen to ensure that the 'one country, two systems' principle is fully respected and applied. the european union attaches great importance to the stability, economic prosperity and democratic development of hong kong, which in turn depend on respect for the fundamental rights and freedoms enshrined in the law, including the right to peaceful assembly, freedom of expression and the independence of the judiciary. hong kong is at a crucial stage in its democratic development. we have repeatedly expressed our support for the introduction of universal suffrage for the election of the chief executive in 2017 and the legislative council in 2020. we believe that responsible government contributes to stability and prosperity, helps maintain hong kong's credibility and its position as a key international business centre. the eu welcomes the fact that a public consultation has taken place and that the people of hong kong have been able to express their views on electoral reforms. the government received more than 130,000 proposals, which shows that hong kong has a highly active civil society and citizens who aspire to a high level of political participation. the debate, however, highlighted political polarization within hong kong society and the difficulty of finding a compromise, especially on the procedure for nominating candidates for the role of chief executive. in late august, the standing committee of the national people's congress of china adopted a decision on electoral reform that many in hong kong deemed too restrictive and conservative: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the appointment of a new member of the commission. although legally in accordance with the basic law, politically this decision was difficult for many hong kong citizens to accept and has raised protests, which have been going on for more than three weeks now. the protests were largely peaceful, thanks to considerable restraint on the part of both the protesters and the police forces, although unfortunately there were some incidents. the hong kong government, while supporting the decision taken by beijing, believes that there is the necessary flexibility to find a compromise solution. we welcome the talks between the government and the student representatives yesterday. they are the first step towards a dialogue that could lead to a solution acceptable to all parties. we have on many occasions expressed to our interlocutors in hong kong the european union's support for the introduction of universal suffrage. we have also expressed our concern about the situation to representatives of the chinese ministry of foreign affairs in hong kong. in their meetings with mr leung, the president of the european commission, in brussels in may, presidents van rompuy and barroso stressed the importance for us of the rule of law, fundamental freedoms and rights and the introduction of universal suffrage. in both hong kong and brussels, our consultations are continuing in close coordination with the member states, which are following developments with the greatest interest. we sincerely hope that the parties will continue to dialogue and reach a consensus on a fair electoral system.
on behalf of the epp group. we have all, i think, been following very closely what has been happening in the last two months in hong kong, an important partner of ours, both commercially and politically, and i would like, first of all, to express my regret that the union has been silent or so silent about the situation in hong kong. i think we should not shy away from defending democracy in all parts of the world, to say how important freedom of expression, political freedom, among other things, to participate in elections and to vote, is at all times. the universal vote has no value if the process of validating the nominations is restricted before the vote. and i was reminded, as i watched what was happening in hong kong, of an old observation he made more than half a century ago, about totalitarian regimes, raymond aron, who said that in these regimes, it's not the voters who decide who rules, but the rulers who decide who votes. in hong kong, there's a little nuance that's been introduced, because we have the impression that it's not the voters who decide who governs, but the governors who select the candidates. this is unacceptable, and from the point of view of the union, as we understand democracy and i would say from the point of view of the promises made by beijing many years ago. of course, i was pleasantly surprised by the predominantly peaceful nature of the demonstrations and i hope that both sides will continue to show restraint and avoid the use of force, because if the situation were to become complicated in terms of violence, things would certainly take on a very serious dimension. yesterday's dialogue can, i believe, be a step towards finding a mutually acceptable solution, but for that, i believe the beijing authorities must show an open attitude and accept the demands for more representativeness in the process of determining the candidates.

acting president of the council (on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy). - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since pakistan began its transition to democracy in 2008, the european union has strengthened its relations with pakistan. the adoption in 2012 of a five-year plan has broadened and deepened our political dialogue. in this context, we are discussing a number of issues, including governance and human rights. the granting of the generalised system of preferences (gsp+) to pakistan from 1 january this year provides a further opportunity for deepening dialogue and assessing progress on human rights. since 2008, pakistan has maintained a moratorium on the death penalty. the european union regularly reiterates to pakistan its firm stance against the death penalty, which is a cruel and inhuman punishment. the eu delegation is constantly monitoring the situation and calls on pakistan to maintain the moratorium. during the 2014 strategic dialogue, pakistan confirmed its intention to maintain the moratorium. blasphemy laws are the most important tool of oppression of religious minorities and stipulate that insulting the koran is punishable by life imprisonment and that using derogatory terms against the prophet is punishable by death. a number of death sentences for blasphemy have been issued by numerous courts, but none have been carried out so far. usually, defendants are acquitted or released on bail by the courts of appeal. this means that they may spend several years in prison awaiting trial. the main criticism of the laws is that the punishment death penalty is disproportionate to the nature of the crime. however, another serious concern is that a considerable number of cases of blasphemy are based on false statements. the complaint is made, in most cases against muslims, but also against non-muslims, to resolve personal disputes or to fuel sectarian and interfaith tensions. such abuse seems to have increased dramatically in recent decades. pakistan has acknowledged the abuses and has committed to do everything possible to prevent them. as stated in the european union guidelines on the promotion and protection of freedom of religion or belief, adopted by the foreign affairs council on 23 june 2013, 'laws criminalising blasphemy and restricting freedom of religion or belief [...] may have a serious inhibitory effect on freedom of expression and freedom of religion or belief; the european union recommends the decriminalisation of these offences.' the eu will also strongly oppose the use of the death penalty, corporal punishment or deprivation of liberty as sanctions for blasphemy. in the case of asia bibi, the european union is following developments very closely. last thursday, the lahore high court upheld the verdict of the trial court, which sentenced her to death for blasphemy in 2010. asia bibi now has 30 days to appeal to the supreme court of pakistan. the high representative/vice-president has repeatedly expressed his regret and deep concern at the decision of the lahore court to uphold the death sentence of asia bibi. cathy ashton hoped the verdict would be overturned quickly by the supreme court. the european union calls on pakistan to ensure full respect for all its citizens for the human rights enshrined in the international conventions to which it is a party. asia bibi is the first woman to be sentenced to death for the crime of blasphemy and her case has raised a lot of hype in europe. nevertheless, his case is not unique. let me congratulate the european parliament on its strong commitment to human rights in pakistan, expressed through numerous resolutions and political mobilization. the european union, through its delegation in islamabad, will continue to follow asia bibi's case closely and to call for her release. although the european union does not consider itself to be intervening in an ongoing judicial proceeding, it will consider raising this case and the wider issue of the death penalty and the blasphemy law with its pakistani counterpart. we will continue to urge the government in islamabad to consider reducing the number of crimes punishable by the death penalty and to respect its obligations towards freedom of expression and freedom of religion and belief. these issues were discussed in the human rights dialogue held in islamabad in june. the next opportunity will be next week when the special representative stavros lambrinidis visits pakistan. finally, as i have already mentioned, the gsp+ regime provides a very useful framework for assessing and promoting human rights progress in pakistan. thank you, mr. president, thank you for your attention.
on behalf of the epp group. in the last term, we addressed asia bibi's situation and the issue of pakistan's blasphemy laws in four resolutions. despite these pressures, asia bibi's appeal against her death sentence was rejected by a court last week. the conviction is simply absurd and i would like to recall the circumstances that gave rise to this important debate in pakistani society and that led to the unfortunate conviction. so in 2009, asia bibi took water from a well and offered it to another woman, a muslim woman, who refused it on the pretext that asia is a christian and that the water is therefore impure. there was an altercation, and asia bibi is today on trial for blasphemy, and more than that, she is on death row awaiting execution by hanging. i would like to remind you that while they provide for the death penalty, the blasphemy laws in pakistan do not contain any standards of proof, nor a requirement to prove a specific intent, nor a penalty for false allegations, and worse than all of this, they do not contain any clear indication of what constitutes blasphemy. the laws are often used for personal vendettas and to persecute religious minorities and especially christians. the case of asia bibi is emblematic of this. i hope that the appeal to the supreme court of pakistan will remedy this injustice and that the rule of law will be restored. on the other hand, the possibility of pardoning asia bibi provided for in the constitution must also be considered to end the ordeal of this woman. i also hope that the security of asia bibi and her family will be ensured by the pakistani authorities. indeed, we must not forget that once a person is accused of blasphemy, his security and that of his family is at stake. the vast majority of people accused of blasphemy in pakistan do not, by the way, end up being executed, but are either lynched or killed while in custody. asia bibi's family has been forced into hiding by death threats and fears, according to statements in the press, that she will be killed once released. beyond that, i think the pakistani authorities must urgently revoke the blasphemy laws, so that such abusive trials, which have nothing to do with the idea of justice and tolerance, do not get any faster.

in writing. - the decision of the european union unilaterally to extend market access to ukrainian goods on its territory until the end of 2015 is a an act of generosity, showing that there is no such thing as a ‘geopolitical plot’ against any of ukraine’s traditional partners, notably russia. russia’s products will be free of direct competition from eu products in ukraine, which is a painful condition imposed by russia on ukraine and accepted by the eu as part of its effort to facilitate a peaceful resolution of the ukrainian crisis. in order to enforce this arrangement, the eu agreed to give up on its own market access to ukraine, as negotiated in the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement (dcfta), the full enforcement of which will have to wait until 2016. it is a selfless response from the eu, in stark contrast to any zero-sum ‘encirclement’ game. i am also particularly reassured by the introduction of a provision for democracy and human rights conditionality to be respected by ukraine in exchange for the trade preferences. ukraine has to behave as a modern liberal democracy, respecting human rights, including minority rights, in order to have the continued solidarity of western liberal democracies. with the inclusion of these conditions, i was happy to support the measure.

madam president, the eu can only achieve its 75% employment target if it succeeds in strengthening the position of women in the labour market and in reducing the gender employment gap. although equality between men and women is a core value of the european union, several current studies show that there are still significant differences in the work experience of men and women and in the work-life balance. there are many reasons for this situation, which vary from country to country, and there can be no single european solution. one of the fundamental reasons is the lack of childcare solutions. most mothers do not work or work only part-time because child-care facilities are either lacking or too expensive. only a few member states have achieved the goal of providing care for children before school age. based on their experience, the solutions are: 1. to provide childcare facilities that better reflect the working hours of parents, 2. to provide childcare allowance, 3. to amend the laws on childcare leave, 4. to provide the possibility of flexible working hours. to achieve this, the commission and the council should address this issue more strongly in the european semester.

in writing. - the convention on choice of court agreements is designed to provide greater legal certainty and predictability for parties to international agreements and disputes by creating an optional system of judicial dispute settlement. the objective of the convention is to promote international trade and investment through enhanced judicial cooperation by introducing uniform rules of jurisdiction. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it seeks to strike a balance between the need to guarantee the parties that the courts of their choice will resolve the case and the need to allow states to pursue aspects of their public policies, such as respect for the guarantee of the exclusive jurisdiction of states. the report virtually complements the objectives underlying the eu rules on the extension of jurisdiction by creating a harmonised set of rules within the eu with regard to third states that will become contracting parties to the convention.

in writing. - the global development framework implements in practice the principles on which the european union is founded, namely freedom, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms and the rule of law. eu member states are obliged to instill these principles in their citizens, thus making a significant contribution to the eradication of european problems. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that this global development framework has the beneficial purpose of raising public awareness of the current problems facing the european area, assessing them and countering the problems in the years to come. key issues such as human rights violations, armed conflict and terrorism, climate change, food insecurity, migration, corruption, tax fraud and evasion, unemployment, and financial and economic crises still pose challenges to eu member states. that is why i believe that the common goal of the 28 states is to partner with their citizens, as well as with the european institutions, to jointly inspire respect for and the application of the eu's pillar principles.

in writing. — it is crucial for the european union to adopt a strong, cohesive and unified policy for global development in the post-2015 period. the interdependence of progress in the main priority areas laid out in the report makes it vital that they be tackled in unison. article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes eradication of poverty as one of the primary objectives of the eu development policy. however, poverty and inequality cannot be combated without improving education. conversely, education cannot be efficiently improved without combating poverty and inequality. as such, policy coherence for development is imperative. i support this initiative and believe that the eu must provide the necessary legislative framework and mobilise the necessary financial resources to effectively address all the priorities laid out. besides providing the appropriate legislative and institutional framework, the new global framework needs to include the necessary tools for monitoring, assessing and enforcing these mechanisms.
in writing. - as pope francis stressed in his speech today, 21 november 2014, we must put the european citizens, the people and their basic needs at the centre of our attention. i believe that the first step to be taken is to combat inequalities of whatever nature. reducing inequalities between member states and, by implication, between the people of the union is the basis for sustainable development, which can lead to the eradication of poverty. in my view, poverty eradication can be achieved through three key conditions: the absence of armed conflict, the prevention of climate disasters and the improvement of productivity in the agricultural and fisheries sectors. the new global development framework, eu and the global development framework for the period after 2015, voted today, is the key to creating these necessary conditions. good governance for sustainable and balanced global development in the post-2015 period is directly linked to one of the main millennium development goals: halving the number of people suffering from hunger and poverty.
in writing. - while providing reasons for cautious optimism, the global poverty figures show us that one and a half billion people still live in absolute poverty, deprived of food, easy access to water, healthcare, education and security. i believe that joint action is needed to make the european union openly and unequivocally the world's exporter of know-how in all areas that have an impact on living standards - education, good governance, legislation, public health. absolute poverty also exists in the eu, even if it looks, perhaps, different from the poverty accentuated by civil wars and conflicts in other parts of the world. i believe that poverty within the borders of the european union and poverty in the rest of the world must be tackled in parallel. while national governments in the 28 eu countries, but especially in eastern europe, have a great deal of responsibility in promoting national policies and using the resources made available by the eu to eradicate poverty, the european union must act as one to accelerate poverty reduction in the rest of the world.
in writing. - i support the rapporteur's proposal to set a secondary target of reducing child poverty in the europe 2020 mid-term evaluation, and to use objective 'poverty' indicators for the evaluations to measure poverty rates in the member states, precisely to help identify those at risk of being excluded.
in writing. — the europe 2020 strategy has set specific employment, education and social targets that the eu must strive to achieve. it is encouraging to see that progress has been significant on some areas, such as tertiary educational attainment, which currently stands at 36.9% with a 40% target, or early leavers from education, which currently stands at 12.0% with a 10% goal. it is, however, alarming that in other areas progress has been slow or non-existent. the major economic and social problems of the eu, unemployment and poverty, do not appear to react sufficiently to the european union's initiatives, and in some member states they are even increasing. the 68.4% employment rate in 2013 and the 122.6 million people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2013 put us very far from the targets of 75% and 96.4 million, respectively. i strongly believe that we need renewed efforts in these areas and that, without more cooperation between the eu and the member states and without sufficient spending, we may not reach the europe 2020 goals. if we do not act now, we may be faced with worsening situations instead of the improvements that each eu citizen is looking forward to.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the social and employment aspects of the eu 2020 strategy. it is essential that the elements of the european strategy are implemented in order to make its beneficial results visible in the shortest possible time. the european union needs to act quickly to tackle the social problems generated by the economic crisis. the resolution calls for social issues to be given priority on the european agenda.
in writing. - the europe 2020 strategy risks remaining a document full of good intentions and objectives, in the absence of clear and decisive action first at european level and then, equally and even more importantly, at the level of the 28 member states. less than six years away from the deadline for strategy 2020, the situation with regard to employment figures in europe is far from what the eu has set itself. at this rate, the gap between the eu's more developed countries and the poorest, such as romania, risks widening. i would draw particular attention to how member states have managed to achieve the europe 2020 objectives. the absence of prompt action, of concrete measures to stimulate the economy, to encourage investment and to reduce and combat unemployment, can have serious consequences, leading to a sharp increase in inequality within the union. i am confident that in the near future, member states will make every effort and take a much more ambitious and concrete approach in translating the objectives of the 2020 strategy into national targets.
the way in which the conciliation procedure has been conducted shows a rare lack of respect on the part of the council. the fact that member states have not been able to reach a clear agreement is worrying, but this is the result of the fact that the states were not represented at a decision-making level. the situation is all the more difficult as debts pile up at european level. the bills have to be paid. there are financial resources to pay these bills. the credibility of the european union depends on this and on its seriousness towards the beneficiaries. the council has to understand that these beneficiaries are from their own countries, regions, cities, are companies or ngos from their own countries. i don't understand, honestly, what the problem is. we as meps are responsible to the citizens we represent. the board seems to have forgotten that it is also responsible to them. we need political will in the council and in the member states, if not for the european parliament, if not for the citizens, at least for him and his political ambitions, which, without the budget, cannot be realised.
in writing. november 25th marks the international day for the elimination of violence against women. violence against women is one of the most insidious violations of human rights and exists on every continent, in every country and culture. they exist equally in economically developed countries and in developing countries. rape, rape as a weapon of war, forced marriage, early marriage, dowry killings and honour killings, trafficking in women and girls, female genital mutilation and sex-selective abortion are all manifestations of violence against women. now, we have alarming statistics worldwide. un estimates show that abuses against women are on the rise. the most common form of violence against them, globally, is physical violence. on average, at least one in three women is beaten, forced into sexual intercourse, or otherwise abused. it is necessary to move from words to deeds, by applying the measures that prove to be most effective in combating gender discrimination. states need to allocate more resources to making the fight against violence against women a priority, as promoting equal opportunities, non-violent behaviours and non-stigmatisation of victims is a necessity.
in writing. every day, violence is manifested physically or in more insidious ways, against women of all ages, all over the world. gender-based violence should not be tolerated in societies that want to be modern. we must ensure firm principles for the protection of women, children and all those who find it difficult to defend themselves. violence against women knows no borders, it extends across europe. it is a phenomenon which undermines the foundations of the european society we want to build. we cannot accept living in a european society where at least 45% of women have been subjected to some form of violence or discrimination in their lifetime. we cannot accept that more than a quarter of all european women are victims of gender-based violence and physical abuse without us doing something about it. we are investing in the principles of the istanbul convention on the elimination of violence against women. romania has rapidly acceded to the principles of the convention and will shortly ratify this document. i believe that together we can defeat all forms of violence against women. just together!
written. given the current context, where we are facing a considerable number of deaths and illnesses caused by working conditions at the workplace, it is clear that we have a duty to eu citizens and, of course, the desire to get better legislation in this area. the commission must come to parliament with concrete legislative proposals. all employees have the right to adequate and high protection at work, regardless of the member state, the size of the employer or the type of potential illness. businesses, in turn, need support to better and more correctly implement the relevant rules. we have a new commission and a new parliament that must commit to improving this legislation. we can no longer ignore the number of cancers linked to working conditions or the worrying number of musculoskeletal disorders in the member states. all of these have a direct impact on the health of the population, but also on the performance of employees.
mr president, the principle of equality and non-discrimination is enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the charter of human rights. the employment equality directive has been transposed into law by all member states, yet people with disabilities still face social and economic discrimination in the eu. the unemployment rate for people with disabilities is twice that of the general population. this is because few jobs offer disadvantageous access or other reasonable accommodation for these people. we have to move on. reasonable accommodation should not only be a matter of positive discrimination but also a legal requirement. at the same time, we must combat the trap of a disability support culture and develop active labour market policies. but first, we need to be clear about where we're going and what our goals are. member states should collect statistics on disability and on equality and develop strategies based on good practice.
in writing. the stress tests and asset quality assessment of the major european banks are also significant for the economies of the non-euro area member states. the majority of banking assets in these member states are in banks whose majority shareholders are euro area banks. noting that these tests have not resulted in major problems for many banks in the euro area, we point out that economic sanctions against russia, as well as the situation in ukraine, may put banks with large exposures in the two countries in difficulty. we also expect proposals from the european commission to implement the policy decisions taken by the g20 leaders on 'banks too big to fail'.
mr president, i will support the council's proposals to align the powers conferred on the european central bank with the new supervisory function of the major banks in the european union. we can argue that this power, without the power to apply sanctions in case of violation of the rules, the decisions of the european central bank, as well as without the power to obtain the information necessary for the exercise of the supervisory function, would have undermined the credibility of the entire supervisory process, as well as the credibility of the european central bank. i would also like the european central bank and the council to take parliament's recommendations into account, as they bring more clarity both in terms of the transparency needed in those processes and in terms of the relationship between the european central bank and the central banks of the member states.
in writing. developing the infrastructure and boosting the economy of the newly-acquired countries must be one of the priorities of the european fund for strategic investments. closing the gap between the old and new member states is an imperative for deepening european integration and also represents a significant opportunity to boost growth and create new jobs. aligning and better connecting european transport infrastructure, for example, from romania and other new member states is not just a concrete proof of solidarity, but can be a profitable business for all involved. i therefore advocate channelling european investment to boost the less developed regions of the eu and creating transport and energy supply networks to strengthen the project of european integration. at the same time, i believe that effective and urgent measures are needed at union level to encourage private investment and to make the labour market more flexible, as well as to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. otherwise, it will be difficult to reach the target of eur 315 billion, which the european commission wants the strategic fund to attract as additional investments in the period 2015-2017.
in writing. – europe needs more prosperity, job creation, stability and sustainable growth. this can only be achieved through further investment. the investment plan is an ambitious and viable step in that direction aiming at adding around eur 330 billion to the eu gdp over the next three years and creating up to 1.3 million jobs in key strategic areas, such as energy, transport, education, research and innovation. the economic crisis has generated a crisis of confidence in europe, we need to attract private investments in order to boost the attainment of genuine, growth-generating european projects. we have the right tools at our disposal and on top of that, we have been presented with a fresh innovative investment plan that can streamline all the resources we have at our disposal. i ask all the member states to fully support and actively take part in this project in order to help restore a sustainable and stable european union.
in writing. climate change is affecting the world, not just europe. as an elected representative, i have a responsibility to present the views of the citizens i represent. and citizens seem to have been taken out of the programme you presented, commissioner. some citizens misperceive climate change, and others (most) say that nothing coherent is being done to improve the situation. why would you do that? because they see money being spent with minimal effects, they see emissions moving from one country to another by moving waste, old cars, old technologies from one country to another. they see how governments accept the cutting of forests. today i heard "should" many times, but i didn't hear "how"! that is why i believe that both the european commission and the council must present integrated projects within and between eu countries, but also between the eu and the rest of the world. i think we need better regulation, mandatory, not voluntary, because everything that's done wrong in one country affects the rest of the world. the council and the commission have an obligation to find solutions that deliver concrete results so that 'climate change' does not remain just a slogan.
i welcome the approach of the european institutions to their concern about climate change. i believe that if we act now, the costs of food production and environmental protection for the global, european and national economies can be reduced in the future. all the world's states must take appropriate measures to establish globally coordinated regional and macro-regional plans that are capable not only of responding to climate change, but also of preventing its effects, in order to protect the society in which we live and its citizens. every month, every year that passes without making firm decisions about the risks of climate change means that we don't think about our living conditions, but more than that, it means that we don't care about the planet that we leave to our children. the call to all actors (governments, international organisations, non-governmental organisations and sub-national actors) must be answered, and the answer can only be better international cooperation in action against climate change. we must not forget that food security and safety, especially for vulnerable people, is affected by the effects of climate change.
in writing. — the report on ecb statistical data collection allows the ecb to perform its new tasks for the prudential supervision of credit institutions (single supervisory mechanism). the report establishes that any exemption of reporting agents must be justified and made public. by doing so it increases the level of transparency. the report also amplifies the typology of collected data and adds the fundamental principle of proportionality in the definition and imposition of statistical reporting requirements: the ecb, when imposing sanctions, will have to distinguish between types of misconduct and whether infringement is intentional or negligent. our group has managed to include amendments that ensure greater transparency on exemption of reporting agents and protection of confidential data used by ecb when performing its new supervisory tasks. i congratulate the rapporteur roberto gualtieri not only for excellent work but for being able to achieve a large consensus in the committee on economic and monetary affairs as well. i support the adoption of the report as it strengthens the ecb’s power in the exercise of its supervisory tasks, with the ultimate goal of better controlling and regulating the european banking system.
in writing. — this regulation of the power of the ecb to impose sanctions is a step forward in the banking union process, a process that is one of our means to end the current economic crisis that is threatening the well-being of eu citizens and to prevent another crisis in the years to come. i welcome the positive aspects that our committee has introduced and especially the higher level of transparency in infringement procedures. i also strongly support the amendment presented by my colleague jonás fernández that would transfer ecb supervisory function sanction revenue from this institution to the single resolution fund (srf). this amendment avoids conflicts of interest in the ecb and increases srf credibility and resources that will permit faster recovery of the banking system. while i consider many of the changes introduced to be positive, i have abstained on the modification of (ec) regulation 2532/98 for the following reason: i, along with my political associates, disagree with the epp party’s amendment that would delay publication of the decision ‘until all legal means have been exhausted’. this would eliminate the timeframe for collection of sanctions and consequently contradicts the principle of transparency that is one of the main pillars of the s&d political view.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the european central bank's power to impose sanctions because, on the way to the creation of a real banking union at the level of the euro area, but also with the participation of some of the member states which have not yet adopted the euro, the ecb's role is very important. we need to tighten the supervision of the european financial system, and that is the ecb's role. however, for regulations to prove effective, they must be accompanied by a monitoring and enforcement mechanism. we need more transparency, without which the effects of the financial crisis cannot be fully removed. the confidence of markets must be matched by the confidence of citizens and all those involved, and this is achieved through increased transparency of all new regulations and mechanisms that will ultimately constitute a truly functioning banking union in europe.
in writing. - the european union must continue to play a very active role in the fight against the global climate crisis, and the new commission must ensure that programmes to protect the environment and combat the effects of climate change can receive adequate funding. in all its actions, the eu must take into account that climate change policies need to be linked to the actions taken following the rio conference and in line with the millennium development goals and the post-2015 agenda.
