in writing. - president juncker has successfully passed the no-confidence test raised by the motion of censure against his cabinet, following allegations of tax concessions offered to certain corporations during his time as head of the luxembourg executive. i spoke against the motion of censure in the first place because, as a lawyer, i understand that any possible accusation must first be soundly argued and investigated as such by the competent bodies. secondly, i voted against because i am convinced of the need for a stable framework for the functioning of the community institutions. trust in the eu institutions is essential, any adverse effect could be economically disastrous, upsetting financial markets and increasing uncertainty among european citizens. current issues such as the conflict in ukraine, the threats of the islamic state, as well as domestic challenges in implementing the jobs, growth and investment package, need a stable climate at european level. the overwhelming vote against, with over 61%, confirms the high level of confidence that the juncker commission has in the european parliament. and last but not least, the rejection of the censure motion has once again demonstrated that parliament stands united in the face of the destructive intentions constantly promoted by the eurosceptic parties.
in writing. - the motion of censure was a gift for the juncker commission: it allowed it to be reconfirmed and re-legitimised politically. its rejection by an overwhelming vote by all the mainstream political parties was natural: it would have been irresponsible to plunge europe into a major crisis at the behest of populist parties. that said, my vote was one for reason more than for persons, and i hope clarity will be brought on all the matters that may cast a shadow over the mandate of this commission.
in writing. - we voted on the joint resolution on the delays in the start of the 2014-2020 cohesion policy. i was also one of the initiators of the motion for a resolution tabled by the ppe group in the ep on this subject. the commission's credibility is undermined by delays in the implementation of cohesion policy 2014-2020, coupled with arrears in the payment of invoices for the 2007-2013 programming period. it is of the utmost importance that the ec and the member states demonstrate accountability, especially as cohesion policy funds, together with co-financing by the member states, represent a significant proportion of public expenditure closely linked to economic growth in the eu. new programmes to strengthen investment, stimulate job creation and increase labour productivity need to be implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. - the convention on the rights of the child is ratified almost universally, but is far from being universally applied, with children's rights continuing to be violated in many parts of the world as a result of violence, abuse, exploitation, poverty, social exclusion and discrimination. humanitarian crises continue to have a devastating impact on children, with over 59 million children directly affected by crisis in 2014, particularly in conflict zones. today, it is estimated that there are 250,000 child soldiers in the world, of which 40 percent are girls. we must condemn the use of children for terrorist activities or military purposes and provide psychological support and assistance to all children who have been exposed to violent events or are victims of war. we need effective measures to protect children from the effects of armed conflict, to end the use of children in armed forces or armed groups and to end impunity for crimes against children. the promotion and protection of the rights of the child is a priority of eu human rights policy. it is fundamental to defend children involved in armed conflict not only because they are suffering in the present and because the future belongs to children, but also because they have inherent and inalienable rights.
in writing. a quarter of a century after the adoption of the un convention on the rights of the child, millions of children worldwide continue to be abused, discriminated against, harassed, exploited through labour or sex, deprived of basic rights to education and health, subjected to slavery, violence, forced marriage or military recruitment at an early age. unfortunately, violations of children's rights are still reported, including in eu member states, with a clear correlation between education and family living standards and the traumas suffered by children. therefore, more efforts are needed to combat child poverty and ensure access to free primary school education for all children. we have the framework defined by the eu agenda for the rights of the child, so member states and the european institutions need to act more strongly to eradicate poverty and combat the vicious circle of disadvantage. increased attention is needed to counter violence against children, their harassment and exploitation both online and through illegal cross-border trafficking in human beings. i call on the european forces to monitor more closely the application of directives 2011/36/eu and 92/2011/eu by the member states in this regard.
in writing. — every year, over 7 million child deaths worldwide could be prevented, over 59 million children are victims of humanitarian crises, and over 1 billion children are victims of abuses such as neglect, abuse, sexual exploitation, kidnapping, human trafficking, and many other rights violations in the european union, in the eu’s partner states, as well as worldwide. twenty-five years ago, all the member states of the european union ratified the un convention on the rights of the child. the promotion of children’s rights is a fundamental objective of the european union’s policies. despite this, the progress made in the last 25 years, although remarkable, is insufficient. presently, in the eu alone, between 10 and 20 million children will have suffered some form of assault during their childhood. it is imperative that we take all the steps necessary to ensure that the most vulnerable, and at the same time the most important citizens of the eu, the children, receive adequate protection and support, and, as such, i fully support this initiative.
i voted in favour of this resolution because the digital single market is the implementation of the third and final wave of the technological revolution, the digital revolution. the interconnection of markets is a key condition for the functioning of the european union's economy and the ability to adapt to technological developments is an inevitable measure for maintaining global competitiveness. the digital economy needs to respond to market challenges by increasing technological capacity, with high performance in multiple fields and which can bring numerous job opportunities on the labour market. the digital single market faces, however, numerous challenges due to the stratification of european markets. the diversity of those markets currently creates barriers both between potential users in the member states and those in third countries. there are successful initiatives, such as the european procurement portal, which have created new opportunities for smes to grow across borders. the expansion of e-commerce activities has created new opportunities for european firms, but in some countries this process has been slow to take off due to low consumer confidence. however, the creation of a single certification system for businesses operating online would increase consumer confidence.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution as the digital single market is one of the most innovative sectors of the economy, with a major role in boosting the eu's competitiveness, from e-commerce to telecommunications. i believe that there is a need for increased support for european initiatives in the field of new technologies, given their potential in the eu's post-crisis recovery. we are facing some major challenges at the moment, which the eu needs to address through a coordinated strategy to develop a digital single market. i mention in particular the problem of market fragmentation, the lack of interoperability in the european union and the protection of personal data and privacy. last but not least, we are affected by differences in the access of european citizens to the internet, especially in some rural regions. excessive market concentration and abuse of dominant positions by certain operators are also a concern. concrete action is needed to ensure a level playing field and i am referring in particular to the separation of search engines from other commercial services, as there is a risk that search engines market secondary services on the basis of the information they obtain.
in writing. — the fragmentation of the digital market in the european union has been a significant barrier to the expansion of the itc private sector. the need to be compliant with the legislations of multiple member states is an expensive bureaucratic burden for established enterprises, while for many smes and entrepreneurs it is simply unfeasible. this severely hampers not only the growth of the digital sector in the eu, but also of adjacent service sectors. according to the estimates, the implementation of a european digital single market would create millions of jobs and contribute to a 4% increase of the gdp of the eu by 2020. this would be a welcome boost in a period of high unemployment and stagnant economy throughout the eu. i support this initiative as i believe it benefits both sides of the argument. as stated in this resolution, on one hand, businesses will have easier access to a wider market, implicitly leading to job creation and economic growth, while on the other, consumers will benefit from cheaper, better and more varied digital services.
in writing. — i voted for the digital single market resolution because the implementation and completion of a digital single market would offer great economic benefits and would have a positive impact on the daily life of eu consumers and citizens. the digital single market will also create new jobs especially for highly skilled workers and will make an important contribution to the creation of quality and sustainable employment. i voted for the enforcement of eu competition rules in the digital single market, which will boost competitiveness and the growth of the market. this resolution is a step further for development of e-commerce, consumer access and choice of goods and services in the long term. and last but not least, the digital single market is one of the areas of progress which would help the eu to recover from the economic crisis because through the digital market the possible economic gain is up to eur 260 billion per year.
in writing. — whether economic or social, the cost of not accelerating the completion of our digital single market is simply too high. however, one must proceed in a fashion that strikes the perfect balance between consumer protection and enhancing the competitiveness of our sluggish continental economy. in this context, i voted in favour of a resolution that emphasises the urgency of doing away with barriers that prevent reaping the benefits of a truly connected europe: legal uncertainties and an uneven playing field for businesses, slow internet access, restricted internet traffic or roaming charges. it is a sensible initiative that flags our deficiencies and points digital europe in the right direction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the problem of child malnutrition is one of the main factors that prevents developing countries from getting out of poverty and giving children a chance at life. improving child nutrition is a key factor in the development of a healthy population, a factor that automatically leads to economic growth and social progress in these countries. a number of studies have shown that malnutrition is caused by a lack of essential elements such as calcium, iron, vitamin a, and also by problems that occur during breastfeeding. these deficiencies can cause stunted growth or even death, due to illness of the mother or the child. so developing countries cannot get out of poverty and they cannot get ahead economically unless their populations are nutritionally secure. and for that to happen, it's going to take the european union and the developed countries to step in and help us treat and combat child malnutrition.
in writing. - it is well known that child malnutrition is linked to food insecurity and household poverty, inadequate care and feeding, unhealthy living conditions and inadequate health services. almost one billion people continue to suffer from hunger and, even worse, at least 225 million children under five years of age worldwide suffer from acute and chronic malnutrition and stunted growth as a result of chronic maternal and child malnutrition, with an estimated 2.6 million of these dying each year in developing countries. i voted for ensuring that universal access to nutritionally adequate food and the fight against child malnutrition remain the most important targets within the overall objective of eradicating hunger in the post-2015 agenda, including the eradication of all forms of malnutrition by 2030. so, 25 years after the adoption of the un convention on the rights of the child, it is disappointing to see that some signatory states have not yet been able to create an enabling environment to ensure that children have access to adequate nutrition.
in writing. as one billion of our fellow citizens suffer from hunger and as this scourge affects hundreds of millions of children, victims of chronic malnutrition and infant mortality, i support the resolution calling for the eu to provide more support through its development aid programmes to fight hunger in developing countries. malnutrition is the leading cause of infant mortality, responsible for over one third of all illnesses in children under five years of age. that is why i believe that sustained efforts must be made to combat food trafficking, improve purchasing power, help small farmers and distribute food more efficiently. unfortunately, some progress made since the 1996 world food summit was cancelled out by the food crises of 2008 and 2011. the cycle of rural-to-urban migration and extreme poverty is also perpetuated in many poor regions of the world. in these circumstances, it is clear that the reduction in funds for agriculture under the 10th european development fund was a mistake and i ask the council to reconsider this harmful amputation.
in writing. — at least 225 million of the world’s children under the age of five are suffering from acute and chronic undernutrition or from stunted growth as a result of chronic child and maternal undernutrition. there is estimated data of 2.6 million of such children dying every year in developing countries. also one out of three people in developing countries are suffering from chronic deficiency of essential vitamins and minerals, which drastically increases their susceptibility to birth defects, infection and compromised development. the fight against child undernutrition and the provision of universal access to adequate nutritious food should remain one of the most important targets of the post-2015 agenda. it is thus critical to make every possible effort to ensure that this goal is properly achieved. i welcome the commission’s commitment to investing eur 3.5 billion between 2014 and 2020 in improving nutrition in some of the world’s poorest countries. i call on the commission to scale up its commitments as regards nutrition-specific interventions in order to meet its objective of reducing by 7 million the number of stunted children under the age of five by 2025.
in writing. the european union must keep environmental protection at the top of its agenda and i believe it will be beneficial for it to join the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). it will also allow for enhanced cooperation with other non-eu countries to protect endangered species. we must not forget for a moment the great diversity of plants, animals and habitats that europe has, in a territory that is quite small compared to other continents. according to experts, half of europe's wetlands have been drained, and nearly three quarters of the dunes in france, italy, and spain have disappeared. the most valuable habitats for wild fauna and flora are protected by law, but many are in poor condition and need to be restored. on the other hand, almost half of europe's mammals and a third of its reptiles, fish and birds are threatened with extinction. this is mainly because their habitats are being reduced as urban areas develop and some of the land is allocated to infrastructure projects such as roads. as such, we need to protect all of these species, both for current and future generations.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report repealing council directive 93/5/eec of 25 february 1993 on the assistance to be given to the commission and cooperation between member states in the scientific examination of questions relating to foodstuffs. following regulation (ec) no 178/2002 of the european parliament and of the council, the scientific tasks entrusted to the scientific committee for food have been taken over by the scientific committee and the groups of the european food safety authority (efsa). efsa has also become the body competent to promote scientific cooperation with member states and competent national bodies operating in the areas falling within the competence of the authority. the report thus provides a clear regulatory framework in line with existing rules, which is intended to further strengthen the european framework for food safety. i believe that food safety in the eu and in the world is a key factor for the development of a healthy population, a factor which automatically determines economic growth and the harmonious development of society.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote on the assistance to be given to the commission and the cooperation between member states in the scientific examination of food-related issues and agree to the creation of a regulatory framework that is as simple, clear and stable as possible for businesses, workers and citizens.
in writing. food safety and the creation of the best conditions for public health care are a constant concern of the eu. this concern is all the more timely as the public debate generated by the eu negotiations for new free trade agreements has brought many of the concerns of european citizens into the public spotlight. the eu must ensure the highest standards of food safety, and this must be achieved through scientific processes. that is why i voted for the report on the scientific examination of food problems. the report repeals council directive 93/5/eec, which has become obsolete, and thus updates european legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation on the accession of the european union to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora. the fact that the european union can join cites as a member after having held observer status demonstrates that the eu is fully capable of pursuing its own objectives in line with its environmental policy. the convention on international trade in wild fauna and flora (cites), to which 178 countries, including all eu member states, are parties, is an important international instrument aimed at protecting endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of over 35 000 species. given that the european union is an economic and political partner, its accession to the convention is nothing but a normal step, which will result in much better protection and conservation of european fauna and flora.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) and believe that the european union's accession to cites will reflect and optimise current practices for the protection of endangered species of flora and fauna, which cover some 35 000 species.
in writing. ‒ i support the european union's accession to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), as this accession is a global confirmation of the eu's environmental concerns. initially limited to the level of states and open from 2013 to regional integration organisations, accession will not affect the individual rights and obligations of eu member states, previous signatories of cites. european environmental policy already aims to protect species whose survival may be threatened by international trade and stipulates a licensing system for import-export-re-export operations, as well as rules on documents of origin for species covered by the convention. the eu has also adopted a number of legal instruments on this subject which are binding on the member states. in these circumstances, i believe that, by joining cites and taking over part of its trust fund, the eu must commit itself more firmly at international level to enhancing cooperation to protect the almost 35 000 species listed in the annexes to the convention and to strictly comply with the rules governing trade in this area.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the accession of the european union to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). this accession represents an opportunity for the eu to become fully involved in the implementation of the convention.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ep recommendation on the eu's accession to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). i welcome the fact that, thanks to the amendment of the convention, the eu, as an organisation of sovereign states, has also been able to accede to it. international trade must not become a tool for reckless exploitation of the environment, which accelerates the harmful phenomenon of the disappearance of new and new species. this concern is shared by many eu citizens and is reflected in today's ep decision. cites, which entered into force in 1975, is an important international instrument essential for the protection of endangered species of flora and fauna. under cites, all import, export and re-export operations and introductions of species of marine origin covered by the convention must be authorised through a licensing system.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision renewing the agreement on cooperation in science and technology between the european community and ukraine. the agreement on cooperation in science and technology between the european community and ukraine was signed in copenhagen on 4 july 2002. the agreement provided that it would end for an initial period on 31 december 2002 and be renewed by agreement of the parties for additional periods of five years. by decision 2011/182/eu of 9 march 2011, the council approved the renewal of the agreement for a further period of five years, until 8 november 2014. the renewal of the agreement for five years is in the interest of both parties in order to maintain continuity in the scientific and technological relations between ukraine and the european union. the european union must now, more than ever, support ukraine's efforts to align with the european union and its desire to be part of the european union in the future. the science and technology agreement will further add value to this industry in europe and, together with ukraine, will make europe much stronger on the world market.
in writing. ‒ i support the recommendation on the renewal of the agreement on cooperation in science and technology between the european community and ukraine. the agreement not only perpetuates a joint act that expired on 7 november 2014, but also strengthens bilateral cooperation at a critical moment for ukraine. the renewal of the agreement must, in my view, be followed by more effective cooperation in practice to facilitate access to specialist information, to deepen research and innovation and to better exploit the results of scientific activities at international level. research in eastern europe is suffering from chronic underfunding and an exodus of specialists, which is starting to have a boomerang effect on the education system and the competitiveness of these societies. i therefore believe that the eu-ukraine partnership must, especially in the new geopolitical context and ukraine's orientation towards the system of democratic values, aim at improving local conditions for the exploitation of the expertise of its own specialists.

in writing.– this report aims at reacting to the commission’s proposal on the adjustment of the member states’ (ms) national contributions to the financing of the eu budget. as it has emerged, a number of ms have underpaid their contributions to the union’s budget over a number of years, while others have overpaid theirs. against this background the commission adopted a proposal to amend the existing rules in order to give ms the possibility, under specific circumstances, of making available the amounts of own resources after the current deadline of 1 december. although the commission’s proposal aims at giving ms more flexibility, it also risks making the current own-resources system even more complex and less transparent. furthermore, the commission’s proposal could create a precedent which would affect the level and timing of payments to benefactors. since we are already facing a growing shortage of payments, this scheme could influence the implementation of the 2014-2020 mff and the credibility of the union’s budget. a real remedy to overcoming the deficiencies of the current system is an extensive reform of the eu’s own-resources system that takes the european parliament proposals into consideration as well as the work carried out by the high-level group on own resources.

rapporteur.– madam president, for the eu this file is a gesture that is symbolic in purely economic terms, but is of great political significance at a critically historic juncture for moldova and, indeed, for our entire european neighbourhood. for moldova, it is a breath of fresh air in a sector of vital importance for the moldovan economy: fruit growing. its importance, however, goes beyond apples and plums, as we shall see in a moment. it also serves as a practical demonstration of solidarity in the face of hardship. the eu and moldova signed their association agreement on 27 june 2014. the moldovan parliament quickly ratified it on 2 july 2014. as if by coincidence, shortly thereafter an import ban was imposed by russia on agricultural products from moldova. on 7 august 2014, russia also imposed a ban on food imports from the eu itself in the context of the ukrainian crisis, which, of course, is linked to the wider question of our eastern neighbourhood. the root of the problem lies in the fact that russia sees itself, wrongly of course, as the object of some sort of geopolitical plot by the western world. it is a conflict generated by a dramatic clash of world views. it is the 19th century fighting the 21st century. blood, invasion from within, propaganda, lies and apples became the ingredients of a very strange new form of warfare. seeking some relief, the moldovan authorities have turned to the eu requesting urgent support to reduce the economic impact of the russian ban, in particular for the most important products of moldovan food growers: apples, plums and table grapes. the commission decided to respond positively. the council agreed and i hope we, the parliament, will also give our blessing this week. the ban is hurting moldova’s economy in a rather dramatic way. agriculture accounts for around 40% of moldova’s gdp. its horticultural sector alone employs a quarter of a million people – that is 10% of the active moldovan population. obviously they mostly live in rural areas and they cultivate small and medium family plots. a few words on the legal context of this proposal: the autonomous trade preferences (atps) are an instrument whereby a trading power, such as ourselves, may offer concessions to a country in order to support its economy without asking for trade concessions in exchange. atps for moldova were originally introduced by the eu in 2008 by the very regulation that we are amending this week. the commission now proposes to amend the atp regulation by introducing three new duty-free quotas for fresh apples (40 000 tonnes), tables grapes and plums (10 000 tonnes each). the quotas will apply until the end of 2015, when the whole regime will expire. the quotas for the three products concerned are extremely limited in volume compared to the potentially competing eu production. for apples, for instance, which is the most sensitive product, it is only 0.4% of our production, and they address very different market segments than most eu production. more specifically, in light of the cultural and geographical proximity with romania, it is very likely that most of the additional volumes of the three products will be absorbed easily by the romanian market. for apples, for example, romania this year has a fall of 22% in production, and the quota under discussion tonight covers only 8% only of romanian production. so there is still a gap there to be filled by others. a few words now in romanian.sper ca autoritățile moldovene să reușească să transforme aceste cote într-o poveste de succes, care să ajute cu adevărat fermierii moldoveni. și aș vrea să fac un apel și la operatorii economici din românia, să folosească această oportunitate cu deschidere față de colegii din republica moldova. merele, prunele și perele din moldova sunt foarte gustoase și vă asigur că ele vor fi apreciate de consumatorii români dacă le vor găsi pe piață.

rapporteur.– madam president, i would like to thank the commissioner and her services for the hard and quick work on this file. i would also like to thank the colleagues who have contributed tonight. i have noticed a lot of common sense in the overwhelming majority of reactions and i believe i have found the proper metaphor to describe this regulation that we will be adopting tomorrow: leverage – and the leverage effect is very fashionable these days. with this resolution we might have an even better factor than 1 to 15. with a very, very small effort on the eu economy side, we will have a very significant effort on the moldovan side. now some very brief reactions to the other comments. mr scholz, i fully agree with you that there should be policies to make sure the moldovan gdp structure includes more diversification and higher added value. i hope the association agreement will be an important instrument in providing for this – and i am personally convinced that it will – including by means of fdi, which will be able to reap the benefits of the huge single market. on enlargement, this is about plums and apples, it is not about enlargement. there are many, many veto players in the enlargement game, and there is no issue whatsoever of surreptitiously pulling moldova into the eu by adopting a regulation on apples. that said, it is a free world and moldovans are free to want to join europe, and political actors and civil society actors in europe are free to support their choice, so we will have a political and democratic process. madame la présidente, monsieur schaffhauser, on blâme la victime pour le viol. on évoque ici la négation de l'identité moldave, mais c'est vraiment du délire. personne ne nie l'identité moldave. personne ne force la moldavie à faire un choix, quel qu'il soit. c'est un pays démocratique, qui fait ses choix démocratiquement.
in writing. the agreement to introduce autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova has led to increased trade and increased exports have had positive effects on the moldovan economy. the european union has become moldova's main trading partner. more than half of the exports and almost as much of the imports are with the eu, confirming that moldova has fulfilled its commitments to the eu and made progress on economic reforms. i would like to stress that the agricultural sector represents 40% of the moldovan economy and provides jobs for about 250 thousand employees. the free access of moldovan agricultural products to european markets contributes to the strengthening of a sector that is essential for the moldovan economy. i am convinced that the presence of agricultural products on eu markets will mean on the one hand an increase in the performance of the agricultural sector and, by implication, an adaptation to eu rules, thus making it easier for moldova to fulfil the pre-accession conditions. on the other hand, moldovan citizens confirmed their pro-european orientation in the parliamentary elections in november. the economic component of the eu association agreement is therefore a natural step towards fulfilling european aspirations.

in writing. one of the foundations of the eu is the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community. the eu must not lose sight of this foundation, but must continue to invest in the steel industry, which is essential for economic growth. this sector provides 350 000 direct jobs and several million related jobs. i believe that investment at eu level in high-tech industries and by implication in the steel industry becomes imperative to avoid their offshoring outside the eu. i call on the commission to ensure the competitiveness of european industry on the world market and to ensure real fair competition. this is possible through the effective use of the european globalisation adjustment fund and the european social fund. the commission should also use the european regional development fund to make the necessary investments in research and innovation to revitalise this sector, in particular in innovative production processes and energy efficiency. last but not least, i ask the commission to closely monitor the situation of romanian combines in order to avoid further closures or sales to competitors in third countries.
in writing. — in the face of lowering global demand and an increasingly uneven global playing field, the steel industry, once the backbone of the european economy, is currently going through tough times. heavy yearly reductions in production capacities, massive layoffs all over the continent and the looming threat of europe switching from exporter to a net importer of steel, all form one depressing reality. given this state of affairs, my vote goes in favour of putting some action behind today’s political rhetoric calling for a european industrial renaissance. while not sacrificing environmental standards or the voice of our steel workers in the process, european steel needs a clear support plan to get back on the track of growth. our union’s long-term industrial competitiveness is clearly at stake here.
in writing. the economic recovery in europe depends to a large extent on a strong manufacturing industry, in which the steel industry must play a key role. we urge the commission to speed up the preparation of the roadmap for industrial policy announced for the first part of 2015 to revitalise european industry on the world market with a view to ensuring a level playing field, while guaranteeing high social and environmental standards in the eu. the commission should also allocate part of its investment package to long-term viable infrastructure projects and to innovation in industrial macro-projects, including energy efficiency and low carbon projects, which could also significantly boost eu steel demand. i stress that investment in research and innovation is crucial for the recovery and relaunch of the european economy in general and the steel industry in particular. it is essential to support the steel sector, including through the strategic development of new key steel-using sectors, thus creating incentives for efficient production processes, strengthening the internal market and stimulating skills development.
in writing. in the first nine months of 2014, according to the international organisation for migration, at least 3 072 people lost their lives in the mediterranean. it is well known that traffickers in human beings and members of illegal immigration networks profit from illegal immigration. these networks pose a major risk to the lives of migrants and a problem for the eu. member states have a duty to respect their international obligations in the field of rescue at sea. i believe that a global approach to migration is essential, as is a constructive assessment of the overall strategy of cooperation with third countries, including sub-saharan africa, north africa and the middle east, on humanitarian, financial and political assistance.
mr. president, the issue of the cia's use of torture has been a polarizing issue in public opinion in the united states for years. the release of the senate report last week confirmed the existing rift within the american political class. democrats and republicans are deeply divided on a number of issues, namely, whether this report accurately reflects what happened, whether the procedure followed was itself correct, and even whether this report should have been published given its potential security implications. all of these issues are being questioned and disputed in the united states. we don't have a unified view that comes from the united states. personally, i would like to stress that i feel very close to the position expressed by republican senator john mccain, who supported the release of the report and criticized the cia's practices that would, in his opinion, cause harm to american security interests. i thought it was very wise when senator mccain said, "we make mistakes, we make mistakes, we fix those mistakes, and we commit to never doing them again". no one can claim today that the practices highlighted in the cia report continue. it's actually an episode that belongs to the past. president obama ended the interrogation program in 2009. i would say that the desire to clarify things was very clear in the united states, and i think that's the main lesson that we have to take away. it's a healthy thing for a political regime to seriously examine its own drift.
mr president, the attacks of 11 september 2001 in the united states, as well as those in madrid, london and boston, have shown us that no nation is secure, and that terrorism can strike anywhere, anytime and with unimaginable power, with the lives of millions of people constantly at risk. these things have caused nations around the world - not just the united states - to join forces in a common cause, to abandon defensiveness and to react. today's situation, where the islamic state is able to recruit more and more followers, perhaps also because of a polarization of society, shows us that peace, security and the safety of the citizen are values that are always in danger. innocent people fall victim to savage acts of terrorism every day, and recent tragedies show us that these threats take a domestic form, in other words they come from the holders of european passports. the detention centres have emerged as a consequence of the fact that terrorism does not take into account borders and, at the same time, of the need to identify its causes and, above all, to find answers to what needs to be done to eliminate or at least reduce this phenomenon. that's why i think that over-politicizing this phenomenon is not in anyone's interest. however, and i stress 'however', we can never agree to inhuman means of obtaining information. torture, inhuman and degrading treatment must be rejected under all circumstances. to do otherwise would only turn the victims into stones, and their guilt would be no less. the common goals of all nations must be to uphold international human rights standards, and at the same time we must be concerned about the safety of our citizens, wherever they may be.
it is certainly commendable that such a report could be produced in the united states, stating that cia agents extracted information from suspects by methods incompatible with human rights. but i think we should end our polite words here, because i find the cia's practice of this kind of thing outrageous, even though the president of the united states says that this is a thing of the past. while it is not impossible that other countries may use similar methods, it is a matter of concern that the united states may do so, putting human rights protection in the last place when its interests dictate. although the administration of justice in a state of law is sometimes slow and circumstantial, i think it is the respect for this that distinguishes democracies based on freedom and the rule of law from other parts of the world. if we don't hold ourselves to our own self-made standards in some cases, we have learned nothing from the lessons of the 20th century.

in writing. – the topic of cia secret prisons and practices during the ʽwar on terrorʼ keeps regularly surfacing. most of the times, that re-surfacing is due to journalistic investigation based on ʽundisclosedʼ sources which, because of their anonymity, cannot be challenged. the difference this time is that the report is authored by the us senate, until recently dominated by the democrats. consequently, the report has come under heavy attack from an array of personalities and institutions – many directly linked to the political and security sectors – for political bias and incorrectness. romania was a ʽtargetʼ from the very beginning, although the site of the so-called secret detention facility kept circling around – the mk air base, bucharest, dobrogea, etc. even if the us senate report does not mention any country, journalistic articles were capable of ʽidentifyingʼ it, again based exclusively on ʽjournalistic sourcesʼ linked to the washington post newspaper! it is clear that, under the circumstances, the report is being used as an opportunity to name countries which otherwise are not named. if torture and illegal practices against anybody, including notorious criminals who have the blood of thousands on their hands, are unacceptable, than pure political speculation is equally unacceptable.

mr president, every year armed conflicts, persecution, a lack of economic prospects, human rights violations and natural disasters force millions of people to leave their homes in the horn of africa to embark on dangerous journeys through multiple countries and to cross the mediterranean sea in their efforts to reach europe. during their journey, their hopes for personal safety and for a better future are often destroyed by organised criminal gangs of smugglers and traffickers, by lack of food and water and by unsafe transportation while travelling. once here in europe they are often welcomed with racism, exploitation and exclusion. however, if we step up efforts, our policies will change the lives of millions of people. our decisions will improve the well-being and the living conditions of immigrants. to do this we must first make sure that our development policies address the root causes of immigration. if we support governments, civil organisations and individual citizens in developing countries to implement good governance and to create a more prosperous society that gives a chance to its citizens, then migration finally becomes a free personal choice. secondly, we must remember the benefits that well-protected and integrated migrants have for development, in fuelling growth, innovation and entrepreneurship both in the countries that the people come from and in those they move to. well-managed migration can reduce poverty in the countries of origin by remittance transfers. job opportunities can motivate young people to acquire appropriate skills. there will be a rise in the exchange of goods, capital and knowledge. we are all aware of the fact that migration will only rise in the future, but if we can make it clear in our own minds and to the general public that there is an undeniable positive interconnection between migration and development, then migration will cease to be another world problem and will start being part of the solution. luckily, the interconnection was made clear in the council conclusions adopted last friday on migration in eu development cooperation. this is a necessary first step, and i look forward to hearing how the european commission will implement these conclusions.
